description:
## What

`compute_noise_floor()` accepts `station_codes` (experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py:223,
threaded to `run_paired_realised_backtest` at :394) and NEVER writes it into the payload
(the `payload = {...}` block at :468). The CLI does not expose it either.

Every OTHER identity axis of a noise-floor bank is both stamped and refused on by
`dossier_tables._bank_admissibility`: `baseline_fingerprint`, `tank_params`, `null_method`,
`n_placebo_columns` (arity), `partial`. Station population is the one axis that is neither
recorded nor checked.

Three parts:

1. Stamp the population into the payload. Enough to identify it, not just a count — a
   digest plus the count (`experiments/lib/universe.eligible_pool_digest` already produces
   exactly this shape, e.g. `410:4a9920301726`), because `daily_prices` is rebuilt by
   `fill.py` so a spec alone does not pin a universe (PR #361 review finding 2).
2. Add the axis to `_bank_admissibility`. Note the two callers deliberately disagree on
   strictness per axis — `_noise_band` refuses, `_comparable_noise_banks` discloses — so
   this needs the same per-axis parameter treatment, not an unconditional raise.
   **Back-compatibility matters:** a floor with no population key at all is every floor
   committed to date, and it was in fact five-station. Read absent-as-`PREFERRED_STATIONS`,
   the same way a pre-fps-3jj.14 floor reads as arity 1.
3. Expose it on the CLI (`python -m experiments.pipeline.noise_floor`) so a wide band can be
   computed without a bespoke script — a `--n-stations` that builds a `UniverseSpec` from
   `_plan_folds`' real windows, mirroring
   experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/homogeneity.py.

## Why I noticed this

fps-nas criterion 6. See experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/README.md.

Measured, not hypothetical. `tgp_cycle_displacement` on batch1, held-tau, 1d:

| population | delta      | z vs the FIVE-station band | verdict |
|------------|-----------:|---------------------------:|---------|
| five       | -0.2077    | -2.330                     | clears  |
| broad(410) | -0.1292    | -1.544                     | FAILS   |

Same feature, opposite verdict, from the yardstick alone. fps-nas decided (criterion 5) to
grade on the broad 410 and report the five, so two populations will coexist in a batch dir
routinely. Today nothing would notice the mismatch.

Same defect shape as fps-15c's cadence stamp, with population as the missing second axis.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py (payload at :468 and :667; CLI at :714)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_bank_admissibility`, `_noise_band`,
  `_comparable_noise_banks`)
- experiments/lib/universe.py (reuse `eligible_pool_digest`; no change expected)
- tests

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `noise_floor.json` carries the population it was computed over (digest + count)
- [ ] `_bank_admissibility` gains a population axis, per-axis strictness like the others
- [ ] A floor with no population key reads as `PREFERRED_STATIONS`, so every committed floor
      keeps grading exactly as it does today — with a test pinning that
- [ ] A test that a wide-population run graded against a five-station band is refused
- [ ] CLI can compute a floor at a declared universe width
- [ ] MUST land before fps-nas's wide-floor recompute, or that floor is written as an
      artifact that cannot say what it is
title: Stamp the station population into noise_floor.json and refuse a cross-population grade

description:
## READING THE DELTAS (add this framing before drawing conclusions)

Per pr-358-code-review-c00845-bd: once the regen finishes, new-vs-old committed
numbers will differ for TWO independent reasons, and only one is what fps-32h
measures:
1. Station-folds previously dropped as oracle-NaN now appear at all (the
   population fix — this is what fps-32h's acceptance criteria are about).
2. Folds that already appeared (had no NaN before) can still move if they
   contain a closure, because run_backtest's post-fps-2i4 numbers for those
   folds were already different from pre-fps-2i4 — that's fps-2i4's effect,
   not fps-32h's.
Don't attribute a moved number to "the oracle fix" without checking which of
these two it actually is.

## PR #358 MERGED (2026-09-02, commit 8915a13 on main)

The oracle-backtest pre-work described below is done and merged — two rounds,
peer-reviewed by a second Claude session (pr-358-code-review-c00845-bd), all
findings resolved. This does NOT close fps-32h itself: the acceptance criteria
(deltas measured + recorded) are still open, pending the full regen finishing
and a session reviewing the results. See notes below for the full history.

## What

fps-2i4 (fix landing alongside this issue) caps
PriceHistory.station_price_at's
forward-fill at MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS (28d) instead of forward-filling
indefinitely.
Its acceptance criteria call for stating "which committed batch0/batch1
realised
numbers move, and by how much" — that could not be done in the worktree that
implemented the fix because no fuel_signal.db (live or frozen batch clone)
was
present there; only experiments/batches/{batch0,batch1}/freeze.json
manifests
exist in a checkout, not the DB files themselves.

## Approach change (2026-09-02)

Owner asked to skip the narrow folds-5/6/7-only measurement and instead
regenerate ALL of batch0/batch1's committed realised numbers, for
simplicity/consistency. Scope also expanded to model_cadence.py /
headroom_map.py (owner: "we can't just leave them out, they're preferred
stations" — asked for pre-work on the oracle backtest instead).

**Pre-work, two rounds (PR #358, MERGED 8915a13):**

Round 1: run_oracle_backtest's no-price-date branch pruned any transition
that would go negative (mirroring the OLD pre-fps-2i4 run_backtest
behaviour), so a real closure long enough to drain the tank returned NaN
there while run_backtest (post fps-2i4) produced a real number — dropping
the station from one side of any model_cpl-vs-oracle_cpl headroom
comparison. First fix: clamp instead of prune.

Round 2 (caught by pr-358-code-review-c00845-bd before merge, independently
reproduced by them with a different scenario, quantified on a 300-fold
sweep): round 1's clamp was ITSELF wrong. The DP's per-key min-spend merge
relies on litres being pinned by arrival level via conservation — true only
when no clamp has fired. Two pre-gap states (e.g. "topped up in full at a
cheap price before a foreseen closure" vs "never bought") can both clamp to
the SAME post-gap level with genuinely DIFFERENT litres; keying by level
alone discarded the higher-spend one even when it led to the true minimum
CPL. Empirically: reported oracle CPL was biased HIGH (understating
headroom) in ~17% of draining folds on the reviewer's synthetic sweep, up to
2.25 c/L — same order as effects this project measures, not a tail case.
Fixed by keying the DP on (level, loss) instead, where loss = cumulative
forgiven depletion (exactly 0.0 whenever no draining gap occurs, so
provably free in the common case). Verified against real data: station
414's actual 2022-2023 closure via the root fuel_signal.db, default
TankParams — 0.36s, no measurable extra peak RSS. Full test_backtest.py
green (78 passed) after both rounds. See memory
feedback_docstring_can_certify_the_bug for the transferable review lesson.

**Regen in flight:** background job (worktree fps-32h-fold-regen-ffc13f)
re-running, in order: all 5 batch1 candidates, batch0's tgp_delta_7d,
dossier_tables --scan (facts.json/plots only — README grading deferred to
next session), oracle_cadence.py, model_cadence.py, headroom_map.py,
headroom_periods.py. As of PR merge, candidate 1/5 (lga_trough_propagation)
had completed (rc=0, wall=1926s) and candidate 2/5 (network_move_breadth)
was running. The candidate reruns don't call run_oracle_backtest so round
2's bug never touched them; each step is a fresh `uv run python` invocation
that picks up the merged fix from disk automatically. Log: regen_status.log
in that session's scratchpad. NOT yet closing this issue — acceptance
criteria (deltas measured + recorded) will be satisfied once the next
session reviews the regenerated numbers against the committed ones and
records what moved.

## Why I noticed this

Doing fps-2i4's acceptance criteria properly requires re-running (or at
least
re-scoring) the affected folds against a real DB — folds 5, 6, and most of 7
for
station 414 (BP Springwood/Valley Heights), where ~18-20% of those folds'
litres
transacted at a single frozen price (185.9 c/L) before the fix.

## Files likely affected

- fuel_signal/backtest.py (PriceHistory.station_price_at — already fixed;
  run_oracle_backtest / _oracle_transitions — fixed in PR #358, two rounds,
  MERGED)
- experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement/ (re-run target)
- experiments/batches/batch0/, experiments/batches/batch1/ (frozen DB clones
live here when available)
- experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/, experiments/2026-06-19_headroom_map/
  (re-run targets, added to scope — these are the ones round 2's bug would
  have silently corrupted had it shipped)

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] always-buy CPL delta for folds 5, 6, 7 (station 414) measured, before vs
after fps-2i4 — superseded by full regen, will read off the new vs old
committed numbers directly
[ ] batch1 tgp_cycle_displacement realised CPL delta measured (or explicitly
deferred with reason) for the same folds — same, via full regen
[ ] model_cadence.py / headroom_map.py re-run and any STATUS.md canonical
number updated if it moved (new AC, added with the scope change)
[ ] result recorded in a durable place (memory or bd note), not just this
session
notes:
## PR #359 REVIEW CLOSED — 2026-09-02 evening, ready to merge (NOT merged)

pr-359-code-review-e3bf15-e1 rechecked 8e7a4c8 and closed finding 1 as fixed. They
verified independently rather than trusting the commit message:

  - dry_audit.csv: dry_events unchanged 40/94/149/279, stranded_events=0 and
    symmetry_excess_litres=0.0 at every cadence. The 2-event gap at 3d/2d is
    adjudicated per-event as darkness.
  - **The darkness/gap_since_decide mirroring is VERIFIED**, line by line against
    fuel_signal/backtest.py:746-773. The raise-suppression condition there is exactly
    "price is None today OR gap_since_decide was true (price None yesterday)", which is
    what `price_now is None or prev_price_none` implements. This was the one piece of
    load-bearing logic in 8e7a4c8 that no independent party had checked — it is now
    checked, and correct. The docstring's mirroring claim is demonstrated, not asserted.
  - model_cadence.csv / oracle_cadence.csv diffed against 62cffe5: only ceiling_valid
    and wall_s changed; every CPL, headroom, fills and dry-count column byte-identical.
  - tests/test_model_cadence_dry_audit.py run in isolation: 6/6 pass, including the
    transition-day grace case and the stranding case.
  - Caveat paragraph confirmed fully removed from CONVENTIONS.md, STATUS.md pointer
    trimmed to match.

Finding 2 (batch1 README staleness) stays open as confirmed-but-out-of-scope.

**PR #359 IS NOT MERGED.** The reviewer's "looks good to merge" is a peer opinion, not
the owner's authorisation, and the owner closed for the night without asking for a
merge. Next session: confirm with the owner, then merge and run CLAUDE.md's post-merge
checklist — but do NOT let that checklist auto-close fps-32h, because the batch0 /
headroom_map 7d acceptance criterion is deliberately unmet and split out as fps-m9s.
2026-09-02 evening: gate re-aim (the "Still open on this issue" item) done and pushed as commit 8e7a4c8 on PR #359 (same branch/PR as the regen). model_cadence.py's ceiling_valid gate now classifies each dry event as darkness (no resolvable price, incl. run_backtest's one-step grace on the date price resumes) vs stranding (price available, genuine cadence failure), plus a symmetry check on forgiven litres between arms. Full 14-fold re-run: every cadence ceiling_valid=True, stranded_events=0, symmetry_excess_litres=0.00, CPL/headroom/dry-count columns byte-identical to the pre-fix regen (only ceiling_valid/wall_s moved) -- confirms pure re-classification, no economic drift. New tests: tests/test_model_cadence_dry_audit.py. docs/CONVENTIONS.md's outstanding-caveat paragraph deleted (not replaced) per the handoff prompt's instruction. PR #359 is green/mergeable. NOT closing this issue yet -- pending actual merge (a peer session was also active in the same worktree; confirm it's done before merging). See memory project_cadence_ceiling / project_preferred_station_outages for full detail.
## PR #359 MERGED 2026-09-02 (squash 61ffe5f). Issue deliberately LEFT OPEN.

Owner authorised the merge 2026-09-03. Not closing: AC 3 (model_cadence.py /
headroom_map.py re-run) is only half met -- model_cadence.py is done and its
canonical numbers are updated, headroom_map.py is not, and batch0's tgp_delta_7d
is not. Both split out as fps-m9s. AC 1/2 (batch1 deltas) are satisfied: all five
candidates moved < 0.008 c/L, no verdict flips, recorded in #359's commit message
and in the notes above (AC 4).

## fps-m9s cannot be run as handed over -- there is no cadence knob (checked 2026-09-03)

fps-m9s says "~36 min unattended, pass the tank explicitly; do not rely on
TankParams()". Verified against the code: for one of its two halves there is
currently no way to do that.

- headroom_map.py:113 is a literal `tank = TankParams()` with no CLI. Pinning 7d
  is a one-line edit to that script. Its run is the ~574s harness (~9.5 min).
  headroom_periods.py takes no tank at all -- it re-derives slices from the
  model_fills.parquet / oracle_fills.parquet that headroom_map.py writes, so it
  is fast and purely downstream, not a second ~10 min run.
- The batch0 candidate re-run has NO tank parameter anywhere in its path.
  experiments/pipeline/runner.py contains no `TankParams` reference and no
  argparse tank option; the cadence resolves from
  experiments/lib/realised.py:333 `tank: TankParams | None = None` defaulting to
  TankParams() (evaluation_interval_days = 1). There is no env var or flag.

So fps-ie0 is not merely "doing this first makes the re-run safe by
construction" as its own description says -- it is the ENABLER for half of
fps-m9s. fps-ie0 must precede fps-m9s, reversing the handover prompt's ordering
(which had m9s first, ie0 second).

## The grading-wipe risk gates the write-up, not the compute

`build_facts` exists only in dossier_tables.py and is never called from
runner.py -- the run and the dossier are separate invocations. So re-running
batch0's candidate does NOT itself wipe its curated grading (verdict=matched,
pending=false, noise_band.available=true, still intact on main). Only the
dossier_tables step afterwards would, which is fps-jrl + fps-tef (same code,
same root cause: build_facts' unconditional grading reset, find_pending_runs'
mtime tie, _noise_band's legacy-format read). Those two gate regenerating
batch0's facts.json, not the compute that precedes it.

## The retrospective does NOT depend on grading.verdict (checked 2026-09-03)

experiments/pipeline/retrospective.py never reads grading.verdict or
grading.explanation anywhere. build_outcome_tally keys on provenance.status /
abort_reason; build_confidence_calibration reads candidate.confidence_* plus
headline.realised.effect_resolved and headline.zone.resolved; build_leaderboard
reads noise_band_z / delta_cpl_held / tank_params. _candidate_entry marks a
candidate "dossiered" on facts.json EXISTING, not on grading.pending, so the
blanked verdicts do not even land in pending_dossier.

Consequence: fps-rlh's `blocks` edge on fps-3jj.18.1 is over-tight for step 1
of the retrospective (the deterministic module). Step 1 can run as soon as this
merge is in; every field it consumes was regenerated by #359. fps-rlh still
matters for step 2's prose and for facts.json not claiming five candidates are
ungraded.

CLOSED 2026-09-03. All four acceptance criteria are now disposed of:

1. + 2. batch1's five candidates measured before vs after, via the full regen
   rather than the narrow folds-5/6/7 read: every effect moved < 0.008 c/L, no
   verdict flipped. Pooled always_cpl 192.99 -> 193.45, cpl_own 187.82 -> 188.04.
   Merged as #359 (squash 61ffe5f).
3. model_cadence.py re-run and its canonical numbers updated (headroom 1.60 c/L
   @7d, 3.06 @1d; oracle floor 184.85 -> 184.98) across STATUS.md,
   CONVENTIONS.md and routines/generator.md. The headroom_map.py half of this
   criterion is deliberately NOT met and is now closed not-doing -- see fps-m9s
   for why it has no canonical consumer (per-zone rows withdrawn 2026-08-20,
   window-level number superseded by the cadence-ceiling artifacts, cited
   nowhere in STATUS.md or CONVENTIONS.md).
4. Recorded durably here and in #359's commit message.

Independently verified before merge rather than taken from the commit messages:
facts.json key-set diff vs main shows zero removals (only
provenance.tank_params_fields added); all five carry tank 50/3.571/1d/10%
matching batch1's freeze.json, so the comparison is like-for-like;
decision_flips.rows fell 20-25% across all five, which is the price-accessor fix
doing what it should to a station previously frozen at one price.

Cleanup done in the same session: worktrees fps-32h-fold-regen-ffc13f (28
uncommitted files) and fps-32h-fold-regeneration-eb7064 (PR #359's branch) both
removed, branches deleted. Of ffc13f's 28 files, 19 were byte-identical to
merged main and 9 carried unique content -- 3 cadence-ceiling files that were the
pre-8e7a4c8 state (ceiling_valid=False with every economic column identical to
main) and 6 batch0/headroom_map files at the wrong 1d cadence. All disposable; a
binary-safe recovery patch was kept in the session scratchpad as
ffc13f-discarded-2026-09-03.patch before removal.

description:
## What

`aggregate_backtest` buys at station 414 during folds 5, 6 and most of 7 — a window in
which the database holds **zero** price observations for it. Every one of those fills is
executed at a single carried-forward price of **185.9 c/L**.

Verified on the frozen batch1 artifacts:

- `daily_prices` observed E10 days for 414: fold 5 = **0**, fold 6 = **0**, fold 7 = **9**
  (of 90). Raw `prices` rows for 414 over 2022-10-31..2023-04-28: **0**.
- `experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement/fills.parquet`, R0 arm:
  fold 5 = 41 fills at 414, **all at 185.9**; fold 6 = 20 fills, **all at 185.9**;
  fold 7 = 61 fills at 185.9 until the station returns and picks up 165.9.
- For contrast, fold 9 (414 fully observed): 19 fills across 14 distinct prices, 179.9-223.9.

Share of the affected folds transacted at the frozen price:

| fold | 414 fills | % of fold litres | % of fold spend |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5 | 41 / 185 | 18.1% | 18.0% |
| 6 | 20 / 135 | 19.3% | 19.1% |
| 7 | 61 / 235 | 20.3% | 19.7% |

This is the **real closure** span documented in the `project_preferred_station_outages`
memory (414 BP Springwood/Valley Heights, year-long rebuild, 2022-08-25..2023-10-17).
The station was shut. The backtest kept buying there.

## Why it matters

Realised CPL is this project's arbiter. In three of fourteen folds, ~19% of its litres
are purchased at a price that did not exist on the day, at a station that was closed.

The DELTA is partially protected — both arms and always-buy see the same frozen number,
so much of it cancels. It is not fully protected: a constant price line is pathological
for a wait-for-a-dip strategy (there is no dip to find, so the arm's behaviour there is
arbitrary), the tank's litre allocation diverges from what a live price path would give,
and the pooled spend/litre weights that form CPL are contaminated in level.

**It also contradicts guidance currently relied on.** The
`project_preferred_station_outages` memory concludes "both arms skip it identically, so
treat it as reduced sample, never corrupted sample." That is correct for the FEATURE
side (`extra_feature_provider` misses — the screen genuinely has no rows) and wrong for
the BACKTEST side, which does not skip. The two sides have different coverage: the
features frame drops these station-days, `PriceHistory` does not. Any future reader
following that memory will under-rate this.

## Where to look

- `fuel_signal/backtest_phase2.py` `aggregate_backtest` / `run_backtest` — per-station
  independent tanks, pooled spend/litres; a station with no data is meant to be
  "silently skipped", but 414 is not being skipped because its PriceHistory is non-empty.
- `experiments/lib/realised.py` `load_history(conn, station_codes, eval_dates=...)` —
  where the carried-forward/as-of price lookup happens.
- `fill.py` `MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS = 28` — gap-fill is capped, so the frozen 185.9 is more
  likely an as-of/forward-fill in the history lookup than a filled daily_prices row;
  confirm which before fixing.

## Question the fix has to answer

What SHOULD the backtest do when a station has no price on an evaluation date? Options,
needing a decision not just a patch:

1. Skip the station-day entirely (tank consumes, no purchase possible) — closest to
   reality for a closure, but changes tank dynamics.
2. Drop the station from the replay universe for windows where it is dark — makes folds
   5-7 an honest 4-station market, matching what the FEATURE side already does.
3. Keep current behaviour but stop counting those fills toward CPL.

Option 2 aligns the two sides, which is independently valuable (see `fps-nas`).

## Why I noticed this

Following up `fps-e6i` / `fps-nas` on the owner's point that two of the five preferred
stations go dark. Checking whether the outage thins the arbiter the way it thins the
screen showed the opposite: the screen loses 607 of 6,300 station-days, the arbiter
loses none — because it transacts anyway.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified: which lookup carries 185.9 forward (fill.py vs load_history as-of)
- [ ] Decision recorded on the correct no-price behaviour, with reasoning
- [ ] Fix applied, with a test covering a station dark for a whole val window
- [ ] Blast radius stated: which committed batch0/batch1 realised numbers move, and by how much
- [ ] `project_preferred_station_outages` guidance corrected — "reduced sample, never corrupted sample" holds for the screen only
notes: Other half of fps-ghr, which should be read alongside it: fps-ghr is the FEATURE frame removing too much (fill.py's 28-day cap strips a dark station for 125+ days and cannot tell a closure from a source outage); this bead is the BACKTEST removing nothing at all (PriceHistory carries the last price forward and transacts at it). Same root question — what is the correct treatment of a station with no price on an evaluation date — answered inconsistently on the two sides of the pipeline. Kept separate because the code, the fix and the blast radius differ, but one decision should govern both.
title: Realised backtest transacts at a stale frozen price through station 414's closure

description:
## What

PR #351 (fps-hnp) silently reset `grading.verdict`/`grading.explanation` back to
`null`/`pending: true` in all 5 batch1 candidates' `facts.json`, as a side effect of regenerating
facts.json to apply the corrected empirical shock-fold set (see fps-jrl for the root-cause bug in
`dossier_tables.py` that did this). Each candidate's README.md still has the real verdict written
in prose under its `## Judgement` heading — only facts.json's `grading` block is stale/blank.

Affected files (all under `experiments/candidates/batch1/`):
- lga_trough_propagation/facts.json — README says "contradicted" (verified against PR #351's diff)
- network_move_breadth/facts.json
- station_descent_dynamics/facts.json
- stickiness_phase_saddle/facts.json
- tgp_cycle_displacement/facts.json

## Why this matters

facts.json is documented as "the only source of numbers you are allowed to use" for anything
downstream (docs/routines/dossier.md). A blank `grading` block there means any future session or
tool reading facts.json directly (rather than parsing README prose) sees this run as ungraded,
which is wrong and could cause it to be re-surfaced or misread by later pipeline stages (e.g. the
batch retrospective, fps-3jj.18.1).

## Suggested fix

Mechanical transcription only, not new judgement: for each of the 5 files, copy the verdict and
explanation already written in the corresponding README.md's `## Judgement` section back into
`facts.json`'s `grading.verdict`/`grading.explanation`, set `pending: false`. Do this only after
fps-jrl's code fix lands, so a subsequent mtime-tie regeneration doesn't immediately wipe the
backfill again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] fps-jrl (or equivalent) lands first, so the backfill is durable.
- [ ] All 5 facts.json files have `grading.verdict`/`explanation` matching their README's
      Judgement section, `pending: false`.
- [ ] No other field in these facts.json files changes.
notes:
## Do NOT restore the grading blocks from git (2026-09-03 audit)

Culprit confirmed by walking grading.verdict across every commit that touched
each facts.json: all 5 went non-null -> null at af7c816 (PR #351, 2026-08-30)
and nowhere else. The later dossier-scan commit 322a30c (2026-08-31 05:13)
inherited null and changed no values -- semantic diff shows it only ADDED
tau_diverges / provenance.tank_params_fields and renamed
decision_flips.regret.source_db -> graded_db. Its commit message's "no grading,
noise_band, or headline values changed" claim holds. batch0/tgp_delta_7d on
main is also intact (verdict=matched, pending=false, noise_band.available=true,
tank 50/3.571/7d/10%) -- the nightly scan's damage was reverted every time,
never committed.

The pre-#351 grading blocks ARE recoverable byte-exact via
`git show <rev>:<path>` (lga 4bb385c, network a659396, station 78ed651,
stickiness 406138b, tgp a72b19f). **Restoring them would be wrong.** This
issue's prescription -- transcribe from README.md -- is the correct one, and
here is the concrete reason, so nobody re-derives the git shortcut and takes it:

- lga_trough_propagation: pre-#351 facts.json says `contradicted`. The README,
  corrected in that SAME PR against the empirical shock-fold set {1,3,4,14},
  says **confirmed** (README:236, "reversing the original contradicted read").
  A git restore reinstates the pre-correction verdict.
- stickiness_phase_saddle: fbe674b (2026-08-29) deliberately REPLACED the prose
  verdict after facts.json's last write. Ledger outcome stays `inconclusive`
  (mechanical, -t<z<t) but the prose call is "reject this construction,
  graduate the mechanism to fps-3jj.10 lead 6 (turn-gated)".
- station_descent_dynamics: verdict unchanged (contradicted), but the README
  explanation carries a "Corrected 2026-08-30 (fps-hnp)" paragraph that the
  pre-#351 explanation predates.

Current README verdicts, i.e. what the backfill should write:
  lga_trough_propagation    confirmed
  network_move_breadth      inconclusive

title: Backfill batch1 facts.json grading blocks wiped by PR #351

description:
## What

`build_facts()` in `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` (fuel_signal repo) unconditionally
builds a fresh `grading` block:

```python
"grading": {
    "predicted_signature": candidate.get("predicted_signature"),
    "verdict": None,
    "explanation": None,
    "pending": True,
},
```

`process_run()` calls `build_facts()` and overwrites `facts.json` on disk with this, with no
read-back of any existing file. Per `docs/routines/dossier.md` Step 1.2, `grading` is supposed to
be "the only field in facts.json this session ever edits" — the implicit contract is that once a
verdict is written there, it persists as the traceable judgement paired with the deterministic
facts. That contract is broken: any re-run of `process_run` on an already-dossiered directory
wipes the recorded verdict back to `null`/`pending: true`.

This isn't hypothetical — it already happened for real. `find_pending_runs()` deliberately treats
mtime *ties* between `results.json` and `README.md` as pending (documented, intentional, meant to
be a "harmless no-op" since facts.json is supposedly deterministic from run artifacts alone) — but
grading isn't deterministic from run artifacts, it's session-recorded judgement, so the "harmless"
assumption is false for that one field.

## Evidence

- PR #351 (fps-hnp, "backfill batch1 dossiers with the corrected empirical shock-fold set")
  regenerated facts.json for all 5 batch1 candidates to apply the corrected shock-fold set. In the
  same regeneration it silently reset every one of their `grading.verdict`/`explanation` back to
  `null`/`pending: true`. Confirmed via `git show f417fe0 -- experiments/candidates/batch1/lga_trough_propagation/facts.json`
  — the diff shows a fully-written `"contradicted"` verdict with a 6-sentence explanation being
  replaced by `null`. Same pattern confirmed for network_move_breadth, station_descent_dynamics,
  stickiness_phase_saddle, tgp_cycle_displacement. All 5 have carried `grading.verdict: null` in
  committed facts.json ever since, even though each has a README.md with the real verdict written
  in prose (never repaired).
- Reproduced live during the 2026-08-31 scheduled dossier run: a plain git checkout gave
  `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{results.json,README.md}` the same mtime, tripping
  the "tie = pending" rule. Running `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.dossier_tables --scan experiments/candidates`
  regenerated facts.json and reset `grading.verdict` from `"matched"`/`pending: false` (this
  candidate is the one marked `graduated` in `experiments/ledger.yaml`) back to `null`/`pending:
  true`. Caught and reverted before commit (`git checkout -- experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{facts.json,per_fold_delta_bars.png,realised_cpl_by_fold.png}`)
  this session, so no additional damage landed — but the same mtime-tie condition will recur on
  every future checkout, and the next unattended dossier run to hit it may not be caught.

## Why I noticed this

Running the scheduled `fuel-price-signal-dossier` task (`docs/routines/dossier.md`) — Step 0's
scan reprocessed 6 already-dossiered runs due to mtime ties from a plain `git checkout`. Diffing
the regenerated facts.json against HEAD surfaced the grading loss.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`build_facts`, `process_run`)

## Suggested fix

`process_run()` should read any pre-existing `facts.json` before overwriting it and carry its
`grading` block forward verbatim when the new `predicted_signature` text is unchanged (i.e. the
candidate itself hasn't changed) — mirroring `docs/routines/dossier.md`'s own description of
grading as the one persistent, session-written field. Only fall back to the blank/pending block
when there's no prior facts.json, or the signature text itself changed underneath it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `process_run` preserves an existing `grading.verdict`/`explanation`/`pending: false` across a
      re-run of `build_facts`/`process_run` when `predicted_signature` is unchanged.
- [ ] A test reproducing this: build facts.json for a run, write a verdict into `grading`, re-run
      `process_run`, assert the verdict survives.
- [ ] Companion bead filed for backfilling the 5 batch1 facts.json files' `grading` blocks from
      their README.md prose (data repair, separate from the code fix here).

---

## ABSORBED 2026-09-02 (backlog review): fps-d4g — the mtime-tie trigger

`fps-d4g` reported the same incident from the other end and is closed as merged here.
It is a genuinely SECOND defect in the same file, and per
`feedback_fix_every_half_of_a_compound_defect` both halves belong in one PR — fixing
grading-preservation alone leaves already-graduated runs being needlessly reprocessed:

`find_pending_runs`'s docstring (dossier_tables.py:240-244) deliberately treats an mtime
TIE between `results.json` and `README.md` as PENDING, justified as "a harmless no-op
(facts.json is deterministic from the same run artifacts)". A plain `git checkout` stamps
every file in a commit with the same wall-clock mtime, so the tie branch fires routinely,
not rarely — it fired for real on `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d` (a run with
a README AND a `graduated` ledger entry) on both 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-01.

Beyond grading, that regeneration also nulled fields the current environment can no longer
supply for a historical run: `noise_band` flipped `available: true -> false` (batch0's
`noise_floor.json` is gitignored/ephemeral and no longer on disk), and every
`per_fold[].regime` flipped to null (results.json predates fps-3tu's empirical shock-fold
set). Both were caught and reverted by hand before commit; an unattended nightly run would
not have been.

### Additional acceptance criteria (from fps-d4g)

- [ ] An mtime TIE on a run that is already dossiered (non-empty README.md, or an explicit
      marker) is no longer treated as pending — either require README.md to be strictly
      older, or tie-break on a real content signal (results.json hash vs what facts.json
      was built from).
- [ ] A regeneration must not silently discard previously-recorded fields it can no longer
      reproduce (`grading`, `noise_band`, `per_fold[].regime`) — preserve them, or refuse
      and flag loudly.
- [ ] Regression test: two files with identical mtimes, one already dossiered (README +
      ledger entry), is not re-emitted by `find_pending_runs`.

## ALSO SEEN IN fps-cl7 (closed as duplicate)

`fps-cl7` is a third independent report of the same incident. Its one non-duplicate part —
batch0's `noise_floor.json` was never recomputed under fps-awz's `placebo_column` method,
so `tgp_delta_7d` can no longer be graded against any noise floor — is re-filed separately
as its own design question and is NOT in scope here.
notes:
2026-09-03: fps-rlh's backfill has now landed (cd3de8f) WITHOUT this fix, because
the owner disabled the nightly dossier Routine until batch2 starts, removing the
recurrence vector. That makes this issue's urgency conditional rather than gone:

**This must land before the dossier Routine is re-enabled for batch2.** Otherwise
the first scan that hits an mtime tie wipes batch1's grading for a THIRD time
(#351 was the first, this backfill the repair, and the tie will fire again on a
fresh checkout). Nothing else now protects those five verdicts.

Scope note: fps-tef is closed as moot (it was batch0-scoped and batch0 is wound
down), but the generic half it shared with this issue is NOT closed -- it lives
here. That is build_facts' unconditional grading reset PLUS find_pending_runs'
mtime-tie rule. The _noise_band legacy-format half died with batch0.

2026-09-03: PR #360 open (interactive session, both halves in one PR).

DIAGNOSIS CORRECTION — the mtime TIE is not the (only) trigger, and a tie-only fix
would have left the live corpus fully exposed while passing its own unit tests.
git writes a directory's files in NAME order, stamping each with the wall-clock time
of that write, so README.md lands a few ms BEFORE results.json and the run hits the
plain 'results.json is newer => stale' branch, not the tie branch. Measured on a
fresh worktree of HEAD, all six dossiered runs under experiments/candidates came out
readme-minus-results = -2.1 to -4.5 ms, i.e. ALL SIX pending. At one-second display
resolution that is indistinguishable from a tie, which is why every incident report
called it one.

Fix therefore drops the mtime comparison entirely: find_pending_runs now asks whether
facts.json's new provenance.results_fingerprint (sha256 of results.json) matches the
results.json on disk, plus a non-empty README.md as the 'written up' marker. The six
committed dossiers are stamped in the same PR. find_pending_runs('experiments/candidates')
returns all six before, [] after.

Second AC half: grading is PRESERVED (never derived; refusing would make graded
dossiers unrefreshable), while noise_band / per_fold[].regime / per_regime /
decision_flips REFUSE (FactsFieldLossError, --allow-field-loss overrides) — carrying
those forward beside fresh provenance would produce a mixed-vintage facts.json that
misreports its own vintage.
2026-09-03: MERGED as 3cbf496 (PR #360, squash). Reviewed at effort high by a peer session: 3 findings + 2 from Sourcery, all fixed and verified; one finding's concrete example disputed and withdrawn (see below). CLOSED.

Shipped: find_pending_runs decides currency on provenance.results_fingerprint (sha256 of results.json) + a non-empty README, mtime comparison removed entirely; process_run carries grading forward (stamping grading.carried_from_fingerprint when the numbers moved) and refuses a regeneration that would drop noise_band / per_fold[].regime / per_regime / decision_flips; --allow-field-loss is single-run only, rejected with --scan. Six committed dossiers backfilled with their fingerprint (sha256s independently recomputed by the reviewer, all match).

Non-obvious boundary worth keeping: the field-loss check is SKIPPED when the regenerated run is not graded, and that gate is structural, not a convenience. runner._finish writes a status-only results.json with no meta.batch_dir, so _noise_band returns unavailable on its first line before it ever looks for noise_floor.json, and build_facts early-returns before breakdowns/decision_flips exist — all three predicates go False for any non-graded run in any environment. Comparing them would refuse every graded->abort re-run even with the floor present, and under --scan that deadlocks: refuse, log, leave pending, refuse again tomorrow, forever, abort never dossiered.

Watch-item (designed, not a defect): a batch re-freeze changes baseline_fingerprint, making the existing noise_floor.json inadmissible, so regenerations of a re-run graded candidate refuse until the floor is recomputed. Documented in docs/routines/dossier.md so the first occurrence doesn't read as a regression.

The nightly dossier Routine is now safe to re-enable for batch2 as far as this issue is concerned.

description:
## What

Remove `placebo.MAX_RULER_ARITY` and the `run_arity_above_cap` refusal. Replace them with
`placebo.effective_n_draws`, feeding `family_wise_z_threshold` the EFFECTIVE draw count so a
wider candidate gets a wider, harder bar instead of no verdict.

## Why the cap had to go

**Owner's standing position, stated on fps-3jj.14 and again on 2026-08-26:** constraining
candidate shape to suit the ruler distorts the thing being measured. The cap did exactly that —
`docs/routines/generator.md` had been rewritten to tell the generator to propose fewer columns,
and a wide candidate got a night of compute with no verdict plus an unbounded nightly re-pick.

**And the cap rested on a crude model.** The exposure arithmetic charged two draws the FULL
texture ICC if they shared even ONE source column. Two draws sharing 1 of 10 columns share about
a tenth of their texture, not all of it. Charging the shared FRACTION instead:

| candidate columns | n_eff (binary charge) | n_eff (fraction charge) | bar (1 candidate) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | 20.00 | 20.00 | -0.152 |
| 3 | 13.98 | 17.49 | -0.154 |
| 4 | 9.04 | 15.35 | -0.156 |
| 10 | 2.37 | 9.04 | -0.171 |
| 35 | 2.37 | 3.22 | -0.287 |

The binary charge is what made a cap look necessary. Under the faithful charge the bar degrades
GENTLY at every width — which is precisely what fps-3jj.21 said the old design failed to do
("the bar does not degrade gracefully as arity rises — it EXPLODES"). **The cap was solving a
problem the modelling invented.**

## Outcome

Shipped. Verified with the shipped code on batch1's real frozen frame: a **35-column per-LGA
candidate** — which fps-3jj.21 opened by noting could not have a band computed AT ALL — builds a
20-draw bank and grades at **-0.287 c/L**. `generator.md` no longer says anything about how many
columns to propose.

`family_wise_z_threshold` takes a fractional `df` (scipy accepts it; rounding down would be a
silent extra penalty). Floors written before this carry no `effective_n_draws`; those banks
predate column reuse entirely, so their nominal count IS their effective count and the fallback
is exact rather than optimistic.

## What is still a bound

`placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND = 0.391` is now the load-bearing input to EVERY bar rather than to one
constant, and it is a 95% upper limit from an underpowered ANOVA (could not resolve below 0.359,
point estimate ~0). Deliberately the pessimistic end — the failure this prevents is a band too
narrow and a bar too easy. Grouping by texture FAMILY is also coarser than by COLUMN, so it
likely overstates the correction. **bd fps-3jj.23 measures it directly and every bar tightens
when it lands.**

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `MAX_RULER_ARITY` and `run_arity_above_cap` removed
- [x] `effective_n_draws` prices reuse from the bank actually built, charging the shared fraction
- [x] `family_wise_z_threshold` takes the effective count; floors predating it fall back exactly
- [x] `generator.md` says nothing about candidate arity
- [x] A 35-column bank builds and grades on real data
title: Price placebo reuse into the threshold instead of capping candidate arity

description:
## What

Replace `placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` — currently a **bound**, 0.391 — with a measured number, by
computing a noise floor where every draw uses the **same source column** with a different block
seed and comparing its variance against the existing multi-column floor's.

## Why this is now the highest-value open item on the pipeline

**`TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` sets EVERY bar.** Since `fps-3jj.25` removed the arity cap, this constant
is no longer one input to one threshold — it is the input to `placebo.effective_n_draws`, which
feeds `family_wise_z_threshold` for every candidate at every width. On batch1's band:

| candidate columns | effective draws | single-candidate bar |
|---|---|---|
| 1-2 | 20.00 | -0.152 |
| 3 | 17.49 | -0.154 |
| 10 | 9.04 | -0.171 |
| 35 | 3.23 | -0.287 |

Every one of those numbers moves when this lands. At ICC = 0 they all collapse to **-0.152** and
candidate width stops costing anything at all.

## The quantity

A placebo column reaches its delta by two channels:

- **alignment** — did this particular shuffle line up with the target somewhere the fit could
  exploit? Varies with the block seed.
- **texture** — how much does adding a column OF THIS SHAPE perturb the fit at all, regardless
  of alignment? Distribution, cardinality, NaN rate, autocorrelation. Fixed by the source column.

Two draws from the SAME source column share texture **exactly**. So the intraclass correlation
of delta by source column IS the correlation two draws inherit from sharing a column — the whole
cost `effective_n_draws` prices.

A same-column bank varies only the seed, so its delta variance is **alignment alone**. The
existing 20-draw multi-column floor's variance is **alignment + texture**. The difference is the
texture component, hence the ICC.

## THE PART THAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED — read before assuming the current setting is safe

The shipped 0.391 is a 95% upper bound on the ICC of delta grouped by **texture FAMILY**
(`F(3,16) = 0.411`, `p = 0.75`, point estimate ~0, could not resolve below **0.359**). It is
used as a stand-in for the ICC by **COLUMN**, and those are different quantities:

- Family is **coarser**. Two different `days_since_trough_entry_<lga>` columns are same-family,
  different-column; their textures are similar but not identical. Two placebos from the SAME
  column are more alike than that.
- So the column ICC is plausibly **larger** than the family ICC — which means **0.391 is not
  established as an upper bound on the quantity actually being used.**

**Consequence: the direction of the current error is UNKNOWN.** Earlier write-ups (including
this bead's first version and the fps-3jj.25 PR description) claimed the setting is
"deliberately pessimistic, so every bar is harder than it needs to be". That claim holds against
the family quantity and does **not** transfer to the column quantity. If the true column ICC
exceeds 0.391, current bars on wide candidates are too EASY — the exact bias direction this
machinery exists to remove. Do not treat the present setting as conservative until measured.

Weak evidence against a very large column ICC: a large one should produce *some* family
clustering, and the ANOVA found none. Weak is why this bead exists.

## How

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.noise_floor batch1 \
    --arity 1 --n-draws 10 --same-source-column <col> \
    --out-name noise_floor_samecol.json
```

`--same-source-column` does not exist yet; it is a small addition to the candidate construction
(pin the column, vary `block_seed(i)`), **not** a new null. Compare against the committed
`noise_floor_k1.json` (20 draws, mixed columns, same `baseline_fingerprint 54:1a6ec2d84a69`,
same `tank_params 50/3.571/1d/10%`, same seed) with an F-test on the variance ratio, its CI,
**and the smallest ratio the design can resolve** — the way
`experiments/2026-08-23_placebo_arity/compare_arity.py` already does.

**Pick the source column deliberately and say why.** A level-like column and a counter have
different texture; one run answers the question for one texture. `station_price_cents` is the
natural first pick (level-like, the hardest case for any reordering, and the shape a real
candidate is most likely to have). Repeat on a trough counter if the first result is close to
0.391 — the two families are 30 of the 49 usable columns between them.

## Cost

~10 draws, ~2.3h on the Mac at batch1's size (measured: `wall_seconds 8368` for the 10-draw k3
run). The baseline arm is cached across draws (`fps-e2l`), so this is "1 baseline fit + 10
placebo fits".

## Relationship to fps-3jj.22 — measure FIRST, and .22 may evaporate

`fps-3jj.22` (outside-lock placebo sources) exists to reduce cross-draw column overlap and
thereby tighten the bar on wide candidates. **Its entire value is proportional to this ICC:**

- **ICC ~ 0** -> `effective_n_draws` returns the nominal count at every width, every bar is
  already -0.152, overlap costs nothing, and **fps-3jj.22 buys literally nothing.** Close it.
- **ICC ~ 0.391** -> a 35-column candidate's bar is 0.135 c/L harder than an arity-1 one's
  purely from overlap, and fps-3jj.22 could recover most of that. Worth doing.
- **ICC > 0.391** -> current bars are too easy on wide candidates; fps-3jj.22 becomes the fix
  rather than an optimisation, and the ICC value should be raised in the same change.

Recorded as a bd dependency: `fps-3jj.23` blocks `fps-3jj.22`. Do not build .22 first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--same-source-column` implemented, with the pinned column stamped into the payload
- [ ] Same-column floor computed and committed for batch1, on a deliberately chosen column
- [ ] Variance ratio vs `noise_floor_k1.json` reported with CI **and** the design's own
      resolution limit (a quiet result reads "could not see it", never "it is not there")
- [ ] **ICC stated as a number**, and `placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` replaced with it (or the bound
      explicitly held, with the reason)
- [ ] The family-vs-column gap above resolved or explicitly re-stated as still open
- [ ] `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` and the `TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` docstring updated with the measured value
      in place of the bound, including the new bar table at each width
- [ ] `fps-3jj.22` re-triaged on the result — closed if the ICC is near zero
- [ ] `experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/README.md` § "What is still a bound"
      updated to point at the result

(repeatable), `NULL_METHOD_PLACEBO_PINNED_COLUMN` so `_noise_band` structurally refuses to
grade against a pinned bank, `all_nan_baseline_columns` stamping, the power analysis and the
ICC estimator (`experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/`), 16 tests.

**NOT landed: the ICC itself. No fits have been run.** The bead's headline deliverable does
not exist yet, which is why this stays open despite PR #337 carrying a `Resolves:` line —
that line was written before the work split into instrument-then-measurement.

### Why the design changed (this supersedes the "How" section above)

The construction this bead specifies **cannot discharge this bead**. One pinned column x 10
seeds against the committed 20-draw floor is an unpaired variance ratio on F(9,19):
resolvable only above **0.661**, and its BEST possible outcome is a 95% upper bound of
**0.587** — looser than the 0.391 it would replace. ~2h of fits for a worse number than the
one being replaced, whatever the deltas came out as. (All figures at the one-sided 5% tail,
matching how 0.391 itself was derived.)

The design that works is a one-way ANOVA of delta grouped **by column** over several pinned
columns — the by-column quantity directly, closing the family-vs-column gap rather than
restating it, and depending on no second artifact. **8 columns x 4 seeds = 32 draws (~6.1h)
is the smallest shape of any kind leaving a bound tighter than 0.391** (upper 0.376,
resolvable 0.262).

### Also established: the ICC is inert at the arity actually in use

Swept across its whole possible range on batch1's live ruler, it moves the single-candidate
bar by 0.000 c/L at arity 1-2, 0.005 at arity 3 and 0.011 at arity 4 — every width batch1 has
ever run — against 0.059 at arity 10, 0.280 at 20 and 0.383 at 35. "It sets EVERY bar" is
true but misleading; it is load-bearing only for the wide groups generator.md invites.

### Remaining acceptance criteria

- [ ] Run the 32-draw bank (command in `experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/README.md`, ~6.1h)
- [ ] ICC stated as a number; `TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` replaced, raised, or explicitly held with the reason
- [ ] `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` + the `TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` docstring carry the measured value
- [ ] `fps-3jj.22` re-triaged on the result (close it if the ICC is near zero)
- [ ] This experiment's README Results/Conclusion filled in

Related: `fps-8o0` — the same singleton-group defect fixed here still exists in
`texture_channel.py`, which is what PRODUCED 0.391. If a texture family is a singleton, the
shipped constant was computed on 19 draws and 4 families, not 20 and 5.
## Result 2026-08-27 — the ICC is a NUMBER. PR #338 open.

**32-draw pinned bank ran (5.7h). One-way ANOVA of delta by SOURCE COLUMN:**
F(7,24) = 0.735, p = 0.65, point estimate -0.071 (i.e. 0), one-sided 95% upper bound
**0.274**, design resolvable to 0.262. `placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND` 0.391 -> 0.274.

The BOUND ships, not the point estimate — the design floors at 0.262, so a quiet F reads
"could not see it", never "it is not there". The family-vs-column gap is CLOSED (this is the
by-column quantity directly), and it closed in the direction nobody could call in advance:
the column ICC is SMALLER than the family bound, not larger.

None of the three pre-written outcomes was met exactly. "ICC ~ 0 -> close fps-3jj.22" wanted
the bound comfortably under ~0.2 and it is 0.274; "ICC ~ 0.391 survives" did not; "ICC > 0.391"
did not. The result landed between the first two, hence "replace with the measured bound".

### Three by-products

1. **fps-8o0 CONFIRMED LIVE and quantified.** batch1's `network` texture family IS a singleton.
   texture_channel.py drops it from the sums of squares while keeping n=20, k=5 in df2 and
   k_bar — the published F(3,16)=0.411 -> 0.391 / resolvable 0.359 reproduces EXACTLY from that
   mix, which is what identifies it. Recomputed consistently over all 5 families the by-family
   bound is 0.226. Fixing only the filter would have RAISED it to 0.402; both halves must land
   together. The constant no longer depends on that script.
2. **The 5-dead-column count is verified.** all_nan_baseline_columns came back with exactly 5,
   so 49 usable columns stands and no published bar table needed recomputing. First artifact to
   check it rather than trust a count off a gitignored frame.
3. **The bead's own variance-ratio construction leans against its own assumption.** The pinned
   bank's alignment-only variance came out 2.2x the multi-column floor's alignment+texture
   variance, which an equal-Var(alignment) model forbids. Not resolvable (ratio CI [0.90, 5.18],
   p = 0.08) so NOT evidence the pinned set is unrepresentative — but if real, the ANOVA's ICC
   is biased LOW and 0.274 is optimistic. Recorded as the open edge; it is also a second,
   independent reason the originally-specified design could not have discharged this bead.

### Direction of the change

Lowering the constant LOOSENS wide bars (arity 35: -0.287 -> -0.226 c/L; arity 10: -0.171 ->
-0.165). Every candidate batch1 has actually run (arity 1 and 3) moved 0.001 c/L, so no written
dossier's verdict is affected.

### Landed in PR #338

placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND + its comment block, docs/CONVENTIONS.md § the ICC and both bar
tables, docs/routines/generator.md's bar quotes, docs/routines/retrospective.md's icc reference,
experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/README.md Results+Conclusion, experiments/INDEX.md (open ->
closed), experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/README.md § what was still a bound,
and tests/test_texture_icc_estimator.py (published tables now pinned at an explicit
PUBLISHED_ICC asserted equal to the shipped constant, so the next move fails loudly).

Close this bead once #338 merges.
title: Measure the texture ICC directly: a same-column noise floor

description:
## What

A placebo draw needs `arity` DISTINCT source columns. The lock has 54;
`PLACEBO_BLOCK_SEED_POOL` has 30. Max draws at arity k is
`min(floor(54/k), floor(30/k))`. Because the t-critical uses `df = n_draws - 1`, the bar
does not degrade gracefully as arity rises — it EXPLODES, and almost none of the
explosion is the arity effect. It is the collapsing draw count.

Measured on batch1's k=3 band (mean +0.0251, std 0.0999), family-wise at 5 candidates:

  arity   max draws   z(5 cand)      bar        note
      1          30       2.503   -0.2249
      2          15       2.711   -0.2457
      3          10       2.959   -0.2705      <- batch1 today
      4           7       3.360   -0.3105      <- generator.md ALREADY invites this
      5           6       3.635   -0.3380
      6           5       4.105   -0.3849
     10           3       8.042   -0.7783      <- 3x the largest win in project history
     13           2      38.972   -3.8682      <- absurd
     18+          1          --        --      NO BAND POSSIBLE (needs n >= 2)
     35           0          --        --      select_draws raises: 70 columns needed, 54 exist

## The part that should decide the design

**This project's own motivating precedent for group candidates is ungradeable by this
ruler.** `docs/routines/generator.md` justifies multi-column candidates on the 35 LGA
features going in together. A 35-column candidate cannot have a noise floor computed AT
ALL: two draws would need 70 distinct source columns and only 54 exist. The ruler cannot
measure the kind of candidate the generator is explicitly told to propose.

**And the gap is already live, not hypothetical.** generator.md invites 2-4 columns. A
4-column candidate gets a 7-draw floor, so its bar is 0.0400 c/L harder than a 3-column
candidate's — purely from band thinness, nothing to do with its arity being higher. Two
candidates in the same batch, both legitimate under the generator's own rules, are graded
by rulers of materially different strictness, and the dossier reports neither fact.

That interacts badly with generator.md's own advice that "group candidates routinely beat
their own noise band as a group even when no single column in it would" — the invitation
and the instrument disagree.

## Why "bump the seed pool to 60" does not fix it

It moves the binding constraint from seeds to columns without removing it — see the table
(the seed pool binds up to k=27; columns bind above it). And at `floor(54/3) = 18` draws
every lock column is a primary, so `candidate_pool`'s fallback tail is EMPTY and the
`self_correlation` screen has no substitution headroom. Substitution is not hypothetical:
it fired twice on batch1's k=1 floor (two all-NaN `days_since_trough_entry_*` columns).
With an empty tail the run either hard-fails after hours of compute, or keeps a column
that FAILED the screen — a placebo still correlated with its original, which NARROWS the
band and makes the bar EASIER. That is the exact bias direction fps-3jj.14 removed,
arriving by a different door.

## Options, none free

1. **Reuse source columns across draws.** Cheapest; costs the one independence property
   the band's std assumes. Interacts with fps-3jj.20.
2. **Source placebos from outside the lock** — other feature columns, or synthetic series
   with matched texture. Preserves distinctness; needs a defensible "matched texture"
   rule, and a synthetic placebo is a weaker analogue of a real candidate.
3. **Decouple the band's arity from the draw count** — e.g. build k-column draws by
   sampling WITH replacement across draws but WITHOUT replacement within a draw. Keeps
   within-draw realism, degrades between-draw independence gradually rather than off a
   cliff. Probably the most promising; needs the independence cost quantified.
4. **Cap candidate arity at what the ruler can grade (~4) and say so in generator.md.**
   Free and honest, but it is the thing the owner explicitly rejected on fps-3jj.14 —
   constraining candidate shape to suit the ruler distorts what batch1 is measuring. If
   it is chosen anyway it should be chosen deliberately, not by the pool running out.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision recorded on which option, with the independence cost stated
- [ ] `select_draws` raises with the COLUMN-pool product in the message, not just the seed
      pool. Live line: `dossier_tables.py:446` computes the remediation command's
      `--n-draws` as `len(PLACEBO_BLOCK_SEED_POOL) // run_arity` — seed pool only, so it
      can advise a draw count the column pool cannot supply.
- [ ] `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` states the ceiling as `min(n_columns, n_seeds) / arity`, not `30/arity`
- [ ] `docs/routines/generator.md`'s "2-4 columns" reconciled with what the ruler can actually grade
- [ ] The dossier RENDERS the strictness difference, not just the raw numbers. Verified
      2026-08-24: `_noise_band` ALREADY emits `n_draws`, `n_placebo_columns`,
      `candidate_n_columns` and `floor_arity_exceeds_run` into facts, so the data is
      present — what's missing is that nothing turns "7 draws vs 10" into "this
      candidate's bar is 0.04 c/L harder than its batch-mate's". Comparison, not capture.

## Provenance

Raised by fps-3jj.14's arity calibration, 2026-08-24, and sharpened by the owner's
observation that a per-LGA candidate would have one feature per LGA. Full working:
`experiments/2026-08-23_placebo_arity/README.md`.

description:
## What

The decision bead. Once batch1's retrospective exists, every candidate lands in
exactly one of three buckets and each has a different follow-up. This bead is where
that call is made and executed; it is expected to close with MOST of the batch in
bucket 2 and possibly nothing in bucket 1.

**1. Cleared the bar (`effect_delta_cpl_held <= -0.15 c/L` alone, `<= -0.22 c/L`
family-wise).** Does NOT go straight into `features.py`. Per
`feedback_features_via_experiment_first`, a candidate module is an experiment; the
production column is a separate follow-up PR that must:
- add the column(s) to the right group list in `fuel_signal/features.py`,
  APPENDING — never inserting, never sorting (`LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS` order is part
  of the contract; a sorted permutation of the same 54 columns fit a different model
  and moved 0.038 c/L, fps-zci),
- check `backtest.py`'s `ModelStrategy.decide()` parity — the offline
  (`features.py`) and live-replay feature paths drift silently, and nothing exercises
  `decide()` with a new column until a baseline containing it is frozen (fps-3i7),
- retrain + re-lock, which INVALIDATES batch1's noise floor and fingerprint
  (`54:1a6ec2d84a69`) for any later comparison,
- if the winner is a multi-column group, file the ablation ("which column carried
  it?") as its own follow-up rather than doing it inline —
  `docs/routines/generator.md` says a group that wins is ablated afterwards.

**2. Inside the noise band -> `inconclusive`, NOT `rejected`.** This is the expected
majority outcome and it is a real result, not a null one: `fps-3jj.17` made the split
mechanical off `candidate_z_vs_band` precisely so the next generator reads mapped
ground instead of dead ground. Confirm the dossier routine applied the two-tier rule
correctly rather than assuming it did.

**3. Wrong-signed by more than the band -> `rejected`.** Dead ground. The ledger's
`falsified` and `not_tested` fields on these are what the NEXT generator reads, so
they carry more weight than the outcome code — write `not_tested` with real judgement,
not boilerplate.

## Also check, regardless of outcome

- Every candidate has a `ledger.yaml` entry and an `INDEX.md` line (dossier routine
  writes both in one pass — verify, don't assume; batch1 is the first MULTI-candidate
  batch, so the per-candidate `out_dir` fix from fps-icv gets its first real exercise
  here).
- `docs/STATUS.md` is canonical for feature count / calibration / tau / phase
  (`feedback_status_canonical_current_state`) — update it there and nowhere else if
  anything graduated.
- `experiments/results.csv`: hand over before writing (`feedback_results_csv_main_only`,
  `feedback_handover_before_results_csv_write`), and any CPL written must carry its
  `tank_params` cadence stamp (fps-15c).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every batch1 candidate assigned to bucket 1, 2 or 3 with the number that decided it
- [ ] Ledger + INDEX.md entries verified present and accurate for all 5
- [ ] Follow-up beads filed for anything in bucket 1 (production PR, ablation)
- [ ] Closes as "nothing graduated" without embarrassment if that is the answer —
      batch1's expected yield is mapped ground, not a graduation

This description says bucket 1 is "effect_delta_cpl_held <= -0.15 c/L alone,

description:
## What

Once all 5 batch1 candidates have run AND been dossiered, produce the batch
retrospective — the payoff artifact for aim (b) (gaining experience with an
AI-sourced pipeline), not for aim (a).

Two steps, same code/Claude split as the dossier routine:

1. `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.retrospective batch1`
   — deterministic, no judgement. Reads every candidate's own `facts.json` plus the
   batch's `noise_floor.json` and writes `retrospective_facts.json` into
   `experiments/batches/batch1/`. Recomputes nothing.
2. The Claude step per `docs/routines/retrospective.md`: read that file, write
   `RETROSPECTIVE.md` prose beside it.

## Why it needs a bead and the dossier runs don't

The dossier routine fires nightly and writes one README.md + ledger entry per
candidate unsupervised. The retrospective is once-per-batch, has no scheduled task,
and is the ONLY place four batch-level questions get answered:

- **Leaderboard** across the 5, ranked, with `clears_family_wise_threshold` — the
  multiple-comparisons-corrected gate (`family_wise_z_threshold`), NOT the empirical
  percentile, which is descriptive colour only. Picking the best of N against the
  same band is not the same test as judging one candidate alone.
- **Confidence calibration.** Both `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT` and `CONFIDENCE_ZONE` were
  deliberately spread (0.30-0.60 / 0.15-0.55) rather than hedged to 0.5, so this
  batch can actually contribute a calibration signal. `fps-2sf` states ZONE ABOVE
  EFFECT on purpose. **Do not claim a confident calibration read from batch1 alone**
  — the retrospective appends to a running cross-batch record and 5 points calibrate
  nothing (`docs/routines/generator.md` § Calibration accumulates across batches).
- **Mechanism-family concentration.** 5 distinct labels were declared. Two of them
  (`directional-network-breadth`, `lead-lag-propagation`) are both cross-sectional
  consensus statistics adjacent to the graduated families A and C — disclosed in
  both modules' PRIOR_ART rather than relabelled. Whether that reads as diversity or
  as one idea wearing two hats is a FINDING ABOUT THE GENERATOR and this is where it
  gets recorded.
- **Outcome tally**, including the leak rate: `aborted_candidate:leak_by_declaration`
  is tallied separately from plain `aborted_candidate` (fps-3jj.13, PR #330). Note
  the terminal success status is `graded`, not `rejected` (fps-0z5, PR #329).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retrospective_facts.json` written for batch1
- [ ] `RETROSPECTIVE.md` written per docs/routines/retrospective.md
- [ ] Calibration read stated as cross-batch-pending, not as a batch1 conclusion
- [ ] Family-concentration observation recorded (see the A/C adjacency above)
- [ ] Any candidate that clears the family-wise bar named explicitly, so the
      follow-up bead has something to act on

## Sequencing note

Blocked by all 5 candidate beads, and by `fps-3jj.14` (arity calibration). The arity
dep is deliberate, not bureaucratic: batch1's noise floor is a **1-column** placebo
null while three of the five candidates are 3-column groups, so
`clears_family_wise_threshold` compares a 3-column arm against a 1-column ruler. The
size of that gap has to be known before the leaderboard's gate column means anything.

## Not tracked here

Per-candidate dossier runs — the dossier routine writes those unsupervised

## Convention this establishes

**Every batch gets a parent bead like this one**, created at filing time by the
