## What

When a batch1 candidate lands above (worse than) the family-wise detection bar, what
`outcome` does its ledger entry get: `rejected` or `inconclusive`?

This is gap #4 from the fps-3jj.11 readiness review and the last undecided one.

## Why it is urgent rather than merely open

**The dossier routine is now live** (`fuel-price-signal-dossier`, `0 5 * * *`, registered
2026-08-22). It writes the ledger entry itself, unsupervised, the morning after each run.
If this is not decided first, a Claude session picks the label on its own at 5am, five
times, and whatever it picks becomes the record.

The two labels are not cosmetic. `experiments/ledger.yaml`'s own header draws the line:

> `inconclusive` is NOT `rejected`. A rejected claim is dead ground the generator should
> not re-propose; an inconclusive one was measured below the instrument's resolution, and
> the ground may still be open.

So the label decides what the NEXT generator session treats as dead ground. Five wrong
`rejected` rows would close five mechanisms that were never actually tested to
resolution.

## Why the default answer is probably `inconclusive`, and why that is uncomfortable

The batch-level bar is `effect_delta_cpl_held <= -0.22 c/L` (batch1's own noise floor,
5 candidates), `-0.15` judged singly. But `experiments/results.csv` history shows
single-column features landing between 0.03 and 0.26 c/L. So the bar sits at or above the
top of the range this project's features have ever occupied, and the MODAL outcome is
plausibly that 0 of 5 clear it.

If everything below the bar is `inconclusive`, batch1 may produce five `inconclusive`
rows and resolve nothing — which is an honest record but a thin return on five nights.
If everything below is `rejected`, the batch silently closes five mechanisms on an
instrument that provably cannot resolve effects of the size they would have.

Precedent exists and points to `inconclusive`: batch0's `tgp_delta_7d` is recorded that
way, explicitly because +0.0059 c/L was below the arbiter's resolution
(ledger.yaml header, "First use: batch0/tgp_delta_7d, 2026-08-19").

## Options

1. **Bar-relative, blanket.** Below the bar -> `inconclusive`, always. Simple, honest,
   possibly vacuous.
2. **Two-tier.** `inconclusive` when the effect is inside the noise band;
   `rejected` when it is clearly the WRONG SIGN by more than the band (i.e. measurably
   harmful, not merely unresolved). Distinguishes "we could not tell" from "this hurts".
3. **Defer to the dossier session's judgement** with the ledger header as its guide.
   Status quo, and the thing this bead exists to prevent.

Option 2 is the one worth arguing about: it recovers real information from a batch that
otherwise reports nothing, and it is mechanically checkable from
`candidate_z_vs_band`.

## Note on the arity caveat

Whatever is decided interacts with `fps-3jj.14`: a multi-column candidate is currently
graded against a 1-column null, so its z is biased favourable by an unknown amount. A
`rejected` label assigned on a biased-favourable z is worse than one assigned on an
unbiased one -- the candidate looked BETTER than it should have and still failed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rule decided and written into `docs/routines/dossier.md` § the ledger step, so the
      5am session applies it rather than inventing one
- [ ] Rule expressed against a quantity the dossier already has (`candidate_z_vs_band` /
      `clears_family_wise_threshold`), not a judgement call
- [ ] `experiments/ledger.yaml`'s header updated if the vocabulary shifts
title: Below-the-bar candidates: rejected or inconclusive? Decide before the first dossier writes one

description:
## What

`future_min_cents` and `label` sit in the features frame (70 cols) and nothing stops a
candidate module declaring them in `INPUTS`. All three layers of the validation harness
miss it:

- **Restricted-frame check** is a *provenance* check by its own docstring — it stops
  UNDECLARED reads, not forbidden ones. Declaring the target is a legal declaration.
- **Differential PIT test** works by deleting future rows and re-running `add_columns`.
  It catches a function reaching FORWARD ACROSS ROWS. `future_min_cents` is already
  stamped ON the row, so truncating at date T leaves row T's cell untouched, the
  recomputed value matches, and `future_min_cents - station_price_cents` passes clean.
- **All-NaN check** is unrelated.

Found while reading fps-3jj.11 (generator session prep). `validate.py`'s own docstring
calls itself "the whole safety layer for LLM-authored candidate modules, since nobody
reviews the code" — and the oracle is sitting in the frame.

## Shape of the fix (decided with owner)

BLOCKLIST, not allowlist. The hazard is the target — a closed, semantically-anchored set
— not an open category, so default-deny's friction isn't earned. But a name blocklist is
only complete while adding a new frame column forces someone to classify it, and that
forcing function did not exist: `resolve_baseline_columns` asserts on the non-model ->
locked transition (fps-sa1), never on unregistered columns.

- `features.TARGET_COLUMNS` + `features.KEY_COLUMNS` — the label frame's own columns
  (`labels.assemble_training_rows`), split by knowable-at-decision-time.
- `features.unclassified_columns(df)` — every column must be locked / non-model / target
  / key.
- `validate.py` step 0 rejects `INPUTS` naming a target column, before the restricted
  frame is built.
- `freeze_batch` refuses to freeze a batch around an unclassified column. That is the
  forcing function, and it lands on the person adding a column rather than on every
  candidate author.

Test asserts over declaration symbols, never `data/features.parquet` (gitignored; CI
runs bare `pytest -q`, so a real-frame test would silently skip — the second half of
feedback_guard_must_not_reference_what_it_guards).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A candidate declaring `future_min_cents` or `label` aborts at validation
- [ ] A test demonstrates the PIT test does NOT catch a stamped target column
- [ ] Freezing a batch with an undeclared column raises
- [ ] Live `data/features.parquet` and `batches/batch1/features.parquet` classify clean
title: Candidate pipeline: label columns are readable and the PIT test cannot catch them

description:
## The invariant

**Anything that records a realised CPL must record the cadence it was measured at, and
the writer must REFUSE rather than silently omit it.**

`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` states the rule as prose today ("Quote realised CPL and headroom
with the cadence attached — '1.66 c/L of headroom' is not a fact about the model;
'1.54 c/L at 7-day cadence' is"). Prose is not enough: it binds whoever read it, and the
next feature-development mechanism will be written by someone who did not.

## Why enumerating sites is the WRONG scope

An earlier draft of this bead listed four artifacts to patch. That framing is wrong, and
this is the substantive correction: the pipeline dossier is only the most visible offender
*given the current type of work*. Other feature-development mechanisms already exist —
hand-written experiment scripts, `score_phase2`, `backtest_phase2`, ad-hoc analysis
notebooks — and more will be added. A patch-list fixes today's four and guarantees the
next mechanism is not on it.

So the deliverable is the ENFORCEMENT, with today's sites as instances that must pass it,
not as the scope.

## The precedent to generalise

`log_experiment` (`fuel_signal/evaluate.py:299`) already does this correctly:

    if realised_spend_cpl is not None and tank is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "realised_spend_cpl was passed without tank — a row with a realised CPL "
            "and no tank_params stamp is exactly the ambiguity fps-xx1 exists to "
            "prevent. Pass the TankParams the backtest ran with."
        )

Two properties worth copying exactly:

1. **It refuses.** Not a warning, not a default, not a `None` that reads as 7d.
2. **It derives the stamp from the object that ran**, via `format_tank_params(tank)`,
   never from a caller-supplied string — so the stamp cannot disagree with what produced
   the number. Same rule as `baseline_fingerprint`.

## Deliverable

- [ ] One shared stamping path every artifact writer uses, so a new writer inherits the
      behaviour instead of reimplementing it. `format_tank_params` already gives the
      rendering; what is missing is a single place that pairs it with a CPL.
- [ ] Writers RAISE on a CPL without a tank, wording modelled on `log_experiment`'s.
- [ ] **A test that enforces the invariant generically**, not one assertion per site: for
      every artifact-writing entry point, a CPL without a tank must raise. Ideally also a
      structural check over written artifacts — a dict/row carrying a CPL-shaped key and
      no cadence key is a failure. That check is what catches mechanism number five.
- [ ] `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` upgraded from a quoting style note to a stated contract, with
      the refusal named, so the prose and the code say the same thing.

## Today's instances (must pass the above, not define it)

Verified against batch0's own artifacts. The harness already carries it —
`experiments/lib/realised.py:316` puts `"tank": dataclasses.asdict(tank)` into
`RealisedResult.meta` — and every artifact downstream rebuilds its own meta by hand and
drops it:

| writes a CPL | carries cadence today |
|---|---|
| `experiments/results.csv` (`log_experiment`) | YES — the precedent above |
| `RealisedResult.meta` | YES |
| runner `results.json` -> `meta` | NO |
| dossier `facts.json` -> `provenance`, and the generated README | NO |
| `freeze.json` | NO |
| `noise_floor.json` | NO |

- [ ] All six pass, and batch0's existing artifacts are backfilled or explicitly marked
      7d so the re-lock does not leave them ambiguous.

## Why P1

Blocking precondition for the cadence re-lock (`fps-oqz`). `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` requires
that after a re-lock "every subsequent row is stamped so pre- and post-change rows are
mechanically distinguishable". Without this, a 7-day and a 1-day dossier are
byte-comparable and mean different things.

## Relationship to fps-awz

fps-awz adds the REFUSAL GUARD on the consuming side: `_noise_band()` should refuse
(`available: false`) on a tank/cadence mismatch exactly as it already refuses on a
fingerprint mismatch. That guard cannot be written until the stamp exists. Do this first,
or both together.
title: A recorded CPL without its cadence must be a refusal, not a convention

description:
## What

The batch noise floor (`experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py`, fps-3jj.9) and the gate that
reads it (`retrospective.build_leaderboard` / `dossier_tables._noise_band`) do not measure
the quantity a candidate is judged on. Three changes, in descending order of importance:

1. **Replace the seed-swap null with a placebo-column null.**
2. **Gate on distance, not rank.**
3. **Raise the draw count from 5 to ~20.**

Blocks filing batch 1 (bd `fps-3jj.11`, the first 5-candidate batch) — batch0 could not
expose any of this at n=1.

## Why 1 — the null measures a different operation than the test

A candidate's `delta_cpl_held` is: hold seed, data and folds fixed, **add one column**,
measure the CPL move. Both arms therefore share everything except the column, so the fit's
idiosyncrasy is common-mode and cancels in the difference.

The current floor is: hold columns fixed, **re-roll the seed** (42 vs 47, 43 vs 48, ...),
measure the CPL move. Two independent fits, nothing shared, both arms' full wander present.

These are different perturbations and there is no fixed ratio between them, so the band
cannot be rescaled into the right one — it has to be re-measured. Direction is knowable
even if the magnitude isn't: the seed swap is unpaired, so it is too WIDE, and the gate
built on it is too strict. `noise_floor.py`'s own docstring already hedges exactly here
("a floor, not the true band").

Empirical support from batch0: the baseline and candidate arms made identical decisions on
**741 of 752 fills**. The paired comparison is a near-cancellation; the seed swap is not.

**Replacement:** a bank of placebo columns — same seed, same folds, one column added, the
only difference from a real candidate run being that the column carries no information.

**The construction is the hard part, and it can fail in the opposite direction.** A pure
white-noise column gets ignored by the trees, producing a null that is too NARROW and a
gate that is too permissive. The placebo must resemble a real feature in distribution and
autocorrelation while having its alignment to the target destroyed — e.g. a large time-shift
or block permutation of an existing column. Note the parent design's warning (fps-3jj,
"Per-run arms"): a within-date permutation is a no-op for a market-wide series like
`tgp_delta_7d`, where every station shares a value on a date. The permutation axis must
match the axis the column actually varies on.

**This partially reopens a decision recorded in fps-3jj**, which rejected placebo arms. That
objection was to running ONE placebo PER NIGHT — a single draw of the null, compared against
a noisy candidate, and a per-candidate cost. It does not apply to a bank of placebo draws
computed once at batch setup, which is the same shape as the floor being replaced.

## Why 2 — the gate cannot resolve what it claims

`dossier_tables` scores a candidate by EMPIRICAL rank: `(deltas > delta).mean() * 100`. With
5 draws that returns only {0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100}, while
`retrospective.family_wise_percentile_threshold(5)` = 99.0. The gate therefore collapses to
"beat all 5 draws", whose null probability is 1/6 = 16.7% per candidate (nominal 1%) and
~60% family-wise across 5 candidates (nominal 5%). Tightening the threshold changes nothing,
because the statistic has no finer resolution to give.

Fix: gate on the already-computed `candidate_z_vs_band` (distance in band standard
deviations) with a t critical value, honest about sigma being estimated from few draws. Keep
the empirical percentile as descriptive colour in the dossier — it reads well — but do not
let it drive `clears_family_wise_threshold`.

## Why 3 — sigma from 5 points is shaky, and change 2 leans on sigma

Change 2 makes the gate depend on the band's spread, so the spread needs to be worth
trusting. ~20 draws. Cost is ~2 baseline fits per draw at batch setup (one overnight, once
per batch, already inside `batch_freeze`).

## Why this matters economically — the current bar rejects the entire feature history

The current 5-draw band (mean -0.0135, std 0.142 c/L) puts the honest single-candidate bar
around 0.35 c/L (normal) to 0.55 c/L (t, 4 df). Against `experiments/results.csv` — every
realised CPL number this project has logged, one window, 7d cadence:

| date | CPL | features | tau | what changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 05-07 | 191.78 | - | - | always-buy baseline |
| 05-08 | 190.35 | 10 | 0.40 | first model (logreg) |
| 05-31 | 189.02 | 50 | 0.60 | LightGBM + 40 features |
| 06-08 | 187.99 | 54 | 0.55 | + 4 network features |
| 06-12 | 185.94 | 54 | 0.25 | calibration redesign, NO feature change |
| 06-14 | 185.32 | 54 | 0.25 | cycle bug fix, NO feature change |

No single feature has ever delivered 0.5 c/L here. The two feature steps were blocks: 40
columns bought 1.33 c/L (~0.03 each), 4 columns bought 1.03 c/L (~0.26 each, confounded with
a tau move). The largest single win in the table, 2.05 c/L, added no features at all. A bar
that rejects every feature ever shipped is a broken instrument, not a high standard.

Caveat on that comparison: those rows are single-window, measured against the previous best,
not paired A/B on identical folds. Only ONE feature in this repo's history was ever graded on
the paired realised arbiter (`tgp_delta_7d`, +0.0059 c/L, retracted). So there is no
historical distribution on this instrument to calibrate against — which is itself the reason
to get the null right before spending 5 nights generating one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Placebo-column construction implemented, with the choice of construction documented and
      its permutation axis justified against the market-wide-series no-op trap
- [ ] Sanity check that the placebo is genuinely uninformative AND genuinely used by the model
      (a column the trees never split on measures nothing)
- [ ] Band recomputed on the new null; the old seed-swap band retained as a separate
      fit-stability diagnostic, not deleted (it measures something real, just not this)
- [ ] Gate reads distance (t-based `candidate_z_vs_band`), not empirical rank
- [ ] Empirical percentile still reported in the dossier as colour
- [ ] Draw count ~20; verified that `batch_freeze` computes the new floor atomically and it
      stays fingerprint-gated (fps-cf8)
- [ ] The new honest bar stated as a number, and sanity-checked against the results.csv
      history above

Parent design: `fps-3jj`. Blocks: `fps-3jj.11`.
title: Noise floor measures the wrong null: rework the ruler and the gate before batch 1

description:
## What

`experiments/results.csv` carries `realised_spend_cpl` and
`realised_savings_vs_always_buy_pct` — the two numbers `fps-fii` just proved are
cadence-dependent — and **nothing on the row records the tank or cadence that
produced them**.

Add a `tank_params` column alongside `baseline_fingerprint`, derived inside
`log_experiment` rather than passed in (same rule as the fingerprint: a row's
stamp can never disagree with what actually ran).

## Why this is P1 and why it BLOCKS fps-929

This is fps-zci's failure mode with a different contract. That issue's lesson:
two runs' numbers side by side with no mechanical commensurability check, and the
population where the drift hides is exactly the rows with no stamp.

`fps-929` re-picks tau against daily-cadence economics and may recommend moving
the canonical cadence from 7 days to 1. **If it does, and this column does not
exist yet, its own results.csv row is indistinguishable from the 7-day rows it
must be compared against.** Stamp before you decide.

Magnitude, so this is not theoretical — same model, folds, seed and columns:

    cadence   realised CPL   headroom
    7d        189.67         1.54
    2d        187.85         2.69
    1d        187.82         2.97

Cadence moves realised economics by more than most feature decisions do.

## Design

- **A readable literal, not a hash.** `baseline_fingerprint` hashes because 54
  pipe-joined names are unreadable at a glance. TankParams is four numbers — the
  values ARE the glanceable form. Suggested: `50/3.571/7d/10%`
  (size / daily / interval / floor). A reader must be able to see "7d" without
  decoding anything.
- **Derived, not passed.** `log_experiment` should take the `TankParams` object
  (or import the canonical one) and format it, so the column cannot drift from
  the run.
- **Migration asserts the default, not null.** Unlike `baseline_fingerprint`'s 29
  null rows, we can be positive here: `score_phase2.py:491` constructs a bare
  `TankParams()` with no CLI override, and `git log -S"evaluation_interval_days="`
  shows the default was never anything but 7. So backfill the 6 realised-CPL rows
  with the default's literal rather than leaving them empty — an empty stamp
  should mean "predates the field", and here nothing does.
- `log_experiment` hard-fails on header drift, so this means migrating the file
  (see the `baseline_fingerprint` precedent).

## Also

`score_phase2` has no way to run a non-default tank. That is currently a FEATURE
(it is why the historical rows are unambiguous) — if a cadence flag is ever added,
it must not be addable without this column existing first.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `tank_params` column in `experiments/results.csv`, derived in `log_experiment`
- [ ] All 29 existing rows migrated; the 6 with a realised CPL carry the 7-day default literal
- [ ] Test: a row written under a non-default tank is distinguishable from a default one
- [ ] docs/CONVENTIONS.md § "The decision cadence is a lock parameter" cross-links this
- [ ] `fps-929` is not started until this is merged

## Related

- `fps-fii` / experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/ — established that cadence moves the numbers
- `fps-929` — blocked by this
- `fps-zci` — the precedent this copies (baseline_fingerprint)
- `fps-5mn` — cadence safety (which cadences are legal at all)
title: Stamp the tank/cadence contract into results.csv (blocks any cadence re-lock)

description:
## What

`run_backtest` silently clamps a tank that would go negative to 0 and carries on
(`tank_level = max(0.0, tank_level - daily * interval)`, backtest.py:481). The
driver covers distance the purchased litres do not pay for, so CPL's denominator
is understated — and understated selectively on exactly the paths where waiting
looked cheapest.

The root cause is the emergency rule at backtest.py:498. Its own comment says it
exists "to avoid running dry before next evaluation" — forward-looking. Its test
is `tank_level / size < floor_fraction` — backward-looking. It asks "am I low
NOW?" when the thing it guards is "can I reach my next chance to buy?".

## Proposed fix

    elif tank_level < depletion or tank_level / tank.tank_size_litres < tank.floor_fraction:

Keeping the floor term as a separate reserve concept and adding never-dry as its
own condition. `_oracle_transitions` must get the SAME condition in the same
change — it mirrors the engine's fill/emergency logic by design.

Then replace the `max(0.0, ...)` clamp with an assertion: under the new rule a
wait cannot strand the tank, so if it fires, something else is wrong.

## Why NOT the stricter variant

`tank_level - depletion < floor*size` reads more natural but fires an emergency at
level 25 on the 7-day grid where today it does not — moving every production
number and invalidating comparability with results.csv, STATUS.md, #262 and the
batch dossiers. Not worth it to fix a failure mode that does not occur at the
cadence those numbers were measured on.

## Merge gate (non-negotiable)

The fix must be a NO-OP at the default 7-day config. Derived: the default lattice
is {0, 25, 50} and both predicates agree at all three levels; verified likewise at
2d and 1d (29 reachable levels, identical decision, exact rational arithmetic).
So:

- [ ] 7d realised backtest reproduces always 193.41 / model 189.67 / oracle 188.14 EXACTLY
- [ ] if it does not, STOP — `experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/`'s conclusions
      are retracted rather than patched, and this fix needs rethinking

## Also in scope

`validate_never_dry(tank)` — enumerate the reachable lattice and flag configs where
a level lands in the open `(floor*size, D)` interval. On the default tank: cadences
1, 2, 7 safe; 3, 4, 5, 6, 8-14 not. The CLI exposes `--tank-size`, `--daily-use`
and `--eval-interval` with only positivity checks, so `backtest --eval-interval 3`
silently returns a wrong CPL today. This is a user-facing surface, not just an
experiments concern.

## Files likely affected

- fuel_signal/backtest.py (`run_backtest`, `_oracle_transitions`, new validator, CLI)
- tests/test_backtest.py — several tests build aggressive tanks and will need
  expectations updated; `test_oracle_stays_ceiling_and_faithful_in_gap_tank`
  (line 506) already constructs this scenario but only checks the oracle against
  always-buy (never-dry), never against a WAITING strategy

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Emergency rule tests reachability of the next decide point
- [ ] `_oracle_transitions` kept in sync in the same commit
- [ ] Clamp replaced by an assertion
- [ ] `validate_never_dry` + test covering safe/unsafe cadences on the default tank
- [ ] Test that a WAITING strategy cannot strand the tank at 3d
- [ ] Merge gate above satisfied and recorded in the PR body
- [ ] `run_oracle_backtest`'s docstring caveat about being a ceiling only over
      never-dry strategies updated — under the fix, engine strategies are never-dry
      by construction at any cadence

## Related

- `fps-fii` / experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/ — where this was found; its
  3-day row (109 dry events / 389 L) is the evidence, and its 7d/2d/1d rows are
  provably unaffected (0 dry events in 10,150 depletion steps)
title: Fix run_backtest's run-dry clamp: emergency rule must test what its comment claims

description:
## What

`TankParams.evaluation_interval_days = 7` is a default, not a fact about the world.
Re-run the oracle at finer cadences (3-day, 1-day) over the same windows and stations
and see how far the ceiling moves. Then re-run the model arm at the same cadences to
see whether headroom actually grows.

## Why this is the highest-value open question

The whole diminishing-returns judgement rests on one number:

    always-buy      193.41 c/L
    model           189.79        <- captured 3.62 (69%)
    perfect oracle  188.14        <- 1.66 still available (31%)

That 1.66 c/L is the entire justification for "we're near the floor, stop doing
feature work". But it is measured under a **7-day decision grid**, and the tank
dynamics make that grid extremely coarse: a 50 L tank burning 25 L per interval means
the car MUST fill at least every second interval, so the strategy's whole freedom is
*which of two adjacent weeks to buy in*. Measured on the #262 ledgers, **66% of the
model's fills are forced emergency floor-fills** (oracle 51%) — only about one fill in
three is a decision at all, ~250 real decisions across the entire experiment.

An oracle allowed to check daily can exploit within-week dips the weekly grid cannot
see, and prices move several c/L inside a week during a cycle. So the true ceiling may
sit well below 188.14 and the prize be materially larger than 1.66.

## Why it is cheap

`run_oracle_backtest` is **fit-free** — the oracle pass costs no model training, so
sweeping cadence on the oracle alone is nearly free and answers "how much bigger could
the pot be?" on its own. Only the model-arm rerun (to get true headroom rather than
just the ceiling) needs the fitted models, and those are per-fold and already
amortised.

## Honest caveats to carry into the writeup

- A finer cadence gives the MODEL more chances too, so headroom does not automatically
  grow — ceiling and model both move. Report both arms, not just the ceiling.
- A bigger *available* pot says nothing about the *recoverable* fraction; the
  leaky-ceiling caveat (perfect foresight includes unforecastable information) is
  unchanged.
- Cadence has to stay realistic: it is a claim about how often the owner would
  actually check and act, not a free parameter. Ask before assuming daily is usable.
- Window-level only. Do NOT slice the result by cycle zone — see
  fps-1785999730023-4-264564ac; per-zone decomposition is not identified.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/<date>_cadence_ceiling/ (new)
- reuses fuel_signal/backtest.py `run_oracle_backtest` + `TankParams` unchanged

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Oracle CPL at 7d (reproduces 188.14), 3d and 1d cadence over the same 14 windows / 5 stations
- [ ] Model CPL at the same cadences, so reported headroom is like-for-like
- [ ] A statement of how the 31%-remaining figure moves, with the leaky-ceiling caveat restated
- [ ] Window-level only; no per-zone slicing
- [ ] Explicit note on whether the finer cadence is behaviourally realistic for the owner

## Related

- fps-1785999730023-4-264564ac (closed) — where the tank/forced-fill numbers came from
- fps-x0f — this resizes the prize that determines whether its step 3 is worth running
title: Resize the oracle ceiling: is 1.66 c/L an artifact of the 7-day decision cadence?

LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS is the single symbol (re-exported as experiments.lib.constants.BASELINE_COLUMNS); tests/test_feature_contract.py asserts ORDERED equality against lgbm_calibrated.joblib (verified locally, 54:1a6ec2d84a69) with artifact-independent structural checks alongside it because that test skips in CI; an AST detector fails if any live module re-handrolls the composition; NON_MODEL_COLUMNS + non_model_columns() give computed-but-excluded columns a machine-readable reason, and the detector deliberately does not consult the lock so it can catch a column wrongly IN the lock; baseline_fingerprint() is stamped into experiment meta.json, batch freeze.json, run results.json/facts.json and a new results.csv column. description:
## What

We keep running experiments against the wrong baseline. Two instances found so
far; the mechanism is general, so there will be more.

- **fps-sa1**: `batch_freeze.resolve_baseline_columns()` resolves R0 to 64
  columns by *discovering* brand-trough columns in the features frame. The lock
  is 54. Every batch0 candidate was graded against production-plus-10-rejected-
  features, and it took a dedicated investigation (fps-nor) to notice.
- **fps-nor**: June's `realised_tgp.py` (54, correct) and batch0 (64) were
  compared head-to-head for two months as if commensurable.

## Why this keeps happening

1. **There is no symbol for "the locked feature set."** It is the expression
   `FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS + NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS`, retyped by
   hand at ~20 call sites across experiments/. Landing a feature group means
   editing all of them; a script written before #216 silently carries a 50-column
   baseline. `experiments/lib/README.md` says constants drift "is exactly what
   this lib prevents" — but the single most consequential constant in the system
   is the one thing NOT in `experiments/lib/constants.py`.

2. **The features frame is deliberately a SUPERSET of the model contract, and
   nothing records why.** Columns sit in features.csv for three different
   reasons: in the lock; evaluated and rejected (Phase 4b brand troughs,
   2026-06-02); held out pending graduation (`tgp_delta_7d`, #271). The code
   cannot tell these apart, so anything that resolves scope by inspecting the
   frame — `discover_brand_feature_columns()` — cannot distinguish "not in scope"
   from "in scope". Note the asymmetry that produced fps-sa1: `tgp_delta_7d` is
   excluded by *name*, brand troughs are included by *discovery*, and both are
   the same category of column.

3. **Nothing is verified against ground truth.** `data/models/lgbm_calibrated.joblib`
   carries the authoritative `feature_columns` list. No test, no experiment, and
   no pipeline step compares anything to it.

4. **Results do not carry the identity of the baseline they were measured
   against.** `experiments/results.csv`, experiment `meta.json`, and the batch
   dossier `facts.json` record the numbers but not a fingerprint of R0. That is
   why two incommensurable runs could be compared for two months without anything
   flagging it. This item is the DETECTOR, not just the fix — without it the next
   instance is equally invisible.

## Proposed shape (open to revision — the point is the direction)

1. `fuel_signal/features.py`: one `LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS` symbol (keep it as the
   group composition so the groups stay meaningful, but bind it to one name).
   Plus `NON_MODEL_COLUMNS: dict[str, str]` mapping each computed-but-excluded
   column to its reason, so category (2) becomes explicit rather than emergent.
2. `batch_freeze.resolve_baseline_columns()` stops discovering and returns the
   locked set, asserting the frame contains it and that no `NON_MODEL_COLUMNS`
   leaked in. (fps-sa1 — can land first and be refactored onto this.)
3. A test asserting `LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS == joblib["feature_columns"]` when
   the artifact is present, skipped when it isn't (the artifact is gitignored).
4. Re-export as `experiments/lib/constants.BASELINE_COLUMNS`; update
   `experiments/TEMPLATE_paired_wfcv.py` (currently hand-rolls the composition
   plus a hardcoded `assert len(...) == 54`) and `experiments/lib/README.md`.
5. Record a baseline fingerprint — `n_baseline_columns` plus a short sha256 of the
   sorted column list — in experiment `meta.json`, batch `facts.json`, and a new
   `results.csv` column. Cross-run comparisons can then be checked mechanically
   instead of by eye.

Item 5 is the one that changes the failure mode from "silent for two months" to
"caught at write time"; items 1–4 reduce how often it fires.

## Not in scope

Re-scoring historical experiments whose baseline predates #216 — those were
correct at the time. This is about making the CURRENT contract unambiguous and
machine-checkable, not retconning the ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One importable symbol is the only way any code names the locked feature set
- [ ] A test fails if that symbol and the on-disk model artifact disagree
- [ ] `resolve_baseline_columns()` no longer discovers columns from the frame
- [ ] Computed-but-excluded columns carry a machine-readable reason
- [ ] Every new experiment result records a baseline fingerprint
- [ ] docs/CONVENTIONS.md documents the "declare, never discover" rule
title: Single-source the feature-scope contract (model, pipeline, experiments) and fingerprint it in results

description:
## What

fps-g31 made `aborted_pipeline` / `aborted_environment` release the bd claim so the
candidate goes back on the queue. There is no budget on that, and no age gate.

**This blocks the whole queue, not just one candidate.** `claim_next_candidate`
(launch.py:201) claims with `bd ready --sort oldest -n 1`, and a released bead keeps
its original creation date. So a candidate that fails retryably is always the oldest
unassigned bead and is re-claimed ahead of everything else, every night, forever.
One doomed candidate consumes the nightly slot indefinitely and nothing else in the
queue ever runs.

Re-rated P3 -> P1 on that basis (2026-08-18). The original filing assumed the cost
was "one wasted nightly run"; it is actually total queue starvation. Found by a
review session on PR #303 after the initial CodeRabbit pass raised the unbounded-retry
shape without the head-of-line consequence.

The runner's outcome taxonomy has said "Retry once" for `aborted_environment` since
fps-3jj. Nothing has ever implemented the "once". Before fps-g31 that was harmless
because nothing retried at all.

## Mitigating factors (why this is P1 and not P0)

- Every abort now posts a bd comment (`_finish`, fps-g31), so a starved queue leaves
  a visible nightly trail rather than going silent.
- The two config-shaped causes that would trigger it are now guarded up front:
  `_check_fold_geometry` rejects an impossible inner/outer pair in a second, and
  `read_run_status` no longer crashes the sweep on a malformed file.
- It needs a PERSISTENT fault. A transient one (locked DB, disk blip) retries and
  succeeds, which is the behaviour fps-g31 wanted.

## The actual design question

Where does the count live? `results.json` is overwritten by each re-run — and as of
fps-g31 it is also DELETED at the start of each run — so it cannot hold it. Options:

- a `retry_count` convention in the bd issue (survives, visible, but bd has no typed
  field — description/label convention)
- counting the `[pipeline] ... aborted_` comments already on the bead (no new state,
  but parses prose)
- a sidecar in the run dir that run_candidate does not clear

Prefer whichever keeps queue state in ONE place — the split between `results.json`
(run outcome) and bd (claim state) is what made fps-g31 hard to see.

Consider also whether an exhausted candidate should be de-prioritised rather than
hard-stopped, so it stops head-of-line-blocking without being silently dropped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A candidate that aborts retryably N times stops being auto-released, and says
      so on the bead rather than going quiet
- [ ] A candidate awaiting retry does not starve the rest of the queue
- [ ] The runner docstring's "Retry once" either matches the implementation or is
      reworded to match reality
- [ ] Test: two consecutive retryable completions of the same claim; the second does
      not release
- [ ] Test: a retryably-failing candidate does not prevent a second queued candidate
      from being claimed
title: Retryable aborts have no retry budget — a persistently broken batch re-runs nightly forever

description:
## What

The nightly candidate pipeline cannot complete ANY candidate. First live run
(fps-32p, tgp_delta_7d, 2026-08-17) aborted after 514.8s with:

    realised: no OOF folds over fold-train — pass a smaller inner_fold_params

Three separate defects, all in experiments/pipeline/, none in the candidate.

### 1. inner_fold_params is never supplied (the actual blocker)

launch.py:build_runner_cmd() passes only --batch-dir/--candidate/--bead-id.
runner.py:main() exposes no fold options. So run_candidate() gets
inner_fold_params=None -> {} -> run_paired_realised_backtest ->
_train_calibrate_select_tau -> pool_oof_predictions -> walk_forward_folds()
with its default train_min_days=1825.

Outer fold 1's train window is EXACTLY 1825 days, by the same default. An
inner walk-forward needing 1825 train days + 7 buffer + 90 val can never fit
inside it. Verified on batch0:

    outer fold  1: train 2016-10-30..2021-10-28 (1825d) -> 0 inner folds (8 at 1095)
    outer fold  2: train 2016-10-30..2022-01-26 (1915d) -> 0 inner folds (9 at 1095)
    outer fold 14: train 2016-10-30..2025-01-10 (2995d) -> 12 inner folds (21 at 1095)

Fold 1 is planned first, so it aborts before doing any realised work. This is
candidate-independent and 100% reproducible: every candidate dies identically.

Every prior realised caller passes INNER_FOLDS explicitly:
  experiments/2026-06-20_leading_indicators/realised_tgp.py:55
  experiments/2026-06-18_late_descent_gate1/realised_by_regime.py:57
  experiments/2026-06-19_headroom_map/headroom_map.py:118
all with {"train_min_days": 1095, "val_days": 90, "step_days": 90}. The
pipeline is the first caller that doesn't — the lib default was simply never
meant to be used bare.

### 2. The failure is misclassified as aborted_candidate

runner.py:299-313 routes realised.py's ValueErrors to aborted_candidate. The
comment there already anticipates this exact case ("a bad inner_fold_params
default would hit every candidate run against this batch the same way") and
picks aborted_candidate anyway, for want of a better code. Result: a pipeline
misconfiguration is recorded as the candidate's fault, and would poison the
batch retrospective (fps-3jj.8) if more candidates had run.

### 3. An aborted run is silently invisible

- runner.py:_finish() returns before the post_bd_comment() call at line 386,
  so NO bd comment is posted on any abort path. fps-32p carries only the
  "[launch] validated, launched detached" comment.
- launch.py:find_stale_claims() skips any issue that has a results.json
  (line 125) AND requires a traceback tail (line 127). An abort writes a
  results.json and no traceback, so stale recovery can never reclaim it.

Net: fps-32p is stuck in_progress/assigned forever with no visible signal.
The queue silently drains one candidate per night into the same hole.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] runner.main() accepts --inner-train-min-days / --inner-val-days /
      --inner-step-days (and outer equivalents), defaulting inner to
      {"train_min_days": 1095, "val_days": 90, "step_days": 90}
- [ ] A module-level DEFAULT_INNER_FOLD_PARAMS constant, referenced (not
      re-literalled) by runner and documented as matching the prior
      realised-experiment convention
- [ ] New status for pipeline-caused aborts (or reuse aborted_environment)
      so realised config errors are not attributed to the candidate
- [ ] post_bd_comment fires on EVERY terminal status, including _finish()'s
      early returns
- [ ] find_stale_claims recognises an aborted results.json as reclaimable,
      not as a completed run
- [ ] Regression test: a candidate run against a batch whose fold 1 train
      window equals train_min_days produces >=1 inner OOF fold
- [ ] Regression test: an aborted run posts a bd comment
- [ ] fps-32p reopened and re-run once merged

## Notes

Run evidence: experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{run.log,results.json}
Wall was 8m36s, not the ~67min initially assumed (run.log born 21:59:21,
results.json 22:07:57; the [launch] comment on fps-32p timestamps 11:59 UTC).
The WFCV screen itself completed fine — 14 folds x 5 seeds x 2 arms — so only
the arbiter half is broken.
title: Pipeline: realised backtest aborts every candidate (inner_fold_params default), and the abort is invisible

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/launch.py`'s `main()` calls `launch_detached(cmd, candidate_path.parent)`
with no override, and `experiments/pipeline/runner.py`'s CLI `main()` calls
`run_candidate(batch_dir, candidate_path, bead_id=bead_id)` with no `out_dir` — both default
`out_dir` to `candidate_path.parent`. Since candidate modules are flat siblings
(`experiments/candidates/<batch>/<name>.py`, per generator.md's Filing section and
launch.py's own module docstring), `candidate_path.parent` is the **whole batch directory**,
shared by every candidate filed against that batch — not a per-candidate subdirectory.

## Why I noticed this

An independent code review of PR #301 (fps-3jj.6, dossier routine) traced dossier_tables.py's
`find_pending_runs` work-queue logic (any directory with `results.json` and no `README.md`)
against the actual merged launch.py/runner.py and found the directory model doesn't match:

1. Batch night 1: candidate A's runner writes `results.json`/`rowpreds.parquet`/`fills.parquet`/
   `run.log` into `experiments/candidates/<batch>/`.
2. Dossier routine picks it up, writes `README.md` into that same shared directory.
3. Batch night 2: candidate B's runner writes its OWN `results.json`/etc into the SAME directory,
   overwriting candidate A's artifacts in place (data loss — A's real results are gone, and
   nothing dossiered A's overwritten run first if timing is unlucky).
4. Dossier routine's `find_pending_runs` sees `results.json` exists (now B's) AND `README.md`
   already exists (from A) → this directory is permanently excluded from the queue.
   **Candidate B, and every candidate after A in this batch, is silently never dossiered.**

Since batch sizing is deliberately 1 → 5 → 10-15 (fps-3jj parent design), this breaks the
pipeline starting at batch 2 — every candidate but the first in a multi-candidate batch is
affected.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/pipeline/launch.py` (`main()`, `launch_detached` call site)
- `experiments/pipeline/runner.py` (CLI `main()` — no `--out-dir` flag exposed at all)
- `docs/routines/launch.md` (documents the current, wrong, shared-dir behaviour)
- `tests/test_launch.py` (would need a regression test asserting two candidates in one batch get
  distinct out_dirs)

## Suggested fix

Give each candidate its own out_dir, e.g. `candidate_path.with_suffix("")` (so
`experiments/candidates/<batch>/tgp_delta_7d.py` → `experiments/candidates/<batch>/tgp_delta_7d/`)
— this also happens to match the run-directory convention `docs/routines/dossier.md` already
assumed (and flagged as unverified) before this bug was confirmed. Either thread an explicit
`out_dir` through launch.py's `build_runner_cmd`/a new runner.py `--out-dir` CLI flag, or have
runner.py's default computation do this itself instead of `candidate_path.parent`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two candidates filed against the same batch get distinct out_dirs; neither's artifacts are
      overwritten by the other
- [ ] `docs/routines/launch.md` updated to state the real out_dir convention
- [ ] Regression test in `tests/test_launch.py` (or `tests/test_runner.py`) covering this
- [ ] `docs/routines/dossier.md`'s "Known gaps" section updated once this lands (currently states
      the mismatch as confirmed-broken, pending this fix)
title: Launch/runner give every candidate in a batch the SAME out_dir — later candidates overwrite earlier ones, dossier never sees them

description:
## What
Give the dossier an empirical noise band to quote a candidate's delta against, instead of the
reader's intuition.

BACKLOGGED 2026-08-17, deliberately. Not blocking the pipeline — see "Why deferred".

## Why this exists
The dossier is *written* by an unattended routine with no feel for scale, so a delta of ~0.008c can
be recorded as a finding when nothing real happened. It bites hardest at the retrospective, where
ranking N candidates and taking the max is a multiple-comparisons operation the old
one-at-a-time workflow never performed.

## Why deferred
The original design called for a placebo arm; that was dropped (see fps-3jj) because one draw per
night compares a noisy number against a noisy ruler. The replacement — a batch-setup calibration
run of "uninformative draws" — inherits the unanswered question: *what is an uninformative draw?*

Pure noise is a weak null (the model discards it easily, so everything clears the bar). A permuted
column needs a permutation axis that matches the axis the candidate claims to carry information on
— and for a market-wide series like `tgp_delta_7d`, where every station shares a value on a given
date, a within-date permutation is a no-op. So even the first candidate would have needed a custom
ruler, which is evidence against a single universal one.

Owner's call: the distribution is more reliably learned by looking at 10-20 real experiment results
and grouping them than by constructing a synthetic null now. Revisit once that feel exists.

## Starting idea for whoever picks this up
**R0 vs R0 on a different seed set.** Fit the baseline with SEEDS = (42..46), fit again with
(47..51), take the realised-CPL delta. Same columns, same data — the delta is pure pipeline noise by
construction, and it needs no definition of an "uninformative column", so the market-wide-series
problem never arises. Frozen batch data means it is computed once and cached.

Limit: it measures fit instability, not the specific perturbation of *adding a column*, so it is a
floor rather than the true band. A candidate inside it is definitely noise; a candidate just outside
it is not necessarily signal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A band (not a point) computed once per batch and persisted in the batch dir
- [ ] Dossier prints every candidate's delta against it as a number
- [ ] Retrospective applies it at the ranking step

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj
title: Pipeline: empirical noise band for dossier deltas

description:
## What

`.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` gates worker PRs on **all three** labels (lines 35-40):

```
--label "claude-authored" \
--label "chore" \
--label "auto-merge-ok"
```

CLAUDE.md's worker PR-creation rule ("For each PR", step 3) applies only `claude-authored` + the
issue's original label. **`auto-merge-ok` is never applied by anything.** Every worker-opened chore PR
is therefore permanently ineligible for the automated merge path and sits open until merged by hand.

Verified in this repo 2026-08-13: the label gate is real, and the PR rule as written does not satisfy it.

## Provenance — rescued from a lost worker run

This finding is the worker routine's own, from its 2026-08-13 20:00 UTC run. It observed PR #288 sitting
fully green (tests, Sourcery, auto-merge job all success) since 2026-08-11 and still unmerged two days
later, diagnosed the label gap, and filed it locally as **fps-3xr** — which never reached the shared
Dolt DB because `bd dolt push` hit the egress-proxy 403 (fps-sk0). That local clone is gone. This bead
re-files the finding from an environment where push works.

Corroborating detail from the same run: PR #287 only merged because the owner did it by hand. So has
#288 (merged 2026-08-13 20:40 UTC). Every worker PR to date has been hand-merged — the automated path
has never once fired, and its non-firing has been invisible because a human kept unblocking it.

## Why P1

- The auto-merge path is documented as working (docs/automation.md state machine) and does not.
- It compounds the WIP cap: the worker exits immediately when any `claude-authored` PR is open, so an
  un-merged PR does not just fail to merge, it **halts all worker pickup** until the owner intervenes.
- fps-3jj adds three more scheduled routines; the merge path should be understood first.

## Fix options (pick one — needs a decision, not just a patch)

1. **Add `auto-merge-ok` to CLAUDE.md's PR-creation rule.** Simplest. But it makes every worker PR
   auto-mergeable by default, which is presumably not why a third opt-in label was introduced.
2. **Drop `auto-merge-ok` from the workflow's required set.** Same effect, fewer moving parts.
3. **Keep it as a deliberate owner opt-in** and fix the *documentation* instead — docs/automation.md's
   state machine currently implies auto-merge is the normal path when in fact it requires a manual
   label. This may be the original intent, in which case nothing is broken except the docs.

Option 3 is plausible enough that this should not be silently "fixed" toward 1 or 2 without the owner's
call on what the third label was for.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Owner decides which of the three options is intended
- [ ] Workflow and/or CLAUDE.md and/or docs/automation.md reconciled so all three agree
- [ ] One worker PR observed traversing the intended merge path end to end
title: Worker PRs can never auto-merge: CLAUDE.md never applies the auto-merge-ok label

close_reason: Filed on a false premise — closing as invalid. I assumed a 2026-08-14 09:00 UTC worker run had already happened, conflating the session's Sydney-local date with UTC. Actual: at time of filing it was 2026-08-13 23:24 UTC; the last run was 2026-08-13 20:00 UTC, 40 min BEFORE PR #288 merged at 20:40 UTC. Pickup rule 1 has not yet had an opportunity to fire, so there is no evidence of a defect. fps-e9z was still correctly closed by hand (the work is done) — that pre-empted rule 1 rather than compensating for it. If fps-e9z had still been open after the 2026-08-14 09:00 UTC run, THAT would have been the signal; re-open this if so.
description:
## What

PR #288 merged 2026-08-13 20:40 UTC. It is labelled `claude-authored` + `chore` and its body contains
`Resolves: fps-e9z`. Worker pickup rule 1 ("close out bd issues resolved by your own merged PRs since
the last run") should therefore have closed fps-e9z on the 2026-08-14 09:00 UTC run. It did not —
fps-e9z was still open at P1 on 2026-08-14, and was closed by hand during the fps-3jj design session.

The owner merged #288 manually, which is the normal path (auto-merge.yml gates on age + green checks;
either way the worker's job is only to notice it merged afterwards).

## Prime suspect: fps-sk0

The worker's `bd dolt push` is blocked by an egress-proxy 403 (fps-sk0, now P1). If that is the cause,
the worker did run `bd close fps-e9z` locally in its container, then failed to push — so the closure
was silently discarded when the container was torn down. **This is exactly the symptom fps-sk0
predicts**, and if confirmed it means fps-sk0 is not merely "state doesn't sync" but "the worker
appears to do its job and silently loses all of it".

Check this first — it is the cheapest to confirm and would make this bead a duplicate.

## Other hypotheses, in order

1. **fps-sk0 (above).**
2. **The worker did not run at all.** Rule 0 installs `bd` fresh every run via
   `npm install -g @beads/bd@1.1.2`; a failure there is specified to fail hard and stop. Check the
   Routine's run history for the 2026-08-14 09:00 UTC run.
3. **Rule 0's Dolt-remote reconstruction failed** — no token available, so `bd dolt pull` gave the
   worker a stale DB in which fps-e9z's state was already ambiguous.
4. **Rule 1's query window is wrong.** It says `gh pr list --label claude-authored --state merged`
   "(recent ones)" without a concrete bound. If the implementation caps results in a way that missed a
   PR merged ~12h earlier, that is a real bug in the rule as written.
5. **Rule ordering.** Rule 1 runs before the rule-3 "exit if any open claude-authored PR" bail-out, so
   ordering should be fine — but verify the routine actually executes them in the documented order,
   given fps-6zj (the routine's stored prompt is a stale pre-Beads workflow that does not contain
   rule 1 at all). **If the run followed the embedded stale prompt rather than CLAUDE.md, rule 1 was
   never executed** — which would make this bead a duplicate of fps-6zj instead.

Note hypotheses 1 and 5 point at the two beads just raised to P1. This bead may well resolve as
"symptom of fps-sk0 and/or fps-6zj" rather than a distinct defect — confirming which is the point.

## Why this matters

Rule 1 is the only automatic path from "worker PR merged" to "bead closed". If it is silently broken,
the bd queue accumulates completed-but-open issues, `bd ready` returns work that is already done, and
the worker can re-claim it. fps-3jj adds three more scheduled routines against this same queue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Root cause identified among the hypotheses above (or a new one)
- [ ] If it is fps-sk0 or fps-6zj: close this as a duplicate, and record the confirmed symptom on that bead
- [ ] If it is a distinct defect in rule 1: fix the rule text in CLAUDE.md and verify with one live run
- [ ] Confirm no other merged `claude-authored` PRs have left their `Resolves:` bead open
title: Investigate: worker pickup rule 1 did not close fps-e9z after PR #288 merged

description:
## What
The Claude Code Routine trigger (id `trig_01Mhkd4YLBpuGLhcXLMHaZVQ`, "Fuel Price Signal Chore and Polish Worker") has a `job_config.ccr.events[0].data.message.content` field that is a full pre-Beads-migration prompt: it hardcodes `gh issue list --label "chore,polish" --state open --no-assignee`, `gh issue edit N --add-label design`, `closes #N` commit messages, etc. None of that matches current CLAUDE.md, which moved issue tracking to `bd`/Dolt entirely (2026-08-06, PR #278).

## Why I noticed this
Discovered while triggering a live run to verify the fps-ddf Dolt-remote-auth fix (2026-08-11). The prompt's first line does say "following the rules in CLAUDE.md exactly," and prior live runs (per fps-7z8 notes) did in fact install `bd` and attempt `bd dolt pull` — so the agent appears to be prioritizing the live repo's CLAUDE.md over its own stale embedded step-by-step scaffolding. That's lucky, not guaranteed: the embedded Steps 1-5 are a concrete, detailed alternative workflow sitting right there in the same message, and a future run could plausibly follow the embedded GitHub-Issues steps instead, especially Step 1's PR maintenance logic (`gh pr view N --json reviewThreads`) which doesn't require `bd` at all and could silently run in parallel with/instead of the bd-based flow in CLAUDE.md.

## Files likely affected
Not in this repo's tree — lives in the trigger's `job_config` on the Claude Code Routines platform. Update via `RemoteTrigger` action `update` with a `body` replacing `job_config.ccr.events[0].data.message.content`.

## Suggested fix
Replace the stored message with a short pointer prompt (e.g. "You are the fuel-price-signal worker routine. Working directory: ... Follow CLAUDE.md's 'If you are the scheduled worker routine' section exactly — do not use gh issue commands, all issue tracking is in bd/Dolt.") so there's no stale competing instruction set embedded in the trigger itself.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Trigger's job_config message updated to remove/replace the pre-Beads gh-issue-based instructions
- [ ] One live RemoteTrigger run confirms the routine follows only CLAUDE.md's bd-based pickup rules

## Addendum (2026-08-14, fps-3jj design session)

**There is a SECOND stale copy this bead doesn't cover.** `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/fuel-price-signal-worker/SKILL.md` holds the same pre-Beads content ("Pick up chore/polish **GitHub issues**", `gh pr list`, no bd anywhere) with `Working directory: /Users/esteele/Documents/Claude/fuel-price-signal` hardcoded. It is currently orphaned — `list_scheduled_tasks` returns none — so it is not firing, but it is a live copy-paste hazard and should be deleted or converted at the same time as the remote trigger. So: two stale copies, one remote (firing twice daily), one local (dormant).

**Generalise the fix into a rule, not a one-off edit.** Both copies went stale for the same reason: instructions were *duplicated into the scheduler* rather than referenced from the repo. The suggested fix above (a short pointer prompt) is right — make it the standing pattern for every scheduled task in this project:

- Canonical prompt content lives **in the repo, tracked**: `docs/routines/<name>.md`.
  (`.claude/` is gitignored here, so prompts cannot live there.)
- The scheduler's stored prompt — remote `job_config` message or local `SKILL.md` — is a **three-line shim**: who you are, the working directory, and the repo path to read and follow. Nothing else.

**Priority raised P2 -> P1.** This is a live misconfiguration on an agent that fires twice daily, and it is a prerequisite for fps-3jj: the feature-engineering pipeline adds three more scheduled routines against the same bd queue, and adding automation on top of a known-miswired automation is the wrong order.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Local `~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/fuel-price-signal-worker/SKILL.md` deleted or converted to a shim
- [ ] `docs/routines/` established as the tracked home for routine prompt content
title: Worker Routine's stored job_config prompt is stale (pre-Beads gh-issue workflow)

description:
## What
The worker Routine's `bd dolt pull`/`push` still fail with no way to authenticate. This is the "Known gap" documented in CLAUDE.md's worker section, now root-caused precisely via a live triggered run on 2026-08-11.

## Root cause (confirmed live, 2026-08-11)
- `bd`'s Dolt `sync.remote` is `git+ssh://git@github.com/edwinsteele/fuel-price-signal.git`.
- The Routine's container has no `ssh` binary.
- The environment's git `insteadOf` proxy rewrites only match `git@github.com:` and `ssh://git@github.com/` — not the `git+ssh://` scheme `bd` actually uses — so the rewrite never fires and the connection has no way to authenticate.
- This is a step beyond (and now supersedes in precision) the earlier "1Password-gated SSH key" framing — the deeper issue is the scheme mismatch, not just key availability.

## Why I noticed this
CLAUDE.md ([lines 27-35](../CLAUDE.md)) already flagged this as an unresolved known gap since the Beads migration (2026-08-06). Today's session (fixing the separate bd-binary-missing issue, now resolved — see git log `f7c2db8`/`1f3c2ec`/`77b4986`) got a much sharper live diagnosis of *why* it fails, which is worth acting on rather than leaving as prose only.

## Candidate fixes (owner decision needed — this is why it's `design`, not `chore`)
1. Point `sync.remote` at an `https://` URL with a token (deploy token or PAT) reachable from the Routine's environment.
2. Add a git `insteadOf` rule specifically for `git+ssh://git@github.com/` (mapping to whatever transport the environment can actually authenticate).

Both require a decision about which credential mechanism is acceptable to expose in the Routine's environment — not something to pick unilaterally.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide fix approach (https+token vs insteadOf rule)
- [ ] Implement + verify via a live `RemoteTrigger run` that `bd dolt pull` succeeds in the Routine
- [ ] Update/remove the "Known gap" paragraph in CLAUDE.md once resolved
- [ ] Confirm the worker can progress past rule 0 to actually claim and PR a real chore/polish issue end-to-end
title: Fix Dolt remote auth for worker Routine (git+ssh:// scheme not covered by insteadOf)

## What
16 open Dependabot alerts as of 2026-08-09 (12 high, 4 moderate), all against transitive deps in uv.lock:
- **Pillow 12.2.0** (13 alerts, mostly high — decompression-bomb-check bypasses across several loaders, heap OOB writes in paste/crop/RankFilter/ImageCmsTransform, a JPEG2000 DoS, an OS command injection in WindowsViewer.get_command(), an EPS infinite-loop DoS). Patched: 12.3.0. Pulled in via `matplotlib>=3.10.9`.
- **soupsieve 2.8.3** (2 alerts, high — memory exhaustion via large comma-separated selector lists, ReDoS in the selector parser). Patched: 2.8.4. Pulled in via `beautifulsoup4>=4.14.3`.
- **setuptools 82.0.1** (1 alert, medium — MANIFEST.in exclusion bypass via NFC/NFD Unicode normalization collision on macOS APFS/HFS+). Patched: 83.0.0.

None of these are pinned or ceiling-constrained in pyproject.toml, so the patched versions should be resolvable without a pyproject.toml change — likely just `uv lock --upgrade-package pillow --upgrade-package soupsieve --upgrade-package setuptools` (or `uv lock --upgrade` if that's cleaner) followed by `uv sync`.

## Why I noticed this
User spotted "16 vulnerabilities" in the GitHub UI (Security → Dependabot) while working on the CI DB/model pipeline (PR #279) and asked for it to be tracked separately.

## Files likely affected
- uv.lock (regenerated)
- pyproject.toml (only if a version ceiling turns out to be needed — shouldn't be)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `uv lock` picks up Pillow >=12.3.0, soupsieve >=2.8.4, setuptools >=83.0.0
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` pass — matplotlib (reliability plots, shap plots) and beautifulsoup4 (tgp.py's AIP xlsx scrape) are both real runtime dependents, not just transitive noise, so actually exercise those paths rather than trusting a lockfile bump alone

title: Resolve 16 open Dependabot alerts (Pillow, soupsieve, setuptools)

That issue would stay `in_progress` forever, invisible to `bd ready`, effectively lost.

## Why I noticed this

description:
## What

`experiments.lib.io.write_meta` always writes `out_dir / \"meta.json\"`. An experiment
directory with more than one script therefore has exactly one meta.json, owned by
whichever script ran last.

Live instance: `experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/` has both `timing.py`
and `homogeneity.py` calling `write_meta(HERE, ...)`. The committed meta.json is
homogeneity's (top-level keys `candidate`, `universe_spec`, `populations`, `runs`,
`homogeneity`); timing.py's baseline block and tank stamp were overwritten and are
not recoverable from it.

## Why I noticed this

Found while fixing fps-6rm (the unstamped `timing.json`). fps-6rm's fix incidentally
mitigates the data loss — each script now writes write_meta's stamped return value
into its OWN artifact, so the baseline/tank provenance survives in timing.json and
homogeneity.json regardless of who won meta.json. The clobber itself is untouched:
meta.json still silently claims to describe the whole directory while describing one
script, which is a trap for the next multi-script experiment dir.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/lib/io.py` (`write_meta` — e.g. an optional `filename=`/`stem=`
  parameter defaulting to `meta.json`, so callers sharing a directory can disambiguate)
- `experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/{timing,homogeneity}.py` (callers)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two scripts in one directory can each write their own meta artifact without
      overwriting the other
- [ ] Existing single-script callers keep writing `meta.json` unchanged (no artifact churn)
- [ ] Decide whether `2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/meta.json` is regenerated or
      left as-is with the ambiguity documented
title: write_meta hardcodes meta.json, so two scripts in one experiment dir clobber each other
