description:
## What

fps-nas criterion 5 decided: grade candidates on the broad 410-station Sydney population,
report the five. The placebo noise floor every candidate is graded against is still
five-station, so it must be rebuilt at the grading width.

Run against batch1's frozen snapshot:

```
PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.noise_floor batch1 \
  --n-stations 410 --n-draws 40 --out-name noise_floor_n410.json
```

(exact flag names depend on what fps-916 lands.)

**`--out-name`, NOT `--force`.** Every dossier written to date was graded against
`noise_floor.json`. Write the wide band beside it. `_comparable_noise_banks` (fps-30p) already
exists precisely so a second bank in the same directory is read and disclosed rather than
ignored — see feedback_committed_artifacts_before_new_compute.

**Draw count: 40, not the default 10.** Station count is no longer the binding constraint on
resolution; draw count is. `family_wise_z_threshold(n_candidates=1, n_draws=n)` gives:

    n=10 -> 1.923    n=20 -> 1.772    n=30 -> 1.727
    n=40 -> 1.706    n=60 -> 1.685    n=100 -> 1.669

Flat past 40, and the margin on batch1's best candidate is thin enough (z -2.33 against a bar
of 1.923) for 0.2 of a bar to matter. The owner has stated up to 5x compute on batch freezes
and candidate runs is cheap, so the draw count is not the place to economise.

## Cost

Measured at n=410 in experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/: ~72 s/arm-fold
(2024s for 14 folds x 2 arms). `BaselineCache` makes a floor "1 baseline fit + N placebo
fits", so 14 x (40+1) = 574 arm-folds ~= 11h. At 10 draws it is ~3.1h. Overnight job.

## The question it answers

Whether the placebo band narrows with universe width the way the fold-clustered sd did
(exactly 2.00x, 0.7982 -> 0.3992, for 102x the decisions). This is ASSUMED in fps-nas's
write-up and explicitly logged there as `not_tested` — it is the whole of this bead.

If it does narrow ~2x, `tgp_cycle_displacement`'s broad delta of -0.1292 scores about -3.1
and clears more convincingly than the five-station figure ever did. If it does NOT narrow,
the criterion-5 decision needs revisiting, because grading on the broad population would then
be strictly harder with no compensating gain.

## Why I noticed this

fps-nas criterion 6. Full context and the verdict-flip table in
experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/README.md.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/batches/batch1/noise_floor_n410.json (new artifact, gitignored DB inputs)
- possibly experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py if the disclosure path needs a nudge

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] BLOCKED until fps-916 lands — otherwise the artifact cannot record its own population
- [ ] Wide floor computed at 410 stations, 40 draws, written under its own `--out-name`
- [ ] `noise_floor.json` (five-station) left untouched
- [ ] Band sd at 410 compared to the five-station band's 0.0999 — does it narrow ~2x?
- [ ] `tgp_cycle_displacement`'s broad delta re-graded against the wide band; result recorded
- [ ] fps-nas's `not_tested` entry for band-narrowing retired with a number
title: Recompute batch1's noise floor at the 410-station grading population

description:
## What

Decide and implement how this repo's operating contract survives being read by a
second agent harness (OpenAI Codex) alongside Claude Code. Today the contract is
split across four files with different loaders, and ~60% of it is either
Claude-only or silently unreachable from Codex. The failure mode is not broken
code — it is broken *epistemics*: a Codex session re-derives settled results,
emits ledger rows that are not comparable to existing ones, and re-litigates
rejected candidates, all while looking perfectly plausible.

This is a design issue because the fix requires choosing a doc architecture
(what is the shared contract, what is harness-specific, where does private
memory get promoted to), not just moving bytes.

## Evidence (measured 2026-09-05, this checkout)

**1. `AGENTS.md` is silently truncated by Codex, mid-sentence, at the worst
possible point.**

Codex's `project_doc_max_bytes` defaults to `32 * 1024` = 32,768 and
**tail-truncates with no warning** in TUI, `exec`, or the VS Code extension
(openai/codex#13386, open). `AGENTS.md` is 40,290 bytes / 421 lines, so 7,522
bytes (18.7%) are dropped.

    $ head -c 32768 AGENTS.md | wc -l
    359
    $ head -c 32768 AGENTS.md | tail -1
    - `.beads/` holds bd's config (git-tracked) and its Dolt database (`.beads/embeddeddolt/`, gitignored

The cut lands inside the *second bullet* of `## Beads` (AGENTS.md:356). Codex
learns Beads exists and then nothing else. Everything below is invisible:

| Section | Line | What Codex never learns |
|---|---|---|
| rest of `## Beads` | 359-366 | `bd dolt pull/push`, `bd ready/show/search`, `--claim`, `bd close`, the `--type=decision` pointer convention, "ignore `bd prime`" |
| `## Automation workflow` | 368 | worker/interactive split |
| `### Issue label taxonomy` | 372 | routing labels, topic labels, priority semantics |
| `### Branch and PR conventions` | 411 | branch naming, PR title format, `Resolves:` line, `--base main` |
| `### Reviewing PRs` | 418 | the worktree-first review shortcut |

    $ head -c 32768 AGENTS.md | grep -c 'bd memories\|bd recall'
    0

Note the recursion: the label taxonomy that tells an agent which label to file
under is itself below the cut, so a Codex session cannot file a correctly
labelled issue.

**2. 147 private memory files (581,733 bytes) are unreachable from Codex.**

`~/.claude/projects/-Users-esteele-Code-fuel-price-signal/memory/` holds the
load-bearing analysis state: canonical cadence 1d, headroom 3.06 c/L, "confidence
prior: IGNORE, never refine", the screen/arbiter population mismatch, the
negative-results ledger, "no feature ever delivered 0.5 c/L alone". Codex starts
cold on all of it.

`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` already has the governing rule — *"Decisions land in repo
docs, not just memory... decisions that govern code structure must be
discoverable and version-controlled"* — it is simply under-enforced, because a
single-agent setup makes memory feel sufficient. A second harness makes the cost
immediate rather than theoretical.

**3. `bd memories` (53 entries) is Claude-only knowledge, and it is the
destructive half.**

`bd recall` appears twice in CLAUDE.md and **zero** times in AGENTS.md's
readable region or CONVENTIONS.md. The memories a cold session breaks first:

| memory | consequence |
|---|---|
| `branch-before-first-commit` | committed to `main` twice historically; each needed `git reset --hard` + force-push |
| `beads-writes-through-to-primary-worktree` | bd writes land in the primary checkout, look like another session's dirt |
| `absolute-path-edit-wrong-worktree` | edits the wrong copy, no error |
| `baseline-fingerprint-before-comparing-runs` | two runs differenced that were never comparable |
| `branch-prs-from-origin-main` | PR branched off a stale local `main` |

**4. Rules that exist only in `CLAUDE.md` (22,974 bytes), which Codex never
opens.** Grep counts across the three files:

| rule | CONVENTIONS | AGENTS | CLAUDE |
|---|---|---|---|
| post-merge checklist | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `git pull --ff-only` step | 0 | 0 | 1 |
| `bd recall` | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| worktree sweep | 1 (passing) | 1 (passing) | 4 |

Also CLAUDE.md-only: "interactive sessions do not pick up `chore`/`polish`",
"never use the `claude-authored` label", and the orientation list.

**5. Precedent already exists in-repo.** `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (448
bytes, added 2026-05-14 in #79) is exactly the shape proposed here: a thin router
into AGENTS.md/STATUS.md/ML_SIGNAL.md/README.md. It has needed no maintenance in
four months. CLAUDE.md is the file that drifted away from that pattern.

**6. No tracked harness config exists.** `.gitignore:2` is `.claude/`, so
`.claude/settings.json` is untracked. Adding `.codex/config.toml` is therefore a
new decision, not a symmetric one.

## The four failure classes

**A. Context that will not load** (items 1-4 above). Silent, and the highest
leverage to fix.

**B. Conventions that are mechanically impossible in Codex.**
`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § PR feedback loop mandates
`ScheduleWakeup(delaySeconds=270)` as *"a mandatory mechanical step, not a
suggestion"*. Codex has no equivalent: its only hook event is
`agent-turn-complete` via `notify`; `notify` is on the project-local config
denylist so it cannot be committed; and repo-local hooks reportedly do not fire
in interactive sessions at all (openai/codex#17532). The rule needs restating in
terms of the *outcome* (poll `gh pr view` after >=270s) with per-harness
mechanisms named, not the Claude tool call. Same treatment for the
`spawn_task` -> `bd create` redirect, whose *intent* (never pivot, file an issue)
is agent-neutral even though the trigger is not.

**C. Sandbox and execution-model mismatch.** Codex defaults to
`workspace-write` with **network access off**. Everything routine here is
network-bound: `gh pr *`, `bd dolt pull/push`, `uv run` dependency resolution,
`history.py` bulk-CSV download, the FuelCheck OAuth path. Worse, worktrees are
nested *inside* the primary checkout, and two things reach outside a
worktree-rooted workspace: (i) the git common dir is
`/Users/esteele/Code/fuel-price-signal/.git`, so `git commit` itself may be
denied; (ii) bd writes through to the **primary's**
`.beads/interactions.jsonl` regardless of which worktree is cwd. This needs to
be *tested*, not reasoned about — it is the kind of thing that half-works and
leaves a partial commit. Also: the pre-commit hook runs
`uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` plus bd's hook, which with network off
may fail inside the hook and surface as a confusing commit error rather than a
clear sandbox denial.

**D. Provenance and attribution.** `auto-merge.yml` gates on
`claude-authored` + `chore` + `auto-merge-ok`; a Codex PR is structurally
invisible to it. `experiments/results.csv` has `git_sha`,
`baseline_fingerprint` and `tank_params` columns but **no column recording which
agent produced the row**, so a mixed ledger cannot be audited after the fact.

## Decisions required (the design content)

1. **Doc architecture.** Preferred: `AGENTS.md` becomes the shared agent-neutral
   contract and drops under 32,768 bytes by moving `## Module structure`,
   `### SQLite schema`, `## Canonical feature set` and similar stable reference
   material to a new `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; `CLAUDE.md` shrinks to the
   `copilot-instructions.md` shape plus genuinely Claude-shaped content (Skill
   invocations, `spawn_task` redirect, model/effort guidance); agent-neutral
   rules currently only in CLAUDE.md move to `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`.
   Alternative considered: keep AGENTS.md long and only raise
   `project_doc_max_bytes`. Rejected as the primary fix because it depends on
   per-machine config that a fresh clone or a CI runner will not have, and
   because ordering matters independently of the cap (process rules should
   precede reference material for any agent with a context budget).
2. **Whether to commit `.codex/config.toml`.** `project_doc_max_bytes`,
   `sandbox_mode`, `sandbox_workspace_write.network_access` and `writable_roots`
   are *not* on the project-local denylist (which covers `openai_base_url`,
   `chatgpt_base_url`, `apps_mcp_product_sku`, `model_provider`,
   `model_providers`, `notify`, `profile`, `profiles`,
   `experimental_realtime_ws_base_url`, `otel`), so a committed file works once
   the project is trusted. Decide whether sandbox relaxation belongs in a
   committed file at all, or only in `~/.codex/config.toml` with the repo
   documenting the required settings.
3. **How much private memory gets promoted, and to where.** `bd remember`
   (reachable by both harnesses via `bd recall`) vs a tracked
   `docs/FINDINGS.md`. Not all 147 — the target is the subset that would change
   a decision, roughly the *Findings that constrain future work* and
   *How to evaluate* sections of the memory index.
4. **Codex's role.** Proposal: Codex is used where statelessness is a feature
   (adversarial diff review via the existing `adversarial-review:codex-review`
   skill, implementing a fully-specified bd issue, self-contained refactors),
   and the stateful analysis loop (candidate evaluation, cadence/baseline
   decisions, anything writing `results.csv` or the negative-results ledger)
   stays with Claude until decision 3 lands. Record this split in the docs so it
   is a rule, not a habit.
5. **A `codex-authored` label**, and whether `auto-merge.yml` should recognise
   it. Default recommendation: add the label for provenance, do **not** extend
   auto-merge to it initially.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` is under 32,768 bytes, and a test in `tests/` asserts it
      (model it on `tests/test_feature_contract.py`). The test message must
      explain *why* the cap exists so a future reader does not simply raise it.
- [ ] Every rule an agent needs before its first git action is inside the first
      32,768 bytes of `AGENTS.md`: `bd` command surface, `bd memories`/`bd recall`,
      the label taxonomy (routing + topic), branch/PR conventions, and the
      "branch before first commit" rule.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` contains no agent-neutral rule that is not also reachable from
      `AGENTS.md` (directly or via a link stated inside the 32 KiB window). In
      particular the post-merge checklist and the `--ff-only` sweep are relocated
      or mirrored.
- [ ] `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § PR feedback loop states the outcome
      (poll `gh pr view` after >=270s) with the Claude and Codex mechanisms named
      separately; `ScheduleWakeup` is no longer the sole stated mechanism.
- [ ] Required Codex settings are documented in-repo (`project_doc_max_bytes`,
      `sandbox_mode`, `network_access`, `writable_roots`), whether or not
      `.codex/config.toml` is committed. If it is committed, `.gitignore` is
      updated deliberately (`.claude/` is currently blanket-ignored).
- [ ] A Codex session launched **from a nested worktree** has been run
      end-to-end at least once and the result recorded in the issue: whether
      `git commit`, `bd close`, and `bd dolt push` succeed, are prompted, or
      fail. If they fail, the documented remedy (launch from repo root, or
      `writable_roots`) is verified, not assumed.
- [ ] The promoted-memory subset from decision 3 exists in its chosen home and
      the corresponding memory files are deleted per the MEMORY.md policy
      ("once promoted... delete the memory file and its index line outright").
- [ ] `experiments/results.csv` gains an `agent` column (and `write_meta` an
      equivalent field) so ledger rows are attributable. Existing rows backfill
      as `claude`.
- [ ] `docs/STATUS.md` or `AGENTS.md` states the Claude/Codex division of labour
      from decision 4.

## Explicitly out of scope

- Wiring `check_freeze_cadence` into the candidate runner — already tracked as
  **fps-ie0**, and it is the correct fix for that specific gap independent of
  this issue. This issue only motivates it.
- Any change to model, features, cadence, or the locked baseline.
- Making the disabled worker Routine work under Codex (see fps-sk0, blocked).
- Parallelism / concurrent-session coordination. The owner has scoped this to
  contract portability, not simultaneous execution.

## Follow-up issues to file after this lands

- `polish`/`pipeline`: hard-assert `baseline_fingerprint` equality before any
  cross-run delta in `experiments/lib/`, rather than relying on the
  `baseline-fingerprint-before-comparing-runs` memory. Turning a convention into
  an assertion is what makes it hold regardless of which agent is driving.
- `chore`/`infra`: a `make check-landed` or `pre-push` hook enforcing the
  existing postcondition (`git status --short` empty AND
  `git log --oneline origin/main..main` empty). The 2026-08-26 eight-stranded-
  commits incident is more likely with two tools that disagree about what
  "landed" means.
- `chore`/`infra`: `codex-authored` label creation, if decision 5 says yes.

## References

- openai/codex#13386 — AGENTS.md silently truncated, no warning (open)
- openai/codex#17532 — repo-local `.codex/config.toml` hooks do not fire
  interactively (open)
- Codex config reference: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference
- Codex sandboxing: https://developers.openai.com/codex/concepts/sandboxing
- Codex AGENTS.md discovery: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md
- In-repo precedent: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (#79)
- Related: fps-ie0 (cadence wiring), fps-sk0 (Routine blocked)
notes:
## Refinement (2026-09-05): "Codex can't use bd" has THREE causes, not one

Follow-up question from the owner: is AGENTS.md a symlink to CLAUDE.md, and is
truncation the only reason Codex misses Beads? Both checked; answers below.

**AGENTS.md is NOT a symlink to CLAUDE.md.** Verified: inodes 53945372 vs
53945277, sizes 40,290 vs 22,974, distinct git blobs, both mode 100644 (a
symlink would be 120000). Symlinking them would also be the wrong fix — the
combined ~63 KB is nearly 2x the 32,768 cap, and CLAUDE.md's Skill/spawn_task/
model-effort content is noise for Codex.

**Beads unreachability decomposes into three independent mechanisms.** The
issue body above over-attributed it to truncation. Corrected:

1. *Truncation of the command surface.* Codex DOES see `## Beads` (AGENTS.md:356),
   the framing sentence, and bullet 1 cut mid-word. `bd` token counts:
   4 before the cut (incl. one incidental `bd show fps-tpy` at line 161) vs 36
   after. So Codex knows a tracker exists but has no verbs — worse than knowing
   nothing, because it invites guessing.

2. *No fallback source teaches the surface.* `README.md` has ZERO `bd` mentions,
   so the natural orienting read teaches nothing. `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` has 9,
   but all use-site (`bd show <id>`, `bd close <id>`) presuming prior knowledge;
   it never teaches the surface and is not auto-loaded by either harness.
   Compounding: `.beads/README.md` (tracked) correctly points to
   "AGENTS.md § Beads ... for the actual conventions (commands, label taxonomy,
   decision-pointer convention)" — an anchor into precisely the truncated
   region. The only breadcrumb in the repo routes Codex into the hole.

3. *The database is absent, and for a worktree-rooted Codex session,
   unreachable.* `embeddeddolt/` is gitignored and exists ONLY in the primary
   checkout (49 MB at /Users/esteele/Code/fuel-price-signal/.beads/embeddeddolt);
   `ls .beads/` in any nested worktree shows only the 4 tracked files. bd finds
   it by walking up. Therefore: (a) a fresh clone has no DB until `bd dolt pull`,
   which is documented only below the truncation point; (b) Codex defaults to
   network off, so that pull fails anyway; (c) under `workspace-write` rooted at
   a worktree, the DB is OUTSIDE the workspace, so reads/writes hit the sandbox
   boundary.

**Consequence for scope.** Cause 3 is structural, not documentary — it survives
both the doc restructure (decision 1) and a raised `project_doc_max_bytes`
(decision 2). It requires `writable_roots` covering the repo root AND
`network_access = true`. This promotes the "run a Codex session end-to-end from
a nested worktree" acceptance criterion from a formality to the load-bearing
verification in this issue: do it BEFORE investing in the doc restructure, since
a negative result changes decision 4 (Codex's role) materially — if bd is
unreachable from worktrees in practice, Codex is confined to repo-root sessions
regardless of how good the docs get.

**Additional acceptance criteria implied:**
- [ ] `README.md` gains a pointer to the bd surface, or the orientation section
      of AGENTS.md is explicit that README is not the entry point for workflow.
- [ ] `.beads/README.md`'s pointer resolves to content that is actually readable
      under a 32,768-byte cap (i.e. § Beads moves above the line).
- [ ] Bootstrap path documented for a checkout with no `embeddeddolt/`: what
      `bd ready` does, and that `bd dolt pull` is the required first step.
## Closing as premature (2026-09-05, same day as filed)

Owner intends to migrate off Beads before integrating Codex, and will scope that
migration separately. This issue is premised on Beads being the tracker, so its
spine does not survive:

- headline impact of the AGENTS.md truncation was "Codex never learns the bd
  command surface" — moot
- cause 2 (no fallback source teaches bd; `.beads/README.md`'s pointer resolves
  into the truncated region) — moot
- cause 3 (49 MB gitignored `embeddeddolt/` outside a worktree-rooted
  `workspace-write` sandbox), which the refinement note promoted to the
  load-bearing verification — moot
- decision 3 (`bd remember` vs a tracked doc as the home for promoted memory)
  collapses to the tracked doc

Re-scope the Codex integration AFTER migration; the shape changes enough that
patching this issue would be more work than rewriting it.

## Tracker-agnostic findings worth keeping (re-verify, don't trust)

These survive any tracker choice. Recorded as commands so a future session
re-measures rather than inherits stale numbers:

    wc -c AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md          # was 40,290 / 22,974 on 2026-09-05
    # Codex default project_doc_max_bytes = 32*1024 = 32,768; TAIL-truncates,
    # silently, no warning in TUI/exec/VS Code (openai/codex#13386, open).
    head -c 32768 AGENTS.md | tail -1  # shows where the cut lands
    # NOTE: removing the Beads section (~1.5 KB) does NOT get AGENTS.md under
    # the cap on its own. The doc split is still required.

    # Rules reachable only from CLAUDE.md, which Codex never opens:
    for t in "post-merge" "ff-only"; do
      grep -ci "$t" docs/CONVENTIONS.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md; done
    # was 0/0/1 for both.

Other durable items:
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (448 bytes, #79, untouched since 2026-05-14)
  is in-repo precedent for the thin-router shape CLAUDE.md should adopt.
- Codex defaults: `workspace-write`, network OFF. `network_access = true` is an
  all-or-nothing legacy switch; the managed proxy gives domain rules, but adding
  rules does NOT enable the proxy by itself.
- The `.git` common dir is at the repo root, so a Codex session rooted at a
  nested worktree may be denied on `git commit` itself. This survives the bd
  migration and still needs an end-to-end test; `writable_roots` is the fix.
- Hosts this repo actually contacts (for an allowlist):
  api.onegov.nsw.gov.au, data.nsw.gov.au, aip.com.au, github.com,
  api.github.com, objects.githubusercontent.com (release redirects — easy to
  miss), pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org. The cdn.jsdelivr.net / fonts.google*
  hosts in inspect.py are browser-side only, not agent-side.
- `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § PR feedback loop mandates `ScheduleWakeup` — a
  Claude-only tool. Restate as an outcome (poll `gh pr view` after >=270s).
- `experiments/results.csv` has no `agent` column, so a mixed-harness ledger
  cannot be audited after the fact.
- `auto-merge.yml` gates on `claude-authored` + `chore` + `auto-merge-ok`; a
  non-Claude PR is structurally invisible to it.

## Superseded by

The Beads-vs-GitHub decision, to be scoped by the owner. Relevant to that
scoping: GitHub shipped native issue dependencies (`--blocked-by`/`--blocking`/
`--parent`/`--add-sub-issue`, JSON fields `blockedBy`/`blocking`/`parent`/
`subIssues`) in gh v2.94.0 on 2026-06-10 — five weeks BEFORE the 2026-08-06
Beads migration. Local gh is 2.98.0 and already has them, so `bd ready`'s
open-and-unblocked query has a native one-liner equivalent. Still opt-in public
preview: confirm it is enabled on this repo before planning around it.
title: Make the agent operating contract portable across Claude Code and Codex

description:
## What

`experiments/lib/universe.py`'s coverage gate counts `daily_prices` rows. That is the
right axis for the REPLAY (`PriceHistory.station_price_at` / `aggregate_backtest`), but
it is not the axis the WFCV screen or a candidate's `extra_feature_provider` needs, and
the two disagree badly on exactly the folds that matter.

Measured on batch1's frozen artifacts (2026-09-05), rows inside each fold's val window:

| fold | station | feature rows | daily_prices | raw prices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 414   | **0** | 86 | 13 |
| 1 | 18517 | **0** | 86 | 13 |
| 4 | 414   | 24 | 31 | 9 |
| 5 | 414   | 0  | 0  | 0 |
| 8 | 414   | **8** | 90 | 29 |

Fold 1: both Blue Mountains stations have ZERO feature rows and 0.96 `daily_prices`
coverage — the current gate passes them without complaint. Fold 8: 414 is at 1.00
`daily_prices` coverage with 8 feature rows.

Cause is known and documented (see the `project_preferred_station_outages` memory):
`fill.py` forward-fills `daily_prices` for gaps <= `MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS`, while
`labels.py` strips 7d before and 90d after a gap from the feature frame. So the two
tables disagree by construction, and the feature side is the stricter one.

## Why I noticed this

Post-merge review of PR #361 (fps-nas). The gate's docstring is not overclaiming — it
says it prevents `aggregate_backtest` silent-skips and dry-tank clamps, which are
price-side and true. But the gate's PURPOSE is a comparable, replayable universe, and a
widened universe gated only on `daily_prices` can admit stations that are heavily
feature-dark, producing `extra_feature_provider` misses (NaN) rather than real rows.
Reduced sample, not corrupted — but silently, and unevenly across stations.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/lib/universe.py (`eligible_stations`, `_window_coverage`, `describe_universe`)
- tests/test_exp_lib_universe.py

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide whether feature-row availability is a GATE or a REPORTED field (report is
      probably right, matching the `observed_fraction_*` precedent — measure, report,
      never filter)
- [ ] `describe_universe` carries a per-window feature-row availability figure for both
      populations, so a homogeneity read can see it
- [ ] The docstring states plainly that `daily_prices` coverage is the REPLAY axis and
      is not a proxy for feature availability
- [ ] Test pinning the fold-1 shape: high `daily_prices` coverage with zero feature rows
title: universe.py gates on daily_prices coverage, which is NOT feature-row availability

close_reason: Small inefficiency (12min/night, only when alternating universes); the one caller that alternates already bypasses the shared cache directly. Reopen if a broad universe becomes the standing grading population.
description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/runner.py`'s `_save_baseline_cache` writes the R0 baseline
cache to a single fixed path, `<batch_dir>/r0_cache.joblib` (`BASELINE_CACHE_FILENAME`),
unconditionally at the end of every `run_candidate` — regardless of which
`station_codes` that run used. `_load_baseline_cache` then compares fingerprints
and, on a mismatch, falls back to a full R0 refit.

Correctness is fine (the fingerprint in `experiments/lib/realised.py`'s
`_baseline_cache_fingerprint` includes `sorted(station_codes)`, so a stale cache
is never silently reused). The cost is not: with fps-nas widening the arbiter's
replay universe, ALTERNATING between the five-station population and a broad one
means every run overwrites the other population's cache, so every run pays the
full R0 refit — the ~12min/night `fps-e2l` exists to save, gone in both
directions.

## Why I noticed this

Writing `experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/homogeneity.py` (fps-nas),
which has to run one candidate at two populations. The obvious implementation —
call `run_candidate` twice with different `station_codes` — is unusable for this
reason, so the script calls `run_paired_realised_backtest` directly instead and
duplicates a little of runner's arm construction. That workaround is fine for one
experiment and wrong as a standing answer if a broad universe is ever adopted as
the grading population.

Verified by reading, not run: `_save_baseline_cache` (runner.py:878) takes only
`batch_dir` and `cache`; the filename has no universe component.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/runner.py (`_save_baseline_cache`, `_load_baseline_cache`,
  `BASELINE_CACHE_FILENAME`)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The cache filename (or a directory under `batch_dir`) carries a short digest
      of the universe the cache was captured under, so two populations can hold
      warm caches side by side
- [ ] A mismatch still falls back to a refit rather than aborting — unchanged
- [ ] Old single-file caches are either migrated or ignored cleanly, never
      mis-read as belonging to the current universe
- [ ] Test covering: run at universe A, run at universe B, re-run at universe A
      hits a cache rather than refitting
title: r0_cache.joblib is keyed only on batch_dir, so alternating station universes thrashes it

description:
## What

Decide two things once `fps-490` reports each locked block's `delta_cpl_held` and z:
1. **Is alpha = 0.10 the right screen bar for batch2?**
2. **Does the locked set carry dead weight worth REMOVING?**

Blocked by fps-490 — do not start before its numbers exist.

## Background: the grading redesign this validates

Reviewing batch1's RETROSPECTIVE (2026-09-05) reached these positions:

- **Drop the batch-level correction entirely.** Bonferroni/BH penalise a candidate for the
  company it keeps, and the batch is an administrative unit — the same 5 candidates filed
  as 5 batches of 1 would face 1.923 instead of 2.9591 on identical evidence. Incoherent.
  The correction is only justified if the rule is "promote the best of N"; the actual rule
  is "grade each on its own merits, and nothing graduates from the screen anyway".
- **Screen each candidate independently against the noise floor at alpha ~= 0.10**
  (z bar 1.451 = 0.145 c/L @ 1d). The noise floor is still required — only the /N penalty
  goes. alpha picked from the ECONOMIC floor (~0.10-0.15 c/L is where a feature stops
  being worth having), not from convention.
- **Nothing graduates from the screen.** Passes go to a combination run first —
  one-at-a-time screening cannot see negative interaction between two features that each
  help alone (they may read the same structure and split model capacity).
- **The signature is read at GRADUATION, not at the screen.** Gating the screen on
  signature would have killed tgp_cycle_displacement, the strongest economic result.
- Multiplicity does not vanish, it MOVES to the combination stage — that is where you
  genuinely choose among alternatives. Pre-register which combinations get tested; do not
  search all 2^k subsets.

Applied to batch1 at alpha=0.10: `tgp_cycle_displacement` (z 2.3295) and
`network_move_breadth` (z 1.8794) pass; the other three do not.

## Decision 1 — is the bar right?

- **All 7 blocks clear 1.451** → bar is validated, adopt for batch2.
- **Some blocks sit inside the band** → EITHER the bar is stricter than the standard the
  locked set was actually held to (loosen it, or accept the locked set was graduated on a
  different currency), OR those blocks are dead weight. Decision 2 disambiguates.

Prediction on record before looking (2026-09-05): the 35-column LGA block clears
comfortably; several small blocks land inside the band.

## Decision 2 — the interesting one: does REMOVING a block help?

A block that contributes ~nothing but adds columns is not neutral — it adds overfit
capacity and dilutes what the model can resolve. Removing it could IMPROVE realised CPL,
not just leave it unchanged. fps-490 measures information content (shuffle in place, capacity
held constant); this asks the different question of whether the CAPACITY itself is a cost.

For any block whose shuffled-vs-intact delta is inside the noise band, run a genuine
**drop** arm (fewer columns, retrain) and compare against the intact baseline. A
significantly NEGATIVE delta_cpl_held means the block is actively harmful and should be
un-locked.

Cautions from prior work:
- `bd recall` / memory `project_shap_redundancy_regime_caveat`: a clean redundancy drop was
  REGIME-SENSITIVE across 4 years — check per-regime, not just the aggregate.
- `feedback_regime_segmented_evaluation`: report median delta + named regressions.
- Un-locking changes `LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS`, which is the declared baseline
  (`feedback_baseline_declared_not_discovered`) — it invalidates the noise floors and every
  candidate dossier measured against it. Treat as a deliberate re-baseline at a batch
  boundary (before batch2 starts), never mid-batch.

## Related

- fps-490 (blocker — the measurement)
- fps-nas — widen the realised arbiter's replay universe (screen on the full network, price
  on the preferred 5). `run_paired_realised_backtest` already takes `station_codes`, so this
  is a one-argument change, and it is the LARGER power lever of the two.
- fps-3jj.19 — batch2; this must be settled before batch2 grades anything.
- fps-q09 — batch-internal redundancy check (owner deprioritised 2026-09-05: SHAP covers it
  at the only point it matters, and nothing graduated).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Written verdict on alpha for batch2, with the locked-block evidence for it
- [ ] Per-block classification: clears / inside band / candidate for removal
- [ ] For any removal candidate, a drop-arm result with per-regime breakdown
- [ ] If any block is un-locked, a stated re-baseline plan (noise floors + 6 dossiers)
- [ ] docs/STATUS.md updated if the screen bar or the locked set changes
title: Act on the locked-block ablation: set the screen bar, and test whether removing a block helps

description:
## What

Run a leave-one-block-out ablation over `LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS` (54 cols) and express
each block's contribution as `delta_cpl_held` against `experiments/batches/batch1/noise_floor.json`,
so locked features can be read on the SAME ruler new candidates are screened against.

## Why now

Batch1's grading is being redesigned (see the sibling issue): drop the batch-level
Bonferroni correction, screen each candidate independently against the noise floor at
alpha ~= 0.10 (bar 1.451 band-sd = 0.145 c/L @ 1d). Before applying that bar to batch2,
check the existing locked set clears it. **If locked features can't clear the bar, the bar
is wrong** (or the locked set carries dead weight — see sibling).

## The gap this closes

The locked set was graduated on **log-loss / hard25**. The bar is in **realised c/L vs the
noise floor**. Different currencies — no committed artifact answers this. Checked
`experiments/INDEX.md` (2026-06-04, 2026-06-05, 2026-06-07 ablations) and
`fuel_signal/loo_ablation.py`: all log-loss. Needs new runs.

## Method — shuffle in place, do NOT drop columns

`run_paired_realised_backtest` takes ONE shared `feature_columns` list across arms
(experiments/lib/realised.py:322), so arms cannot have different column sets. Dropping is
not expressible; it is also the wrong measurement.

Instead overwrite the block's columns with block-shuffled values, the way
`experiments/pipeline/placebo.py` builds a placebo column. Two advantages:
- column count and model capacity stay identical, so only INFORMATION is destroyed
- arity matches the noise band's construction (the band is 3 placebo columns; comparing a
  35-column DROP against it would not be like-for-like — fps-3jj.14's arity concern)

## Blocks (7)

| block | cols |
|---|---|
| `days_since_trough_entry_*` | 35 |
| `cycle_*` (pct_through, days_since_peak, mean_length, last_min_cents, last_max_cents, peak_count) | 6 |
| station price position (station_price_cents, station_minus_last_min_cents, station_minus_last_max_cents, station_minus_sydney_avg_cents) | 4 |
| dispersion (network_px_std, network_px_std_delta_3d, lga_phase_std, lga_phase_std_delta_3d) | 4 |
| LGA reference (lga_mean_cents, station_minus_lga_mean_cents) | 2 |
| brand reference (brand_mean_cents, station_minus_brand_mean_cents) | 2 |
| stickiness_score | 1 |

Blocks are the right unit: you would never add one LGA column without the other 34, and
dropping one of 35 measures nothing because the rest carry the signal.

## Cost

7 paired runs at ~14 min each (batch1's noise floor: 8368s / 10 draws) = ~1.5-2h, less
with `baseline_cache`.

## Files likely affected

- new `experiments/<date>_locked_block_ablation/` (lab-book entry, experiments/** exempt from PR)
- reuse `experiments/lib/realised.py`, `experiments/pipeline/placebo.py` shuffling helper

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Script under experiments/, using experiments/lib scaffolding (not inline scaffolding)
- [ ] Each block reported as delta_cpl_held + noise_band_z + tank_params stamp (fps-15c)
- [ ] Cadence stamped on every CPL; run at 1d to match the batch1 floor
- [ ] Results table in the experiment README + experiments/INDEX.md row
- [ ] Explicit statement of which blocks clear 1.451 (alpha=0.10) and which clear 1.923 (alpha=0.05)
title: Measure each locked feature block against the noise floor in realised CPL

close_reason: Deprioritised 2026-09-05 in the batch1 retrospective review: SHAP redundancy analysis covers candidate-to-candidate overlap at the only point it matters (graduation), and nothing graduated from batch1. Also measured: even collapsing all 5 batch1 candidates to 2 independent ideas leaves the best (z=2.3295) below the N=2 bar of 2.3726 — redundancy could not have changed the batch verdict.
description:
## What

Redundancy in `facts.json` is measured one way only: a candidate's columns against the
54-column LOCK (`redundancy.block_r2` / `per_column_r2` / `predictors_dropped`). Nothing
measures candidate-to-candidate redundancy WITHIN a batch. Add that check, and have it run
before a batch is graded.

## Why I noticed this

batch1's retrospective (`experiments/batches/batch1/RETROSPECTIVE.md`, § Mechanism-family
concentration) found five candidates declaring five distinct `mechanism_family` labels —
full diversity on its face. Two of them, `directional-network-breadth`
(`network_move_breadth`) and `lead-lag-propagation` (`lga_trough_propagation`), are both
cross-sectional consensus statistics over the same station network, differing mainly in
whether the consensus is read as a contemporaneous breadth count or a propagation ordering.

They are also **the only two candidates in the batch that landed `zone_resolved: true`** —
weak evidence they are reading the same underlying structure. The retrospective states
plainly that no instrument can settle it, and files it as `not_tested` / "not testable with
what is built".

This matters more at batch2's planned 10-15 candidates than it did at 5: the chance of two
labels naming one mechanism goes up, not down, and the family label is the only diversity
control the generator currently has. The retrospective's own actionable form of the finding
is "the generator's own family labels are not a sufficient diversity control".

## Design questions to settle (this is the `design` part)

- **What is compared.** Column-to-column |rho| across candidates, or a block R^2 of one
  candidate's columns against another's? The lock-side check already uses block R^2 with a
  0.9 advisory `BLOCK_R2_FLAG`; note the retrospective's caveat that a block figure is the
  MEAN of its members and dilutes a single redundant column by design.
- **Where it runs.** Batch-level, after all candidates are graded (a new artifact beside
  `retrospective_facts.json`), or at freeze/generation time as a gate on what gets filed?
  The existing hard |rho| >= 0.85 gate in the generator IS cross-candidate but runs at
  generation time on declared columns — check whether that gate already covers part of this
  before building anything (`docs/routines/generator.md` § Redundancy).
- **Advisory or blocking.** The lock-side `BLOCK_R2_FLAG` is advisory. A batch-internal one
  probably should be too, at least for batch2 — the point is to make "two labels, one
  mechanism" visible in the retrospective, not to reject candidates automatically.
- **Whether it is retro-computable for batch1.** If yes, running it on batch1 answers the
  open `not_tested` line directly and gives batch2 a calibration point. Note
  `features.parquet` for the batch IS committed-adjacent (`experiments/batches/batch1/`),
  but the per-run parquets are gitignored — see `feedback_verify_artifact_vintage_before_recomputing`.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/pipeline/redundancy.py` (existing lock-side check + `BATCH_RECORD_JSON`)
- `experiments/pipeline/retrospective.py` (if it lands as a retrospective-time artifact)
- `docs/routines/generator.md`, `docs/routines/retrospective.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded on the four design questions above, with the generator's existing
      cross-candidate |rho| gate checked FIRST so this doesn't duplicate it.
- [ ] Candidate-to-candidate redundancy is measurable for a batch, and lands in a committed
      artifact rather than being computed in-session.
- [ ] Run on batch1 if retro-computable, and the `network_move_breadth` /
      `lga_trough_propagation` question answered or explicitly re-filed as unanswerable.
- [ ] `RETROSPECTIVE.md`'s `not_tested` line ("not testable with what is built") updated or
      retired once it is built.
- [ ] Lands before batch2 grades anything.
title: Batch-internal redundancy check: candidate columns against each other, not just the lock

close_reason: Refreshed all five batch1 candidate READMEs to post-#359 facts.json (87a1e40, direct to main under the experiments/** exemption). No Judgement conclusion changed, so no re-grade: the retrospective's signature-grade table (1 matched / 2 inconclusive / 2 contradicted) and its decoupling finding stand. Verified mechanically — 0 mismatches across every headline/zone/per-fold/flip/regret/noise/provenance figure vs facts.json, and the retrospective's own figure-verification pass re-run against the refreshed dossiers (63 assertions, 0 failures). Notable: dark_fill_days went 102/77/64/60/56 -> 0 and provider misses 607 -> 278 (both the fps-2i4/#356 fix seen from two sides), which broke the 6300 = 5x14x90 arithmetic in the shared coverage addendum; only folds 4-7 moved in any candidate. Two single-fold-dependency caveats weakened with figures restated (tgp fold-3 share 95% -> 64%, no longer a sign flip; nmb 69% -> 48%) and one clause of nmb's fps-rlh grading explanation corrected to match. Parquet-derived figures labelled pre-#359 per the AC — fills.parquet is gitignored and the on-disk copy provably predates the regen.
description:
## What

All 5 `experiments/candidates/batch1/*/README.md` quote realised CPL / zone / flip
figures produced BEFORE PR #359's regeneration, while the `facts.json` beside them
(and now their `grading.explanation`, backfilled under fps-rlh in cd3de8f) carry the
post-regen values. The two disagree inside the same directory.

This is a numbers refresh, NOT a re-grading pass. The regen moved every batch1 effect
by less than 0.008 c/L and flipped no verdict, so the ## Judgement conclusions stand
as written — only the figures cited in them are stale.

## Why I noticed this

Doing fps-rlh's backfill 2026-09-03. I deliberately wrote each grading.explanation
from the CURRENT facts.json rather than transcribing the README's numbers, precisely
so facts.json would be internally consistent. That left the READMEs as the stale
side, and made the disagreement explicit rather than hidden.

Known examples (not exhaustive):
- station_descent_dynamics: README cites 439 decision flips; facts.json now has 337.
- tgp_cycle_displacement: README cites shock-zone -0.29 c/L; facts.json now -0.3079.
- Per-fold exclusion figures (e.g. "excluding fold 3 takes the shock-zone delta to
  +0.005") were computed pre-regen and were NOT re-derived by the regen. These need
  either recomputation or an explicit "pre-regen" label -- do not silently update the
  aggregate around them and leave the exclusion figure implying it was recomputed.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/candidates/batch1/{lga_trough_propagation,network_move_breadth,
  station_descent_dynamics,stickiness_phase_saddle,tgp_cycle_displacement}/README.md

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every CPL/flip/zone figure in each README matches the committed facts.json
- [ ] Every figure keeps its cadence stamp (50/3.571/1d/10%) per fps-15c
- [ ] Judgement conclusions unchanged -- if a conclusion appears to need changing,
      STOP and raise it; that is a re-grade, not this task
- [ ] Any figure that cannot be recomputed from committed artifacts (per-fold
      exclusions) is labelled as pre-#359 rather than silently left as current
notes:
## This bead now gates a citation, not just tidiness (2026-09-03)

batch1's RETROSPECTIVE.md (8ba2534) was written and committed BEFORE this refresh.
That was a sequencing mistake on my part: I had argued in fps-rlh's own note that
the README refresh and the grading backfill were "the same pass over the same 5
directories and should be done with it, not separately", then did only the
backfill. Writing the explanations from the current facts.json (correct in
isolation) is what left the READMEs as the stale side.

**What is NOT at risk:** the retrospective's arithmetic. All 36 distinct numbers in
it were traced to retrospective_facts.json or the post-#359 facts.json and verified
programmatically before commit. Exactly one README-sourced figure appears (the
tgp_cycle_displacement shock-zone -0.29) and it is explicitly labelled pre-regen.

**What IS at risk, and the one thing to watch while doing this bead:** the
retrospective's signature-grade table (1 matched / 2 inconclusive / 2 contradicted)
and the "economic rank and signature accuracy are decoupled" finding built on it.
Those rest on each candidate's Judgement CONCLUSION, not on its figures. PR #359
measured every batch1 effect as moving < 0.008 c/L with no verdict flip, so no
conclusion is expected to move -- but that was measured at the aggregate, not
per-README-claim.

So this bead's existing AC ("if a conclusion appears to need changing, STOP and
raise it") is now load-bearing. Concretely:

- If NO conclusion changes: re-run the figure-verification pass over
  RETROSPECTIVE.md against the refreshed dossiers, confirm it still passes, and the
  batch is internally consistent end to end. Nothing else to do.
- If ANY conclusion changes: the signature-grade table, the decoupling finding, and
  fps-3jj.18.2's bucketing all need revisiting BEFORE the retrospective is cited.

A provenance caveat naming this bead was added to RETROSPECTIVE.md itself (85869c7)
so a reader hits it before following a citation into a stale README.

description:
## What

Every nightly dossier scan (`docs/routines/dossier.md` Step 0,
`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py --scan`) flags `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d`
as pending, because its `results.json` and `README.md` share an exact mtime
(2026-08-23 14:37:24) and `find_pending_runs`'s documented tie-break treats ties as
pending (see the function's own docstring, "Ties ... are treated as PENDING, not
dossiered: re-dossiering a run that was actually already written up is a harmless
no-op"). That claim of harmlessness doesn't hold for this run.

Regenerating `facts.json` under the current schema:
- resets `grading` to `{"verdict": null, "explanation": null, "pending": true}`,
  wiping the human-authored "matched" verdict
- sets `noise_band.available: false` with reason "noise_floor.json's null_method
  (None) is not 'placebo_column'" — because `experiments/batches/batch0/noise_floor.json`
  predates the fps-awz placebo-column rework: it's the old paired-seed format
  (`deltas_cpl_held` / `seeds_a` / `seeds_b`, computed 2026-08-19, fps-3jj.9 / PR #311),
  with no `null_method` key at all, not an incompatible or missing floor
- the underlying `results.json` is byte-identical (confirmed: headline
  `delta_cpl_held` 0.005851407340855985 matches the committed facts.json and the
  existing README/ledger entry to every digit) — this is NOT a genuine re-run, just
  a schema-format read failure

The existing `README.md` and the `experiments/ledger.yaml` entry for `tgp_delta_7d`
(outcome: inconclusive) both rest their central argument on the noise-band result
(candidate sits at the 40th percentile of pure fit noise, z=+0.14) — real, valid
data that's still sitting in `noise_floor.json`, just under field names the current
`_noise_band()` check doesn't recognize. Mechanically following the dossier routine
here would silently replace a well-evidenced, already-reviewed document with a
strictly worse one (noise-band evidence gone, verdict reset to pending) — not because
anything new was learned, but because of a schema gap. I reverted the working-tree
regeneration this run (`git checkout --` on facts.json + 2 PNGs) rather than
overwrite the README, but the scan will flag this same directory again every night
until the root cause is fixed.

## Why I noticed this

Running the scheduled dossier routine (`docs/routines/dossier.md`) 2026-09-03.
Step 0's scan only found one "pending" run — this false positive — no genuine new
candidate runs were pending this cycle.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_noise_band`, `find_pending_runs`)
- experiments/batches/batch0/noise_floor.json (legacy format, read-only reference)
- experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/facts.json (currently reverted to committed state)

## Possible fixes (pick one, not prescriptive)

- Teach `_noise_band()` to also read the legacy paired-seed format
  (`deltas_cpl_held`/`seeds_a`/`seeds_b`, no `null_method` key) as a fallback when
  `null_method` is absent, computing mean/std from `deltas_cpl_held` directly.
- Or: have `find_pending_runs` treat a committed `facts.json` with `grading.pending
  == false` as strong evidence the run was already judged, and require README.md to
  be strictly older (not just tied) before re-flagging it as pending — i.e. narrow
  the tie-break so it doesn't refire indefinitely on a directory whose content
  genuinely hasn't changed.
- Or: backfill/migrate batch0's `noise_floor.json` to the current schema (adding
  `null_method: "placebo_column"` plus a `draws` list, if the paired-seed method is
  considered equivalent) so future scans read it natively.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Nightly dossier scan no longer flags `batch0/tgp_delta_7d` as pending when
      nothing has actually changed
- [ ] batch0's noise-floor evidence (40th percentile, z=+0.14) remains readable by
      `dossier_tables.py`, or the gap is at least made visible without destroying
      already-committed grading/noise-band data
notes:
CLOSED moot 2026-09-03. This issue is scoped entirely to
experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d, and the owner has tapped out on

- The nightly dossier Routine that produced the false positive is DISABLED

The half that OUTLIVES batch0 is the generic one, and it is already tracked as

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py:158` `check_freeze_cadence(batch_dir, tank)` refuses
to write an artifact at a cadence the batch's `freeze.json` does not declare (fps-oqz).
It is called from the noise-floor writers only (`noise_floor.py:321`, `:619`).

`experiments/pipeline/runner.py` — the candidate path — never calls it. It resolves the
tank from the current `TankParams()` default (1d since the #323 re-lock) with no reference
to the batch's declared cadence, so running a candidate against a 7d-frozen batch silently
produces 1d numbers stamped into `results.json` beside a `freeze.json` still declaring 7d.

## Why I noticed this

Hit for real during fps-32h's regen (2026-09-02): `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d`
was re-run against `experiments/batches/batch0` (declared `50/3.571/7d/10%`) and came out
stamped `50/3.571/1d/10%`, flipping its headline from `effect_resolved: false`
(delta +0.0059 c/L) to `true` (delta -0.2003 c/L) — entirely the cadence change, not the
fix under test. batch0's `noise_floor.json` is stamped 7d, so the candidate was graded
against a floor from a different cadence; it only failed to bite because that floor's
`null_method` is too old to grade against for an unrelated reason.

`check_freeze_cadence`'s own docstring names this outcome ("split-brained: `freeze.json`
still declaring 7d beside a `noise_floor.json` stamped 1d, with no reader to notice") and
`tests/test_noise_floor.py:335` already asserts batch0-at-`TankParams()` raises. The guard
and its test exist; the runner just isn't behind them.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/runner.py (call the guard before the run, not after)
- experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py (check_freeze_cadence may want to move to a shared
  module rather than being imported from the noise-floor one)
- tests/ (a runner-level test mirroring test_noise_floor.py:331-335)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Running a candidate against a batch whose `freeze.json` declares a cadence different
      from the resolved tank raises, with the existing guard's message
- [ ] A deliberate run at the batch's own declared cadence still works (explicit tank passed)
- [ ] Batches with no `tank_params` stamp in `freeze.json` stay silent (pre-fps-15c manifests)
- [ ] Test added at the runner level, not just the noise-floor level
notes:
2026-09-03: re-justified, priority unchanged, but the REASON changed.

This issue's description says doing it first "would make [fps-m9s's] re-run safe
by construction". fps-m9s is now closed not-doing (batch0 abandoned), so that
motivation is gone. Two things replace it:

1. It is the ENABLER, not merely a safety net. Checked against the code: there
   is currently NO way to pin a candidate run's cadence at all. runner.py
   contains no TankParams reference and no argparse tank option; the cadence
   falls out of experiments/lib/realised.py:333 `tank: TankParams | None = None`
   defaulting to TankParams() (evaluation_interval_days = 1). No flag, no env
   var. fps-m9s's instruction to "pass the tank explicitly" was not actually
   performable for the candidate path.
2. batch2 is where this now bites. fps-cde will run tgp_delta_7d and
   tgp_cycle_displacement as batch2 candidates. Without this guard, a batch2
   candidate run against a freeze declaring one cadence silently stamps
   whatever TankParams() happens to default to that week -- the exact
   split-brain check_freeze_cadence's docstring names, and the exact way batch0's
   headline flipped effect_resolved false -> true during fps-32h's regen.

So: land this before batch2's candidates run, not before any batch0 work.

description:
## What

The `StationPriceSource` Protocol (experiments/lib/flips.py) exposes only
`price_at` and `is_observed`. Neither tells a caller whether a given
`as_of` date falls inside a station's known observation span (a mid-series
gap, e.g. an outage) versus genuinely before/after any observation ever
recorded for that station. `summarise_regret`'s `not reachable` branch
relies on being able to tell these apart, but structurally cannot — both
present identically (every nearby `price_at` call returns None).

This was surfaced by fps-i8x, which described one concrete way the gap
bites: scoring a pre-fps-2i4 flips ledger (built before the price-lookup
gap-cap landed) against the post-fix price source. fps-i8x is now closed
because fps-32h's full regeneration of batch0/batch1 eliminates every
ledger that could trigger that specific scenario — there's no pre-fix
ledger left in the repo to re-score. But the Protocol-level ambiguity
itself was never fixed in code, only sidestepped by removing the bad input.
It will resurface the next time some other price-semantics change makes an
old ledger's assumptions stale and someone re-dossiers it without
regenerating first (dossier_tables.py is explicitly designed to allow
exactly that kind of cheap re-scoring).

## Why I noticed this

fps-i8x's own notes record the fix a PR-356 reviewer proposed and the
issue's author endorsed as strongest: add `first_observed(station_code) ->
str | None` to the Protocol — one line off `self._dates[code][0]` in each
implementation. That fix was never applied; only the symptom (stale
pre-2026-09-01 ledgers) was eliminated.

## What to do

1. Add `first_observed(station_code: str) -> str | None` to the
   `StationPriceSource` Protocol in experiments/lib/flips.py, with a
   docstring explaining what it's for (letting callers distinguish
   "before this station's series starts" from "mid-series gap").
2. Implement it in `_DbStationPrices` (experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py)
   and every test double in tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py /
   tests/test_dossier_tables.py.
3. Update `summarise_regret`'s `not reachable` branch to use it: only treat
   a flip as "genuinely out of range" (current drop behaviour) when
   `as_of` is before `first_observed`; otherwise it's a mid-series gap and
   should be scored some other way (paid-price fallback, or whatever the
   design decision lands on — this issue is about giving the tool the
   information, the scoring policy itself may need a separate decision).
4. Keep tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py::test_summarise_regret_reports_per_fold_unscored_so_decision_counts_reconcile
   (PR #348 finding 6) passing — it pins the genuinely-out-of-range case
   this issue must not break.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/lib/flips.py (StationPriceSource Protocol, summarise_regret)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (_DbStationPrices)
- tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py, tests/test_dossier_tables.py

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `first_observed` added to the Protocol and both implementations
- [ ] summarise_regret distinguishes mid-series-gap from out-of-range using it
- [ ] existing pinned out-of-range test still passes
- [ ] new test covers a mid-series-gap flip and confirms it's no longer
      silently dropped
title: StationPriceSource can't distinguish mid-series gap from out-of-range

Part 2 (batch0's noise_floor.json predates fps-awz's placebo_column method, so tgp_delta_7d can no longer be graded against any floor) is the only non-duplicate content and is re-filed as fps-sjk with a decide-recompute-or-grandfather framing.
description:
## What

Tonight's dossier routine (2026-09-02 05:xx) ran `dossier_tables --scan experiments/candidates`
per docs/routines/dossier.md Step 0. It reprocessed `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d`
(results.json and README.md have identical mtimes to the second — the documented "tie" case in
`find_pending_runs`'s docstring, treated as pending). The regenerated `facts.json` differed
from the committed one in two substantive ways, not just schema noise:

1. **`grading` was reset to `{"verdict": null, "explanation": null, "pending": true}`.**
   `build_facts()` (experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py:332-337) unconditionally rebuilds the
   `grading` block from scratch on every call — it never reads or preserves an existing
   facts.json's grading. `find_pending_runs`'s docstring claims regenerating on a tie is a
   "harmless no-op ... facts.json is deterministic from the same run artifacts" — that's false
   for `grading`, which is Step 1's session judgement, not derived from results.json/rowpreds/fills.
   Any run that already has a README (i.e. already graded) but happens to hit a tie will have its
   recorded verdict silently wiped in facts.json the next time this scan runs. I did not commit
   this — I reverted the working-tree change (`git checkout --` on facts.json + the 2 PNGs
   dossier_tables also touched) rather than let a regression land, since dossier.md's Step 1 only
   covers runs with a fresh facts.json AND no README.md yet — tgp_delta_7d has a README, so it was
   out of scope for me to re-grade it, but the regenerated facts.json was already dirty on disk.

2. **`noise_band.available` flipped from `true` to `false`**: the regenerated reason is
   "noise_floor.json's null_method (None) is not 'placebo_column' — this floor predates the
   fps-awz placebo-column rework (or was computed some other way) and does not grade this run."
   fps-awz (closed 2026-08-21) reworked the noise-floor null "before batch 1" and, per its own
   scope, never touched batch0's existing noise_floor.json. The currently-committed facts.json /
   README / ledger.yaml entry for tgp_delta_7d records `verdict: "matched"` with an explanation
   that explicitly cites the now-invalid noise band ("z=+0.14 vs a band of mean -0.0135, std
   0.142 c/L") as part of the reasoning ("confirming it as inert"). Under current
   dossier_tables.py, that same run can no longer be graded against any noise floor at all.

   Also newly null in the regenerated facts.json: `per_fold[].regime` (all folds) — this is
   *correct*, not a bug: tgp_delta_7d's results.json predates fps-3tu's empirical shock-fold set
   (`meta.shock_folds` is None), so current code rightly reports "shock fold unknown — legacy
   run" instead of the old fixed-index-derived shock/normal tags the committed facts.json carries
   from before that fix. Flagging it here only because it compounds the case for (2): this run's
   already-written dossier increasingly reflects pre-fps-3tu/pre-fps-awz methodology that current
   tooling itself no longer endorses.

## Why I noticed this

Running the nightly dossier routine (docs/routines/dossier.md) and diffing what Step 0 changed
before deciding whether anything fell under Step 1.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`build_facts`, `find_pending_runs`) — the grading-clobber
  gap; a regeneration that finds an existing facts.json with `grading.pending == false` should
  probably preserve it (or `find_pending_runs`/`process_run` should refuse to touch a run that
  already has a README, closing the "tie" loophole that currently invites this).
- experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{facts.json,README.md} — the specific run whose
  grading now rests on a noise band current code has invalidated.
- experiments/candidates/batch0/noise_floor.json (or wherever batch0's is rooted) — never
  recomputed under fps-awz's placebo_column method; not clear if that's an intentional "batch0 is
  grandfathered" decision or a gap.
- experiments/ledger.yaml's tgp_delta_7d entry, currently graduated — worth reviewing whether the
  graduation reasoning still holds once the noise-band citation it leans on is known-stale.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide whether `dossier_tables.py` should preserve an existing `grading` block on
      regeneration (or otherwise stop clobbering it on a tie), and implement it
- [ ] Decide whether batch0's noise_floor.json should be recomputed under the placebo_column
      method (`experiments.pipeline.noise_floor <batch> --force`) so tgp_delta_7d (and any other
      batch0 candidate) can be re-graded on equal footing with batch1+
- [ ] If recomputed and the verdict changes, update tgp_delta_7d's README/facts.json/ledger.yaml
      entry accordingly (it's currently `graduated` in the ledger — a re-grade could matter for
      that status)
title: dossier_tables regen clobbers recorded grading + batch0 noise floor now unavailable under placebo_column method

description:
## What
`experiments/lib/flips.py::summarise_regret` walks a `flips` ledger (fill
records from a completed backtest run) and scores each fill's timing regret by
looking up nearby prices via a `StationPriceSource.price_at` accessor. Since
fps-2i4, `price_at`'s production implementation (`_DbStationPrices` in
`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py`, and the semantics
`PriceHistory.station_price_at` defines) is gap-capped: a station dark for
more than `MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS` resolves to `None` rather than forward-filling.

This creates a real correctness gap when `summarise_regret` is called with a
`flips` ledger produced by a simulator run BEFORE fps-2i4 landed, scored
against a `prices` source built AFTER it (exactly what re-running the dossier
tooling over an old batch's committed `fills.parquet` does — see
`dossier_tables.py`'s own docstring: it's explicitly designed to be
re-runnable against existing artifacts without re-running the backtest).

For a flip dated inside what the OLD (pre-fix) simulator transacted through
during a closure, EVERY offset the regret walk checks — including offset 0,
the fill's own recorded date — now resolves to `None`. `reachable` comes back
empty, and the flip is silently dropped via the `if not reachable: regrets.
append(None)` branch (see flips.py's own docstring/comments, updated in
fps-2i4's PR #356 to describe this without fixing it). This happens
ASYMMETRICALLY across arms (fps-6yi's own historical numbers: 42 candidate vs
14 baseline dark-day flips would be affected), reintroducing the exact
disjoint-basket defect `summarise_regret`'s docstring says must never happen.

## Why a naive fix doesn't work (already tried and reverted in PR #356)
Seeding `reachable` with the ledger's own `paid` price (ground truth for what
was actually transacted, independent of what the CURRENT price accessor says)
fixes this case — but it also silently defeats the ORIGINAL, deliberately
pinned purpose of the `not reachable` branch: catching a fill dated entirely
outside a station's known series (before its first-ever observation, or a
genuinely corrupted ledger row) — see
`tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py::test_summarise_regret_reports_per_fold_unscored_so_decision_counts_reconcile`
(added for PR #348 review finding 6), which the naive fix breaks.

The two scenarios present IDENTICALLY to `summarise_regret` given only the
`StationPriceSource` Protocol's current two methods (`price_at`, `is_observed`)
— neither exposes whether `as_of` falls between the station's actual first and
last-ever observations, which is the actual distinguishing fact.

## What to do
Pick one:
1. Extend `StationPriceSource` with a method exposing the station's known
   observation-date bounds (or an `is_within_series(station_code, as_of) ->
   bool`), so `summarise_regret` can tell "inside a mid-series gap" (score
   using `paid`) from "genuinely out of range" (drop, as today) apart. Update
   both implementations (`_DbStationPrices`, and every test double) plus the
   Protocol docstring.
2. Add an explicit provenance/version check so `_attach_regret`/
   `summarise_regret` refuses (or warns loudly) when scoring a `flips` ledger
   that predates fps-2i4 against a post-fix `prices` source, forcing a
   regenerate-the-ledger step instead of a silent under-count.
3. Accept the current documented-but-unfixed state (the PR #356 docstring/
   comment updates) as sufficient IF no batch predating fps-2i4 (2026-09-01)
   is ever re-dossiered without first regenerating its fills.parquet — in
   which case this issue is really "make that regeneration a hard requirement
   in the batch-pipeline docs," not a code fix.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/lib/flips.py (StationPriceSource Protocol, summarise_regret)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (_DbStationPrices)
- tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py, tests/test_dossier_tables.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision recorded: extend the Protocol, add a provenance guard, or
      document a hard "regenerate first" rule — not left ambiguous
- [ ] If code changes: existing pinned tests (PR #348 finding 6's unscored
      test) still pass, AND a new test covers the fps-2i4 stale-ledger case
      without dropping asymmetrically
- [ ] docs/routines/dossier.md (or wherever batch re-run steps live) updated
      if the decision is "regenerate before re-scoring"
notes:
Fourth option, proposed by PR #356's reviewer (pr-356-code-review-fcf0e4-2c),
which I think is stronger than options 1-3 above and is my recommendation if
someone picks this up:

Add `first_observed(station_code) -> str | None` to the StationPriceSource
Protocol (one line off `self._dates[code][0]` in every implementation).
`summarise_regret` then distinguishes the two `not reachable` cases cleanly:
- `first_observed` is None, or > the flip's date: genuinely before/outside the
  station's known series (or a corrupted ledger row) — keep today's behavior,
  score nothing for that row (regrets.append(None)).
- `first_observed` <= the flip's date: the station HAS real history behind
  this fill, so `reachable` only came back empty because of fps-2i4's gap cap
  scoring a pre-fps-2i4 ledger. Don't silently score it (seeding with `paid`
  is "the original bug wearing a different hat" per the reviewer) — REFUSE
  the whole table instead, returning the same `{"computed": False, "reason":
  ...}` shape `_attach_regret` already uses for a missing frozen DB / empty
  flips (dossier_tables.py:478-495). Turns "please regenerate the ledger
  first" from a docstring warning (only protects a reader who reads it) into
  something the code enforces.

Implementation note if taken: summarise_regret doesn't currently have a
computed/reason return convention (only its caller _attach_regret does) — the
cleanest fit is probably a dedicated exception (mirroring
experiments/lib/realised.py's BaselineCacheMismatch: "config/data doesn't
match, don't silently proceed") that summarise_regret raises and
_attach_regret catches and translates into computed: False, rather than
summarise_regret's return shape varying conditionally.

Left as a follow-up rather than implemented directly in PR #356 (already a
large fix commit for a bug-fix PR; this is an independent, well-scoped design
decision that deserves its own focused PR + review).
title: summarise_regret cannot distinguish a stale pre-fps-2i4 ledger from a broken one

description:
## What

The nightly dossier routine (docs/routines/dossier.md Step 0) ran
`PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.dossier_tables --scan experiments/candidates`
on 2026-09-01 and it flagged `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d` as pending and
regenerated its `facts.json` + two PNGs — even though this run already has a written-up
`README.md` and a ledger entry with outcome `graduated` (tgp_delta_7d's calibration run,
dossiered 2026-08-23, commit cb7d1110).

`find_pending_runs`'s own docstring (experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py:240-244) explains
why: "Ties (equal mtimes ...) are treated as PENDING, not dossiered ... re-dossiering a run that
was actually already written up is a harmless no-op (facts.json is deterministic from the same
run artifacts)." That assumption is false in this case. Both `results.json` and `README.md` had
identical mtimes (2026-08-23 14:37:24 — both last touched by the same commit, most likely via a
`git checkout`/pull-style operation that stamps every file in a commit with the same wall-clock
mtime), so the tie branch fired.

Regenerating was NOT a harmless no-op:
- `grading.verdict` flipped from `"matched"` (with a full explanation) to `null`, `pending: true`
  — the dossier session's one recorded judgement, wiped.
- `noise_band` flipped from `available: true` (mean -0.0135, std 0.142, z=+0.14, 40th percentile)
  to `available: false` — this batch's `noise_floor.json` is apparently gitignored/ephemeral and
  no longer present on disk, so re-running the deterministic pass today can't reproduce a figure
  it already reproduced once and wrote to git.
- Every `per_fold[].regime` flipped from a real value (`"shock"`/`"normal"`) to `null`, and
  `tau_diverges` similarly nulled — schema/data the current environment can no longer supply for
  this historical run.

Had this been fed into Step 1 of the routine unchecked, it would have downgraded an already
human-reviewed, graduated ledger entry based on nothing but a spurious mtime tie plus environment
drift (missing ephemeral noise_floor.json) — not a real re-run of the candidate. I reverted the
regenerated `facts.json`/PNGs (`git checkout --`) rather than writing a new README/ledger entry,
so no bad data landed. `git status`/`git log origin/main..main` were both empty before and after.

## Why I noticed this

Running the scheduled dossier routine (docs/routines/dossier.md) as an interactive/automated
session; `--scan` reported exactly one "pending" run and it turned out to be this false positive,
not real queued work.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (find_pending_runs, ~line 215-280)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] find_pending_runs no longer treats an mtime tie on an already-dossiered run (existing
      non-empty README.md, or some other explicit marker) as pending purely because
      `results.json` and `README.md` mtimes are equal — e.g. only tie-break toward "pending" when
      there's a real content signal (results.json content/hash differs from what facts.json was
      built from), or require README.md's mtime to be strictly older, not "not newer".
- [ ] A regenerated facts.json for a run whose ledger outcome is already `graduated` (or any
      outcome) should not silently discard previously-recorded fields it can no longer reproduce
      (grading.verdict, noise_band, per-fold regime) — either preserve them when a re-run can't
      supply a replacement, or refuse to overwrite and flag loudly instead.
- [ ] Regression test: two files with identical mtimes, one already dossiered (has README +
      ledger entry), should not be re-emitted by find_pending_runs.
title: find_pending_runs mtime-tie rule reprocesses already-graduated runs, silently regressing facts.json

description:
## The question

This project has two goals — the owner's own CPL across five commute stations, and
general usefulness across Sydney. They currently look like they are at cross purposes.
This bead is to establish whether they actually ARE, because nothing in the pipeline
computes both sides.

## What is true today

The model is shared. It trains on all 714 stations regardless of goal
(`realised.py`: `train_df = a.df.loc[p.train_index]`; only the REPLAY is restricted).
So there is no conflict in the model — only in the evaluation.

The whole arbiter side is five stations:

- `station_codes` threads through the batch pipeline as `None`, and `realised.py:377`
  resolves it to `PREFERRED_STATIONS`. Verified empirically: `fills.parquet` for
  batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement holds exactly 5 distinct station codes over 10,809 fills.
- `noise_floor.py` passes `station_codes` the same way, so the NOISE BAND every
  candidate is graded against is also five stations.

Scale of the resulting instrument: 88-219 fills per fold, collapsing to **92 independent
decisions** for the whole run. Against that, no feature in `results.csv` history has ever
delivered 0.5 c/L on its own.

## Why widening is cheap

Per fold per arm, cost is dominated by work that does NOT scale with station count:
`_train_calibrate_select_tau` fits a full LGBM on the whole fold-train (all 714
stations) and then runs a walk-forward OOF loop — several more fits — to fit the
isotonic calibrator. Only `load_history` and the `aggregate_backtest` tank walk scale
with the station list, and that is per-station-day arithmetic plus one `predict_proba`
per station-day. Going 5 -> 50 -> 200 stations multiplies the cheap part only.

Costing is structural, not measured — confirm with a one-fold timing run before
committing to a universe size.

## The proposal to test

Grade candidates on realised CPL over a BROAD Sydney sample; keep five-station CPL as
the reported outcome. This keeps the statistic (path-dependent tank, forced fills, real
economics — NOT log-loss, which is already established as objective-misaligned for
decision-timing features) and changes only the population.

The assumption it buys is **homogeneity**: that a feature helping Sydney-wide helps at
the five. Current support is thin and on the wrong statistic — the per-row LOG-LOSS gain
at the five sits 0.33 SE from the network-wide figure (fps-e6i), which is not the same
as CPL homogeneity.

**Computing both CPLs IS the homogeneity test.** If they track, one arbiter serves both
goals at ~40x the resolution. If they diverge, that is a real finding about the commute
and the goals genuinely do need separating.

## Why I noticed this

fps-e6i (`experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/`) established that the
WFCV screen and the realised arbiter share 0.71% of their rows, which explains the
near-zero per-fold correlation between them. The owner then raised the two-goals
tension directly. Related but distinct: fps-4z6 proposes reporting the SCREEN restricted
to the five (aligning the screen down to the arbiter); this bead proposes the opposite
direction (widening the arbiter up), and the two are alternatives worth deciding between
together rather than separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One-fold timing run at 5 / ~50 / ~200 stations, confirming the cost is fit-dominated
- [ ] Station-sampling scheme chosen and justified (random? stratified by LGA/brand/price level?)
- [ ] Broad-population realised CPL computed for at least one batch1 candidate alongside the five-station figure
- [ ] Homogeneity read out explicitly: do the two CPL deltas agree within their own noise?
- [ ] Decision recorded on which population grades candidates, and which is merely reported
- [ ] Noise floor implications addressed — the band is currently five-station too
title: Widen the realised arbiter's replay universe and test station homogeneity
