Real defect (aggregate.py:46 differences two seed-medians instead of taking the median of the paired per-seed differences; disagrees by up to 0.0127 nats and flips sign on fold 2). But fps-e6i, filed the same session, showed the per-fold screen delta barely predicts the arbiter at all (r=-0.096 all-station), so correcting how a near-uninformative number is aggregated buys little — while changing it would move published per-fold columns for every candidate already graded. Full analysis is on main in experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/README.md (both conventions reported side by side, run.py per_fold_delta_ll(paired=...)), and 'bd recall aggregate-py-unpaired-seed-median' will surface it to anyone who touches that code or reads per-fold screen signs. Reopen if fps-nas makes the screen load-bearing again.
description:
## What

`experiments/lib/aggregate.py:46` computes

```python
fold_run[f"delta_{c}_median"] = fold_run[f"{c}_median"] - fold_run[f"{c}_median_base"]
```

i.e. `median_over_seeds(candidate_ll) - median_over_seeds(R0_ll)` — a **difference of
medians**. The seeds are paired: same data, same folds, same rows; only `random_state`
differs. The **median of the paired per-seed differences** is the better estimator
because it cancels the seed-level fluctuation both arms share. Same argument applies
to `delta_{c}_mean` (there it is algebraically identical, so only the median path is
actually affected).

## Why it matters

Measured on batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement (`fps-e6i`), the two statistics differ by up
to **0.0127 nats** per fold and **flip sign on fold 2** (paired +0.0036, published
-0.0090). That is enough to change a per-fold sign-agreement count — which is exactly
the statistic `fps-e6i` was opened to interpret, and which is cited in that bead's own
framing ("per-fold sign agreement ... is 6/14").

## Why I noticed this

Reconciling a recomputation of `delta_ll_all_median` from
`experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement/rowpreds.parquet` against the
published values in that candidate's `facts.json`. The recompute matched to 0.0 under
the unpaired convention and differed under the paired one, which located the cause.
Full table in `experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/README.md`
§ "Incidental finding".

## Scoping

Changing this changes published per-fold numbers for every candidate already graded, so
it is NOT a silent fix. Options, in order of preference:

1. Add `delta_{c}_median_paired` alongside the existing column, migrate consumers,
   retire the old one once the dossier renders the new.
2. Change in place and re-render affected dossiers.

Consumers to check before either: `experiments/TEMPLATE_paired_wfcv.py:86,240`,
`experiments/pipeline/runner.py:671`, `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py:1461,1549,1652,1660,1662`,
`experiments/2026-06-11_interaction_column/paired_wfcv.py:302`,
`experiments/2026-06-20_leading_indicators/paired_wfcv.py:68`.

Note the headline realised verdicts do NOT depend on this — the arbiter is realised CPL,
not the log-loss screen. The blast radius is the screen's per-fold columns and anything
that reads their sign.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Paired per-seed delta computed and used (or added alongside, with consumers migrated)
- [ ] Test covering the case where the two conventions disagree in sign
- [ ] Every consumer listed above audited, not just the ones grep hits first
- [ ] Note in docs/CONVENTIONS.md that paired designs aggregate the pairing, not the arms
title: Seed aggregation in aggregate.py is unpaired (difference of medians)

They are alternative answers to the same question (the 0.71% evidence overlap fps-e6i measured), not parallel tasks, and fps-nas is the one that produces new information — a restricted screen is better-aligned but LOWER-powered, so it cannot settle anything the current instrument cannot already settle, whereas fps-nas yields the station-homogeneity number that determines whether a restricted screen is worth building at all. fps-nas carries this option forward explicitly in its acceptance criteria. Reopen only if fps-nas concludes the replay universe stays at 5.
description:
## What

The WFCV log-loss screen scores every candidate over the whole station network
(798,649 rows, 714 stations). The realised arbiter replays exactly five stations
(PREFERRED_STATIONS = 261, 414, 429, 585, 18517), which is 5,693 of those rows —
**0.71%**. Nothing in the pipeline reports the screen's delta restricted to that
population, so a network-wide log-loss win is routinely read as a forecast of a
five-station CPL outcome it has no mechanical reason to predict.

Add the restricted figure alongside the network-wide one, per fold and in aggregate,
so the dossier's screen number and arbiter number are commensurable.

## Why I noticed this

`fps-e6i` (experiments/2026-08-31_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/). Measured on
batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement, with the screen's R0 probabilities verified identical
to the arbiter's cached baseline scores to float32 precision (2.98e-08), so the
comparison is exact rather than approximate:

- per-fold corr(arbiter delta_cpl_own, screen delta_ll), ALL 714 stations:
  **-0.096** (paired) / **-0.176** (the convention aggregate.py publishes — reproduces
  the figure already cited in fps-e6i exactly). Sign agreement 7/14 and 5/14.
- the same correlation with the screen restricted to the FIVE stations:
  **+0.478** / **+0.543**. Sign agreement 10/14 and 11/14.
- gap between the two correlations, fold-level bootstrap (20,000 resamples, n=14):
  **+0.574, 95% CI [+0.101, +1.033], P(gap>0) = 0.991**.

Restricting the population is the ONLY change between those rows — same model, same
folds, same seeds, same statistic.

Supporting: per-row gain at the five stations (-1.075e-02) is statistically
indistinguishable from the network-wide figure (-1.319e-02, 0.33 SE apart), so the
five stations are not special; they are just 141x smaller. Fold-clustered 2*SE at the
five stations is 1.459e-02 against a mean of -1.075e-02, i.e. **not resolvable even on
log-loss**, which is a much smoother statistic than realised CPL.

## Caveat to carry into the design

The restricted screen is better-ALIGNED but lower-POWERED. It should be reported as a
second indicator, not as a replacement for the network-wide screen, and its own noise
needs a band the way every other number here does. Do not let it become a new
graduation gate without pricing that.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/lib/aggregate.py (or a new cohort in cohort_ll_map)
- experiments/pipeline/runner.py — persist the restricted per-fold delta
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py — render it next to delta_ll_all_median
- docs/routines/dossier.md — spec the new field

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Screen delta computed and persisted for the arbiter's replay universe, per fold + aggregate
- [ ] Rendered in the dossier next to the network-wide figure, clearly labelled as the aligned-but-lower-powered indicator
- [ ] Its own noise treatment stated (not silently compared against the network-wide band)
- [ ] Backfilled for batch1's five candidates, or an explicit note on why not
title: Report the WFCV screen restricted to the arbiter's replay universe

description:
## What
`tgp_cycle_displacement` went in as two columns — `tgp_cycle_displacement_cents` and
`tgp_cycle_displacement_frac_amp` — and was graded as a block. Run each alone.

## Why I noticed this
`facts.json` for the run contains NO per-column attribution of any kind: no SHAP, no
importance, no gain, no per-column ablation. The only per-column numbers in the entire
artifact are redundancy R2 (`cents` 0.583, `frac_amp` 0.565), which measures
reconstructibility from the lock, not contribution to the result. So nothing distinguishes
"one column did the work", "both did", and "they partly cancelled".

This also lowers the arity from 2 to 1, which matters for the bar: per
`docs/CONVENTIONS.md`'s arity table, 1-2 columns and 3 columns are graded differently, and
this run was already judged against an arity-3 floor one column WIDER than itself
(`floor_arity_exceeds_run: true`, excess 1).

## Related
`fps-1l1` (SHAP importance/orientation in facts.json) remains open and would make this
kind of question answerable without paying for extra runs.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/candidates/<batch>/tgp_cycle_displacement_cents_only.py
- experiments/candidates/<batch>/tgp_cycle_displacement_frac_amp_only.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both single-column runs graded against the correct-arity floor
- [ ] Result stated as: which column carries the effect, or that neither does alone
- [ ] Same batch-size / family-wise-bar question as the tgp_delta_7d re-run resolved first
notes: GATED ON fps-nas (2026-08-31). Not a scoping change — a power problem. fps-e6i measured the arbiter's evidence base: 5 stations, 88-219 fills per fold, collapsing to 92 independent decisions for a whole run. This bead asks the arbiter to resolve the DIFFERENCE between two single-column arms whose parent pair landed at -0.2015 c/L; splitting a block that size across two runs asks for a resolution the instrument does not have. Worse, fps-2i4 (P1) found that folds 5-7 transact ~19% of their litres at station 414 at a frozen 185.9 c/L through a year-long closure, so three of the fourteen folds an ablation would be read across are contaminated in level. Running it now would most likely return two inconclusive verdicts and burn the compute without distinguishing 'one column did the work' from 'neither did' — the exact ambiguity the bead exists to remove. fps-nas decides the replay universe; fps-2i4 fixes the stale fills. Revisit the design after both, and re-check whether fps-1l1 (SHAP in facts.json) makes the question answerable with no extra runs at all.

description:
## What
`tgp_delta_7d` has never been measured at the project's canonical 1d cadence. Its status
is UNTESTED, not rejected. Run it as a **batch2 candidate** so it is graded at 1d against
a floor that actually applies to it.

## Decision 2026-08-31: batch2, not batch1, and not its own batch
Three options were priced:
- **Add to batch1** — batch1's floor and family-wise bar are sized for exactly 5
  candidates (`docs/CONVENTIONS.md`: -0.17 c/L singly, -0.27 c/L at batch size). A 6th
  candidate re-cuts the bar for the other five after they have already been dossiered.
  Rejected.
- **Its own 1d-frozen batch** — a new freeze needs its own noise floor, ~3.8h wall for the
  20-draw version (`fps-3jj.19`). Disproportionate for one candidate. Rejected.
- **A batch2 candidate** — CHOSEN. batch2 (`fps-3jj.19`) is already planned at 10-15
  candidates with its own freeze and floor, and that floor is paid for regardless. This
  costs one slot, ~20 min of run.

Blocked on `fps-3jj.19` accordingly.

## Run tgp_cycle_displacement in batch2 as well
The stated point of this bead was to put both TGP expressions on ONE ruler. Landing only
`tgp_delta_7d` in batch2 does not achieve that — `tgp_cycle_displacement` was graded
against batch1's floor, a different snapshot and possibly a different
`baseline_fingerprint` if anything graduates out of batch1. **Include both as batch2
candidates**, two slots out of 10-15, or the comparison is still cross-ruler.

## Expected outcome, stated before the run
batch2's family-wise correction at 10-15 candidates is STIFFER than batch1's at 5.
`tgp_delta_7d`'s best realised reading to date is +0.0059 c/L (inert, 40th percentile of
batch0's noise floor). It will very probably not clear. **That is an acceptable result and
the reason to run it anyway** — the objective is a VALID 1d measurement that closes the
track honestly, not a graduation. An inert reading that counts beats an ambiguous one that
does not.

## Why the current readings do not count
- **A SECOND, INDEPENDENT reason (resolved 2026-09-05, `fps-sjk`): batch0's floor is
  methodologically retired too, not just its cadence.** `experiments/batches/batch0/
  noise_floor.json` carries no `null_method` — it is a pre-`fps-awz` SEED-SWAP null,
  not the placebo-column null every batch1+ floor uses — so
  `dossier_tables._noise_band()` refuses it and batch0/tgp_delta_7d cannot be graded
  against ANY floor under current tooling. `fps-sjk` closed as **GRANDFATHERED, not
  recomputed**: the shipped CLI cannot recompute it (`check_freeze_cadence` refuses
  `noise_floor batch0 --force` — batch0 declares 7d, `TankParams()` is 1d, no CLI
  cadence override), and it would buy nothing if it could, since +0.00585 c/L is the
  UNFAVOURABLE sign and a narrower placebo band can only hold the entry at
  `inconclusive` or push it to `rejected`. So the batch0 reading fails on BOTH axes —
  wrong cadence AND a ruler that no longer grades — and this bead is now the only
  route to a valid reading. Reasoning: `experiments/batches/batch0/RETROSPECTIVE.md`
  § Grandfathered.
- batch0's +0.0059 c/L is a `50/3.571/7d/10%` number. The re-lock to 1d was `fps-oqz`
  (2026-08-22). batch0's figures were never restated, batch0 cannot be re-frozen (one
  freeze per batch), and `dossier_tables._noise_band()` REFUSES the cross-cadence
  run-vs-floor comparison.
- The June "graduation" at -0.0394 c/L was smaller than that run's own ~0.05 c/L
  single-flip quantum — below the instrument's resolution. That 0.05 is itself a 7d
  quantity and must not be carried across the cadence boundary.
- batch0's own recommendation was "hold" on #271 AND "do not close the track."

## Sequencing
Do `fps-e6i` (tau-distance diagnostic) first. If TGP's log-loss gain turns out to be
threshold-remote, the track can be closed on that evidence and neither batch2 slot is
worth spending.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_delta_7d.py (port from batch0)
- experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_cycle_displacement.py (port from batch1)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both TGP candidates included in the batch2 candidate table at generation time
- [ ] Both graded at 1d against batch2's own floor, family-wise bar quoted for batch2's size
- [ ] Verdict stated against that bar; #271 / fps-2sf closed or explicitly held with a reason
title: Measure tgp_delta_7d at 1d as a batch2 candidate — its only readings are at a retired cadence

description:
## What
Both TGP expressions improve the WFCV log-loss screen and neither reaches the realised
arbiter. Hypothesis: the probability improvement lands on rows nowhere near tau = 0.25, so
the decision rule never reads it. Test it directly — for the rows where R0 and the
candidate probabilities differ most, measure the distribution of |p - 0.25|, and how much
of the total log-loss gain sits within one isotonic step of the threshold.

If the gain is concentrated far from tau, the whole TGP track is answered: not "the
feature is wrong" but "it improves a quantity the decision rule does not consult."

## Why I noticed this
Walking `experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement`. Evidence for the
hypothesis:
- tau_sweep.png: the candidate curve sits ABOVE R0 across essentially the whole tau range
  0.05-0.85 — a uniform ranking improvement — yet `own_tau_median` = `held_tau_median` =
  0.25 on BOTH arms. Better ranking, no relocation of the operating point.
- Per-fold sign agreement between `delta_ll_all_median` and `delta_cpl_own` is 6/14, and
  corr is -0.176 (all) / -0.307 (hard25). Both consistent with zero, neither with a
  positive relationship. (Both series are themselves noise-dominated — median per-fold
  |delta_ll| is 1.28x its own cohort seed_std on `all`, 1.93x on `hard25`, against the
  project's 3x rule — so the disagreement is not itself evidence of anything.)
- Known isotonic plateau at p~0.69 absorbs ~10% of rows — probability mass that can move
  without ever crossing tau.
- Same pattern recorded for `tgp_delta_7d` in batch0 ("helps the screen, sits inside the
  arbiter's noise floor — a case the project has no tooling for yet") and in June.

## Scoping (resolved 2026-08-31)
`rowpreds.parquet` and `fills.parquet` ARE present for all five batch1 candidates — they
are gitignored, so they are absent from secondary worktrees but live in the primary
checkout at `experiments/candidates/batch1/<candidate>/`. **No re-run needed: this is a
lookup, not an experiment.** An earlier revision of this bead flagged a possible ~17 min
re-run; that caveat is withdrawn.

## Files likely affected
- new experiments/<date>_tau_distance_of_logloss_gain/
- reads experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement/rowpreds.parquet (primary worktree)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Distribution of |p - tau| for the highest-|delta p| rows, R0 vs candidate
- [ ] Share of total delta log-loss attributable to rows within one isotonic step of tau
- [ ] Verdict recorded against the negative-results ledger, one entry per claim
- [ ] If the gain is threshold-remote, say so plainly and close the TGP track (fps-2sf, #271)
title: Diagnose whether TGP's log-loss gain lives anywhere near the decision threshold

description:
## What
`experiments/lib/flips.regret_horizon_days` computes a "FIXED, EXOGENOUS ceiling" on
feasible wait days as `round((1 - floor) * size / daily)` (or, with `exact_fields`,
`round(TankParams.max_feasible_wait_days)`). `round()` is Python's round-half-to-even —
on an exact `.5` it can round DOWN, which understates a value documented as a ceiling.
`math.ceil()` would resolve every tie upward by definition instead of float parity.

## Why I noticed this
PR #355 review (fps-o0h, "give derived tank quantities one owner on TankParams") review
finding #5. This predates fps-o0h — `regret_horizon_days` used `round()` before
`exact_fields` existed — so it's out of scope for that PR, which is a refactor with an
explicit acceptance criterion that the locked config's answer (13, for `50/3.571/1d/10%`)
must not move. Switching to `math.ceil()` would change MANY non-tie values too (any
fractional ceiling `round()` currently rounds down), not just the tie cases — a real
behaviour change to a function whose output feeds published regret figures
(`docs/CONVENTIONS.md`'s tank_params contract), needing its own decision and re-measurement
against the fps-6yi committed numbers, not something to fold into an unrelated refactor.

## Files likely affected
- `experiments/lib/flips.py` (`regret_horizon_days`)
- `tests/test_exp_lib_flips.py`
- Any committed dossier numbers that cite a regret horizon derived from a `.5`-adjacent
  ceiling (would need re-measurement, not just a code change)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide: keep `round()` (documented as "nearest", drop the "ceiling" framing) or
  switch to `math.ceil()` (keep "ceiling" framing, accept the behaviour change) — this is
  a judgement call for the repo owner, not a bug with one obviously-correct fix
- [ ] If switching to `ceil`, re-measure the fps-6yi regression numbers this function's
  docstring cites and update them
title: regret_horizon_days rounds ties down, but is documented as a ceiling

description:
## What
`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py`'s `_breakdowns` reads `results["realised_deltas"]`
records by column name (`"fold"`, `"arm"`, `"tau_diverges"`) — that key is written by
`runner.py` as `realised.deltas.to_dict(orient="records")`, i.e. verbatim off
`experiments/lib/realised.py`'s own `deltas` DataFrame (built at realised.py:~628). No test
currently exercises this column-name contract against the REAL `realised.py` output — only
against hand-built fixtures on both sides (test_dossier_tables.py writes results.json records
directly; test_runner.py's `_FakeRealisedFull.deltas` is a hand-declared stand-in).

## Why I noticed this
PR #354 (fps-4je, threading `tau_diverges` through results.json) review finding #4. Verified
live: renaming `tau_diverges` -> `tau_differs` at realised.py:628 and running the full suite
gives 1625 passed, 1 skipped, all green — while `_breakdowns` would `KeyError` on every real
run against that renamed column. Before fps-4je nothing in the pipeline read this column at
all, so a rename was harmless; fps-4je is what made it load-bearing, which is why the pin
belongs in this repo rather than being accepted as a general hygiene gap.

## Files likely affected
- tests/test_realised.py — has an existing fixture (`_install_fakes`/`_cache_test_setup`,
  per the PR #354 reviewer) that builds two arms ("R0"/"candidate") over >=2 folds with
  differing own-tau (0.30 vs 0.35), i.e. a real `tau_diverges=True` case. Add an assertion
  there pinning `deltas`'s column names together with the True case.
- Alternatively/additionally: a test in experiments/pipeline that calls the real
  `run_paired_realised_backtest` (DB-free, using whatever in-memory/synthetic frame
  test_realised.py already uses) and feeds its `.deltas` through `runner.py`'s results-dict
  build AND `dossier_tables.py`'s `_breakdowns`, in one test — the actual end-to-end path,
  not two independently-fixtured halves.

## Acceptance criteria

      renamed or dropped `fold`, `arm`, or `tau_diverges`, without needing a real DB.
- [ ] Confirmed by the same mutation used to find this gap: rename `tau_diverges` ->
      something else at realised.py's `deltas` construction, run the suite, confirm it now

description:
## What

PR #350 (fps-3tu) replaced the fixed-index `SHOCK_FOLDS={1,4,9,13}` with an
empirical shock-fold split, computed once per batch and cached at
`<batch_dir>/shock_folds.json`. The 5 already-published batch1 dossiers
(`experiments/candidates/batch1/*`) were deliberately left untouched by that
PR — their `results.json` predates `meta.shock_folds`, so `dossier_tables.py`
now reports their regime-dependent facts (`per_regime`, `decision_flips`,
the shock-shaded plot) as `computed: false` rather than silently reusing the
superseded constant. This bead is that deferred backfill.

## Audit already done (in the fps-3tu session, not yet applied)

Computed the corrected empirical shock set for batch1 against the current
`data/features.parquet` + 54-column production baseline: **{1, 3, 4, 14}**
(vs the old {1,4,9,13} — folds 4 and 1 survive on different/no grounds
respectively, 9 and 13 drop out, 3 and 14 are new).

Recomputed `zone` (the CONFIDENCE_ZONE regime verdict) against each
candidate's already-persisted `fills.parquet` for the 3 candidates whose
`TARGET` uses the regime axis:

| candidate | old verdict | new verdict |
|---|---|---|
| tgp_cycle_displacement | resolved: **false** (target −0.139 vs other −0.340) | resolved: **false** (target −0.160 vs other −0.288) — same story, narrower gap |
| network_move_breadth | resolved: **true** (−0.306 vs −0.092) | resolved: **true** (−0.211 vs −0.131) — same story, narrower gap |
| **lga_trough_propagation** | resolved: **false** (+0.046 vs −0.379 — mechanism contradicted) | resolved: **true** (−0.107 vs +0.003 — mechanism confirmed) — **FLIPS** |

`lga_trough_propagation/README.md:244` currently quotes the OLD shock
figure (`-0.3794 c/L`) and reads "the specific mechanism is contradicted" —
under the corrected split this candidate's own predicted mechanism is
CONFIRMED, not contradicted. This is the most consequential single fact in
this bead.

## What backfilling actually requires

Cheap — does NOT require re-running the candidates through `runner.py`
(no need to redo the ~15-30min realised backtest per candidate):

1. Compute/cache `shock_folds.json` for batch1 via
   `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m experiments.pipeline.shock_folds batch1`
   (needs the batch's frozen `features.csv`/`fuel_signal.db`, gitignored —
   run from wherever those exist, e.g. after re-freezing or on a checkout
   that still has them).
2. For the 3 regime-axis candidates, reload each `fills.parquet` and
   recompute `zone` via `experiments.pipeline.runner._resolve_zone` with
   the corrected shock_folds — confirmed feasible and cheap in the fps-3tu
   session (milliseconds, a groupby over an already-materialized frame).
   Patch `meta.shock_folds`/`meta.shock_quantile`/`meta.shock_folds_source`
   and `zone` into each candidate's `results.json`.
3. Regenerate `facts.json` + plots for all 5 candidates via
   `experiments.pipeline.dossier_tables.process_run` (deterministic, no
   judgement).
4. **Editorial, not mechanical**: rewrite the 3 affected candidates'
   README.md prose to match the corrected `facts.json` — especially
   `lga_trough_propagation`'s, whose headline narrative inverts. Follow
   `docs/routines/dossier.md`'s conventions.
5. Once batch1 dossiers are internally consistent again, `fps-3jj.18.1`
   (the batch retrospective) and `fps-3jj.18.2` (act on the outcome) can
   proceed on corrected numbers.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/candidates/batch1/*/results.json` (patch `meta`/`zone`)
- `experiments/candidates/batch1/*/facts.json` (regenerated)
- `experiments/candidates/batch1/*/README.md` (3 of 5 need prose changes:
  tgp_cycle_displacement and network_move_breadth are narrower but
  unchanged in verdict, lga_trough_propagation flips)
- `experiments/ledger.yaml` / `experiments/INDEX.md` — check whether either
  quotes the old lga_trough_propagation verdict and needs a matching update

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `experiments/batches/batch1/shock_folds.json` exists
- [ ] All 5 candidates' `results.json`/`facts.json` carry `meta.shock_folds`
- [ ] `lga_trough_propagation/README.md` rewritten to reflect resolved:true
      (mechanism confirmed, not contradicted)
- [ ] `tgp_cycle_displacement`/`network_move_breadth` READMEs updated for
      the narrower (but same-direction) margins
- [ ] `experiments/ledger.yaml`/`INDEX.md` cross-checked for stale numbers
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` green

## What

    noise_floor.json's baseline_fingerprint (None) does not match this run's (None)

This is pre-existing on `main` (predates fps-1x5/PR #349, which left it unchanged since it wasn't in scope for that refactor) — the check itself is correct (`is None or !=` deliberately treats a missing fingerprint as untrusted, matching the "cannot be shown to match, so cannot be trusted" rule the surrounding comment already states), only the message wording is wrong for the both-missing case.

## Why I noticed this
Found while fixing the same self-contradiction on the tank_params axis (peer review of PR #349, fps-1x5) — the fingerprint check has the identical `is None or !=` shape and was never audited for this wording bug.

- `tests/test_dossier_tables.py`

description:
## What

Tank/fill arithmetic has no single owner. `TankParams` (fuel_signal/backtest.py:348) is a
bare dataclass with no methods, so every quantity DERIVED from it is recomputed at each
call site — and in the dossier layer, recomputed from a **rounded display string** rather
than from the dataclass.

Noticed while reviewing fps-2js / PR #348, whose `regret_horizon_days` added the most
recent instance. The review finding there (H=13 is a ceiling no real fill attains) was
really a symptom: tank physics was re-derived in `experiments/lib/flips.py` from a parsed
stamp, without access to the fill model that would have shown a fill's true headroom is
`((1-floor)*size - litres)/daily`.

## Two distinct problems

### 1. The stamp round-trip can flip a derived window, and the mechanism is a ROUNDING TIE

`format_tank_params` (backtest.py:357) is a DISPLAY format — its own docstring says "a
readable literal, not a hash" — and renders daily consumption `:.3f`. The default
`daily_consumption_litres` is 3.5714285714285716, stamped as `3.571`.

**The precision loss only matters where it crosses a rounding tie** (established in PR #348
review round 2, verified both directions on two independent sweeps). Worked example,
`40/2.857/1d/25%`:

    exact:  30 / (40/14) = 10.5          -> round() = 10   (Python banker's rounding, ties-to-even)
    stamp:  30 / 2.857    = 10.500525... -> round() = 11

Over a 560-config sweep (size 40-70, 8-21 day tank life, floor 5-25%, cadence 1d/7d),
**every single horizon disagreement is an exact .5 tie: 12 ties, 0 from any other cause.**
An independent 840-config sweep by the PR #348 reviewer found 24 disagreements, all ties.
So this is NOT general float drift — it is precisely the tie cases, which is what whoever
picks this up should test.

**No locked config is affected.** Both committed stamps (`50/3.571/1d/10%`,
`50/3.571/7d/10%`) give horizon 13 and cascade window 7/8 either way. Latent, not live —
but the stamp is the ONLY tank record reaching the dossier layer (results.json persists
`meta.tank_params`, never the TankParams object), so a future re-lock could land on a tie.

### 2. Fill mechanics are restated, not shared

The authoritative model is `backtest.py`'s `_transitions` (~line 726): BUY fills to full
(`buy_litres = size - level`), emergency targets `0.5 * size`, floor test is
`level / size < floor_fraction`, depletion is `daily * evaluation_interval_days`.
Restatements found:

- `experiments/2026-08-20_headroom_attribution/attribution.py:94,111` hardcodes the
  post-fill level as `25.0` for emergency fills instead of `0.5 * size`
- `experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/model_cadence.py:147` recomputes the run-dry gap
  (`floor_fraction * size`), which `validate_never_dry` also knows
- `experiments/lib/flips.py` derives TWO windows (`cascade_window_days`,
  `regret_horizon_days`) from the stamp

The experiments/ ones are frozen lab-book entries and must NOT be rewritten (CONVENTIONS.md)
— cited as evidence of the pattern, not as work.

### 3. Bonus, cheap: a `source_db` key-name collision

`dossier_tables._attach_regret` writes `summary["source_db"] = str(db_path.resolve())`, so
`facts.json`'s `decision_flips.regret.source_db` and `freeze.json`'s `source_db` are two
DIFFERENT paths under the same key name (the frozen clone vs the freeze-time source). The
value is correct and the docstring above it explains itself, but anyone diffing provenance
across the two artifacts will read the shared name as shared meaning. Rename to `graded_db`
or `frozen_db`. Same family as fps-qbv/#341's `batch_dir` vs candidates-dir confusion —
`bd recall batch-dir-vs-candidates-dir`.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

The missing concept is "what can this tank do", and its absence is what let PR #348 ship a
horizon no fill in the dataset could attain. A `TankParams` that could answer
`feasible_wait_days(litres_bought)` would have made that impossible to get wrong.

## Sketch (not a decision — that is this bead's job)

Give `TankParams` the derived quantities as properties/methods: `full_to_empty_days`,
`max_feasible_wait_days`, `feasible_wait_days(litres)`, `depletion_litres`, `run_dry_gap`.
Then decide the harder question: how the dossier layer gets a real `TankParams` rather than
a parsed display string. Options include persisting the four fields structurally in
results.json's meta beside the stamp, or making the stamp round-trip-exact — the first is
probably right, since the stamp's job is human readability and fps-15c wants it unchanged
and glanceable.

Constraint: `require_tank_stamp`/fps-15c make the stamp a contract, and
`cascade_window_days`' docstring leans on parsing being safe because `format_tank_params`
is its only writer. Any change must keep that contract intact.

## Files likely affected

- fuel_signal/backtest.py (TankParams gains the derived quantities)
- experiments/lib/flips.py (cascade_window_days, regret_horizon_days, parse_tank_params)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (_attach_regret's cadence lookup, source_db rename)
- experiments/pipeline/runner.py / experiments/lib/realised.py (if meta gains structured fields)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Derived tank quantities have exactly one definition, and call sites use it
- [ ] A test sweeps configs and asserts the derived windows agree whether computed from a
      `TankParams` or from its own stamp — **must include the exact-.5 tie cases**, which
      are the only ones that ever disagreed (e.g. `40/2.857/1d/25%`)
- [ ] `regret_horizon_days` and `cascade_window_days` still return 13 and 7 for
      `50/3.571/1d/10%` — this is a refactor, not a re-lock
- [ ] fps-15c's stamp contract and `require_tank_stamp` still hold
- [ ] `decision_flips.regret.source_db` renamed so it no longer collides with freeze.json's
- [ ] experiments/** lab-book entries left untouched
title: Give derived tank quantities one owner — they are re-derived from a rounded display stamp

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py`'s `_attach_run_contributions` (fps-e1w, PR #347)
computes `composition_residual_cpl` as the leftover between a litres-weighted shift-share of
`delta_cpl_own` (own-tau) and the headline `delta_cpl_held` (held-tau). When the two arms'
own-tau selections genuinely diverge, part of that residual is tau drift, not composition
drift — and there is currently no way to tell the two apart from facts.json.

## Why I noticed this

PR #347 code review (fps-e1w) flagged this as finding #3 (PLAUSIBLE). On investigation: a
`tau_diverges` flag already exists — `experiments/lib/realised.py`'s
`run_paired_realised_backtest` computes it per fold (`deltas` return value, ~line 628) — but
`runner.py` never reads `realised.deltas` at all, so the flag never reaches `results.json`.
It's a different, unrelated structure from `results["fold_run_deltas"]` (built by
`aggregate_with_deltas` for the WFCV log-loss cohort figures dossier_tables.py already
consumes) — the reviewer initially conflated the two, which is worth double-checking against
if this gets picked up.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/runner.py (persist `realised.deltas`'s `tau_diverges` per fold into
  `results.json`, e.g. under `meta` or a new top-level key)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_attach_run_contributions`, `_breakdowns` — surface
  the flag per fold so `composition_residual_cpl`'s docstring/dossier.md guidance can point at
  it instead of the current unconditional caveat)
- docs/routines/dossier.md (the run_contribution_cpl bullet currently says the residual "can
  also absorb tau divergence... not currently observable" — update once it is)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `results.json` carries a per-fold (or per-arm) `tau_diverges`-equivalent flag sourced
  from `run_paired_realised_backtest`'s own computation, not re-derived
- [ ] `facts["breakdowns"]["per_fold"]` (or `decision_flips`) surfaces it
- [ ] dossier.md's guidance updated to branch on the flag instead of an unconditional caveat
- [ ] Regression test with a synthetic run where the two arms' own-tau genuinely differ,
  confirming the flag fires and the residual bullet's guidance is actionable
title: Thread tau_diverges through results.json so composition_residual_cpl can separate tau drift from composition drift

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` now validates and scores a noise-floor bank in
TWO independent places:

- `_noise_band()` (~line 701) — the canonical bank
- `_comparable_noise_banks()` (~line 583) — sibling banks (fps-30p)

Both check `baseline_fingerprint`, `tank_params` and `partial`; both compute band
mean/std, call `_resolve_effective_n_draws`, test estimability, and call
`family_wise_z_threshold`. The logic was written twice, on purpose (see below), and has
already diverged.

## Why now — the drift is not hypothetical, it has happened

The float-degeneracy guard exists on ONE side only. `_comparable_noise_banks` (line 655)
pairs its estimability test with `float(np.ptp(deltas)) > 0`; `_noise_band`'s
`band_std_usable` does not, and that gap is a live misgrade path tracked as **fps-tnz** —
`np.std` of twenty identical `0.01`s is 1.78e-18, which sails past `> 0` and yields a z of
order 1e18 that `-t < z < t` reads as a confident REJECT. One fix landed in one copy. That
is exactly the failure mode duplication produces, arriving within a single session of the
duplication being introduced.

Raised as findings #6/#7 of a peer `/code-review` of PR #345 and **declined at the time
for a good reason that has now expired**: unifying means touching the canonical checks,
and #345's headline promise was that canonical grading is untouched (with a test pinning
it). That constraint applied to that PR, not to the codebase.

## What is deliberately different, and must SURVIVE any unification

These are not accidents to be normalised away — each has a recorded reason:

- **`null_method`**: canonical REFUSES a non-`placebo_column` bank (fps-awz, unconditional,
  line 737). Siblings REPORT it instead, because a pinned-source bank measures a genuinely
  different null and its z is still worth seeing labelled. Note the promote hint in the
  arity refusal must keep applying the STRICT rule — a relaxation correct for reading is
  not correct for recommending (peer review of #345).
- **Arity**: canonical refuses a floor narrower than the run (biased in the candidate's
  favour) and discloses a wider one via `floor_arity_exceeds_run`. Siblings refuse
  neither, disclosing narrower via `narrower_than_run` — refusing would delete the use
  case, since fps-6yi was resolved by an arity-1 bank against a 2-column run.
- **`check_fingerprint=False`**: `retrospective.py`'s `_batch_noise_summary` reuses
  `_noise_band`'s math with a dummy `results`, so identity checks must stay bypassable.

A shared helper therefore needs the strictness to be a PARAMETER (refuse vs disclose per
axis), not a single fixed contract. If that turns out to make the helper harder to read
than the duplication, say so and close this as won't-fix with the reasoning recorded —
that is an acceptable outcome, but it should be a decision rather than drift.

## Sequencing

Do **fps-tnz first** — fix the live defect in the canonical copy, so unification is a pure
refactor over two copies that already agree, rather than a refactor that also has to carry
a behaviour change. Merging a bug fix and a refactor in one diff is how the next
divergence gets missed.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_noise_band`, `_comparable_noise_banks`)
- experiments/pipeline/retrospective.py (`_batch_noise_summary` — the `check_fingerprint=False` caller)
- tests/test_dossier_tables.py

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] fps-tnz landed first; both copies agree on degeneracy before any refactor begins
- [ ] One place decides "is this bank usable" and one place computes mean/std/n_eff/z/threshold
- [ ] Per-axis strictness is explicit and parameterised (`null_method`, arity), with the
      reason for each divergence carried into the shared code, not lost in the merge
- [ ] Every existing test still passes UNCHANGED — in particular
      `test_noise_band_canonical_grade_is_untouched_by_siblings` and the promote-hint tests
- [ ] A test that would FAIL under the old duplication: assert both paths reject the same
      degenerate bank, so the next one-sided fix is caught
- [ ] `retrospective.py`'s dummy-results path still works
title: Unify the noise-bank comparability contract — _noise_band and _comparable_noise_banks have already drifted

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py:846`:

    band_std_usable = bool(np.isfinite(band_std) and band_std > 0)

`band_std > 0` does not catch "every draw landed on the same value" — the exact case
`noise_floor.py`'s docstring names and this line exists to guard. `np.std` of twenty
identical `0.01`s is **1.78e-18**, not `0.0`, because 0.01 has no exact binary
representation. Measured:

    value 0.0    std=0.0                      ptp=0.0
    value 0.01   std=1.7797887332061147e-18   ptp=0.0
    value 0.02   std=3.5595774664122295e-18   ptp=0.0
    value 187.8  std=2.9160058604848984e-14   ptp=0.0

So `band_std_usable` reads True, `candidate_z_vs_band` becomes
`(delta - band_mean) / 1.78e-18` — of order 1e18 — and `docs/routines/dossier.md` step 3's
mechanical `-t < z < t` split reads that as a confident REJECT (`z >= t`) on a bank that
carries no information whatsoever. The guard's intent is right; only its test is.

Fix: pair it with an exact degeneracy check, `float(np.ptp(deltas)) > 0`, which is zero iff
the draws really are identical regardless of representation.

## Why I noticed this

Found while fixing the same defect in the SIBLING-bank path added by fps-30p (PR #345). A
test written for the sibling path with `deltas_cpl_held: [0.01] * 20` failed because the
bank came back `comparable: True` — the sibling path is fixed on that PR with the `np.ptp`
pairing, and the canonical path was deliberately left alone there because #345 promised not
to touch canonical grading behaviour (it has a test pinning exactly that).

## Likelihood

Low but not zero, and the failure is silent and confident. Real placebo draws never
coincide, so this needs a degenerate bank — a hand-written fixture, a bank computed against
a frozen/constant series, or an `--n-draws` run where the placebo column turned out inert.
The consequence is the worst kind: not a refusal, but a wrong grade in the confident
direction, written into `experiments/ledger.yaml` as `rejected`.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py:846 (`band_std_usable`)
- tests/test_dossier_tables.py

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `band_std_usable` also requires `float(np.ptp(deltas)) > 0`
- [ ] Test: a canonical floor of 20 identical `0.01` draws yields `available: false` (or
      null `candidate_z_vs_band`), NOT a ~1e18 z
- [ ] Test covers exact-`0.0` draws too, so the pre-existing path stays green
- [ ] Check whether `retrospective.py`'s `_batch_noise_summary` (which reuses this math with
      `check_fingerprint=False`) needs the same guard
title: _noise_band's canonical band_std_usable check misses float-degenerate bands

description:
## What

`flip_cpl_baseline` / `flip_cpl_candidate` pool two DISJOINT sets of fills on
different days at different cycle positions, so their difference is not a saving
and has no stable denominator. Replace (or supplement) it with a per-fill
measure defined identically on both arms:

    regret = price paid − cheapest price at that station over the next H days
             (0 = bought the optimum; lower is better)

Litres-weight it, report per arm per fold plus an ALL row.

Follows `fps-e1w`, which fixes the DISPLAY of the existing measure. This changes
WHAT is measured and is deliberately separate -- do fps-e1w first.

## Why

Prototyped 2026-08-29 on batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle. Three concrete gains:

1. **Cycle-normalised, so cells are comparable.** A fill at 172.90 in Nov 2024
   and one at 205.90 in May 2024 are not comparable as prices -- the cycle moved
   between them. That is the actual root cause of exploding flip deltas.
   "How much better could you have done that week" is comparable.
2. **It pools.** `flip_cpl_delta` is not additive, so there is no run-level row.
   Regret gives one: on fps-6yi, baseline 6.22 vs candidate 6.21 c/L,
   difference -0.02 -- i.e. "both arms buy about equally well", which is right,
   consistent with the -0.0735 headline, and something the current table never
   says at all. Dispersion also halves: 6.6 c/L vs 13.7 for raw price.
3. **Thin cells read truthfully.** fps-6yi fold 13 currently prints -32.73 c/L.
   Under regret it reads baseline 4.53, candidate **0.00** -- the candidate
   bought the exact optimum. Same underlying fill, far better description.

It also exposes a divergence the current table cannot. fps-6yi fold 4
contributes +0.0437 to the headline (unfavourable) while its regret says the
candidate was 0.84 c/L BETTER. Not a contradiction -- regret measures decision
quality, the contribution column measures economic outcome including volume and
composition. When they disagree, the difference came from WHAT was bought, not
WHEN.

## What it does NOT fix

Every fold cell still fails its own 2*SE test. Nothing rescues 3-16 decisions
per fold. And the ALL row's ±1.92 assumes fills are independent; widening for
cascades (303 fills, 87 decisions) gives ±3.59 against a -0.02 difference -- so
the run-level row is honest but still cannot detect a small effect. Do not sell
this as a significance fix; it is a legibility and poolability fix.

## Design questions to settle

- **Horizon H.** The prototype used 7d arbitrarily. Derive it from cycle length
  (`cycle_mean_length`) rather than pick it -- see
  `feedback_derive_thresholds_from_reference_distribution`. A horizon shorter
  than the descent understates regret; longer than a cycle makes every fill look
  bad.
- **Dark days.** 56 of fps-6yi's 303 flips fall on days with no DB price for
  station 414 (a real outage, not a features.parquet artifact). The prototype
  forward-filled. Decide and document: ffill, exclude, or report separately.
  Non-random -- the outages thin and tilt specific folds.
- **Price source.** `dossier_tables.py` does not currently take DB access. The
  realised replay reads `PriceHistory` from the batch DB, and
  `features.parquet` has DIFFERENT coverage (it was missing 80 of the 303 flip
  days). Use the DB -- it is the source the fills actually came from. Verified:
  all 247 flips on real DB price days match their executed price exactly.
- **Same-station only?** The prototype compares against the same station's own
  forward prices. A strategy could switch stations, so a cross-station variant
  ("cheapest among the preferred set") is arguably the better counterfactual.
  Costs more, and changes what "regret" means. Pick deliberately.
- **Keep flip_cpl_delta alongside, or drop it?** Recommend keeping it in
  `facts.json` (cheap) but dropping it from the rendered table once regret
  lands, so there is one measure on screen rather than two that disagree.

## Bonus signal worth capturing

Regret SPREAD is itself a quality measure, not just its mean: a strategy that
reliably lands at the low has a tighter distribution. On fps-6yi the candidate
hit exact-optimum on 42.1% of flips vs the baseline's 31.7% (sd 6.28 vs 7.19).
`flip_cpl_delta` cannot express that at all.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/lib/flips.py (new measure)
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (price-source plumbing, rendering)
- docs/routines/dossier.md
- tests/

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] H derived from cycle length, with the derivation recorded
- [ ] Dark-day policy decided, documented, and its affected-fold count reported
- [ ] Per-arm per-fold regret + an ALL row, litres-weighted, with intervals
- [ ] Cascade-widened band on the ALL row, not the naive one
- [ ] Regression test reproducing fps-6yi: all-flip 6.22 vs 6.21, fold 13
      candidate 0.00
title: Replace flip_cpl_delta with a paired per-fill regret measure

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` renders the per-fold decision-flip
table as `n_baseline_only | n_candidate_only | flip_cpl_baseline |
flip_cpl_candidate | flip_cpl_delta`, in fold order. Rework the presentation so
the numbers cannot be read as evidence they can't support. Target shape,
rendered from batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle:

```
fold  regime  flips  decns   litres b/c    flip Δ c/L (± 2·SE)  → run Δ c/L
===========================================================================
   1   shock      0      0          0/0               no flips      +0.0000
   2  normal     50     13      200/425        +1.74 ± 5.96  ·      +0.0558
   4   shock     54     16      250/479        +0.88 ± 6.13  ·      +0.0437
   8  normal     36      5      382/379       +2.58 ± 12.20  ·      +0.0014
   9   shock      3      2         0/79           one arm only      +0.0053
  13   shock      6      3        54/43      -32.73 ± 36.77  ·      -0.0644
===========================================================================
                303     87    2064/2982           not additive      -0.0606
                                                                    -0.0129  composition residual
                                                                    -0.0735  = headline delta_cpl_held
```

## Why I noticed this

The owner has followed up on inflated `flip_cpl_delta` values TWICE (most
recently 2026-08-29 on fps-6yi). It is a presentation defect, not a reader
defect.

Root cause: `flip_cpl_baseline` and `flip_cpl_candidate` pool DISJOINT sets of
fills on different days at different points in the price cycle
(`experiments/lib/flips.py:64`). Their difference is not a saving and has no
stable denominator, so it explodes in thin cells. Measured on fps-6yi: per-fill
flip price dispersion is 13.7 c/L and litres-weighted effective n is 1.0-19.5
per arm, so **0 of 12 folds print a `flip_cpl_delta` larger than twice its own
standard error** -- fold 13's -32.73 sits inside a 2*SE of 36.77. That did not
stop "favourable flips dominate -- 9 of the 12 folds" reaching that dossier's
Judgement as evidence; it is a vote count over unresolvable cells.

## The changes

1. **`→ run Δ c/L` -- the highest-value one.** What this fold contributes to the
   run-level delta, so the reader sees the reconciliation instead of computing
   it. On fps-6yi, fold 13's headline-grabbing -32.73 contributes -0.0644 while
   folds 2 and 4 hand back +0.0995 between them. Build it litres-weighted as a
   shift-share with common weights `w_f = (L_R0,f + L_cand,f) / sum`, so
   `sum_f w_f * (cpl_cand,f - cpl_R0,f)` plus a composition residual reconciles
   EXACTLY to `delta_cpl_held`. Show the residual as its own line -- on fps-6yi
   it is -0.0129, ~18% of the headline, and hiding it would be its own
   distortion. A fills-weighted version does NOT reconcile (it lands on -0.0008
   against a -0.0735 headline); the weighting must match how the headline pools.
2. **Each delta beside its own 2*SE**, and mark it when the delta is inside it.
   Estimate: `s` = per-fill price dispersion (fold-local where n>=4, else
   run-wide); `n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2` with `w` = litres, per arm;
   `SE_arm = s / sqrt(n_eff)`; `SE_diff = sqrt(SE_b^2 + SE_c^2)`. This replaces
   an arbitrary `min_row_cell_n`-style count guard: resolution depends on litres
   and price spread, not fill count. **Print the interval, not the `±`** --
   `-2.68 (-7.6 to +2.3)` -- so no one needs to know what SE stands for.
   (Reviewed 2026-08-29: `± 2·SE` was itself hard to read.)
3. **`decns` -- cascade-collapsed flip count.** `flips.py:22` warns one real flip
   cascades into later differing fills, so `n_flips` overstates independent
   decisions. Count flips with no prior flip at the same station within a window
   (7d used in the review; derive it rather than hardcode). On fps-6yi, 303
   flips are ~87 decisions, and fold 8's 36 flips are 5.
4. **Litres per arm.** `pooled_cpl` is spend-weighted, so a 3.57 L top-up and a
   42.86 L fill count identically in `n_` but not in the CPL. Litres also
   surface something invisible today: on fps-6yi the candidate buys 2982 L
   against the baseline's 2064 across flipped decisions, a 44% difference.
5. **Empty-arm folds must say what happened** -- "no flips" / "one arm only",
   never `nan` or an em-dash the reader has to interpret.
6. **Guidance:** `docs/routines/dossier.md` should state that a `flip_cpl_delta`
   inside its own 2*SE cannot be cited as evidence in the Judgement, and that
   flip counts are a LOWER bound on divergence (already in flips.py's docstring,
   not in the routine).

## Explicitly rejected

**Do not sort by flip population.** Considered and tested 2026-08-29. It makes
the n-vs-magnitude anticorrelation visible, but implies a trust hierarchy that
does not exist -- no cell resolves at any population present, since effective n
tops out at ~19 against 13.7 c/L dispersion. Keep plain fold order.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_decision_flips`, rendering)
- experiments/lib/flips.py (`summarise_flips` -- decns, litres, per-cell SE)
- docs/routines/dossier.md (Step 1 flip reporting + the citation rule)
- tests/test_dossier_tables.py

## Design note -- a new persisted field is required

The `→ run Δ c/L` column needs per-fold per-arm litres and spend, which live in
`fills.parquet`. That file is **gitignored** and never reaches a reader who did
not run the batch locally, so `dossier_tables.py` must compute the column at
build time and persist it into `facts.json`. It cannot be reconstructed later
from the committed artifact. Per `feedback_a_new_facts_field_needs_its_consumer`,
land the emitter and the renderer together.

## Design note -- the SE estimator has a float-degeneracy trap (added 2026-08-29)

The `s` in change 2 above is a standard deviation, and **`s > 0` is not a valid
degeneracy guard**. `np.std` of identical floats is not reliably `0.0`: twenty
identical `0.01`s give `1.78e-18`, because 0.01 has no exact binary representation
(`0.02` -> 3.6e-18, `187.8` -> 2.9e-14; only an exact `0.0` returns `0.0`, and small
n can return exact `0.0` by luck, which is what makes this easy to miss in a test).

**Why it matters more here than where it was found.** A hairline `s` collapses
`SE_arm = s / sqrt(n_eff)` to near zero, so the interval closes to nothing and the
cell renders as **RESOLVED** -- confidently, with a tight interval, in exactly the
thinnest cell. That is the precise inverse of what this whole column exists to
prevent. A guard that fails open toward "this number is trustworthy" is worse than
no guard.

**Not hypothetical.** In `stickiness_phase_saddle`'s own flip rows, two per-arm cells
already have zero price spread: fold 11 baseline (2 fills, both 223.90) and fold 14
baseline (2 fills, both 179.90). The FOLD-level `s` (pooled across both arms, which
is what the spec uses) happens not to degenerate anywhere in batch1 -- the minimum
fold ptp is 2.40 c/L -- so this is a latent trap rather than a live wrong number
today. It becomes live for any fold whose flips all land at one price, which is an
ordinary thing for a station holding price through a flat stretch.

**Required behaviour:**
- Guard with `float(np.ptp(prices)) > 0` alongside the finite/positive check on `s`.
  `np.ptp` is exact and zero iff the values really are identical.
- Degeneracy must trigger the run-wide fallback, not just `n < 4`. The current
  wording ("fold-local where n>=4, else run-wide") gates the fallback on COUNT alone
  and would happily use a degenerate fold-local `s` at n=20.
- If the run-wide dispersion is also degenerate, print **no interval at all** and say
  why. Never a hairline one.

Same defect class as `fps-tnz` (the canonical `band_std_usable` check) and the
sibling-bank fix in PR #345. Background and measurements: `bd recall
np-std-float-degeneracy`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `facts["decision_flips"]["per_fold"]` carries decns, per-arm litres,
      per-cell 2*SE, and the run-contribution figure
- [ ] Contribution column + composition residual reconciles to
      `headline.realised.delta_cpl_held` (assert in a test, not by eye)
- [ ] Deltas render as an interval; cells inside their own 2*SE are marked
- [ ] `s` is guarded with `np.ptp`, degeneracy falls back to run-wide dispersion
      (not gated on count alone), and a fully degenerate case prints NO interval.
      Test with a fold whose flip prices are all identical -- assert it renders
      unresolved, NOT a hairline interval
- [ ] Empty-arm folds render a reason string
- [ ] Fold order preserved (no population sort)
- [ ] dossier.md carries the citation rule
- [ ] Regression test against batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle reproducing the
      numbers in the table above
title: Redesign the dossier decision-flip table so flip_cpl_delta cannot be misread

description:
## What

`docs/routines/dossier.md` requires a `not_tested` list but says nothing about
what makes an entry sound. Add two rules:

1. **State whether the test is possible, and with what.** "X was not measured"
   is not enough — say whether X is measurable now (and from what), blocked on
   a named artifact, or permanently untestable by this pipeline. A reader acts
   very differently on "pending" than on "never".
2. **Check before writing.** Before a line of the form "Y would resolve this",
   look for Y: enumerate the batch directory, and read the CURRENT status and
   CLOSE REASON of any bead cited. Never stake a recommendation on the outcome
   of a bead filed in the same session — you do not know how it will close.

## Why I noticed this

`stickiness_phase_saddle` (fps-6yi, batch1), dossiered 2026-08-27. All three of
its `not_tested` lines were wrong, each in a way rule 1 or 2 would have caught:

- "Worth a second look once `fps-1l1`'s SHAP gap is closed" — the dossier FILED
  fps-1l1 and staked its recommendation on the outcome in the same document, on
  the same day. It closed down the "don't capture" branch: no SHAP field will
  ever exist, and dossier.md:80 now grades SHAP-shaped signatures inconclusive
  permanently. "Pending" was actually "never".
- "A same-arity floor could resolve it either way" — two comparable banks were
  already committed in the batch directory it read `noise_floor.json` from, and
  both answer it (z=-0.81, -0.88, vs -0.99 on the graded bank). See fps-30p.
- "decision_flips has no station-level stickiness data, so only the coarser
  half of the prediction is checkable" — true as stated, but it concluded the
  mechanism was uncheckable when `decision_flips.rows` plus the batch DB
  localised it cleanly (edge concentrates at cycle turns; litres-weighted 7d
  regret 0.33 c/L candidate vs 21.62 baseline on turn-adjacent flips).

The `not_tested` field is the payload of the negative-results ledger
(`reference_negative_results_ledger`) and feeds the next batch's generator, so a
wrong line here is not inert — it either sends work at closed ground or hides
open ground.

## Files likely affected

- docs/routines/dossier.md (the not_tested guidance in Step 3)
- possibly experiments/ledger.yaml's header, which documents the field

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] dossier.md states both rules with the fps-6yi failure as the worked example
- [ ] The three feasibility categories are named (measurable now / blocked on a
      named artifact / permanently untestable) with the reader consequence of each
- [ ] Explicit prohibition on staking a recommendation on a same-session bead
- [ ] Cross-references fps-30p (enumerate the batch dir before claiming a
      missing ruler) and fps-i2o (untestable-by-construction signatures)
title: dossier.md: a not_tested line must state feasibility, not just absence

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py`'s `_noise_band()` reads one floor by
fixed filename (`NOISE_FLOOR_FILENAME` = `noise_floor.json`) and grades the
candidate against that single bank. Batch directories routinely hold more than
one. Enumerate `noise_floor*.json`, keep every bank whose `baseline_fingerprint`,
`tank_params` and `n_windows` match the run, and report the candidate's z
against each — canonical bank first, the others as corroboration.

## Why I noticed this

Dossiering `stickiness_phase_saddle` (fps-6yi, batch1). Its `not_tested` said a
floor matching the candidate's own 2-column arity "could resolve it either way"
— while two comparable banks sat in the same directory `noise_floor.json` was
read from, and both answer it:

| bank | draws | arity | null_method | band mean / std | z |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| noise_floor.json (graded on) | 10 | 3 | placebo_column | +0.0251 / 0.0999 | -0.99 |
| noise_floor_k1.json | 20 | 1 | placebo_column | -0.0089 / 0.0800 | -0.81 |
| noise_floor_icc.json | 32 (eff 14.7) | 1 | placebo_column_pinned_source | +0.0278 / 0.1152 | -0.88 |

An arity-2 band sits between the arity-1 and arity-3 banks by construction, so
no comparable ruler brings |z| near t=1.92. That turned an open `not_tested`
line into a closed one with three numbers, at zero compute — the k1 bank alone
cost ~3.8h to build and was already paid for. See
`feedback_committed_artifacts_before_new_compute`.

This also retires a recurring class of `not_tested` line ("a different-shaped
floor might move the call") that the dossier routine currently has no way to
resolve on its own.

## Design notes

- Fingerprint match is already required by `_noise_band()` (fps-cf8) — apply the
  same refusal per bank, and SKIP non-matching banks silently rather than failing.
- `null_method` differing (e.g. `placebo_column_pinned_source` vs
  `placebo_column`) is not disqualifying but must be REPORTED beside the z — the
  banks measure slightly different nulls.
- The canonical bank stays authoritative for the ledger `outcome`. The others
  are corroboration and must never change the mechanical grade.
- Arity should be surfaced per bank so `floor_arity_exceeds_run` reads against
  the right one.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_noise_band`)
- tests/test_dossier_tables.py
- docs/routines/dossier.md (Step 1 noise-floor reporting)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `facts["noise_band"]` carries a list of every comparable bank with its
      draws, arity, null_method, band mean/std and the candidate's z
- [ ] Non-matching-fingerprint banks are skipped, with the reason recorded
- [ ] The canonical bank still solely determines the ledger outcome
- [ ] Test covers: multiple banks present, one bank with a mismatched
      fingerprint, and the single-bank (status quo) case
title: _noise_band(): grade against every comparable noise-floor bank, not just noise_floor.json

description:
## What

`experiments/candidates/TEMPLATE.py`'s `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` comment says only
"describe expected sign/magnitude and where it concentrates". It carries no
constraint that the prediction be expressible in quantities the pipeline
actually persists. Add one: a signature must be gradeable from
`facts.json` — `decision_flips` (per-fold counts, per-fill rows with price /
litres / date / station), `per_fold`, `per_regime`, `per_axis`, `headline`.
Name SHAP explicitly as the known-bad case.

## Why I noticed this

`fps-1l1` closed 2026-08-27 with its lesson applied to the GRADER only:
`docs/routines/dossier.md:80` now says a SHAP-shaped `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE`
grades `"inconclusive"` **always**. Nothing was added on the AUTHORING side, so
candidates can still be written with untestable signatures — and each one will
now auto-grade inconclusive forever, which is worse than the old behaviour
because it looks like a measurement.

`stickiness_phase_saddle` (fps-6yi, batch1) is the worked example. Its
signature was "the SIGNED and ABSOLUTE columns are both used and DISAGREE in
orientation somewhere in the SHAP surface" — ungradeable. A 2026-08-29 review
found the same mechanism WAS testable from `decision_flips.rows` plus the batch
DB: the edge concentrates at cycle turns (litres-weighted 7d regret 0.33 c/L
candidate vs 21.62 baseline on turn-adjacent flips, across 5 folds) and is too
rare to pay (~5% of flipped litres, -0.88 c/L worse on the rest). Had the
signature read "the edge concentrates near cycle turns", the dossier routine
would have reached that on the first pass instead of grading it untested.

fps-1l1's own second acceptance criterion anticipated this — "future
PREDICTED_SIGNATUREs should avoid them or phrase them in terms of
decision_flips/per_fold data instead" — but that text landed in dossier.md as a
grading rule, never in the template as an authoring rule.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/candidates/TEMPLATE.py (the PREDICTED_SIGNATURE comment block)
- docs/routines/dossier.md (cross-reference, so the two stay in step)
- possibly the generator prompt, if it templates signatures independently

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] TEMPLATE.py states the constraint and lists the gradeable fact families
- [ ] SHAP named as the specific known-bad case, with the fps-1l1 decision cited
- [ ] A worked good/bad pair in the comment (SHAP-orientation phrasing vs the
      equivalent decision_flips phrasing), using stickiness_phase_saddle
- [ ] dossier.md:80 cross-references the template so the rule has one home
title: TEMPLATE.py: require PREDICTED_SIGNATURE to be testable from persisted facts

description:
## What

`experiments/lib/constants.SHOCK_FOLDS = frozenset({1, 4, 9, 13})` is a hardcoded
fold-index set used to tag walk-forward-CV folds "shock" vs "normal" throughout the
live batch1 pipeline (`experiments/pipeline/runner.py`, `experiments/pipeline/
dossier_tables.py`, `experiments/lib/folds.py`, and directly in several batch1
candidate scripts). It drives every regime-segmented economics figure the dossier
reports (e.g. "shock -0.3794 c/L" style lines in ledger.yaml entries).

Found while closing `fps-tpy` (documenting the 2022-03 NSW source-data hole):
`walk_forward_folds(train_min_days=1825, val_days=90, step_days=90)` — the exact
params `experiments/lib/folds.py` uses — currently produces fold 2's val window as
`2022-02-03 to 2022-05-03`, which contains the Ukraine invasion (2022-02-24), the
NSW source-data collapse (2022-03-12 to 2022-03-21, see AGENTS.md § Known source
data limitations), AND the federal fuel excise cut (2022-03-30) — arguably the
single most dramatic shock window in the whole 2016-2026 dataset. `SHOCK_FOLDS`
does **not** flag fold 2 as shock. It flags fold 1 (val 2021-11-05..2022-02-02,
ends 3 weeks before the invasion), 4 (2022-08-02..2022-10-30), 9
(2023-10-26..2024-01-24), and 13 (2024-10-20..2025-01-17) — none of which line up
with an obvious documented global fuel-price shock.

## Why this is plausible, not just a one-off miscount

`walk_forward_folds()`'s fold boundaries are computed from `pre_test_dates.min()` —
the actual earliest date in whatever `df` is passed in — not a fixed calendar
constant. As more historical CSVs get downloaded/backfilled over the project's
life, that min date (and the warm-up-adjusted effective min date once lagged
features are computed) can shift, which shifts every fold's absolute date range
and therefore what "fold 1", "fold 4", etc. actually mean in calendar terms.
`SHOCK_FOLDS` was set once (introduced in the `experiments/lib/` scaffolding
extraction, PR closing #229, June 2026) as a fixed index set and has not been
re-verified against a growing data range since.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/lib/constants.py` (the `SHOCK_FOLDS` definition)
- `experiments/lib/folds.py` (`iter_folds_with_baseline_fit`, the shared fold+regime iterator)
- `experiments/pipeline/runner.py`, `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` (consumers)
- Every `experiments/2026-06-*/paired_wfcv.py` script that hardcodes its own local `SHOCK_FOLDS = frozenset({1, 4, 9, 13})` copy (grep for `SHOCK_FOLDS` — about a dozen hits)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide the right fix: recompute the correct index set against the CURRENT
      data range and re-verify periodically, OR replace index-based regime tagging
      with a date-range/event lookup (e.g. a small table of known shock windows:
      Ukraine invasion 2022-02, excise cut 2022-03/09, etc.) that's robust to the
      data range growing.
- [ ] Verify what folds 1, 4, 9, and 13 currently correspond to in calendar terms
      and whether they were ever intentionally chosen for real shock events, or
      whether the set has silently drifted from its original meaning.
- [ ] If the fix changes which folds are "shock", audit whether any published
      dossier/ledger economics conclusions (batch0/batch1) would read differently
      under corrected regime labels — this could be a re-read of existing results,
      not necessarily a re-run.
- [ ] Fix propagated to the shared `experiments/lib/constants.py` and NOT
      re-duplicated as another hardcoded local copy in whichever script lands it.

## Related

- `fps-tpy` (closed) — where this was found, documenting the 2022-03 NSW source
  data hole in AGENTS.md § Known source data limitations.
title: SHOCK_FOLDS={1,4,9,13} misses the Ukraine/excise/data-hole fold, verify against current data range

description:
## What

`runner.py` stamps `extra_feature_provider_hits`/`_misses` into `results.json`'s `meta` only on the GRADED path (runner.py:656, inside the full results dict). The abort path builds `meta` with `wall_seconds` only:

    "status": status, "candidate": {"name": name}, "error": error,
    "abort_reason": abort_reason, "meta": {"wall_seconds": wall_seconds},

(runner.py:1022, `_finish`). So a run aborted BY `_check_provider_health` — the 100%-miss case, runner.py:587-593 — persists no provider counts at all.

Since fps-qbv (PR #341) `dossier_tables._validation` reads those keys and reports `extra_feature_provider_hits`/`_misses`/`_miss_rate`. On an aborted-at-100%-misses run all three come back `None`, which is indistinguishable from:

- a legacy `results.json` predating the provider stamp, and
- a candidate with no `EXTRA_FEATURE_PROVIDER` at all.

The dossier reader therefore cannot tell total provider failure from "field not recorded", in exactly the run where coverage is 0% — the same class of blindness fps-qbv exists to close. The counts ARE available at abort time (`provider.stats` is live at runner.py:587).

## Why I noticed this

Found during the fps-1l1 code review of PR #341 (bd-fps-qbv, `claude/fps-qbv-021405`). Agreed with that PR's author (fps-aam session) that it is real but out of that PR's stated scope — #341 deliberately changed no `runner.py` — so it was split out here rather than scope-creeping the PR.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/pipeline/runner.py` (the `_finish` meta dict, ~line 1022; provider is in scope at the 587-593 abort site but not at `_finish`'s signature — passing the stats through is the actual work)
- `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` `_validation` (may want to distinguish "aborted on provider health" from "not recorded" in its rendered text once the data exists)
- `tests/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_dossier_tables.py`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run aborted by `_check_provider_health` persists `extra_feature_provider_hits`/`_misses` in `results.json` `meta`.
- [ ] `build_facts` on such a run reports `extra_feature_provider_miss_rate == 1.0`, not `None`.
- [ ] `None` still means "not recorded" (legacy run, or candidate with no provider) and is distinguishable from 100% misses by a dossier reader.
- [ ] Other abort statuses (non-provider aborts) are unaffected — they legitimately have no provider stats and must stay `None` rather than gaining a fabricated 0.
- [ ] Test covering the 100%-miss abort end-to-end (runner writes -> build_facts reads).
title: Stamp extra_feature_provider stats on the aborted-candidate results.json path

description:
## What
PR #340 (fps-8o0) fixed texture_channel.py's ANOVA (singleton-drop + k_bar) but left two things now stale:

   ```python
   if abs(rho_hi - TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND) > 5e-4:
       print(f"  !! MISMATCH — this run measures {rho_hi:.3f}; update TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND "
             "or record why it differs.")
   ```

   0.391, this fires and reads as "lower the shipped constant" — but TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND=0.274 is
   a by-COLUMN quantity from a different, unaffected script (fps-3jj.23/#338) and is correct as
   shipped. The by-FAMILY 0.226 this script measures is superseded, not a replacement candidate.
   Sibling `experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/measure_icc.py:325` has the right one-sided form
   (`if anova["icc_upper"] > TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND`) — match that shape, or replace the block with a
   note that this script no longer sources the shipped constant.

2. Two stale cross-references #340 falsified without updating:
   - `experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/measure_icc.py:109`'s comment — "Inherited from
     `2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/texture_channel.py`, which still has it — tracked

   - `experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/README.md`:268/270 — "the defect fixed in
     `measure_icc.py` still lives in `texture_channel.py`" and describes the now-removed

## Why I noticed this
Found by an independent peer-session code review of PR #340, run after it had already merged.
Verified against origin/main before filing.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/texture_channel.py
- experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/measure_icc.py
- experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/README.md

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MISMATCH block no longer suggests lowering TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND to a superseded by-family number
