description:
## What

`experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/texture_channel.py` filters its ANOVA groups
with `if len(g) > 1`, silently discarding any texture family represented by a single draw. A
singleton contributes nothing to the WITHIN-group sum of squares (correctly) but does
contribute to the BETWEEN-group sum of squares, so dropping it discards real signal — and the
reported `n`/`k` are computed after the drop, so nothing in the printed output reveals it.

Fix: drop the `len(g) > 1` filter and guard instead on "at least one group has >1 member"
(otherwise df2 = 0). See `experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/measure_icc.py::_anova_icc`, which
was corrected this way in PR #337, and `tests/test_texture_icc_estimator.py` for the shape of
the test.

## Why I noticed this

The same defect was found in `measure_icc.py` during review of PR #337 (fps-3jj.23) — that
file inherited the pattern from `texture_channel.py`. Fixed there; left here because it is
outside that PR's diff.

## Does it change the shipped number?

**Unknown, and worth checking as part of the fix.** `texture_channel.py` is what produced
`placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND = 0.391` (the 95% upper bound on the by-FAMILY ICC). Its grouping is
`texture_family()` over batch1's 20 committed k1 draws across ~5 families, so whether any
family is a singleton depends on the draw composition. If one is, the shipped 0.391 was
computed on 19 draws and 4 families rather than 20 and 5, and the constant moves.

Check first, then fix: if the number moves, it is a correction to a live constant and needs
the same care as any re-lock, not a silent edit.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/texture_channel.py
- experiments/pipeline/placebo.py (TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND, only if the number moves)
- docs/CONVENTIONS.md (only if the number moves)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Determine whether any texture family in batch1's k1 floor is a singleton
- [ ] Report whether 0.391 changes, and by how much
- [ ] Filter removed, guard added for the all-singleton case
- [ ] If the number moves, TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND and its two doc sites updated together
notes:
## ANSWERED 2026-08-27 (from fps-3jj.23's run): YES, the number moves — and by more than the
## filter alone. Fix both halves together or the correction points the WRONG WAY.

This bead asked "does the singleton drop change the shipped 0.391? Unknown, check first."
Checked. **batch1's `network` texture family IS a singleton** (11 lga_trough_counter, 3
cycle_magnitude, 3 price_level_other, 2 cycle_phase, **1 network**), so the defect is live on
the exact artifact that produced the constant.

**It is not one defect but two, and they interact.** texture_channel.py filters
`if len(g) > 1` — dropping that draw from the sums of squares — while computing
`n = len(draws) = 20`, `k_bar = n / k_groups = 20/5 = 4.0` and `df2 = n - len(groups) = 16`.
So the published F comes from 19 draws over 4 groups while df2 and k_bar come from 20 over 5.

  variant                                    n     k   k_bar   F           p       ICC     upper   resolvable
  all 5 families, consistent (CORRECT)       20    5   3.20    F(4,15)=0.330  0.854  -0.265  0.226   0.391
  singleton dropped, consistent              19    4   3.82    F(3,15)=0.411  0.748  -0.182  0.402   0.374
  as texture_channel.py actually computes it  19/20 4/5 4.00    F(3,16)=0.411  0.748  -0.173  0.391   0.359

The third row reproduces the shipped 0.391 AND its published "could not resolve below 0.359"
exactly — that exact match is what identifies the mechanism rather than merely suggesting it.

**The trap this bead exists to prevent, made concrete: fixing only the `len(g) > 1` filter
RAISES the constant to 0.402. Fixing the whole computation LOWERS it to 0.226.** A partial fix
would have moved a live grading constant in the opposite direction from the truth. Do both.

**No longer urgent, because the constant no longer depends on this file.** PR #338 replaced
placebo.TEXTURE_ICC_BOUND with 0.274 — the by-COLUMN quantity measured directly on a 32-draw
pinned-source bank (fps-3jj.23), which does not route through texture_channel.py at all. So
this is now a script correction plus a note in
experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/README.md that its published 0.391 / 0.359
were wrong on their own terms. That README already carries the corrected table (§ "What was
still a bound, and is now MEASURED"); the script itself is untouched.

Acceptance can shrink accordingly: drop the `len(g) > 1` filter, guard instead on "at least one
group has >1 member", derive n/k/k_bar/df from the SAME group list, and assert the corrected
run prints 0.226 rather than 0.391. Pattern + test shape:
experiments/2026-08-27_texture_icc/measure_icc.py::_anova_icc and
tests/test_texture_icc_estimator.py.
title: texture_channel.py drops singleton texture-family groups from its ANOVA

description:
## What
`facts.json` (written by `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py`) has no field carrying per-column SHAP importance or sign/orientation information. Several candidates' `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` (the dossier routine's grading target, see `docs/routines/dossier.md` Step 1.2) make claims specifically about SHAP structure -- e.g. stickiness_phase_saddle (fps-6yi, batch1) predicted "the SIGNED and ABSOLUTE columns are both used and disagree in orientation somewhere in the SHAP surface" as the distinguishing signature separating a real saddle from a weaker "outliers are decoupled" story. The dossier routine has no facts.json field to check this against and had to grade the run's mechanism-level claim as untested.

## Why I noticed this
Dossiering `experiments/candidates/batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle/` (2026-08-27 nightly dossier run). `cycle_phase_breakdown.png` only plots raw column values vs `cycle_pct_through` by regime (a sanity check of the feature construction), not model-usage/SHAP data -- so even the one conditional plot that looked most relevant didn't cover it.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide whether SHAP importance/sign summary is worth capturing routinely (cost: SHAP computation on top of an already ~1000s run) or whether PREDICTED_SIGNATURE authors should stop making SHAP-shaped predictions the dossier step can never test.
- [ ] If captured: add a `facts["shap_summary"]` (or similar) field with per-column mean |SHAP| and sign-agreement stats, referenced by dossier.md Step 1.
- [ ] If not: note in dossier.md (or a candidate-writing guideline) that SHAP-orientation predictions are untestable by this pipeline as it stands, so future PREDICTED_SIGNATUREs should avoid them or phrase them in terms of decision_flips/per_fold data instead.
title: dossier_tables.py facts.json carries no SHAP importance/orientation data

description:
## What

`batch1/noise_floor.json` — the ruler all five batch1 candidates were graded against — contains
the `fps-3jj.20` seed collision. Draw 10 reuses draw 1's seeds 97/101/103, giving placebo
correlations 0.965 / 0.778 / 0.765 against it. **It is not one unlucky pair: draw 10 is a
near-copy of draw 1 across all three columns.** So the bank is worth roughly **9 effective
draws, not 10**.

`fps-3jj.21` fixed the construction but **deliberately did not recompute that floor**, because
recomputing moves the ruler under dossiers already written against it. That was the right call
for the dossiers. It is an open question for the **retrospective**.

## Why it matters specifically at the retrospective

`fps-3jj.18.1` is where the batch is RANKED, and ranking is the multiple-comparisons step the
one-at-a-time workflow never performed — `fps-3jj`'s own design doc says so. It is exactly where
band quality stops being cosmetic:

- `family_wise_z_threshold` takes `df = n_draws - 1` from the **nominal** 10, not the effective
  ~9. So the t-critical is computed as though the band were better estimated than it is.
- Two draws that are near-copies also shrink the sample std slightly.

Both errors point the same way: **the bar is marginally too EASY.** Small — but the retrospective
is where a small optimism gets promoted into "candidate X cleared the batch-level bar."

## The actual question, and it is a judgement call

**Does the retrospective run against the committed ruler, a recomputed one, or both?**

- **Committed only.** Consistent with every dossier already written. Carries the known
  optimism.
- **Recomputed only.** Cleaner band, but the retrospective would then rank against a ruler no
  dossier used, and the per-candidate write-ups would cite different numbers from the batch
  verdict.
- **Both, and report the difference.** Most defensible and the cost is one ~2.3h floor run
  (10 draws at arity 3; the fix means it can now be 20 if wanted). If the ranking is unchanged,
  that is a one-line "the collision did not matter here" and the question is closed properly
  rather than carried. If it changes, that is a finding in itself.

Recommend the third. Note the recomputed floor is NOT comparable draw-for-draw to the committed
one (`docs/CONVENTIONS.md` — a recompute after 2026-08-26 differs wherever substitution fired),
so the comparison is band-to-band, not draw-to-draw.

## Do not confuse with

- `fps-3jj.23` — measures the texture ICC to set `MAX_RULER_ARITY`. Different quantity, different
  purpose. This bead is about one specific committed artifact.
- `fps-3jj.22` — high-arity placebo sources. Unrelated.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A decision recorded on which ruler the retrospective ranks against, with the reason
- [ ] If recomputed: the band-level difference reported, and whether any candidate's
      rejected/inconclusive verdict moves
- [ ] `experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/README.md` § Consequence for existing
      floors updated with the outcome
notes:
Decision (2026-08-27): the retrospective ranks against the COMMITTED ruler. Recompute REFUSED — and the reason is rigour, not cost.

Overturns this bead's own recommendation (option 3, "both, and report the difference"), on three findings:

1. fps-3jj.25's reuse correction does not catch this collision and CANNOT. placebo.effective_n_draws prices shared SOURCE COLUMNS; draws 1 and 10 share none (30 picks, 30 distinct columns), so _resolve_effective_n_draws returns the nominal 10.0 exactly. Against CONVENTIONS' own measured table the machinery charges the cheap channel (same column, different seed: median |rho| 0.038) at icc=0.391 and the expensive one (different column, same seed: max |rho| 0.971) at ZERO. Deliberately NOT fixed: block_seed's never-restarting counter closed the seed channel by construction, so a fix would be unreachable code that also moves the ruler under five written dossiers. Every batch1 facts.json emits a reassuring effective_n_draws: 10.0 for a bank worth ~8.6 — do not quote that field as evidence a band is clean.

2. The bias is exactly computable with no compute, and is monotone-HARDENING so it can only demote, never promote. Priced at the pair's observed 0.836 correlation the bank is worth 8.57 effective draws: bar moves -0.1670 -> -0.1727 (1 candidate) and -0.2706 -> -0.2850 (5 candidates, the batch gate). No candidate is wrongly FAILED by the committed ruler; only one inside |z| in [1.9226, 1.9797) at nc=1 or [2.9591, 3.1030) at nc=5 could be wrongly PASSED. Free per-row check, now a standing instruction in docs/routines/retrospective.md. All four dossiered candidates (|z| = 0.523 / 0.926 / 0.987 / 1.805) sit outside it; tgp_cycle_displacement gets the same check when it runs.

3. The recompute is a WORSE instrument than the closed form. A fresh 10-draw band estimates its own std to +/-23.6% (1/sqrt(2(n-1))) = +/-0.0697 c/L on the nc=5 bar — 4.8x the 0.0144 c/L bias it would remove. Its "difference" would be dominated by resampling luck: a ranking change unattributable, no change proving nothing. Compounded by the existing non-comparability rule for post-2026-08-26 recomputes.

Incidental: the retired noise_floor_k1.json carries the same defect (20 draws, two collided pairs on seeds 97 and 101, n_eff likewise reading nominal 20.0). It is the k=1 baseline behind CONVENTIONS' "two thirds of the k1->k3 move is thinness, not arity" attribution. Both floors biased the same direction, so it self-cancels: the gap moves -0.0536 -> -0.0637 c/L at nc=5. THE TWO-THIRDS CLAIM SURVIVES — cite it without a caveat. Recorded so nobody re-derives the concern.

Landed doc-only on main: 1c56a52, 7336945 (docs/CONVENTIONS.md, docs/routines/retrospective.md, experiments/2026-08-26_placebo_draw_independence/README.md). All 14 quoted numbers verified against a clean recomputation.
title: batch1's committed ruler carries the seed collision — does the retrospective need to account for it?

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` builds `facts.json`, which is the ONLY thing a
dossier session reads. Three fields that materially change how a run reads are computed
and retained elsewhere but never make it in:

1. **`meta.realised_seed`** (in `results.json`). `_provenance()` carries `meta["seeds"]`
   — the WFCV screen's seed list — but not the single seed the realised backtest ran on.
   A dossier therefore prints "seeds [42, 43, 44, 45, 46]" next to a headline CPL that is
   one draw with no error bar. Fix: add `realised_seed` to `_provenance()`'s dict.

2. **`meta.extra_feature_provider_hits` / `_misses`** (in `results.json`). These say how
   much of the realised replay ran with the candidate's columns absent. `_check_provider_health`
   only errors at 100% misses, so partial coverage passes silently — batch1 ran at 9.6%
   (607/6300) on every candidate and no dossier could report it. Fix: carry both counts
   (or the derived miss rate) into `facts["validation"]`, beside the existing
   `candidate_column_nan_rate` — which describes the OFFLINE frame and is easily misread
   as covering the replay.

3. **`per_column_r2` / `max_column_r2`** (in `experiments/candidates/<batch>/batch.json`,
   written by `redundancy.write_batch_record` at generation time). The block figure is the
   MEAN of the members, so a single lock-redundant column is diluted out of view; the
   per-column numbers already exist and answer the "is this just <locked column> in
   different clothes?" falsification test that several candidates declare. Fix: read the
   batch record in `build_facts` and surface it, e.g. `facts["redundancy"]`.

## Why I noticed this

Reviewing `experiments/candidates/batch1/lga_trough_propagation/` on 2026-08-26. All
three gaps let a plausible-but-wrong reading reach the committed dossier and its
ledger.yaml entry. Details in that dossier's "Review addendum — 2026-08-26" section.

For (3) specifically: the candidate's declared falsification test named
`lga_trough_breadth_7d` as the suspect column, but the retained `per_column_r2` shows
`lga_leader_lead_days` at 0.855 is the most lock-reconstructible member — the opposite
column. The grading session could not see it.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py (`_provenance`, `_validation`, `build_facts`)
- experiments/pipeline/redundancy.py (a reader for the retained batch record)
- docs/routines/dossier.md (Facts section — already amended to REQUIRE stating the
  realised seed; this bead makes it available from facts.json rather than results.json)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `facts.json` carries `realised_seed` distinctly from the WFCV `seeds` list
- [ ] `facts.json` carries the provider hit/miss counts under validation
- [ ] `facts.json` carries per-column R² against the lock from the batch record
- [ ] Absent/legacy inputs degrade gracefully (older results.json lack these keys)
title: facts.json omits realised_seed, provider hit/miss counts, and per-column R²

description:
## What

The NSW FuelCheck published price history for roughly **12-24 March 2022** is
incomplete at source. This is not a bug in this project and there is no alternative
source. It needs recording as a known data limitation so results spanning that window
are not read as signal.

## Evidence

Row counts in `data/raw/` (NSW bulk CSVs as downloaded, before any processing), all
grades, all NSW:

```
10/03/2022   3581
12/03/2022    289
13/03/2022    163
16/03/2022     95
20/03/2022     49     <- ~98% below normal
25/03/2022    727
29/03/2022    691
30/03/2022   2836
01/04/2022   8882
```

`data/cleaned/` mirrors this exactly, so nothing in this project's download, clean or
ingest path caused it.

Corroboration: in the batch1 DB, P95 and P98 sit at **zero events statewide** from
2022-03-11 to 2022-03-29 while E10/U91 continue at reduced volume. Zero premium price
changes across NSW for 19 days is not a market condition. Meanwhile the network E10
median moved 183.9 -> 176.9 -> 185.8 -> 198.9 across the same window, so the missing
stations were demonstrably not holding a flat price.

The 2022-03-30/31 spike (515 and 549 stations reporting E10) is the federal fuel excise
cut (~22 c/L, effective 30 March 2022) forcing a near-universal reprice.

## No alternative source exists (checked 2026-08-25)

- **data.nsw.gov.au** publishes exactly one March 2022 resource,
  `d707be7a-dbb9-47a7-ae57-599428731fac` ("FuelCheck Price History March 2022", XLSX,
  2.08 MB, created 04/04/2022). It has never been revised - metadata last touched
  01/05/2022, data last updated 04/04/2022. There is no replacement or corrected file.
- **Our extraction is complete.** Rows per MB of published XLSX is near-constant across
  neighbouring months: Feb 51,441 rows / 2.63 MB = 19.6k/MB; Mar 39,496 / 2.08 MB =
  19.0k/MB; Apr 71,771 / 3.62 MB = 19.8k/MB. We got the whole file; the file is small.
- **data.gov.au** harvests the same NSW dataset and points at the same resources. Not
  an independent copy.
- **NSW real-time Fuel API** (api.nsw.gov.au Product 22, V1 NSW / V2 NSW+Tas) serves
  live prices only. It cannot be queried retrospectively for 2022.
- **data/snapshots/** in this repo starts 2026-08. No 2022 coverage.

Conclusion: the gap is permanent. Plan around it rather than trying to fill it.

## Related, and now resolved: composition drift

This event is also what produced the panel jump (575 -> 642 stations) that the original
fps-ghr was filed about. That question is now **measured and bounded** - no action
needed, recorded here so it is not re-investigated:

Chain-linked index test (each day's change measured only over stations present on both
consecutive days, then cumulated; divergence from the naive mean is composition drift
by construction), 2021-11-05..2025-04-17, 1260 dates x 714 stations:

- total drift over 3.4 years: **+0.461 c/L**; range -1.181 .. +0.568
- daily |drift change|: **median exactly 0.0000**, p99 0.0959, max 0.5669 (2022-06-29)
- concentrated in ~8 days across 3.4 years

So composition churn moves the network aggregates by up to ~0.6 c/L on a handful of
days and nil otherwise. It feeds `station_minus_sydney_avg_cents` and the
`station_minus_lga/brand_mean` derivatives, so those days carry a real bias, but it is
not a first-order threat and does not justify reworking the aggregates on its own.

Also found: the count of LGAs with a computed `lga_mean_cents` steps 28 -> 30 exactly
at 2022-06-28 as two LGAs cross the ">=3 non-Sticky stations" floor - composition
changes feature *availability*, not just level.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] March 2022 hole documented where an analyst will actually hit it (docs/, and the
      negative-results ledger header or an equivalent "known data limitations" note)
- [ ] Decide how folds spanning 2022-03 are treated in evaluation - excluded, flagged,
      or accepted with a caveat - and record the decision
- [ ] Check whether any other window in 2016-2026 shows the same signature (a
      panel-wide collapse in daily event counts); if so, document those too
- [ ] Composition-drift numbers above recorded so the question is not reopened

## Related

- fps-ghr - the fill-cap defect that turns this 2-3 week source hole into a 125+ day
  exclusion for 81 stations
title: NSW source data for 12-24 March 2022 is incomplete and unrecoverable - document as a known limitation

description:
## What

The experiment pipeline's `decision_flips` instrument diffs the two arms'
`fills.parquet` on the key `(fold, station_code, date)`. A fill that happens on the
SAME day in both arms but at a DIFFERENT volume is therefore counted as a common
fill, not as a flip — so the flip table understates how much the arms actually
diverge, and `flip_cpl_baseline`/`flip_cpl_candidate` are pooled over an incomplete
set of differing fills.

Add volume-difference detection: report same-date-different-litres fills as a third
category alongside `n_baseline_only` / `n_candidate_only`, and either fold them into
the flip CPL pools or report them separately.

## Why I noticed this

Found while reviewing `experiments/candidates/batch1/station_descent_dynamics`
(fps-6to). Measured on that run's own `fills.parquet`:

- 439 counted date-flips, but **150 volume-only changes invisible to the metric**.
- Fold 12 is the sharpest case: 13 volume-only changes against only 14 date-flips —
  roughly half that fold's real divergence is unreported.
- Fold 1 has 21 baseline-only and 0 candidate-only fills, making
  `flip_cpl_candidate` 0/0 and `flip_cpl_delta` null. The dossier read that as a
  "candidate stopped buying" shape. It is not: total litres are identical
  (1539.286 L both arms), and 16 of the 169 common fills carry different volumes.
  The real shape is deferral onto fewer, larger, later fills. The null is entirely
  an artifact of this blind spot.

Note total litres purchased is NOT always equal across arms (folds 2, 4, 5, 6, 8,
12 differ; fold 12 by 64 L = 3.9%), so volume accounting needs care rather than an
assumption of parity.

## Files likely affected

- the pipeline module computing `facts["decision_flips"]` (grep for
  `n_baseline_only` under `experiments/`)
- `experiments/candidates/batch1/station_descent_dynamics/README.md` — carries an
  "Instrument caveat" paragraph referencing this bead

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Volume-only differences are detected and counted, not silently pooled as common
- [ ] Flip CPL pools have a documented, tested rule for same-date-different-volume fills
- [ ] A fold where the candidate opens no new buy dates no longer yields a bare null
      with no explanation of the shape
- [ ] Test covers: same date + different litres; unequal total litres between arms
title: decision_flips is blind to volume-only changes (same date, different litres)

description:
## What

A reusable helper (new module, e.g. `experiments/lib/flips.py`) that
identifies individual buy/wait decision flips between two arms (R0 vs
candidate) and reports how much of the realised CPL delta each flip is
responsible for — so "a few large flips carry the delta" can be told apart
mechanically from "one outlier fold/event carries it," instead of by
eyeballing fold-aggregated numbers.

## Why I noticed this

Dossiering `network_move_breadth` (batch1, fps-2l9,
`experiments/candidates/batch1/network_move_breadth/`), the candidate's own
`PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` was specific: the mechanism should show up as a FEW
LARGE decision flips (WAIT->BUY caught early on a restoration), not a smooth
pooled delta. But `dossier_tables.py` only writes fold-level
`delta_cpl_own` into `facts.json` (per_fold, per_regime) — the right
granularity for the *economics* (a fold is an independent tank simulation,
see `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` § Bucketed results), but too coarse to check this
specific claim. The run's headline sat inside the noise band and one shock
fold (13, -1.325 c/L) carried almost the whole regime-level effect; I could
not tell whether that's the predicted few-large-flips mechanism or a single
outlier fold, and graded the signature "inconclusive" partly for that reason
(see the run's `facts.json`'s `grading` block and README `## Judgement`).

**This isn't a one-off gap.** The same "how many decisions actually changed,
and how much did each one matter" question has been answered ad hoc, by hand,
at least twice before, never as a reusable tool:
- `experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/README.md` — "at 1d, moving tau
  0.25->0.35 changes 422 buy/wait decisions and moves pooled CPL 0.062 c/L,"
  computed inline for that one sweep, not via a shared helper.
- `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/README.md` — "the two arms
  differ on 11 of 752 fills (1.5%)" and "one buy/wait decision flip is worth
  ~0.05 c/L pooled" — also computed ad hoc for that run. Note per
  `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` that the ~0.05 c/L figure is a 7-day-cadence quantity,
  NOT a portable constant — a reusable tool must compute its own
  per-batch/per-cadence quantum rather than hardcoding one.

**Manual spot-check on network_move_breadth's fold 13, done by hand
2026-08-24 (not yet a reusable tool — this is exactly what this bead should
make routine):** diffing `fills.parquet` on `(station_code, date)` between
the R0 and candidate arms found 20 differing fills across 4 stations, not
one dominant flip like the `tgp_delta_7d` precedent. Breakdown: station 585
(2 fills each side) delta -25.14 c/L — a clean one-day-early catch at 172.9
vs R0's 207.9 the next day; station 18517 (6 fills each side, spanning
Oct 2024 - Jan 2025) delta -6.02 c/L — a sustained "different tank-refill
timing" cascade, genuinely favourable, not a wash; station 414 (2 R0 / 1
candidate) delta +6.00 c/L — candidate bought early and paid MORE, a real
loss; station 429 (1 candidate fill, no R0 counterpart) not comparable. Net:
3 of 4 comparable stations favour the candidate, one doesn't — a real, mixed
effect spread across several stations, not a single-fold/single-flip
artifact. This is useful precedent for validating whatever this bead builds
(the manual numbers above should reproduce exactly).

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/lib/realised.py` — `RealisedResult.fills` is a per-arm ledger
  of actual BUY events only (`_fill_row`); a WAIT day writes no row, so a
  naive date-set diff between two arms' `fills.parquet` approximates a flip
  (a date where one arm bought and the other didn't) but conflates a true
  decision-crossing with path-dependent cascade effects (tank state at a
  later date depends on every earlier decision) — see station 18517 above
  for a real example of that cascade.
- `experiments/lib/rowpreds.py` / `rowpreds.parquet` — per-row calibrated
  `proba` per (run, seed, station_code, price_date), independent of tank
  state. This is the cleaner substrate: join R0 vs candidate `proba` on
  `(station_code, price_date)`, threshold each at its own arm's tau (or held
  tau), and flag rows where the thresholded decision differs. Note
  `docs/routines/dossier.md`'s existing caveat that rowpreds only covers the
  WFCV-validation-window rows, not the full frame (`per_axis_coverage_note`).
- `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` — see the mechanical trigger
  below; this is where the new `decision_flips` block gets computed and
  written into `facts.json`.

## When this runs — a MECHANICAL trigger, not a per-run judgement call

Discussed with the owner 2026-08-24: don't make this a diagnostic a session
runs "when it seems helpful." That reintroduces exactly the inconsistency
`fps-3jj.17` was filed to remove from ledger outcomes — some dossiers would
get the deeper look and some wouldn't, for reasons nobody recorded, and a
later reader can't tell "nothing to find" from "the session didn't bother."

Instead, `dossier_tables.py`'s Step 0 should compute the `decision_flips`
block unconditionally whenever both hold, using the same `facts.json` fields
`docs/routines/dossier.md` § Step 1.4 already reads:
- `facts["candidate"]["columns"]` has 2+ entries (arity 1 candidates have
  nothing to disaggregate), AND
- `facts["noise_band"]["available"]` is `true` and
  `candidate_z_vs_band` (`z`) is NOT `>= single_candidate_z_threshold` (`t`)
  — i.e. skip only the clean-reject case (candidate is clearly the wrong
  sign vs. the noise band; a flip breakdown adds little once the aggregate
  already says no). Both the `inconclusive` case (`-t < z < t`) and the
  `z <= -t` case (clears noise on the good side, but this pipeline never
  auto-grades `graduated` — see dossier.md) get the block, since both are
  cases a human is likely to look closer at.

When the trigger doesn't fire (arity 1, or noise band unavailable/null, or a
clean reject), `decision_flips` should still be a present-but-explicit field
(e.g. `{"computed": false, "reason": "..."}`) rather than an absent key —
same pattern `noise_band.available` already uses — so no downstream
consumer has to guess whether it was skipped or forgotten.

**Guardrail for how this gets written up once it exists:** a flip-level
story is more vivid than a fold-aggregate number and easy to over-read — one
good anecdote (585's clean catch) can feel more convincing than the
aggregate noise-band test. The dossier's write-up conventions need the same
rule already in place for `per_axis`: flip-level detail is colour
illustrating the mechanism, and must never be presented in a README's
Judgement section as a second arbiter overriding the noise-band call.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A function/module that takes two arms' `rowpreds.parquet` (or a
      `RealisedResult`) plus each arm's tau and returns, per fold, the set
      of `(station_code, price_date)` rows where the thresholded decision
      differs between arms.
- [ ] Reports flip count per fold/regime and the realised-CPL contribution
      attributable to flipped rows vs non-flipped rows, so "few large flips"
      vs "many small flips" is a computed fact, not an eyeball read of
      fold-aggregated deltas.
- [ ] Documents explicitly that a rowpreds-level flip (proba crosses tau
      differently) is not the same thing as a fills.parquet-level
      extra/missing fill (tank state is path-dependent) — states which one
      is being computed and why.
- [ ] Wired into `dossier_tables.py` Step 0 behind the mechanical trigger
      above (arity >= 2 AND noise band available AND not a clean reject),
      writing a `decision_flips` block into `facts.json` — present with an
      explicit `computed: false` + reason when the trigger doesn't fire,
      never just absent.
- [ ] `docs/routines/dossier.md` updated with the write-up guardrail above
      (flip detail is colour, not a second arbiter) alongside the existing
      `per_axis` one.
- [ ] Applied (or explicitly deferred to a follow-up) to re-grade
      `network_move_breadth`'s signature verdict now that the tool exists —
      the manual fold-13 numbers above are the expected reproduction target.
title: Build a reusable per-decision-flip attribution helper

description:
## What

The next turn of the crank. The generator's cadence is an EVENT — "the batch1 queue
has drained and its outcome is recorded" — not an interval, which is exactly why it
is invoked interactively and never scheduled (`docs/routines/generator.md` §
"Decided: interactive, not scheduled"). This bead exists so that event has somewhere
to land instead of being remembered.

Two halves, in order:

1. **Freeze batch2.** `experiments/pipeline/batch_freeze.py` + `noise_floor.py`.
   batch1's floor does NOT carry forward: a new freeze means new draws, possibly new
   columns and possibly a new cadence, so the honest detection bar has to be
   recomputed. **batch1's `-0.15` / `-0.22` c/L are batch1-specific numbers — do not
   quote them for batch2.** Budget ~3.8h wall for the 20-draw floor and do not try to
   shortcut it; it is the gate, not overhead. If anything graduated out of batch1,
   the lock has moved and `baseline_fingerprint` will differ from `54:1a6ec2d84a69`.
2. **Run the generator.** Read `docs/routines/generator.md` in full first. batch2 is
   sized at 10-15 candidates (`generator.md` § Batch sizing), not 5.

## Inputs that will be new by then

- `experiments/ledger.yaml` will carry 5 more entries. Read every one's `not_tested`,
  not just the outcome codes — that field is what stops the next generator being timid.
- batch1's `RETROSPECTIVE.md` (fps-3jj.18.1), including the mechanism-family
  concentration observation. If batch1's two cross-sectional-consensus candidates
  both landed the same way, that is information about the FAMILY, not just about
  those two columns.
- `fps-3jj.10` — human-sourced leads deliberately held back from batch1 so the first
  batch measured what the model proposes unaided. Merge them in here.

## Do at filing time (the convention batch1 established, 2026-08-23)

Create a **parent bead for the batch** (`fps-3jj.18` is the batch1 template), with the
candidate beads as children and the post-drain tasks (retrospective, outcome-action)
as children too. batch1's candidate beads were filed flat and reparented afterwards;
do it in one step here.
title: batch2: freeze the batch and run the generator (10-15 candidates)

description:
HYPOTHESIS: The retail trough is bounded below by the wholesale floor, so how far the
floor has MOVED since this cycle's retail peak sets how deep this particular trough
can go. A cycle that began when the floor was 6 c/L higher than it is now has room for
a deeper trough than a cycle of identical length and phase whose floor never moved.
Neither TGP expression tested so far asks this. station_minus_tgp_cents reads today's
floor LEVEL (accurate when the floor is stable, misleading when it is moving — which
is exactly how it failed). tgp_delta_7d reads the floor's velocity over a FIXED 7-day
window with no relationship to where the retail cycle is. Anchoring the displacement
to the cycle's own peak makes it a depth-remaining statistic instead of a level or a
momentum term.

TARGET: axis=regime, expect_concentration_in=[normal], folds=[]
(axis "regime" is the RESERVED FOLD-LEVEL name — "normal" means NON-SHOCK FOLDS.)

PREDICTED_SIGNATURE: Decision-timing. On rows where the floor has fallen a long way
since the peak, the model should WAIT past the point the lock would buy, because the
trough it is approaching is deeper than the network clock implies; where the floor has
been flat or has risen since the peak, it should buy earlier. Expect the effect on
NON-SHOCK folds — the mechanism is about the floor setting trough depth in an ordinary
cycle, and the shock folds are exactly where the previous TGP gap candidate was
measured to HURT (+0.011 log-loss). A SHOCK-concentrated win here would therefore be
evidence AGAINST the stated mechanism rather than for it, and should be read as such.
Magnitude expectation is small: results.csv history puts single-column features at
0.03-0.26 c/L and both prior TGP expressions landed inside the noise band.

CONFIDENCE_EFFECT: 0.30
CONFIDENCE_ZONE: 0.55
(ZONE deliberately ABOVE EFFECT: I am much more confident about WHERE this would show
up than about WHETHER it shows up, because the shock-axis behaviour of the TGP gap is
already measured and points the other way.)

MECHANISM_FAMILY: wholesale-lead

PRIOR_ART: Adjacent to two ledger entries on the same upstream series.
(1) station_minus_tgp_cents — REJECTED: helps calm (-0.012) but hurts shock (+0.011),
because today's TGP is accurate when the floor is stable and misleading when it is
moving. Its not_tested says outright: "AND THE OPEN ONE: whether the gap helps on
LATE-DESCENT rows specifically. It was rejected on the SHOCK axis, which is not the
axis its mechanism targets — the same oracle diagnostic that fed this rejection also
measured gap -> depth-remaining at r2=0.63."
(2) tgp_delta_7d — INCONCLUSIVE (+0.0059 c/L on the corrected 54-column baseline; the
June 2026 graduation retracted 2026-08-19). Its not_tested names "horizons between 7
and 14 days" and "whether ANY TGP expression helps on the LATE-DESCENT axis
specifically".
What differs mechanically: this is neither a level nor a fixed-window velocity. It is
a DISPLACEMENT between two dates chosen by the retail cycle itself — immune to the
level's stability problem (a difference, so the reconstruction's unknown constant
cancels) and with a horizon set by the cycle's age rather than an arbitrary 7 days. It
is also NOT the gap: it never compares a retail price to a wholesale price, so it
cannot reproduce the floor-proximity brake that cancelled velocity's pre-spike buy in
gap_x_vel7 (also rejected). Successor context: bd fps-x0f asks whether ANY TGP
expression earns a place rather than assuming one has.

CONSTRUCTION NOTE (read before judging the result): the frame carries the floor's
7-day CHANGE, never its level, and no new dataset may be pulled in. The level is not
needed. Writing S(t) for the trailing 7-day sum of the floor, tgp(u) - tgp(u-7) =
S(u) - S(u-1), so cumulating tgp_delta_7d/7 telescopes EXACTLY to MA7(t) -
MA7(origin). The origin's unknown constant is common to every row and cancels in the
peak-to-today difference. So the column is an exact 7-day-SMOOTHED floor displacement,
not a proxy — but it is smoothed, and a sharp one-day wholesale move is attenuated.

COLUMN COUNT: 2 (tgp_cycle_displacement_cents, tgp_cycle_displacement_frac_amp) —
recorded for fps-3jj.14's arity calibration.

SCREEN (experiments/candidates/batch1/batch.md, full frame, 2,084,203 rows):
block R^2 vs the locked 54 = 0.574 (max single column 0.583, flag at 0.9). Note the
screen's predictor set is the LOCK ONLY, which excludes tgp_delta_7d
(NON_MODEL_COLUMNS, evaluated-inconclusive) — PR #331 fixed exactly that bias, which
had scored batch0's own tgp_delta_7d at block R^2 = 1.000 and told against this
ground specifically. Highest cross-candidate |rho| involving this candidate: nothing
in the reported top-10. Within-candidate |rho| 0.853 (disclosure only, never gated).
Validation harness clean; NaN rate 0.05%.

Batch: experiments/batches/batch1
Module: experiments/candidates/batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement.py
title: tgp_cycle_displacement candidate — wholesale displacement over the retail cycle (batch1)

description:
HYPOTHESIS: cycle_pct_through is a NETWORK clock (one value per date), but a
station's willingness to follow that clock is a per-station property. A chronically
cheap, competitive station tracks the cycle closely: at phase 0.9 it really is near
its own trough. A chronically dear or erratic station is only loosely coupled to it —
the same phase reading carries much less information about where that station's price
is going next. So the SAME clock value should drive different buy/wait decisions at
different stickiness levels. The lock hands the model both terms separately and
nothing else; a gradient-boosted tree can only approximate their product through
nested axis-aligned splits, which is the representation limit that made the LGA and
network groups worth engineering explicitly.

TARGET: axis=regime, expect_concentration_in=[], folds=[]
NO ZONE CLAIM, deliberately — only CONFIDENCE_EFFECT is graded. A cross-sectional
station property has no reason to prefer any fold, and stating a spread-out
expectation honestly is worth more to the calibration record than inventing a zone.

PREDICTED_SIGNATURE: Decision-timing. For stations with near-zero stickiness the
decisions should be essentially unchanged (the product is ~0 there, so the columns add
nothing), and the flips should concentrate on the TAILS of the stickiness distribution
— buying EARLIER on high-|stickiness| stations at late phase, because the network
clock is over-promising a trough those stations will not fully follow. The
distinctive signature to look for is that the SIGNED and ABSOLUTE columns are both used
and disagree in orientation somewhere in the SHAP surface. If only abs_sticky_x_phase
is used, the real content is "outlier stations are decoupled" rather than a saddle — a
weaker and different claim. Expect it to spread across folds rather than concentrate.

CONFIDENCE_EFFECT: 0.35
CONFIDENCE_ZONE: 0.15
MECHANISM_FAMILY: station-heterogeneity-interaction

PRIOR_ART: The saddle itself is the one item in experiments/ledger.yaml flagged as
open and never pursued: "Left genuinely open: the stickiness x cycle_pct_through
opposite-orientation saddle, surfaced unexpectedly in step 1 and never pursued"
(2026-06-05_phase_lookup_nonparametric, not_tested). Adjacent to two rejected
candidates from the SAME experiments, and the difference matters: both of those
(station_price_cents - interp(trough, peak, cycle_pct_through), and the non-parametric
E[norm_price | phase] lookup) engineered a PHASE-RESIDUAL and both failed the same way
— additive-neutral, ablation-negative, because the diagonal projection DISCARDS the
absolute anchors the sibling features carry. The durable constraint recorded there is
"no phase-residual variant should be pursued without an architecture that PRESERVES
the absolute anchors". This candidate is not a residual: it ADDS two columns and
removes nothing, so every anchor stays in place. Also adjacent to A_x_shallow_elong
(#231, rejected and backwards) as another explicit interaction column — noted as a
real warning, not dismissed. The difference is that #231's interaction was built on a
corner the oracle diagnostic had already shown A reads MISLEADINGLY, whereas neither
stickiness_score nor cycle_pct_through has been shown to misread anywhere. Also see
feedback_partner_score_substitution (a partner-score plateau conflates substitution
with interaction) as the standing caution. project_sticky_station_exclusion is not
violated: nothing is aggregated, this is a per-row product.

COLUMN COUNT: 2 (sticky_x_phase, abs_sticky_x_phase) — recorded for fps-3jj.14's
arity calibration.

SCREEN (experiments/candidates/batch1/batch.md, full frame, 2,084,203 rows):
block R^2 vs the locked 54 = 0.450 (max single column 0.722, flag at 0.9). Highest
cross-candidate |rho| involving this candidate: nothing in the reported top-10 —
both columns are effectively uncorrelated with the rest of the batch, and their
within-candidate |rho| is 0.019. Validation harness clean; NaN rate 2.6% (the
stickiness_score NaN rate on the live frame).

Batch: experiments/batches/batch1
Module: experiments/candidates/batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle.py
title: stickiness_phase_saddle candidate — the stickiness x cycle-phase saddle (batch1)

description:
HYPOTHESIS: The Sydney trough is not a moment, it is a wave — individual LGAs bottom
on different days and the wave runs from a known set of early LGAs outward. The 35
days_since_trough_entry_<lga> clocks are all in the lock, but the model reduces them
through 35 axis-aligned splits, and the ONE cross-sectional summary it is handed
(lga_phase_std) is a dispersion statistic: sign-blind and order-blind. Std cannot
distinguish "a third of the network has just bottomed and the rest is about to
follow" from "a third bottomed six weeks ago and the rest is mid-descent", yet those
are opposite buy/wait situations. Breadth (how many have turned), its velocity (is
the wave still spreading) and the leaders' head start (is there anyone left to
follow) recover exactly what the std discards.

TARGET: axis=regime, expect_concentration_in=[normal], folds=[]
(axis "regime" is the RESERVED FOLD-LEVEL name — "normal" here means NON-SHOCK FOLDS,
not zones.assign_regime()'s row-level cycle phase, which shares the level name.)

PREDICTED_SIGNATURE: Decision-timing. The model should keep waiting while
lga_trough_breadth_delta_3d is positive and lga_leader_lead_days is large (the wave is
still arriving, cheaper prices still spreading), and buy once breadth velocity rolls
over toward zero with leader lead already collapsed (everyone who was going to cut has
cut, and the restoration is next). Expect the flips to be WAIT -> BUY moves a few days
earlier than the lock makes them, concentrated on NON-SHOCK folds: the wave is a
property of the ordinary cycle, and in a shock window the wholesale move overrides the
propagation order entirely. FALSIFYING signature: gains driven by
lga_trough_breadth_7d's LEVEL alone with the velocity and leader-lead columns inert —
that would mean this is lga_phase_std in different clothes rather than the order
information it claims to add.

CONFIDENCE_EFFECT: 0.45
CONFIDENCE_ZONE: 0.45
MECHANISM_FAMILY: lead-lag-propagation

PRIOR_ART: Directly adjacent to family C (lga_phase_std, lga_phase_std_delta_3d —
GRADUATED, in the lock), whose ledger entry records exactly this as untested:
"Whether a leader-WEIGHTED consensus beats an unweighted LGA std — the lead/lag roles
are known ... but were never used to weight this statistic." What differs mechanically:
lga_phase_std is the sample std of the same 35 clocks, a scale statistic invariant to
WHICH LGAs hold which values; these are order/level statistics over the same panel and
are invariant to nothing. A dispersion measure and a breadth count can move in opposite
directions (std rises when a few LGAs run far ahead; breadth rises only when many have
already turned), so this is not a reparameterisation. Also adjacent to family A and,
through it, to the standing note that A and C both decode "the network is converging on
a trough" — this candidate is in that same super-family and the batch record should be
read with that in mind (see network_move_breadth, the batch's other cross-sectional
candidate). Caveat carried from project_lga_leadership: LGA leadership is TIME-VARYING,
and the Phase 4 SHAP verdict retired Penrith (directionally right, predictively inert —

confirming Blue Mountains and Randwick. The leader set in the module is therefore the

lga_leader_lead_days) — recorded for fps-3jj.14's arity calibration.

Batch: experiments/batches/batch1
Module: experiments/candidates/batch1/lga_trough_propagation.py
title: lga_trough_propagation candidate — how far the trough wave has spread across LGAs (batch1)

description:
HYPOTHESIS: The retail descent is a sequence of discrete cuts, and the SHAPE of a
station's own cut sequence says how much of the descent is left. A station still
cutting 1-2 c/day is mid-descent; a station whose recent pace has collapsed toward
zero while its 14-day pace was steep has arrived at its floor and is now exposed to
the restoration. The lock cannot express this. Measured on the live frame, EVERY
dynamic column in the lock is network-level (max 1 distinct value per date):
cycle_pct_through, cycle_days_since_peak, cycle_mean_length, cycle_last_min_cents,
cycle_last_max_cents, cycle_peak_count, network_px_std*, lga_phase_std*. The only
station-varying locked columns are contemporaneous LEVEL differences — none of them
is a rate. station_minus_last_min_cents is the closest substitute and is a distance
to a NETWORK trough, not a station velocity.

TARGET: axis=regime, expect_concentration_in=[], folds=[3, 7]
Fold-expressed on purpose: a row-level cycle-phase axis cannot carry a COST claim
(path-coupled pooled CPL, fps-grp) and folds can. 3 and 7 are the two folds the
ledger names on the elongation / descent-shape axis (fold 3 is the counterexample
where A helps extended descent strongly at -0.26; fold 7 is the shallow-elongated
problem fold). Only the fold claim is graded — expect_concentration_in is empty.

PREDICTED_SIGNATURE: Decision-timing, not accuracy. The model should stop waiting
earlier on rows where station_descent_decel has gone positive (recent pace slower
than the trailing pace) at moderate cycle_pct_through, and keep waiting longer where
it is negative (cuts still accelerating). Expect a MODEST number of buy/wait flips
concentrated in elongated cycles, where the network clock and the station's own pace
diverge most — i.e. exactly the shallow-vs-steep-within-elongated distinction the
#214 oracle diagnostic found invisible in network_px_std until phase > 1.4. If the
mechanism is real, per-fold contributions should be largest in folds 3 and 7 and
near-zero elsewhere; a UNIFORM improvement across all 14 folds would be evidence the
columns are working as generic momentum rather than as a descent-shape reading.

CONFIDENCE_EFFECT: 0.45
CONFIDENCE_ZONE: 0.30
MECHANISM_FAMILY: station-own-price-dynamics

PRIOR_ART: Adjacent to three rejected attempts on the shallow-elongated corner, all
of which built their fix out of family A (network_px_std): elongation_ratio +
cycle_descent_slope_so_far (R_raw, #214 — rejected, fold 7 +0.0092),
is_extended_shallow_descent (null, ~-0.0001), and A_x_shallow_elong / A_x_other /
A_x_smooth (#231 — rejected and BACKWARDS, fold 7 went +0.018 -> +0.040). What
differs mechanically: all three supplied the model with derived NETWORK quantities
(dispersion, network cycle elongation, network descent slope). The ledger's own
not_tested on the A_x_* entry says the open ground is "whether any OTHER intra-series
signal carries the shallow-vs-steep-within-elongated distinction — the oracle
diagnostic tested A specifically and is silent about trough-proximity, cross-LGA/brand
late-descent consensus...". These columns are neither A nor a network aggregate: they
are the individual station's own cut sequence, a quantity with no representative at
all in the 54-column lock. Also adjacent to cycle_mean_length (rejected, "accuracy !=
objective"): this candidate makes NO claim to estimate the cycle better, only to
change WHEN the model acts.

COLUMN COUNT: 3 (station_px_change_3d, station_px_change_14d,
station_descent_decel) — recorded for fps-3jj.14's arity calibration. Note
station_descent_decel is an exact linear combination of the other two and is supplied
deliberately: a gradient-boosted tree splits on axis-aligned thresholds and cannot
form a linear combination of two features.

SCREEN (experiments/candidates/batch1/batch.md, full frame, 2,084,203 rows):
block R^2 vs the locked 54 = 0.408 (max single column 0.642, flag at 0.9) — the
LOWEST in the batch, consistent with the "no representative in the lock" claim.
Highest cross-candidate |rho| involving this candidate = 0.445
(station_px_change_3d <-> network_move_breadth.network_rise_breadth_3d), gate 0.85.
Within-candidate |rho| 0.903 (station_px_change_3d <-> station_descent_decel) —
disclosure only, never gated. Validation harness clean; max NaN rate 1.24%.

Batch: experiments/batches/batch1
Module: experiments/candidates/batch1/station_descent_dynamics.py
title: station_descent_dynamics candidate — the station's own descent trajectory (batch1)

description:
HYPOTHESIS: The Sydney cycle ends with a coordinated restoration: a subset of
stations jumps 20-30 c/L within a day or two and the rest follow over the next few
days. For a buyer the cost of being one day late to that turn dwarfs the gain from
one more day of a 1-2 c/L descent, so the single most valuable thing the model could
know is that peers have STARTED jumping while this station has not. It cannot
currently know it: network_px_std measures the SPREAD of the cross-section and is
invariant to direction — a handful of stations 20 c/L above the pack and a handful
20 c/L below produce the same reading. Counting the share of stations moving UP
versus DOWN over a fixed window recovers the sign the dispersion statistic throws
away, as a participation count robust to the size of any one station's jump.

TARGET: axis=regime, expect_concentration_in=[shock], folds=[]
(axis "regime" is the RESERVED FOLD-LEVEL name — SHOCK_FOLDS {1,4,9,13} vs the rest
— not zones.assign_regime()'s row-level cycle phase, which shares the level name
"normal".)

PREDICTED_SIGNATURE: Decision-timing, in the most direct form in this batch. Rows
where network_rise_breadth_delta_2d turns sharply positive should flip WAIT -> BUY
one to three days earlier than the lock manages, and the saved cents per flip should
be LARGE (a restoration is worth 20-30 c/L vs ~1-2 c/L for a day of descent). So the
expected signature is FEW decision flips carrying an outsized share of the pooled
delta; if the pooled delta instead comes from many small flips spread evenly, the
columns are working as generic momentum and the restoration-timing story is not what
is paying. network_fall_breadth_3d should mostly cause the model to WAIT longer, so
the two level columns are expected to push in opposite directions, not reinforce.

CONFIDENCE_EFFECT: 0.60
CONFIDENCE_ZONE: 0.35
MECHANISM_FAMILY: directional-network-breadth

PRIOR_ART: Adjacent to family A (network_px_std, network_px_std_delta_3d —
GRADUATED, in the lock) and through it to family C. Stated plainly rather than
relabelled: this batch files TWO cross-sectional-consensus candidates (this one and
lga_trough_propagation) and the batch record should be read with that in mind. What
differs from A: A is a scale statistic (a std) on price LEVELS within a cohort; these
are signed participation COUNTS on price CHANGES. A cannot distinguish up from down
and is dominated by the few largest deviations; a breadth count is direction-explicit
and caps every station's contribution at one vote. A's own ledger not_tested flags
its unresolved defect as "the missing axis is descent shape, not elongation" — a
directional breadth reading is one candidate for that axis, though this module claims
restoration timing specifically. Also adjacent to family B (discount-cohort gap —
REJECTED, flat), whose not_tested asks "whether B's signal lives in its VELOCITY
rather than its level"; this is a velocity-of-participation statistic over the whole
network rather than a level gap between two brand cohorts. Cautionary precedent held
in view: is_post_covid (rejected, null) — "the tree gains nothing from being told".

COLUMN COUNT: 3 (network_rise_breadth_3d, network_fall_breadth_3d,
network_rise_breadth_delta_2d) — recorded for fps-3jj.14's arity calibration.

SCREEN (experiments/candidates/batch1/batch.md, full frame, 2,084,203 rows):
block R^2 vs the locked 54 = 0.522 (max single column 0.671, flag at 0.9);
highest cross-candidate |rho| involving this candidate = 0.593
(network_fall_breadth_3d <-> lga_trough_propagation.lga_trough_breadth_7d),
gate 0.85. Validation harness clean; max NaN rate 0.09%.

description:
## What

Two of the fps-3jj.11 readiness gaps, closed together because they are the same thing
from two ends: the batch record is the artifact that makes MECHANISM_FAMILY legible, and
MECHANISM_FAMILY was the field it most needed.

**#7 — batch record.** `redundancy.write_batch_record` writes `batch.md` + `batch.json`
beside the candidate modules on every screen run. generator.md § Batch record asked for
exactly this (families, the rho matrix marked cross- vs within-candidate, per-candidate
block R^2); nothing produced one, and batch0 never got one.

- JSON because the question the record exists to answer later — "did the generator
  produce five variants of one idea?" — is a group-by, not a close reading.
- Written at SCREEN time, not filing time: these are the numbers that justified filing. A
  record regenerated afterwards measures whatever the modules say *then*, which is the
  residual risk generator.md already accepts for post-filing hand edits.
- Skips loudly rather than guessing if the modules span two directories.

**#5 — MECHANISM_FAMILY was write-only.** generator.md makes it a REQUIRED DISCLOSURE
specifically so that "five uncorrelated candidates that all encode one story" becomes
visible rather than being a gate the generator learns to game. But:

- `runner.py` never copied it into `results.json`, so nothing downstream could see it.
- `dossier_tables.build_facts` therefore had no field for it.
- `retrospective.build_leaderboard` could not report family concentration.
- `experiments/candidates/TEMPLATE.py` — the file a generator session copies — omitted
  the field entirely, so only batch0's hand-written module ever had one.

All four fixed, with tests asserting it reaches facts.json and leaderboard rows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] batch.md + batch.json written by the screen; single-family batch called out; NOT
      DECLARED marked
- [x] MECHANISM_FAMILY reaches results.json -> facts.json -> leaderboard rows
- [x] TEMPLATE.py carries the field
- [x] generator.md § Batch record describes what is generated rather than what to write
title: Batch record writer + MECHANISM_FAMILY plumbing (gaps 7 and 5)

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/redundancy.py` — the two mechanical checks
`docs/routines/generator.md` requires before any bead is filed, as a module rather than
hand-rolled per session:

- Pairwise |rho| ACROSS candidates — HARD GATE. Within-candidate correlation reported,
  never gated (gating it would ban the multi-column group shape by the back door).
- Block R^2 of each candidate against the existing column set — reported and flagged at
  0.9, not gated, matching generator.md's "rework before filing" framing.

## The threshold (fps-3jj.11)

`PAIRWISE_RHO_THRESHOLD = 0.85`, set empirically against the 54 locked columns' own
correlation structure rather than by feel: 25% of locked pairs are already at |rho| >=
0.7 (so a 0.7 gate rejects candidates for being no more similar than a quarter of
production), the highest locked pair is 0.971 (`cycle_pct_through` vs
`cycle_days_since_peak` — the same quantity in two units, both locked), and only ~1%
reach 0.85. Error asymmetry settles the rest: a false reject costs one redesign inside
the generator session, a false accept costs a night of a five-night batch.

## Two bugs the real-data smoke test found that the unit tests did not

1. A one-candidate/one-column batch produces zero pairs; `pd.DataFrame([])` has no
   columns, so sorting on `abs_rho` raised `KeyError`. That is batch0's exact shape.
2. **Five LGA trough columns are 100% NaN in the live frame** (`bayside`, `waverley`,
   `hunters_hill`, `botany_bay`, `lane_cove`), so a complete-case mask over all
   predictors selected ZERO rows and every R^2 came back NaN — a silently useless screen
   reporting `nan` for the whole batch. `placebo.py` meets the same five (INDEX.md: "5
   all-NaN skipped, 49 usable"). Now dropped explicitly, with the count and names
   disclosed in the report, and a NaN block R^2 prints "NOT MEASURED, investigate"
   rather than a bare `nan`.

Sanity check now asserted both in tests and by the smoke run: a candidate that IS an
existing column scores block R^2 = 1.000.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] rho gate + block R^2 implemented, threshold empirically justified in-code
- [x] Within-candidate correlation disclosed, not gated
- [x] Validation runs before columns are correlated (catches a label read here, not in 5 nights)
- [x] 13 tests; both smoke-found bugs have regression coverage
title: Redundancy screen for candidate batches (rho gate + block R2)

description:
## What

`compute_noise_floor` adds exactly ONE placebo column per draw — hardcoded through
`placebo.make_placebo_series`, the function signature, and the CLI (no arity parameter
anywhere). `batch1`'s band (mean -0.0089, std 0.0800, n=20) and the -0.217 c/L
family-wise gate that follows from it are therefore 1-column quantities.

`docs/routines/generator.md` meanwhile argues — correctly, on this project's own history
— that a candidate should be 2-4 columns when the mechanism needs it: the 35 LGA
features went in together, the 4 NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS went in together for ~1 c/L,
and the only feature ever measured alone came in at +0.006 c/L.

So a k-column candidate is graded against a 1-column null. More columns = more
opportunity for the fit to find something, inflating the candidate arm's variance
against a band that doesn't know it. `candidate_z_vs_band` is biased favourable by an
unknown amount.

## Decision (owner, 2026-08-22)

Do NOT cap candidates at one column. Batch1's primary aim is (b) — learning how this
pipeline behaves — so constraining candidate shape to suit the ruler would distort the
exact thing being measured. Measure the gap instead; the ruler's arity sensitivity is
itself an aim-(b) finding, and is reusable for batch2 (10-15 candidates).

## Sequence

Generation happens FIRST — it is cheap and reversible, and the calibration should be
sized to the column counts the batch actually contains rather than a guess.

1. Generator proposes 5 candidates; record each one's column count.
2. Night 0: one calibration noise-floor run at the batch's modal (or max) arity.
3. Nights 1-5: the candidates as normal.

One extra night total.

## Draw count

10 draws, not 20 (~1.9h rather than ~3.8h at 1d cadence). The question is "is the band
materially wider at k=3 than at k=1", not "what is the k=3 band to 3 significant
figures". A gate-quality band is not needed to answer a variance-comparison question.

## Work

- Multi-column placebo draws (k columns per draw, k a parameter).
- `n_placebo_columns` stamped into `noise_floor.json`.
- **Consuming-side guard in `dossier_tables._noise_band`**: refuse to grade a k-column
  candidate against a j-column band. Same failure class as `baseline_fingerprint`,
  `null_method` and `tank_params`, all of which are already guarded — and fps-v8o exists
  because the cadence version of exactly this was missed once.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `compute_noise_floor` takes an arity parameter; payload records it
- [ ] `_noise_band` refuses an arity mismatch with an actionable message
- [ ] Calibration run at batch1's modal arity, 10 draws, recorded
- [ ] Finding written up: how much does the band widen with k?

Parent design: fps-3jj. Blocks the batch1 verdict, not the batch1 runs.
title: Noise floor is a 1-column null; candidates are multi-column — measure the arity gap

description:
## What

`experiments/pipeline/runner.py`'s `STATUS_REJECTED = "rejected"` is the terminal
status written to every candidate's `results.json` after a FULL GRADED RUN
completes — win, loss, or in-between. It is not a verdict; it just means "the
pipeline finished and produced real numbers", as opposed to STATUS_DISQUALIFIED
(structural/contract violation) or STATUS_ABORTED_CANDIDATE (crashed). The name
collides badly with what a human reading raw results.json/facts.json would assume
"rejected" means, and could cause a candidate that actually cleared the noise-band
gate to be misread as having failed.

Rename to `STATUS_GRADED = "graded"` — lines up with `_grade_run()`
(runner.py:568), the function that actually sets it, and carries no value judgment.

## Why I noticed this

Surfaced while explaining the noise-floor honest-detection-bar concept
(fps-aay/fps-cds) to the owner: a candidate scoring like a historical winner
(e.g. -0.15 c/L) but not clearing the family-wise gate would show
`status: "rejected"` in its results.json even though the pipeline didn't reject
it in the everyday sense of the word.

## Scope (confirmed via grep, 2026-08-22)

- **Code**: `experiments/pipeline/runner.py` — constant def (line 132) + 2 write
  sites (line 574, 633) + `TERMINAL_STATUSES` frozenset (line 144).
  `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` — 2 hardcoded literal `"rejected"`
  comparisons (lines 144, 253) that don't even import the constant from
  runner.py — fix that single-sourcing gap in the same change (import
  `STATUS_GRADED` instead of hardcoding the literal).
- **Tests**: `tests/test_launch.py`, `tests/test_dossier_tables.py`,
  `tests/test_retrospective.py`, `tests/test_runner.py` — ~30 occurrences,
  all hardcode the literal string rather than importing the constant.
- **Docs** (prose mentions, update wording not just the token):
  `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/routines/dossier.md`,
  `docs/routines/retrospective.md`, `docs/feature-pipeline.md`.
- **3 historical committed JSON artifacts** — migrate the literal string value,
  not the numbers:
  - `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/results.json`
  - `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/facts.json`
  - `experiments/batches/batch0/retrospective_facts.json`

No backwards-compat shim — this repo's convention is a clean rename + migrate,
not an accept-both-values transition period (small, fixed, known set of
historical files).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `STATUS_REJECTED` renamed to `STATUS_GRADED` (value `"graded"`) in runner.py
- [ ] `dossier_tables.py`'s two literal comparisons replaced with an import of the
      renamed constant
- [ ] All test-file literal occurrences updated to the new value/constant
- [ ] The 5 docs' prose updated to say "graded", not "rejected"
- [ ] The 3 historical JSON artifacts' `status` field values updated to
      `"graded"` (data/numbers unchanged)
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` passes
title: Rename STATUS_REJECTED to STATUS_GRADED (confusing terminal-status naming)

description:
## What

`fuel_signal/backtest.py`'s `--daily-use` CLI option defaults to the literal
`round(50.0 / 14, 3)` = `3.571`, while `TankParams.daily_consumption_litres`
defaults to `50.0 / 14` = `3.5714285714285716`. They are NOT equal:

    CLI default   : 3.571
    TankParams    : 3.5714285714285716
    14d drain diff: 0.006 L

But `format_tank_params` renders daily use as `f"{daily:.3f}"`, so BOTH stamp as
`50/3.571/1d/10%`. A CLI-default run and a bare-`TankParams()` run are therefore
**stamp-identical while consuming marginally differently** — a collision the
fps-15c contract structurally cannot see, since the stamp is the only thing it
compares.

The effect is tiny (0.006 L over a 14-day drain) and may never change a decision.
The problem is the class, not the magnitude: fps-15c's whole premise is that the
stamp cannot disagree with what produced the number.

## Why I noticed this

Flagged by review on PR #323 (fps-oqz, the 7d→1d cadence re-lock) as "pre-existing,
adjacent to the diff" — that PR fixed the same defect class one option away
(`--eval-interval` carried its own hard-coded `default=7`, now sourced from
`TankParams()` and pinned by `test_cli_eval_interval_default_tracks_tankparams`).
Deliberately left out of #323 to keep the re-lock scoped.

## Files likely affected

- `fuel_signal/backtest.py` (the `--daily-use` option, ~line 1067; `format_tank_params`, ~line 357)
- `tests/test_backtest.py`

## Options

1. Source the CLI default from `TankParams().daily_consumption_litres` like
   `--eval-interval` now does. `show_default` then prints `3.5714285714285716`,
   which is ugly but honest.
2. Widen the stamp's precision so the two render differently.
3. Round `TankParams`' own default to 3.571 so CLI and dataclass genuinely agree.
   Changes realised economics very slightly — would need the same re-lock ceremony
   as fps-oqz, so probably not worth it for 0.006 L.

Option 1 is the cheapest honest fix; option 3 is a re-lock and should not be done
casually.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLI `--daily-use` default and `TankParams.daily_consumption_litres` cannot
      silently differ while producing the same stamp
- [ ] A test pins the relationship (mirroring `test_cli_eval_interval_default_tracks_tankparams`)
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` green
title: CLI --daily-use default is a rounded literal that stamp-collides with TankParams

description:
## What

fps-awz's placebo-column construction (`experiments/pipeline/placebo.py`) uses a circular
time-shift, screened against `shift_autocorrelation <= MAX_SHIFT_AUTOCORRELATION` before any
backtest fit runs (`screen_draws`). Verified against a real full screen of batch0's 54 locked
columns: the screen doesn't reject a random subset — it systematically excludes an entire
category of feature. ALL FOUR cycle-magnitude columns (`cycle_last_min_cents`,
`cycle_peak_count`, `cycle_mean_length`, `cycle_last_max_cents`) and every price-LEVEL column
(`station_price_cents`, `lga_mean_cents`, `brand_mean_cents`, `stickiness_score`) failed
screening on batch0 — none of them can ever appear in the bank, at any threshold on this
construction, because a circular shift cannot decorrelate a slowly-varying/level-like series
from itself regardless of offset size. The 20 draws that DID survive were dominated by
counters/phase/differences (12 of 20 were `days_since_trough_entry_<lga>` columns).

## Why this matters

A real candidate feature can be level-like (`experiments/results.csv` has examples). The
noise band this construction produces characterizes "what adding a fast-varying column does
to realised CPL", not "what adding an arbitrary column does" — the null and the thing it
grades aren't drawn from the same population of column-types. Not a bug in the current
construction (it's honest about what it can and can't cover — see `placebo.py`'s own
docstring, added alongside this bead), but a real gap in what the noise floor's band
actually represents, worth closing rather than living with indefinitely.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/pipeline/placebo.py` — a new construction (block-permutation over
  contiguous date ranges, preserving a level-like column's own values within each
  reordered block, is the natural candidate — a circular shift's failure mode here is
  specifically the "adjacent-in-time-implies-similar-value" property, which a block
  reorder breaks without needing the value itself to change often).
- `experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py` — would need to either run a SECOND, separate bank
  for level-like columns, or replace the circular-shift construction outright depending on
  how the new construction's own screening behaves.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decide whether to (a) add a second block-permutation construction alongside the
  circular-shift one, gated to level-like columns only, or (b) replace circular-shift
  entirely if block-permutation turns out to cover both cases adequately
- [ ] Verify the chosen construction against real batch0 data the same way fps-awz's was
  verified (a full screen, not just a few hand-picked columns)
- [ ] Update `placebo.py`'s "NAMED LIMITATION" docstring paragraph once this is closed
title: Placebo-column null systematically excludes level-like features (block-permutation alternative?)

## What

Once fps-awz's real noise-floor recompute has run against batch0 (`noise_floor.py batch0 --force` under the new placebo-column construction), add a short passage to `docs/routines/generator.md` stating the new honest single-candidate detection bar as a number — the generator brief currently deliberately says nothing about effect-size magnitude, because the bar wasn't known until the ruler was rebuilt (fps-awz).
