description:
## What

Run batch setup for batch1: batch_freeze.freeze_batch() against a refreshed
DB, which
since fps-cf8 also computes the batch's noise floor as its own final step.

## Why this needs to be its own bead

It was previously an intention, not a work item — and it is the step where a
batch is
BOUND to (a) a data snapshot, (b) a baseline column contract, (c) a noise
floor, and
(d) a decision cadence. Everything upstream converges here, and nothing
downstream can
be re-pointed afterwards without re-running the whole batch. With no bead
for it, the two
constraints below had nowhere to attach and fps-3jj.11 could have been
generated and
frozen at 7d by simple omission.

## Hard preconditions (both, not either)

- fps-awz — the noise floor currently measures the wrong null (seed-swap
rather
than a placebo column) and the gate reads an empirical rank that cannot
resolve its own
threshold. Freezing before this lands bakes the broken ruler into the batch,
and the
floor is computed AT freeze time, so it cannot be swapped afterwards without
a
re-freeze.
- fps-oqz — the 7d->1d cadence re-lock. Owner's decision 2026-08-21:
**batch1 is to
run at 1d.** A cadence re-lock invalidates any existing noise floor, so
a freeze before
the re-lock is a freeze that must be thrown away.

Landing either one AFTER this freeze means redoing this freeze. Do not start
batch1's
nightly runs with either outstanding.

## Also required before running

- DB refresh is **hard-gated**: if the refresh fails, abort setup. Never
freeze onto stale
data (fps-3jj parent design).
- Record the snapshot date; every dossier states it.
- Confirm the frozen TankParams reads 50/3.571/1d/10%, not the 7d default —
this is
the check that the re-lock actually took effect in the artifact rather than
only in the
source. Depends on fps-15c having made that stamp exist at all.

## Absorbed from fps-cds (closed as superseded 2026-08-22)

fps-cds asked for the same "state the post-rework honest bar as a number"
deliverable this bead's last AC already covers, sourced from a batch0
`--force` recompute that `check_freeze_cadence` (fps-oqz) now refuses post
re-lock — the honest bar has to come from THIS freeze's floor instead, not
a batch0 recompute. Folding in the one thing fps-cds named that this bead's
AC list didn't: `docs/CONVENTIONS.md:101` has a matching TODO placeholder
(added by fps-awz's PR #321) that ALSO needs the real number filled in
alongside generator.md, and its current text still points at the stale
`noise_floor.py batch0 --force` instruction — fix that wording too when
filling it in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] DB refreshed, refresh success verified before freezing
- [ ] batch1 frozen; freeze.json records snapshot date + baseline fingerprint +
the
1d tank stamp
- [ ] Noise floor computed atomically by freeze_batch (fps-cf8), on the fps-
awz null,
with its own fingerprint + cadence stamp matching the freeze
- [ ] The post-rework honest detection bar stated as a number, carried into
docs/routines/generator.md per fps-awz's follow-up note, AND into the
docs/CONVENTIONS.md:101 TODO (fps-cds) — fixing that TODO's stale
`batch0 --force` wording in the same edit
title: Freeze batch1 at 1d cadence against the reworked noise floor

description:
## Decision

**Move `TankParams.evaluation_interval_days` from 7 to 1.** Owner's decision,
2026-08-21. This is a deliberate re-lock under `docs/CONVENTIONS.md`, with the same
ceremony as changing `LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS`: recorded rationale, stated before/after,
every subsequent row stamped.

## Rationale (owner's, recorded verbatim in substance)

1. **Uniformity** — a daily fill cadence matches the daily price cadence. One clock, not
   two.
2. **Maximum resolution** — the finest decision grid the data supports.
3. **A choice every day** is the intended product experience.

## Considered and NOT taken: 2-day

Recommended by the fps-929 session on the hassle trade-off, and explicitly overridden by
the owner on the rationale above. Recorded here because "recorded rationale" means
recording what was rejected too, at the numbers it was rejected at (τ=0.25 throughout,
from `experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/tau_sweep.csv`):

| cadence | CPL | fills/station/yr | one fill every | emergency % |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 7d | 189.67 | 44 | 8.4 days | 67.6 |
| 2d | 188.00 | 83 | 4.4 days | 37.5 |
| 1d | 187.82 | 135 | 2.7 days | 21.4 |

7d->2d buys 1.67 c/L; 2d->1d buys a further 0.18 c/L for ~52 more fills a year. The
mechanism is visible in the emergency column: at 7d two-thirds of fills are FORCED, and
that is what the model cannot work around. By 2d most of the decision freedom is already
recovered.

Anyone revisiting this should argue against the rationale above, not re-derive the table.

## What this is NOT

Established by fps-929 (`experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/`), so do not re-litigate:

- **Not a retrain.** `_train_calibrate_select_tau` takes no `TankParams`; the fit is both
  tank- and tau-invariant. That invariance is what let fps-929 replay 36 cells off one
  fit.
- **Not a tau change.** Best-tau-in-hindsight beats tau=0.25 by 0.062 c/L at 1d — 2% of
  that cadence's headroom, off 422 changed decisions. tau stays 0.25.
- **Not a production code change.** `evaluation_interval_days` is consumed only by the
  backtest engines. `decide()` is called from exactly one place (`backtest.py:589`,
  inside `run_backtest`) — there is no production inference path through the model. The
  live daily signal is `fuel_signal/signal.py`, which is rule-based, does not load the
  model, does not know what a tank is, and already emits daily.

Cadence is an **evaluation** parameter: an assumption about the driver's behaviour that
every published number is conditioned on. The 1.85 c/L is only realised if the owner
actually checks and acts daily.

## Code changes (small)

- `fuel_signal/backtest.py:353` — the default itself.
- Four assertions pinned on the literal `50/3.571/7d/10%`:
  `tests/test_score_phase2.py:369`, `tests/test_backtest_phase2.py:196-197`,
  `tests/test_evaluate.py:347`.
- Tests that pass `evaluation_interval_days=7` explicitly keep working and should be
  KEPT — 7d coverage stays valuable, and a test that follows the default tests nothing
  about the default.

## Doc sweep (the actual work)

Every published CPL/headroom figure changes meaning simultaneously. At minimum:
`docs/STATUS.md` (canonical model state), `docs/routines/generator.md` (quotes 1.54 c/L
at 7d as the headroom the generator aims at -> 2.97), `docs/CONVENTIONS.md` (the cadence
section itself, plus the `50/3.571/7d/10%` example at line 127), `experiments/INDEX.md`
rows for #262 / fps-fii / fps-929, batch0's dossier and RETROSPECTIVE, and the
`project_cadence_ceiling` / `feedback_oracle_ceiling_capability` memories.

Existing `results.csv` rows need no edit — they are already stamped `50/3.571/7d/10%` by
fps-xx1, which was the precondition for this being possible at all.

## Ordering

- **Blocked by `fps-15c`** (stamp the cadence into runner `results.json`, dossier
  `facts.json`, `freeze.json`, `noise_floor.json`). Without it the ceremony's
  "mechanically distinguishable" requirement cannot be met for pipeline artifacts.
- **Interacts with `fps-awz` and the batch1 freeze.** A cadence re-lock invalidates any
  existing noise floor. Either land this BEFORE the batch1 freeze, or accept that batch1
  is a 7d batch and re-lock afterwards. Do not land it mid-batch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Default changed; the four stamp assertions updated; explicit-7d tests retained
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` green
- [ ] Before/after recorded: 7d 189.67 -> 1d 187.82 at tau=0.25, same folds/stations/seed
- [ ] Doc sweep complete — no surviving CPL or headroom figure without a cadence
- [ ] A fresh `results.csv` row stamped `50/3.571/1d/10%`, sitting distinguishably beside
      the 7d rows
title: Re-lock the decision cadence from 7d to 1d

close_reason:
SIGNAL-CONTENT LIMIT. The operating-point explanation is ruled out.

experiments/2026-08-21_tau_cadence/ (README + tau_sweep.csv + tau_sweep.png). 12 tau x 3 cadences off one paid walk-forward fit, 14 folds / 5 stations / seed 42 / 54 cols (54:1a6ec2d84a69), all 36 cells dry-free.

Best-tau-in-hindsight vs production tau=0.25: 7d +0.009, 2d +0.086, 1d +0.062 c/L. The 1d gain is 2% of that cadence's 2.97 c/L headroom. The hypothesis is directionally right and economically irrelevant - the optimum does climb 0.20/0.30/0.35 as the grid refines, and it is worth nothing.

Decisive line is the flip count (acceptance criterion 3), and it inverts the usual reading: at 1d, moving tau 0.25 -> 0.35 changes 422 buy/wait decisions for 0.062 c/L. The changes cancel. That is a real measurement of NO effect, not an underpowered measurement of a real one - much stronger than a small-flip-count null. At 7d the comparable move changes 8 decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Realised CPL vs tau at 1d, same folds/stations/seed/columns: DONE, plus 2d and 7d for contrast.
- Stated verdict: signal-content limit.
- Decision-flip count behind the sub-0.1 c/L deltas: DONE (422 / 132 / 8).
- If tau moves, re-lock recommendation: tau does NOT move. NO re-lock, docs/STATUS.md unchanged.

Method caveat recorded in the README: the sweep picks tau in hindsight, so a flat curve RULES OUT the operating point while a dip would only have upper-bounded a gain. The curve is flat, so the definitive half is the half that applies.

Untouched and much larger: cadence itself. The model is 1.85 c/L cheaper at 1d than 7d regardless of tau, but fills 2332 times vs 752 (9.9 L mean fill vs 28.8) - roughly 3x the servo visits, a cost CPL does not price. That remains a deliberate re-lock decision, not an experiment output.

Consequence for fps-3jj: feature work IS the right lever at fine cadence, and the batch1 freeze can proceed at 7d without re-freeze risk from a cadence change.
description:
## What

`experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/` (fps-fii) held tau at the production
0.25 at every cadence. That was correct for isolating the cadence effect — tau
selection is tank-independent (`_train_calibrate_select_tau` takes no TankParams),
so holding it constant is what makes the arms comparable. But it means the daily
arm is **the production model operated as-is, not tuned for a regime with 7x more
decisions**.

Re-run the OOF tau selection against daily-cadence economics and see how much of
the 2.97 c/L headroom closes with NO new features.

## Why this is the highest-value next move

The cadence sweep found the model plateaus where the oracle does not:

    cadence   model    oracle   headroom   captured
    7d        189.67   188.14   1.54       71%
    2d        187.85   185.16   2.69       65%
    1d        187.82   184.85   2.97       64%

Model gains 1.82 c/L going 7d->2d, then **0.03 c/L** going 2d->1d, while the
oracle keeps improving. Captured share falls monotonically as the model is handed
more chances. Two competing explanations, and they imply completely different work:

1. **Operating-point limit** — tau=0.25 was chosen under weekly economics where
   nearly every decision is forced; a model with 12 wait-rungs instead of 1 should
   plausibly be choosier. Fix is free: re-pick tau. No new data, no new features.
2. **Signal-content limit** — the features genuinely carry no more exploitable
   information, and the plateau is real.

**A tau sweep separates them, and it is cheap.** Until it is run, "the signal is
the binding constraint at daily cadence" is a hypothesis, not a finding — and any
feature work started before it risks attacking a problem that a threshold move
would have solved.

## Approach

- Reuse the fps-fii harness pattern: one paid walk-forward fit, replayed at
  cadence 1 across a tau grid (the fits are cadence- AND tau-invariant, so the
  whole sweep is replay-only and costs minutes, not hours).
- Report realised CPL vs tau at 1d, against the 7d curve for contrast.
- Apply the tau-sweep inertness diagnostic: near-coincident sweeps = inert.
- Count decision flips before believing any sub-0.1 c/L delta (~0.05 c/L per flip
  pooled at 7d — note that quantum is itself a 7-day quantity and will be smaller
  per-flip at 1d, since there are ~7x more chosen fills).

## Honest caveats

- The oracle ceiling is leaky: 2.97 c/L is an upper bound on a partly
  unforecastable prize. Closing part of it via tau does not make the rest reachable.
- Window level only. No zone slicing (`fps-1785999730023-4-264564ac`).
- If tau moves materially, the production lock changes and STATUS.md's canonical
  model state needs updating — that is a lock decision, not an experiment output.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Realised CPL vs tau at 1-day cadence, same 14 folds / 5 stations / seed / columns
- [ ] Stated verdict: operating-point limit vs signal-content limit
- [ ] Decision-flip count supporting any delta below ~0.1 c/L
- [ ] If tau moves: an explicit recommendation on whether to re-lock, with STATUS.md impact

## Related

- `fps-fii` / experiments/2026-08-20_cadence_ceiling/ — the plateau this explains
- `fps-x0f` — its step 3 is gated on how big the prize actually is; this sizes the
  free portion of it
title: Re-pick tau for daily-cadence economics before any further feature work

description:
## What

fps-1785999730023-4-264564ac found that per-zone headroom is not identified, because
allocating a path-coupled total cost across sub-periods has no unique answer. That
defect is not specific to the #262 headroom map. Find every other place in this repo
that does the same thing and mark what is affected.

## The test to apply

A quantity is at risk if BOTH hold:
1. it is a cost/economics aggregate over a strategy whose value is path-dependent
   (a buy now changes what is possible later — which is true of every tank-based
   backtest here), AND
2. it is reported sliced by a time-varying label (cycle regime, quarter, month,
   volatility band, fold sub-period).

A quantity is safe if it is natively stamped at a moment: per-row log-loss, per-
decision accuracy, prices, predictions. Window-level totals are also safe — that is
the level `run_oracle_backtest` optimises and where `oracle <= model` holds by
construction.

## Named suspect, already identified

`experiments/2026-06-18_late_descent_gate1` reports **realised saving% by regime**
(normal 0.64% / late_descent 2.13% / overdue 4.06%, pooled 1.87%). That is per-regime
CPL from a per-fill ledger — structurally the same decomposition that failed. It is
one of the three mutually-inconsistent late-descent findings listed in fps-x0f, and if
it is unidentified then that reconciliation gets simpler rather than harder. Its
Layer-1 proxy regret (normal 1.05 / late_descent 1.72 / overdue 1.32) needs the same
check.

Note this one is measured against always-buy rather than the oracle, so it does not
produce impossible negatives as a tell — the defect would be silent. Absence of
negatives is NOT evidence of safety.

## Other places to check

- `experiments/results.csv` — CPL and saving% are stored columns; is any row a
  period-sliced economics figure rather than a window-level one?
- The #262 monthly episode table and its ~+/-3 c/L monthly noise floor
- Any per-fold economics reported as if fold were a zone (folds ARE separate windows,
  so these are probably safe — confirm rather than assume)
- `fuel_signal/evaluate.py` / `score_phase2.py` reporting paths

## What to do with what you find

Do not silently rerun or delete anything. For each affected result: annotate it in
place (experiments/INDEX.md row + ledger.yaml entry) the way the TGP graduation and
the #262 per-zone rows were annotated, stating what is withdrawn and what survives.
The point is that a future cold session reading these files is not misled — the same
failure mode that kept a retracted TGP graduation alive for two months.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/INDEX.md, experiments/ledger.yaml (annotations)
- docs/CONVENTIONS.md — add the rule, see acceptance criteria

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every period-sliced economics figure in experiments/ and fuel_signal/ enumerated, with a safe/at-risk verdict and the reason
- [ ] The 2026-06-18 gate1 per-regime saving% verdict decided explicitly
- [ ] Affected results annotated in INDEX.md + ledger.yaml, not deleted
- [ ] docs/CONVENTIONS.md gains the rule: a zone comparison is readable only when the gap between zones exceeds the gap between free bookkeeping conventions — and the corollary that this is a bias term, so more data does not fix it
- [ ] #262's own 2026-06-19 INDEX row annotated with which of its rows are withdrawn (per-zone: all; window-level 1.66 c/L: stands) and its status revisited
title: Audit: what else in this repo slices a path-coupled total by time period?

description:
## What

Batch setup is currently two commands that must be run in the right order by hand, and
nothing checks that they agree. Make it one operation, and make disagreement detectable.

**Part A — the correctness guard (must-have).**

`experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py` writes `noise_floor.json` with:
`deltas_cpl_held, seeds_a, seeds_b, fold_subset, partial, computed_at, git_sha`.

It does NOT record `baseline_fingerprint`, though `freeze.json` does
(`"baseline_fingerprint": "54:1a6ec2d84a69"`). Consequently `_noise_band()` in
`dossier_tables.py:253` validates exactly one staleness condition — the `partial`
flag from `--fold-subset`, which it refuses correctly — and takes everything else on
trust: file exists => grade against it.

So a floor computed against one baseline can silently grade a candidate run against a
different one. That is precisely the failure class that cost batch0 two full runs:
fps-sa1 (64 columns instead of 54, +0.0941) and fps-zci (right 54 columns, sorted
instead of production group order, 52/54 positions differing, +0.0439). Convention
`feedback_baseline_declared_not_discovered` says compare `baseline_fingerprint`
before comparing any two runs' numbers — the noise floor is a run whose number is
compared against EVERY candidate's, and it is the one run that does not carry one.

`git_sha` is not a substitute: it catches harness drift but not a re-lock (the lock
and the floor can move independently within one commit) and false-positives on every
unrelated commit.

**Part B — the atomicity fix.**

`batch_freeze.py` pins three of the things the floor depends on (frozen
features.parquet, cloned DB, resolved baseline columns + fingerprint). The noise
floor is a separate command the operator must remember to run afterwards, and
nothing enforces either the ordering or the correspondence. "Once per batch" is
therefore a convention, not a property of the code.

Note fold geometry is a fourth dependency and is also unrecorded in `freeze.json`:
`DEFAULT_INNER_FOLD_PARAMS` (runner.py:189) and `outer_fold_params` are code
constants overridable per-call. tau does NOT need pinning — it is derived per fold by
`pick_tau()` (experiments/lib/realised.py:202), so it moves as a consequence of the
other three rather than being an independent input.

Freeze is already a long, hard-gated operation (`refresh_db()` runs `make update` +
`make features` and raises on failure), so folding a ~10-fit step into it is
consistent with its existing shape rather than a new burden.

## Why I noticed this

Reviewing whether tgp_delta_7d should graduate (fps-1785999729707-1-0301bf82 / #271).
The noise floor (fps-3jj.9) is what settled it — candidate +0.0059 at the 40th
percentile of a band with std 0.142 c/L — so the floor is now load-bearing for every
graduation decision, and batch2 (fps-3jj.11) is unblocked and will need its own.
Worth landing the guard before batch2 runs rather than after it produces a number.

Related: every successful graduation invalidates the floor (a 55th column changes the
model whose noise was measured), so the recompute trigger is real and recurring, not
hypothetical.

## Files likely affected

- experiments/pipeline/noise_floor.py — stamp provenance; optionally expose a callable entry point

## What

`experiments/pipeline/batch_freeze.py:80` `resolve_baseline_columns()` returns
`FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS + NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS + discover_brand_feature_columns(df)`
= 64 columns. The locked production model is 54.

The 10 extra `days_since_trough_entry_<brand>` columns are Phase 4b, which was
**evaluated and rejected** on 2026-06-02 (docs/STATUS.md:123 — lost 9/14 folds in
paired WFCV, non-shock regression at fold 11). They stay computed in features.csv
but are excluded from the lock. AGENTS.md:317 says so explicitly: "Brand trough
columns are excluded from the locked baseline until a separate ablation graduates
them." Verified against the artifact: `data/models/lgbm_calibrated.joblib` carries
54 `feature_columns`, last `lga_phase_std_delta_3d`, no brand columns.

The docstring says it "mirrors train_lgbm.py's default resolution" — and it does,
but train_lgbm's *default* is not the lock; the lock is `--no-brand-features`
(train_lgbm.py:205, STATUS.md:36). Mirroring the CLI default instead of the lock
is the bug.

## Why it matters

Every batch0 candidate was graded against production-plus-10-rejected-features,
on both the WFCV screen and the realised arbiter (runner.py:368 reads the same
baseline_columns.json). This is the root of the tgp_delta_7d June-vs-batch0
disagreement (bd fps-nor): the two candidate arms land 0.0013 c/L apart while the
baselines differ by 0.132 c/L, so the "sign flip" is a baseline artifact.

## Fix

- `resolve_baseline_columns()` returns the locked set; assert the frame contains
  every locked column, and assert no known non-model column leaked in.
- Flip `tests/test_batch_freeze.py:41`
  (`test_resolve_baseline_columns_is_sorted_and_includes_brand_columns`) — it
  currently pins the wrong behaviour.
- Re-freeze batch0 (or bump its baseline_columns.json) and re-run the batch0
  candidate(s) against the corrected R0.

Prefer taking the single-source symbol from the parent design issue if that lands
first; otherwise inline the correct composition and let the parent refactor it.

close_reason:
Resolved 2026-08-19. Two causes, neither of them a real disagreement about the world.

1. WRONG BASELINE (lead 1, confirmed but reframed). batch0's 64-col R0 was not the production baseline — batch_freeze.resolve_baseline_columns() appended discover_brand_feature_columns(df), pulling in the 10 Phase 4b brand-trough columns that were EVALUATED AND REJECTED on 2026-06-02. This issue's own framing ('10 new columns that did not exist in June') was wrong twice: they landed 2026-06-02, 18 days BEFORE the TGP experiment, and they are rejected, not new. June's 54-col BASE was the correct, production-faithful baseline. Fixed: bd fps-sa1 / PR #309. General problem: bd fps-zci (P1).

2. BELOW THE INSTRUMENT'S RESOLUTION (not previously suspected, and the more important finding). On the CORRECT 54-col baseline against the same frozen snapshot: pooled delta_cpl_held = +0.0059 c/L. Not a rejection, not a graduation — inert.

2x2 (pooled cpl_held; R0_64 anchor reproduced batch0's 189.6600 exactly, so this is a faithful reproduction):
  54-col June vintage     189.7923 -> 189.7529   -0.0394
  54-col batch0 snapshot  189.6717 -> 189.6776   +0.0059
  64-col batch0 snapshot  189.6600 -> 189.7541   +0.0941

Swing attribution: baseline composition +0.0882, data vintage +0.0453.

Why resolution is the real story: per-fold pooled contributions span -0.209 to +0.654 c/L for a +0.006 total (largest fold ~110x the pooled result, near-total cancellation); the arms differ on 11 of 752 fills; fold 10's single differing fill is worth -0.046 c/L pooled. One decision flip ~ 0.05 c/L — LARGER than the -0.039 that graduated this feature in June. -0.039, +0.006 and +0.094 are all a couple of flips from zero and from each other.

Also ruled out: the TGP series is bit-identical between June's xlsx and batch0's column (3520 dates, max|diff| 0.0). Fold 13 (lead 2) is moot — its dominance was an artifact of the 64-col baseline (+1.09 there, +0.127 on the correct one); on the correct baseline the biggest contributor is fold 8, a normal fold. The identity of the dominant fold changes with the baseline, which is itself the diagnosis.

VERDICT ON #271: stays on HOLD, on corrected reasoning — the evidence that graduated it never cleared the arbiter's resolution, not because batch0 rejected it. Track NOT closed: the WFCV log-loss screen likes the feature consistently and independently of the baseline defect. Unblocking step is fps-3jj.9 (noise floor, promoted P3 -> P1), not another paired run.

Evidence: experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{README.md,diagnostic_baseline_composition.py,baseline_composition_*.csv}, commit 025adae. Still open: why the 54-col baseline improved 0.1206 c/L between June's vintage and the 2026-08-10 snapshot (always_cpl identical to the decimal; plausible mechanism is gap-fill adding historical rows for stations outside the 50 preferred).
description:
## What

tgp_delta_7d graduated the realised arbiter 2026-06-22 (pooled realised
delta_cpl -0.039 c/L, experiments/2026-06-20_leading_indicators/). The
AI-sourced pipeline's batch0 re-test (2026-08-18, bd fps-32p, held-out
known-graduate check) rejected it: pooled delta_cpl_held +0.0941, opposite
sign. A follow-up diagnostic ruled out implementation mismatch as the cause
(experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/diagnostic_asof_provider.py:
reproducing June's exact .asof-by-date provider instead of the pipeline
harness's exact-(station,date)-lookup gave a BIT-IDENTICAL result — 910/910
hits, same +0.0941 to the decimal, same per-fold table). So the disagreement
is real, not plumbing. Full detail and all numbers:
experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/README.md.

Owner wants to understand this disagreement properly before deciding
anything about the #271 TGP re-lock (currently on hold).

## Leads to check, in order of how promising they look

1. **Baseline composition changed (strongest lead, not yet tested).** batch0's
   R0 baseline (64 cols) = June's exact 54 BASE columns PLUS 10 new
   `days_since_trough_entry_<brand>` brand-trough columns that did not exist
   in June. Brand-trough distance and TGP-floor distance are thematically
   adjacent ("how close to the bottom") -- plausible tgp_delta_7d's
   incremental value shrank/reversed because a related signal is now already
   in the baseline. Test: rerun the realised backtest with a baseline that
   EXCLUDES the 10 brand-trough columns (June's original 54-column BASE) on
   the SAME batch0 snapshot/seeds/folds, using the diagnostic script's asof
   provider as a template. If the sign flips back, this is the answer.
2. **Fold 13 idiosyncrasy.** Fold 13 (window 2024-10-20 to 2025-01-17) alone
   drives ~all of the pooled shock-regime harm (+1.09 of the folds's
   contribution; the other 3 shock folds are flat/mildly helpful). Worth
   understanding what actually happened in that window -- a specific
   historical event the floor-velocity signal misread, vs a general property.
3. **Data-vintage decay.** Whether the June-to-now data vintage shift itself
   (new months of price history, revised TGP data, etc.) explains the flip,
   independent of (1) and (2). Weakest lead since fold 13's window predates
   both runs' cutoffs -- what's "new" is mostly the baseline and ~2 months
   of additional recent data at the tail, not a rewrite of history.

description:
## What
`fuel_signal/backtest.py`'s `ModelStrategy.decide()` builds its live feature
dict by looping `LGA_FEATURE_COUNCILS` to populate `days_since_trough_entry_<lga>`,
but has no equivalent loop for brand-axis trough columns
(`days_since_trough_entry_<brand>`, e.g. `_7_eleven`, `_bp`). `PriceHistory`
has no `brand_days_since_at()` method and no brand-trough cache fields at all.

## Why I noticed this
Manually launched the fuel-price-signal candidate pipeline against batch0
(`tgp_delta_7d`, bd fps-32p) and it aborted with:

    ValueError("feature 'days_since_trough_entry_7_eleven' is in
    feature_columns but no value was produced for it (extra_feature_provider
    must supply every added column).")

Root cause: `experiments/pipeline/batch_freeze.py:resolve_baseline_columns()`
composes batch0's 64-column baseline as `FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS
+ NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS + discover_brand_feature_columns(df)` — mirroring
`train_lgbm.py`'s default, fine for the WFCV screen (reads the precomputed
`features.csv` frame directly). But the realised backtest replays through
`ModelStrategy.decide()`, which recomputes features live via `PriceHistory`
and never got brand-trough support when brand troughs were added
(`3f2dd29`, "brand-axis trough event feature", ~3 months ago) — it only
touched `features.py`/`train_lgbm.py`, not `backtest.py`. The `R0` baseline
arm has no `extra_feature_provider` (`experiments/pipeline/runner.py:468`),
so this is candidate-independent: every candidate run against batch0 aborts
here identically, same failure class as fps-g31 but a different missing
piece. `aborted_pipeline`'s "retry once" won't help — needs a code fix.

## Fix
Mirror the LGA wiring, using the brand machinery that already exists for the
offline path (`fuel_signal/brand_leadership.py` — `qualifying_brands()`,
`brand_slug()`, `compute_pit_strict_days_since_trough_brand()`):
- `PriceHistory`: add `brand_days_since_by_key` + `qualifying_brands` fields,
  and a `brand_days_since_at(as_of, brand)` method mirroring `lga_days_since_at`.
- `load_history()`: call `qualifying_brands(conn)` unconditionally (cheap,
  mirrors the always-available `LGA_FEATURE_COUNCILS` constant), and
  `compute_pit_strict_days_since_trough_brand(conn, eval_dates, qualifying_brand_list)`
  gated on `eval_dates` (mirrors the existing LGA gating).
- `ModelStrategy.decide()`: loop `history.qualifying_brands` after the LGA
  loop, populating `days_since_trough_entry_<brand_slug(brand)>` the same way.

## Files likely affected
- fuel_signal/backtest.py
- tests/test_backtest.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `ModelStrategy.decide()` populates brand-trough columns natively (no
      KeyError) when `feature_columns` includes them
- [ ] Regression test mirroring `test_model_strategy_decide_with_54feat_calibrated_artifact`
      but with brand-trough columns in `feature_columns`
- [ ] `uv run ruff check . && uv run pytest -q` green
- [ ] batch0's `tgp_delta_7d` (fps-32p) re-run succeeds past this abort
title: Wire brand-trough features into ModelStrategy.decide()

description:
## What

experiments/pipeline/batch_freeze.py's refresh_db() hard-gates the DB (make update:
pull, db, fill, classify, lga-leadership) — aborts loudly rather than freeze a stale
DB. But it never regenerates data/features.csv/.parquet (that's a separate manual
step, `uv run python -m fuel_signal.features`), and freeze_batch() just snapshots
whatever's currently on disk with no freshness check against the just-refreshed DB.

## Why I noticed this

Filing batch0 (fps-32p, tgp_delta_7d known-graduate check) after running `make daily`:
batch_freeze.py succeeded but froze a features.parquet last regenerated 2026-06-15
(snapshot_date 2026-05-30) even though the DB had just been pulled current to
2026-08-17 — over two months stale, silently. Caught by eyeballing freeze.json's
snapshot_date; nothing in the tool would have surfaced this on its own. Worked around
manually this time: ran fuel_signal.features (~3 min) before re-freezing.

## Suggested fix

Either (a) refresh_db() also regenerates features.csv/.parquet as part of the hard-gated
chain (matches "abort rather than freeze stale data" already applied to the DB), or (b)
freeze_batch() compares features.parquet's mtime (or its own max price_date) against the
DB's latest price_date post-refresh and aborts/warns if they disagree by more than a
day or two. (a) is probably simpler and more consistent with the existing hard-gate
philosophy.

## Files likely affected
- experiments/pipeline/batch_freeze.py (refresh_db, freeze_batch)
- tests/test_batch_freeze.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] batch_freeze.py aborts (or regenerates) rather than silently freezing a
      features.csv/.parquet that predates the just-refreshed DB
- [ ] Regression test covering a stale features.parquet against a fresh DB

description:
## What
Run an independent code review over experiments/pipeline/runner.py and its
tests (tests/test_runner.py), plus the accompanying fix to
experiments/lib/pit_test.py, before this lands on main. This is genuinely
complex, high-stakes code — it composes three existing subsystems (the
candidate validation harness, the WFCV log-loss screen, and the realised-CPL
backtest, which is the project's economic arbiter) into one call, and a subtle
bug here could silently corrupt every candidate's verdict rather than fail
loudly.

## Where the code lives
Branch `claude/fps-3jj.4-runner`, committed locally but NOT YET PUSHED as of
2026-08-17 (blocked on the 1Password SSH agent being unreachable on this
machine — see bd memory `1password-ssh-push`). Before this review can run
against a PR diff, someone needs to: confirm 1Password/SSH is working, push
the branch, open the PR (title `feat: one-shot candidate runner for
AI-sourced feature pipeline (bd-fps-3jj.4)`, base main). If that hasn't
happened yet when this bead is picked up, do that first.

Use `/code-review` (medium-high effort; consider `ultra` given the stakes)
against the branch/PR once it exists.

## What to look at especially hard
- **experiments/pipeline/runner.py `_resolve_zone`**: the mechanical
  CONFIDENCE_ZONE grading logic (target-cell vs other-cell pooled
  delta_cpl_OWN comparison, the fold/regime/custom-axis union semantics, the
  min_row_cell_n guard). This is new, non-obvious logic with no prior art in
  the codebase to pattern-match against — verify the "in target" fill
  selection (`|=` union of folds_wanted and axis membership) actually matches
  the parent design's "conflation is harmless" intent, and that the
  min-cell-n guard can't be silently bypassed.
- **`_make_lookup_provider`**: the extra_feature_provider seam that supplies
  the candidate's precomputed column value during the live backtest replay.
  Verify the (station_code, date) keying can't misalign with
  `ModelStrategy.decide`'s `as_of`/`station_code` arguments, and that a
  missing-key fallback (`dict.fromkeys(columns)` → None → NaN in the feature
  vector) is the right failure mode rather than a silent wrong value.
- **Exception-to-status-code mapping** in `run_candidate` (which exceptions
  map to `aborted_candidate` vs `aborted_environment`): confirm the boundary
  is right — a bug that maps a real candidate defect to `aborted_environment`
  would trigger a pointless retry; the reverse would give up on an
  environment problem that should have been retried.
- **experiments/lib/pit_test.py's `check_exact=True` fix**: this PR changes
  already-merged code (fps-3jj.2, PR #298) after discovering that
  `assert_frame_equal`'s default `rtol=1e-5` tolerance silently passed a real
  leak on large-magnitude values (a whole-series mean of YYYYMMDD-scale
  price_date differed by ~1.5 out of ~20260812). Confirm the fix is complete
  — check there's no other tolerance-based comparison anywhere in the
  validation harness or runner that could have the same blind spot (e.g. any
  other use of pandas testing assert helpers, or a manual `np.isclose`-style
  check with a relative tolerance against large-magnitude features).
- **R0-caching scope-out**: confirm the runner genuinely refits both arms
  every call (no half-finished caching path left in), matching the deferral
  documented in the module docstring and bd issue fps-e2l.

- [ ] Independent review run and findings reported (via ReportFindings or as
      PR comments per the review tooling's normal output)
- [ ] Any CONFIRMED correctness findings fixed before merge; PLAUSIBLE
      findings triaged with the repo owner

after fps-3jj.4 was implemented, given its complexity and importance to the
pipeline's economic arbiter.
title: Independent code review: fps-3jj.4 candidate runner (validation + WFCV + realised backtest composition)

description:
## What
fps-3jj.4's runner (experiments/pipeline/runner.py) refits BOTH arms (R0 baseline
+ candidate) on every run. The parent design (fps-3jj) calls for caching R0 once
per batch and reusing it across the batch's remaining nights (~12min/night saved
since R0 is bit-identical every night: frozen data + fixed SEEDS + fixed baseline
columns).

## Why this wasn't done in fps-3jj.4
`run_paired_realised_backtest` (experiments/lib/realised.py) couples the
candidate's held-tau score to the baseline arm's OWN per-fold tau, computed
inside the SAME call:

    held = held_tau if held_tau is not None else fitted[arms[0].name][1]

Running R0 and candidate as two separate single-arm calls (to reuse a cached R0)
loses this coupling — the candidate would need to be scored at a tau borrowed
from a run it wasn't part of, which either means passing a fixed held_tau
override (losing "baseline's per-fold own tau" semantics) or re-deriving the
per-fold coupling by hand outside the library.

Confirmed with the repo owner (2026-08-17, fps-3jj.4 discussion) that this is a
real correctness question, not a preference — shipping an approximation risked
silently corrupting the CPL arbiter every downstream candidate depends on. Not
urgent: batch 1 is a single candidate (tgp_delta_7d, one night), so there's
nothing to cache or reuse yet. The design only needs settling before batch 2
(5 candidates, 5 nights) makes the caching benefit concrete.

## Options considered (fps-3jj.4 PR discussion)
1. Extend realised.py: add a cached_baseline param to run_paired_realised_backtest
   (per-fold own_tau + fitted pipeline) so a paired call can skip refitting
   arms[0] and still couple correctly. Touches lib code every experiment script
   depends on — needs care.
2. Cache tau only: persist baseline's per-fold own_tau from night 1, pass it as
   a fixed held_tau override on later nights. Keeps the coupling exactly correct
   with zero lib changes, but still refits the baseline PIPELINE every night
   (losing most of the ~12min/night saving) — only the operating-point choice is
   cached, not the fit itself.
3. Some other seam not yet considered — worth a fresh look once batch 2's actual
   candidate count/cadence is known.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decide the caching mechanism (extend realised.py vs tau-only vs other)
- [ ] If extending experiments/lib/realised.py: existing callers (realised_tgp.py,
      realised_by_regime.py, tests/test_realised.py) still pass unmodified
- [ ] experiments/pipeline/runner.py's run_candidate() reuses the cache when
      present in the batch dir, refits when absent (night 1)
- [ ] Batch 2 (5 candidates) actually exercises the caching path end-to-end

Parent design: fps-3jj. Surfaced during fps-3jj.4 (candidate module format +
one-shot runner) implementation.
title: Design R0-caching seam for run_paired_realised_backtest (fps-3jj batch nights)

description:
## What

Human-sourced candidate leads, held back deliberately so they do NOT contaminate the first
AI-sourced batch. Use these to seed the batch AFTER the first genuinely AI-generated set has been
run and scored.

Each was surfaced during the fps-3jj.3 ledger backfill: a not_tested line in an experiment that
was written down once and never followed up. They are real leads, not speculation — each names the
experiment that left the ground open.

## Why held back

The first AI-sourced batch exists to measure the **idea-generation stage**: what an LLM proposes
unaided, and whether its own CONFIDENCE predicts its hits. Feeding it human leads would make that
measurement meaningless. See the "Ledger contamination" note below — this is not automatically
solved by keeping the leads out of this bead.

## The leads

1. A_residual = A - E[A | phase] — dispersion measured as "is A unusual for its phase?"
rather than "is A high?". The 2026-06-09 analysis says it is constructible PIT-safely from a
rolling per-phase median over previous cycles, and predicts it surfaces elongated-vs-normal
cleanly while NOT solving shallow-vs-steep. Never run.
Source: experiments/2026-06-09_shallow_elongated/
2. **Drop **station_minus_sydney_avg_cents — step 1 of the 2026-06-04 experiment found it had the
HIGHEST partner score but the LOWEST true SHAP interaction, making it a cleaner redundancy-drop
candidate than the engineered feature that experiment actually tested. Costed at ~2 min compute.
Never run.
Source: experiments/2026-06-04_cycle_pct_through_interaction/
3. **Velocity of the discount-cohort gap (family B)** — B was screened at level only and came back
flat. The identical redesign (level -> 7d velocity) is exactly what rescued the TGP series after
station_minus_tgp_cents failed and tgp_delta_7d graduated.
Source: experiments/2026-06-06_late_descent_triplet/
4. **Leader-weighted LGA consensus** — family C uses an unweighted LGA dispersion statistic, but the
lead/lag roles are known (Penrith leads FALLS; Blue Mountains and Randwick lead RISES) and were
never used to weight it.
Source: experiments/2026-06-07_a_c_ablation/ + project_lga_leadership
5. **Regime-dependent tau** — not a feature, an operating-point change. In the 2026-06-16
experiment the tau move was worth ~2x the feature effect (a tau step ~1 c/L vs the feature's
~0.5 c/L) and was never explored on its own. Note this does NOT fit the candidate module format
(add_columns returns a feature column, not a policy) so it likely needs its own experiment
rather than a pipeline slot.
Source: experiments/2026-06-16_regime_cycle_length/
6. **Turn-gated stickiness x phase** — stickiness_phase_saddle (fps-6yi, batch1) graded
inconclusive at -0.0735 c/L, inside the noise band. A flip-level diagnostic (2026-08-29) found
the mechanism IS real but mispriced. On flips landing within 3 days of a >=15 c/L rise, the
candidate's litres-weighted 7d regret is **0.33 c/L vs the baseline's 21.62** — it buys
essentially at the optimum — and those catches spread across 5 folds (2, 3, 8, 10, 13), not one
lucky window. But turn-adjacent fills are only 150 of 2982 flipped litres (~5%), and the
candidate is **0.88 c/L WORSE** on the ordinary-conditions remainder (6.52 vs 5.64). Litres-
weighted regret over all flips: 6.21 candidate vs 6.22 baseline — a dead heat, which is exactly
why the realised delta is ~0. **Redesign:** gate the interaction so it is live near a cycle turn
and inert otherwise, rather than active on every row. Keep arity <= 2 (fps-3jj.21).
**Open question the diagnostic could NOT answer:** what a PIT-safe turn gate is built from. The
diagnostic's turn definition is forward-looking (max price over the next 3 days) and is a
DIAGNOSTIC, not a constructible feature; a live gate needs a same-day proxy (cycle_pct_through
band, days_since_trough_entry, TGP lead) and that substitution is itself the risk — if the proxy
fires on the wrong 5% of rows the edge inverts, since the ordinary-conditions arm is where this
candidate already loses. Caveats on the numbers above: n=11 candidate / n=8 baseline turn-
adjacent flips, the two arms' flips fall on different days (two decision sets, not a paired
test), and an apparent "candidate never buys before a sharp fall" result (0/183 vs 4/120, Fisher
p=0.024) did NOT survive a threshold sweep — p=1.000 at 8-10 c/L, 0.202 at 12, 0.156 at 20 — so
it is withdrawn, not evidence.
Source: experiments/candidates/batch1/stickiness_phase_saddle/ + fps-6yi

## Ledger contamination — considered and dismissed (2026-08-17)

All five leads are also recorded in experiments/ledger.yaml not_tested fields, and the ledger is
handed to the generator by design. So the generator may well propose some of these unprompted.

That is fine, for two reasons:

• These are not privileged human insight — they were written by reading the same experiment READMEs
the generator can read. An LLM re-deriving A_residual off the ledger is not different in kind
from deriving it off 2026-06-09_shallow_elongated/analysis.md.
• The design already requires handing the generator the ledger, and aim (b) is proposal quality and
CONFIDENCE calibration — neither depends on the idea being unaided.

Self-correcting too: anything proposed and run gets its own ledger entry, so whoever picks this bead
up re-reads the ledger first and finds those leads already tested. Check the ledger before filing —
expect this list to have shrunk.

The only claim the batch cannot support is that it was an *unaided* read of generation ability. Not
a claim anyone needs.

## Acceptance criteria

[ ] Ledger re-read first; leads already tested by the AI batch struck from this list
[ ] Remainder filed as experiment beads once the first AI-sourced batch is scored
[ ] Lead 5 (regime-dependent tau) routed to its own experiment, not a pipeline candidate slot

Parent design: fps-3jj

## Folded in from the standing backlog (2026-08-17)

Three long-standing P3 beads are feature candidates in all but name. Folded here rather than left
loose, and closed as superseded on filing:

6. **Brand-level regime feature: chronic pricing strategy as a level statistic** — brand as a
persistent pricing-posture covariate rather than a per-cycle signal.
Was: fps-1785999730218-6-11778893 (gh #—)
7. **Phase 4 v2: symmetric peak-side LGA features (**days_since_peak_entry**)** — the existing LGA
trough features have no peak-side mirror; the cycle is not symmetric so the mirror is a real
hypothesis rather than a completion exercise.
Was: fps-1785999730316-7-c511f10b
8. **Review Sticky/Discount classification threshold** — the current threshold may not be carrying
signal; a re-cut is a candidate in its own right given Sticky exclusion feeds the LGA/Brand
aggregates.
Was: fps-1785999730120-5-048485f0

### Deliberately NOT folded in

These look adjacent but add_columns cannot express them — same reason lead 5 (regime-dependent
tau) needs its own slot. They remain separate beads:

• Tune label percentile (25th vs 33rd) — changes the target, not a feature column
• Revisit FP penalty via model-conditional damage distribution — an objective/policy change
• Tighten per-zone headroom attribution — methodology for the headroom map, not a candidate

## BLOCKED ON fps-3jj.21 — check the arity ceiling before writing any of these up (2026-08-24)

fps-3jj.14 measured the placebo ruler's behaviour with candidate column count and found
it does not degrade gracefully — it collapses. Max draws is min(floor(54/k), floor(30/k)) and the
bar's t-critical uses df = n_draws - 1, so on batch1's band the bar goes -0.27 at k=3, -0.31 at k=4,
**-0.78 at k=10**, and **no band can be computed** at **all at k>=18**. A candidate carrying one
column per LGA is literally ungradeable: two draws would need 70 distinct source columns and 54 exist.

**Lead 4 is the exposed one.** "Leader-weighted LGA consensus" reweights an LGA dispersion
statistic by per-LGA lead/lag roles. Written as 1-3 aggregate columns (a leader-weighted
consensus scalar plus maybe its delta) it is fine. Written as a per-LGA expansion — which
is the natural reading, and which this project has REAL precedent for, since the 35 LGA
features went in together — it cannot be graded by this pipeline at all. Decide the
construction deliberately, not by whichever is easier to write.

Leads 1, 2, 3 are 1-2 columns and unaffected. Lead 5 (regime-dependent tau) is not a
feature and already noted as needing its own experiment.

**What "blocked" means here:** the leads themselves need no gate — they are already
written down. The gate is on turning them into candidate SPECS, which is when arity gets
chosen. This bead's own instruction is to re-read the ledger before filing; re-read
fps-3jj.21's decision at the same moment. Primary edge is on fps-3jj.19 (the batch2
freeze + generator run), where the pool constraint actually bites; this edge is the
earlier warning.

## Folded in 2026-09-02 (backlog review): fps-pld — cross-fuel coupling

9. **Does diesel / U91 / premium lead E10?** Other fuel types are already captured in the
historical CSVs and go completely unused (AGENTS.md § Data strategy), so this costs a
correlation/lag check over data already on disk — no new source, no ingest work, which
is what makes it a batch2 lead rather than a project.The hypothesis is a lead-lag one: if
another grade turns before E10 does, that turn is a same-day-observable signal for the E10
cycle. Note it is adjacent to two things already on record and should engage with both in
its PRIOR_ART rather than being proposed cold:
    • The **wholesale-lead** family (tgp_delta_7d, tgp_cycle_displacement) — same shape
    of claim ("an upstream/parallel series turns first"), and that family has so far
    produced only inert readings. A cross-fuel lead is a different SERIES but not an
    obviously different MECHANISM, which matters for generator.md's >= 3-family spread
    requirement.
    • lga_trough_propagation (batch1, lead-lag-propagation) — same statistical form,
    different axis (fuel grade rather than geography).
**Do the cheap existence check before writing a candidate module**, per
feedback_oracle_diagnostic_pattern: cross-correlate the grade-level Sydney means at
lags 0-14d and confirm a lead exists at all. If nothing leads, this closes on ~an hour
of work and becomes a not_tested -> falsified ledger line rather than a batch2 slot.Arity: 1-2 columns if it survives (a lead spread, maybe its 7d delta), so fps-3jj.21's
arity ceiling does not bite here — unlike lead 4.Was: fps-pld (P3, filed 2026-09-01 from the retired FUTURE_IDEAS.md; closed as folded).

## Folded in 2026-09-05 (backlog review): fps-cde — both TGP expressions, one ruler

10. **tgp_delta_7d and tgp_cycle_displacement, both re-graded at 1d in batch2.** tgp_delta_7d has
never been measured at the project's canonical 1d cadence — its status is UNTESTED, not rejected.
Decision (2026-08-31): batch2, not batch1 (a 6th candidate would re-cut batch1's floor after the
other five were already dossiered) and not its own 1d-frozen batch (a new freeze's own noise floor
is a disproportionate ~3.8h wall for one candidate) — batch2 (fps-3jj.19) is already planned at
10-15 candidates with its own freeze/floor paid for regardless, so this costs one slot and ~20min
of run. **Include tgp_cycle_displacement as a second batch2 slot too** — it was graded against
batch1's floor, a different snapshot; landing only tgp_delta_7d in batch2 leaves the pair on two
different rulers, which defeats the stated point of putting both TGP expressions on ONE ruler.

**Expected outcome, stated before the run:** batch2's family-wise correction at 10-15 candidates is
STIFFER than batch1's at 5. tgp_delta_7d's best realised reading to date is +0.0059 c/L (inert,
40th percentile of batch0's noise floor) and will very probably not clear — **that is an
acceptable result and the reason to run it anyway**: the objective is a VALID 1d measurement that
closes the track honestly, not a graduation.

**Why the current readings do not count:** batch0's floor is methodologically retired, not just its
cadence — noise_floor.json carries no null_method (a pre-fps-awz seed-swap null, not the placebo
null every batch1+ floor uses), so dossier_tables._noise_band() refuses it (fps-sjk, closed
GRANDFATHERED not recomputed — the shipped CLI cannot recompute a 7d floor under a 1d TankParams,
and it would buy nothing since +0.00585 c/L is the unfavourable sign anyway). Separately, batch0's
figure is a 7d-cadence number and the re-lock to 1d (fps-oqz, 2026-08-22) was never restated against
it — dossier_tables._noise_band() refuses the cross-cadence comparison outright. The June
"graduation" at -0.0394 c/L was smaller than that run's own ~0.05 c/L single-flip quantum (itself a
7d quantity), and batch0's own recommendation was "hold," explicitly "do not close the track."

**Sequencing — resolved:** this was gated on fps-e6i (tau-distance diagnostic: if TGP's log-loss
gain turned out threshold-remote, the track could close without spending either batch2 slot).
fps-e6i is now CLOSED and did NOT close the track (per project_tgp_leading_indicator memory) — both
TGP batch2 slots stand.

Files: experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_delta_7d.py (port from batch0),
experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_cycle_displacement.py (port from batch1).

Acceptance carried forward: both TGP candidates included in the batch2 candidate table at
generation time; both graded at 1d against batch2's own floor, family-wise bar quoted for batch2's
size; verdict stated against that bar; #271 / fps-2sf closed or explicitly held with a reason.

Was: fps-cde (P2, filed 2026-08-31; closed as folded).

## Folded in 2026-09-05 (backlog review): fps-7gm — decompose tgp_cycle_displacement's two columns

11. **Ablate tgp_cycle_displacement's two columns separately** (`tgp_cycle_displacement_cents`,
`tgp_cycle_displacement_frac_amp`) — the pair went into batch1 and was graded as a block, but
facts.json carries no per-column attribution (no SHAP, no importance, no gain — only redundancy
R2, which measures reconstructibility from the lock, not contribution). Nothing currently
distinguishes "one column did the work" from "both did" from "they partly cancelled." Running each
alone also drops arity from 2 to 1, which matters: this run was already judged against an arity-3
floor one column wider than itself (`floor_arity_exceeds_run: true`, excess 1).

**All three of its gates are now closed**, unblocking it:
- fps-nas (replay universe) — closed.
- fps-2i4 (stale frozen price at station 414 contaminating folds 5-7 in level) — closed. Before
  this, an ablation would have been read across 3 of 14 contaminated folds.
- fps-1l1 (would a facts.json SHAP field make this answerable with no extra runs?) — closed, but
  via the "no" branch: `docs/routines/dossier.md` now states a `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` claim about
  SHAP orientation always grades inconclusive, and no SHAP field will ever exist in facts.json.
  So the free escape hatch this bead's own gating note hoped for is closed off — the two
  single-column runs are the only remaining way to answer the attribution question.

Same batch-size / family-wise-bar question as lead #10 (tgp_delta_7d) applies here and should be
resolved together with it, per fps-7gm's own acceptance criteria.

Files: experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_cycle_displacement_cents_only.py,
experiments/candidates/batch2/tgp_cycle_displacement_frac_amp_only.py.

Acceptance carried forward: both single-column runs graded against the correct-arity (1) floor;
result stated as which column carries the effect, or that neither does alone.

Was: fps-7gm (P2, filed 2026-08-31; closed as folded).

**Numbering note:** the list above already contains two entries numbered 6 (the turn-gated
stickiness lead, and the brand-level regime feature folded in from the standing backlog).
Pre-existing, not introduced here — but count entries, not numbers, when sizing this list.

description:
## What
Spec the generator session — the Opus/Fable session that proposes candidates and files one bead each.

Must be handed: the canonical column list; the **negative-results ledger**; docs/STATUS.md + the
#262 headroom map (regime axis flat, volatility hump 12-16c, intra-series in diminishing returns);
the no-new-datasets constraint; the fold/regime taxonomy; and that the arbiter is realised CPL, a
decision-timing objective, not accuracy — with cycle_mean_length as the cautionary example, verbatim.

Rules for candidates: every one states a mechanism; says why an existing feature doesn't carry it;
engages with prior art if adjacent to something rejected; declares `TARGET`,
`PREDICTED_SIGNATURE`, `CONFIDENCE`; and the set must span >=3 mechanism families with pairwise
|rho| below a threshold, checked before any bead is filed.

The ledger's job is NOT deduplication — the model reads the column list, so literal duplicates are
already handled. The three real failure modes are: re-proposing *rejected* candidates (not in
features.csv at all, so the column list gives no protection); reparameterisation (tgp_delta_14d vs
tgp_delta_7d, ~0.95 correlated — caught by the free correlation check, not by a prompt); and
redundancy against a *combination* of existing columns (regress candidate on the existing set, look
at R^2 — also free).

Batch sizing: batch 1 = 1 known graduate (`tgp_delta_7d`) to check the pipeline gives the right
answer; **batch 2 = 5**, the first genuinely AI-sourced set — small enough that a runner bug costs
5 nights rather than 10, and re-freezes onto fresher data sooner; batch 3+ = 10-15.

Prompt lives at `docs/routines/generator.md`; scheduler holds a three-line shim only (see fps-6zj).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/routines/generator.md` written and tracked
- [ ] Correlation + R^2-vs-existing-set checks run before any bead is filed
- [ ] >=3 mechanism families spanned in a batch
- [ ] Batch 2 = 5 candidates filed as experiment beads

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj


## Two CONFIDENCE fields (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

The generator states two priors per candidate, not one. Full definition and scoring rules live in
fps-3jj.4 (module format); the generator-side obligations are:

- `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT` — P(pooled realised CPL delta < 0). "Does it move the arbiter at all?"
- `CONFIDENCE_ZONE` — P(the effect concentrates where `TARGET` says). Scored only on candidates
  where `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT` resolved true.

Both are scored against outcomes in the retrospective (fps-3jj.8) — this is the payoff artifact for
aim (b), so the generator must be told explicitly that these numbers are graded, and that spreading
them (rather than filing everything at 0.5) is the point. A batch where every candidate is rated
0.5 produces no calibration signal at all.

`TARGET` carries the machine-resolvable zone claim; `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` stays prose for the
morning reader and for the ledger's `falsified` line. No structured `PREDICTIONS` companion —
`TARGET` already does that job.

## Calibration accumulates across batches (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

Five candidates cannot calibrate anything. The retrospective must APPEND confidences and outcomes to
a running record and read calibration across batches, not within one — otherwise the first
retrospective produces a confident-looking chart off n=5 and it will be believed.

## Diversity rule: rho is the gate, mechanism family is a disclosure (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

The original rule required BOTH ">=3 mechanism families" AND "pairwise |rho| below a threshold".
These are two different controls that fail in opposite directions — neither subsumes the other:

- **|rho|** catches reparameterisation: two candidates ~0.95 correlated (`tgp_delta_14d` vs
  `tgp_delta_7d`) waste a slot. Mechanical and free.
- **Mechanism family** catches what rho cannot: several statistically uncorrelated candidates that
  all encode the same story ("the network is converging on a trough"). Reads as diversity, isn't.

But only rho is checkable. "Mechanism family" has no definition that is not the generator's own
say-so, and a generator that wants five slots will assert three families.

**Decision:**
- **|rho| is a HARD GATE** — a batch cannot be filed with a pair above the threshold.
- **Mechanism family is a REQUIRED DISCLOSURE, not a threshold.** The generator names the family per
  candidate; the batch record stores it. If all five come back in one family, that is visible in the
  dossier and the retrospective and becomes a *finding about the generator* rather than a gate it
  learned to game.

Rationale for the demotion: "asked for five distinct ideas, produced five variants of one" is
exactly the kind of thing aim (b) exists to discover. Making it a gate hides it; making it a
disclosure measures it.

## Redundancy checks run in the generator, not at launch (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

Both free mechanical checks — pairwise |rho| across the batch, and R^2 of each candidate regressed
on the existing column set — run in the **generator session**, before any bead is filed. Launch
validation does not duplicate them.

Two reasons:
- **Pairwise rho is a batch-level property.** Launch validation sees one candidate per night, so it
  structurally cannot perform this check at all.
- **Redesign beats rejection.** A candidate 90% reconstructible from existing columns should be
  reworked before it is filed, not filed, queued, and disqualified five nights later when it
  finally reaches the front of the queue. That is the entire value of "checked before any bead is
  filed".

Residual risk accepted: a candidate module edited after filing is unchecked. Low in a one-machine
setup, not worth a second implementation.

**No coupling to the batch freeze.** The checks run against live `data/features.parquet`, NOT the
frozen batch snapshot — a redundancy screen is insensitive to which day's data it uses (a column
0.95-correlated with `tgp_delta_7d` on Monday is 0.95-correlated on Thursday). The freeze exists to
make cross-night comparison valid, which is a property of the runs, not of a screen. So the
generator session has no ordering dependency on fps-3jj.1 and the two can proceed independently.

## Generator is an interactive session, not a scheduled task (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

The parent design specified three routine prompts (launch / dossier / generator) each with a
scheduled-task shim. Launch and dossier are genuinely nightly; the generator is not — it runs once
per batch (every 5 nights at batch 2, every 10-15 later).

**Decision: the generator is invoked by the owner at batch setup. Two scheduled tasks, not three.**

- **The cadence is an event, not an interval.** "Once per batch" means "the experiment queue has
  drained" — scheduling it would mean designing and maintaining a trigger condition, which is more
  machinery than starting a session.
- **It is the step most worth reviewing before it commits you.** Its output determines what N nights
  of compute run on. Batch setup is already manual and hard-gated (the DB refresh aborts on
  failure), so the human checkpoint already exists there.
- **Costs aim (b) nothing.** Generation is still AI-sourced; only the invocation is human. What is
  being measured — what the model proposes, whether CONFIDENCE predicts its hits — is unaffected by
  who pressed go.

`docs/routines/generator.md` still earns its place as the versioned prompt file (fps-6zj reason:
instructions live in the repo, never duplicated into a scheduler). It is simply invoked manually.

## Revised acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/routines/generator.md` written and tracked; NOT registered as a scheduled task
- [ ] Pairwise |rho| hard gate + R^2-vs-existing-set check run in the generator session against live
      `data/features.parquet`, before any bead is filed
- [ ] Mechanism family recorded per candidate as a disclosure (not gated)
- [ ] `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT` + `CONFIDENCE_ZONE` stated per candidate, and the generator told they are
      graded and that spreading them is the point
- [ ] Batch 2 = 5 candidates filed as `experiment` beads

description:
## What
The retrospective — the payoff artifact for aim (b). Nothing else in the pipeline produces it.

After a batch:
- Leaderboard across all candidates.
- Every candidate's delta against the batch noise-floor band. The ranking step is exactly where a
  noise delta gets promoted to a finding — max-of-N is a multiple-comparisons operation the old
  one-at-a-time workflow never performed.
- Outcome-code tally. A candidate that never ran is *missing data*, not a negative result; folding
  `aborted_*` into `rejected` would bias the calibration below. "2 of 10 candidates were leaky" is
  itself one of the more interesting findings a batch can produce.
- **The generator's `CONFIDENCE` scored against outcomes** — did the ones it rated 0.6 beat the ones
  it rated 0.2? For aim (b) that is probably a more durable finding than any individual feature.

Note for whoever acts on the leaderboard: one-at-a-time additive screening never validates a
*combination*. If 3 candidates each help alone, "graduate all three" does not follow — that is its
own extra run.

Also: write `docs/feature-pipeline.md` once the machinery has settled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Retrospective bead template exists
- [ ] Leaderboard + noise-band comparison + outcome tally + confidence calibration produced
- [ ] `docs/feature-pipeline.md` written

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj
title: Pipeline: batch retrospective

description:
## What
Dossier routine — turns a completed run's artifacts into something readable next morning.

Work queue is self-describing: any experiment dir with `results.json` and no `README.md`. If the
run is still going it exits quietly.

Output is facts, plots, key points and an overall recommendation — deliberately NOT a binary
verdict. It must support starting a session to interrogate it further.

Requirements:
- Per-fold and per-regime breakdown always (replaces the hypothesis-specific `GateSpec.target_fold`,
  which cannot generalise across candidates), plus the candidate's own axis when supplied.
- **Min-cell-n guard**: a 12-level axis produces cells of ~30 rows whose delta is pure noise, and
  they would otherwise print in the same table, same font, as everything else. Flag or suppress.
- Candidate's delta reported against the batch **noise-floor band**, as a number. The reader has a
  feel for the noise range; the routine writing the dossier does not.
- `seed_variance_gate` stays a hard, loud check — a blown-up seed_std on one fold still prints as a
  clean five-seed average and must shout, or noise reads as a finding.
- Grade the run against its own `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` — the teaching artifact, and it writes the
  ledger's `falsified` field almost for free.
- Write the ledger entry AND the INDEX.md row in the same pass so they cannot drift.
  `not_tested` is the only field requiring actual reasoning and is probably the highest-value
  sentence produced per run.
- Parquet artifacts are gitignored and stay local-only; the dossier records the snapshot date so
  results stay attributable.

Prompt lives at `docs/routines/dossier.md`; scheduler holds a three-line shim only (see fps-6zj).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Picks up a completed run unattended and produces a readable README
- [ ] Delta vs noise-floor band printed as a number
- [ ] Per-fold / per-regime / per-axis breakdown with min-cell-n guard
- [ ] seed_variance_gate surfaced loudly
- [ ] Ledger entry + INDEX.md row written in the same pass
- [ ] `docs/routines/dossier.md` tracked

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj


## Code / Claude boundary (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

**Claude does no arithmetic.** A deterministic `dossier_tables.py` reads `results.json` + rowpreds +
fills and emits one `facts.json` plus the PNGs. The Claude step reads `facts.json` and writes prose
only.

Three reasons: numbers in the README trace to a regenerable file (a number computed in-context
cannot be checked short of a re-run); if the Claude step dies the facts already exist on disk, so
the dossier stays re-runnable and its work queue still works; and the overnight Claude burst stays
short, which the design wants.

Rule for the README that follows from this: anything not traceable to `facts.json` is judgement and
must be visibly separated. `not_tested` is exactly that — the one place the routine is supposed to
be reasoning rather than transcribing.

### `facts.json` blocks

| Block | Contents |
|---|---|
| `provenance` | candidate name, batch, **snapshot date**, git SHA, seeds, wall-clock, status code, bd id |
| `headline` | realised CPL per arm + delta (the arbiter); WFCV log-loss delta, explicitly labelled descriptive |
| `breakdowns` | per-fold, per-regime, per-axis — each cell carries `n`, delta, `seed_std`, and a `suppressed` flag from the min-cell-n guard |
| `seed_flags` | the actual list of cells over the 5x threshold, not a boolean |
| `validation` | NaN rate, PIT test result, INPUTS check result |
| `grading` | Claude's read of the run against `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` |
| `noise_band` | null until fps-3jj.9 lands; the slot exists now so the schema does not change later |

**Signature grading stays prose (DECIDED, KISS).** A structured `PREDICTIONS` companion was
considered — it would let code grade each clause mechanically and give the retrospective a
comparable clause hit-rate — and was rejected as over-engineering. Consequence to accept knowingly:
the retrospective's CONFIDENCE-calibration finding rests on Claude's reading of Claude's own
prediction, not on a mechanical check.

## Plots (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

Chosen by auditing which of the ~120 PNGs on disk actually appear in an experiment's conclusion as
the thing that decided or explained the verdict.

**Always, four:**
1. **Per-fold delta bars, signed, shock folds marked.** Per-fold sign flips are the project's most
   repeated lesson — `drop_redundant_pair` and `cycle_pct_through_interaction` both looked good
   until the per-fold view; the cohort-band experiment's whole story was "amplifies, doesn't
   smooth". If the dossier shows one plot, this is it.
   Precedent: `r1_per_fold_hard25.png`, `step5c_perfold_bars.png`.
2. **Mean vs median across seeds.** Makes the seed-variance check visible. `a_c_ablation`'s verdict
   rested on "median >= mean, so most seeds agree", which is invisible in an averaged number.
   Precedent: `r1_mean_vs_median.png`.
3. **Realised CPL by fold.** The arbiter gets its own view, separate from log-loss.
   Precedent: `realised_by_regime.png`.
4. **Tau-sweep over the saved rowpreds.** Universal, not conditional. `regime_cycle_length` nearly
   shipped an operating-point artifact as a feature win (tau worth ~2x the feature effect, wrong
   direction); the sweep is post-hoc over persisted predictions, so it is free. In
   `leading_indicators` all arms landed on tau=0.25 and the plot said "nothing to net out" at a
   glance — exactly the reassurance an unattended dossier should be forced to provide.
   Precedent: `tau_coordinate.png`.

**Conditional — routed off metadata the module already declares, no new fields:**

| Trigger | Plot | Precedent |
|---|---|---|
| `INPUTS` names an external series | overlay vs Sydney E10 | `tgp_vs_e10_overlay.png` — revealed TGP as the floor and the regime-dependent lead |
| candidate touches cycle phase | feature vs `cycle_pct_through`, split by regime | `phase_by_regime.png` / `phase_oracle_cycles.png` — showed shallow-vs-steep is invisible in A until phase >1.4 |
| `add_axis` supplied | per-cell delta with `n` annotated, thin cells greyed | the visual form of the min-cell-n guard |

**Plus one with no precedent, because nobody needed it before:** the candidate column over time with
its NaN band. Nobody reviews this code — one glance that makes a malformed column obvious is worth
having in an unsupervised pipeline.

**Deliberately excluded: per-fold delta scattered against a fold-level covariate**
(`elongation_vs_per_fold_delta.png`). It produced a confident wrong conclusion once — the fold-level
elongation framing later had to be retired because fold averages drowned out a 15%-of-rows subset
carrying 65% of the effect. The row-level bucket breakdown answers the same question honestly.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] `dossier_tables.py` emits `facts.json` + PNGs deterministically, no model in the loop
- [ ] README separates facts (traceable to `facts.json`) from judgement (`not_tested`, recommendation)
- [ ] Four always-plots present in every dossier
- [ ] Conditional plots routed off `INPUTS` / `TARGET` / presence of `add_axis`
