description:
## What
Launch routine + its scheduled task. This is the piece batch 1 exists to validate: claim ->
validate -> launch detached -> exit, surviving session exit.

- Nightly, ~10 min, Claude active. `bd dolt pull` -> claim next experiment bead ->
  run the validation harness -> launch the runner detached -> exit.
- Detached launch must survive session exit: `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null &`, output to `run.log`.
- Queue: `bd ready --label experiment --unassigned --sort oldest -n 1`. The `experiment` label
  exists so the chore/polish worker can never claim a candidate bead and try to implement it in a
  cloud container with no data.
- **Must be a separate scheduled task** from the chore/polish worker: that worker exits immediately
  if any claude-authored PR is open, so sharing the routine means one un-merged chore PR silently
  stops every experiment for days.
- Stale-claim recovery: dir exists, `run.log` ends in a traceback, no `results.json`, started >12h
  ago -> post the traceback to the bead and release the claim.
- Prompt location: `docs/routines/launch.md`, tracked in the repo. The scheduled task's stored
  prompt is a three-line shim (who you are, working directory, which repo file to read) and nothing
  else — `.claude/` is gitignored here. Rationale is fps-6zj: both prior stale prompt copies went
  stale precisely because instructions were duplicated into the scheduler.

N=1 cannot validate stale-claim recovery by waiting — fault-inject it rather than assume it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `experiment` label exists and the chore/polish worker cannot claim those beads
- [ ] Launch routine claims, validates, launches detached, exits — verified surviving session exit
- [ ] Separate scheduled task from the chore/polish worker
- [ ] Stale-claim recovery verified by fault injection
- [ ] `docs/routines/launch.md` tracked; scheduler holds only a three-line shim

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj

## Note: this is a LOCAL Routine
Registered in the Claude app on the owner's Mac, not a cloud Routine. The Dolt-push credential
failure in fps-sk0 was a cloud-container egress/askpass restriction and does NOT apply here —
local `bd dolt push` works with ambient git credentials. Do not import that workaround.
title: Pipeline: launch routine + scheduled task

description:
## What
Candidate module format + the one-shot runner. This is the core: everything else launches it,
validates its input, or reads its output.

Module format (one Python file per candidate, committed to `experiments/candidates/<batch>/`;
`experiments/**` is exempt from the PR rule so the generator can commit straight to main):
`NAME`, `TARGET`, `HYPOTHESIS`, `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE`, `CONFIDENCE`, `COLUMNS`, `INPUTS`,
`PRIOR_ART`, `add_columns(df)`, and optional `add_axis(df) -> pd.Series` (per-row group labels —
the candidate *writes* its slicing axis rather than picking from an enum).

Runner: **two arms, R0 / candidate** (no placebo — see parent). Frozen data + fixed
`SEEDS = (42,43,44,45,46)` + fixed baseline columns means R0 is bit-identical every night, so fit it
once on night 1 and cache predictions in the batch dir.

Emits:
- `results.json` with the status code (`rejected` / `disqualified` / `aborted_candidate` /
  `aborted_environment` — kept distinct for the retrospective, not for retry policy)
- **rowpreds parquet** (`RowPredCollector.to_parquet`) with the axis column written into
  `ident_base`, and the **fills ledger** (`run_paired_realised_backtest(collect_fills=True)`).
  These are what make later re-slicing, regime re-cuts and the tau-sweep inertness diagnostic
  possible with zero refits.
- a self-reported bd comment

Realised CPL is the arbiter; WFCV log-loss is descriptive colour (the two have demonstrably
disagreed — cycle_mean_length, the raw TGP gap).

Hard decision boundary: the pipeline NEVER touches `fuel_signal/features.py`,
`experiments/results.csv`, or `data/models/`. Graduation is a separate, human-initiated PR.

Also: first run gives the per-night wall-clock number, which the design never totalled.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Module format documented with a worked example
- [ ] Run emits results.json + rowpreds/fills parquet + status code + self-reported bd comment
- [ ] Axis column (when supplied) persisted into rowpreds
- [ ] R0 predictions cached in the batch dir
- [ ] Per-night wall-clock instrumented and logged

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj


## Two CONFIDENCE fields (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

`CONFIDENCE` splits into two numbers, because "does it work" and "does it work where I said" are
different predictions and the retrospective wants both. Both are the generator's own stated priors,
scored against outcomes in fps-3jj.8 — the payoff artifact for aim (b).

```python
CONFIDENCE_EFFECT = 0.35   # P(pooled realised CPL delta < 0)
CONFIDENCE_ZONE   = 0.50   # P(the effect concentrates where TARGET says)
```

| Field | Question | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|
| `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT` | does it move the arbiter at all? | pooled realised CPL delta < 0 |
| `CONFIDENCE_ZONE` | does it land where I said? | the cells named in `TARGET.expect_concentration_in` hold a negative delta AND the most negative delta of any cell on that axis, with min-n cells excluded |

**`CONFIDENCE_ZONE` is scored conditionally** — only on candidates where `CONFIDENCE_EFFECT`
resolved true. A candidate that never moved the arbiter has no zone to be right about, and scoring
it would calibrate zone-accuracy on noise.

**No new module field is needed.** `TARGET` is already the machine-resolvable claim about where the
effect concentrates, and the dossier already computes per-axis breakdowns with a min-n guard.
`PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` stays prose — it is what the morning reader gets, and the raw material for the
ledger's `falsified` line. A structured `PREDICTIONS` companion was considered and is NOT needed
now that `TARGET` carries the scoreable version.

Module format becomes:

```python
NAME, TARGET, HYPOTHESIS, PREDICTED_SIGNATURE,
CONFIDENCE_EFFECT, CONFIDENCE_ZONE,
COLUMNS, INPUTS, PRIOR_ART,
add_columns(df), add_axis(df)   # add_axis optional
```

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both CONFIDENCE fields present in the module format and carried into `results.json`
- [ ] Zone resolution computed mechanically off `TARGET` + the per-axis breakdown

## Batch-1 pass criterion is pre-registered (DECIDED 2026-08-17)
Batch 1 runs `tgp_delta_7d`, a candidate that graduated the realised arbiter but is deliberately NOT
in the trained-model contract yet. It is not a re-run of the original experiment (later data vintage;
column computed via `add_columns` rather than the experiment's `extra_feature_provider` closure), so
the pooled delta will land near -0.039 c/L, not on it.

Criterion, fixed before the run: **sign plus concentration** — pooled realised CPL delta negative,
AND gains appearing in the expensive high-headroom folds. Magnitude is explicitly not part of the
test. See fps-3jj for the full rationale and the ordering constraint (do not complete the TGP
re-lock before batch 1).

- [ ] Batch-1 pass criterion recorded in the batch dir BEFORE the run, not after

## Code layout (DECIDED 2026-08-17 — applies across fps-3jj.1/.2/.4/.6, agree before parallel work)

**Pipeline application code lives in a new `experiments/pipeline/` package.**
`experiments/lib/` stays what it is: helpers shared by hand-written experiment scripts, governed by
its README's promotion rule (*extract on the 2nd unchanged copy*). Pipeline modules are first-use by
definition, so putting them in `lib` would break the convention that governs it. Dependency
direction is one-way: `pipeline` imports `lib`; `lib` never imports `pipeline`.

In `experiments/pipeline/`: the batch freezer (.1), the restricted-frame `INPUTS` check (.2), the
runner (.4), `dossier_tables.py` (.6), and the launch/stale-claim helpers (.5).

**One deliberate exception — the differential PIT test goes in `experiments/lib/`.** It is a
general-purpose leak check, and hand-written experiments compute candidate columns in-script too
(standing convention, see memory `feedback_features_via_experiment_first`), so they should be able
to call it directly rather than reaching into the pipeline package.

Rationale for fixing this now: it is the one thing parallel sessions on .1 and .2 would collide on
(both would otherwise invent a package `__init__.py`). See also the concurrency constraints — do NOT
run `uv` concurrently across worktrees (recorded failure: half-synced `.venv`, `ModuleNotFoundError`
for `six`/`py`, fix is `rm -rf .venv && uv sync`), and all `bd` writes from any nested worktree land
in the PRIMARY worktree's `.beads/interactions.jsonl`, so one session should own the beads commits.
title: Pipeline: candidate module format + one-shot runner

description:
## What
`experiments/ledger.yaml` — the compressed, machine-readable residue of every experiment, feeding
the next generator session. Single YAML file, newest-first (matches INDEX.md ordering; one machine,
one writer, so per-entry files buy nothing and cost skimmability).

Fields: `candidate` (NAME), `inputs` (INPUTS), `claim` (HYPOTHESIS), `falsified`, `not_tested`,
`outcome` (status code), `evidence` (experiment dir).

**Keyed on the falsified claim, not the feature name.** `station_minus_tgp_cents` was rejected but
the TGP *series* was not — `tgp_delta_7d` graduated off the same data with a different mechanism. A
generator reading "TGP: rejected" would draw exactly the wrong conclusion, so `inputs` (what data)
is held separately from `claim` (what was asserted).

`not_tested` is the field that earns the ledger's keep: without it the ledger only says "don't go
here", which makes the generator timid. In the TGP case it would have handed the generator the
winning candidate.

Relationship to INDEX.md: both stay. INDEX.md is the reverse-chronological prose lab book;
ledger.yaml is the structured claim record. The dossier routine writes BOTH in the same pass so
they cannot drift.

Scope here: define the format, then one-time hand backfill of the ~20 historical experiment dirs
listed in experiments/INDEX.md (its Result column already carries the mechanism-level detail, it
just isn't in these fields).

Doing this early stress-tests the format before the pipeline starts emitting entries.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Format documented and an example entry committed
- [ ] ~20 historical experiments backfilled
- [ ] Worked example (station_minus_tgp_cents -> not_tested: velocity of the floor) present

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj

description:
## What
Validation harness run before any fitting. Candidate modules are LLM-authored and nobody reviews
the code, so this is the whole safety layer.

1. **`INPUTS` enforcement by restricted frame** — call `add_columns(frame[declared_inputs].copy())`;
   any undeclared read raises `KeyError`. Exact, unevadable, free. This is a *provenance* check
   (INPUTS feeds the correlation/redundancy checks and the ledger's `inputs` field), not a leak check.
   The originally-specified textual lint is DROPPED: it misses the likeliest LLM leak (a whole-series
   aggregate such as `df.groupby('station_code')['price'].transform('mean')` — no `shift`, every row
   sees the station's future) and false-positives on legitimate `closed='right'` windows.
2. **Differential PIT test — the sole leak abort.** Compute on the full frame and on a frame
   truncated at date T; values at dates <= T must be identical. Must abort the night.
   Applies to the optional `add_axis` too: an axis with future info is a leak into the *conclusion*
   ("helps on days that turned out to be troughs" is unactionable at 7am), not into the model.
3. **NaN-rate assert** + report the rate for the dossier.
4. Columns-only smoke, NOT a fit.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Restricted-frame INPUTS check raises on an undeclared read
- [ ] Differential PIT test demonstrably aborts on a known-leaky candidate
- [ ] PIT test covers `add_axis` when present
- [ ] NaN rate asserted and surfaced

description:
## What
Batch freeze — the setup step that makes a batch reproducible. Purely mechanical; no design
decisions remain.

Freeze once at batch setup, then all N nights run on day-0 data. Explicitly accepted: nights 2..N
do not see fresh data. That is what makes cross-night comparison valid.

**No `fuel_signal/` changes required — both seams already exist:**
- Snapshot `data/features.parquet` into the batch dir and call
  `load_features('<batch>/features.csv')`. The loader prefers a `.parquet` sibling when the CSV is
  absent, so this works untouched.
- Pin the SQLite too, via APFS `cp -c` (copy-on-write: near-instant, near-zero disk). Stage B of
  `run_paired_realised_backtest(..., db_path=...)` (experiments/lib/realised.py:210) replays
  economics out of the live DB, so an unpinned DB would silently un-freeze the batch.

Consequence: the DB refresh moves OUT of the nightly path and becomes a one-time batch-setup step,
**hard-gated** — if refresh fails, abort setup. Never run a batch on stale data.

Record the snapshot date somewhere every dossier can read it ("snapshot: data to 2026-08-13").

Frozen data + fixed `SEEDS = (42,43,44,45,46)` + fixed baseline columns means R0 is bit-identical
every night. Caching R0's predictions in the batch dir belongs to the runner (fps-3jj.4); this bead
only has to make that guarantee true.

## Not in scope
The noise-floor calibration originally specified here is split out to **fps-3jj.9** and backlogged —
it still has an open design question (what an "uninformative draw" is) and must not block the freeze.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Batch freeze produces a runnable snapshot with zero `fuel_signal/` changes
- [ ] SQLite pinned via `cp -c` into the batch dir and used by the realised backtest
- [ ] DB refresh hard-gated; batch setup aborts on failure
- [ ] Snapshot date recorded where the dossier routine can read it

Parent design + full rationale: fps-3jj


## Pin the feature contract, not just the data (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

The freeze as originally specified pins the *data* (features snapshot + SQLite) but not the
*baseline feature-column list*, which comes from code. A `FEATURE_COLUMNS` bump landing between
night 2 and night 3 silently changes R0 — and because R0's predictions are cached in the batch dir
after night 1, the run would reuse night-1 predictions against a different baseline and say nothing.
This is not hypothetical: the TGP chip-4 re-lock (fps-1785999729707-1 / gh#271) adds
`tgp_delta_7d` to the contract and is expected to land between batches.

**Decision — pin + fail-fast, not reconciliation.** Batches run to completion; feature-column work
happens between batches. The pipeline does not need to *handle* a mid-batch contract change, it
needs to refuse to pretend nothing happened.

- Write the **resolved** baseline column list into the batch dir at freeze time, sorted.
  Resolved, not the constant names: brand trough columns are DB-derived and discovered from the
  features-CSV header at train time (`discover_brand_feature_columns`), so
  `FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS + NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS` does not fully determine the
  baseline.
- **Per batch, not per candidate bead.** The column list is a property of the batch. Per-bead means
  N copies that can drift, and the check would then pass or fail depending on which candidate
  happened to run.
- At the start of every run, re-resolve the current list and compare. On mismatch, **abort the night
  and print the diff** (which columns appeared/disappeared) rather than just failing — the diff is
  what tells you whether it was an intentional re-lock or an accident.
- Abort maps to `aborted_environment` (external state changed under the batch), not
  `aborted_candidate` — the candidate is fine.

This is also what makes the R0 prediction cache safe. Today it would be keyed on nothing.

## Additional acceptance criteria
- [ ] Resolved baseline column list written into the batch dir at freeze time
- [ ] Every run re-resolves and compares; mismatch aborts the night and prints the column diff

## Code layout (DECIDED 2026-08-17 — applies across fps-3jj.1/.2/.4/.6, agree before parallel work)

**Pipeline application code lives in a new `experiments/pipeline/` package.**
`experiments/lib/` stays what it is: helpers shared by hand-written experiment scripts, governed by
its README's promotion rule (*extract on the 2nd unchanged copy*). Pipeline modules are first-use by
definition, so putting them in `lib` would break the convention that governs it. Dependency
direction is one-way: `pipeline` imports `lib`; `lib` never imports `pipeline`.

In `experiments/pipeline/`: the batch freezer (.1), the restricted-frame `INPUTS` check (.2), the
runner (.4), `dossier_tables.py` (.6), and the launch/stale-claim helpers (.5).

**One deliberate exception — the differential PIT test goes in `experiments/lib/`.** It is a
general-purpose leak check, and hand-written experiments compute candidate columns in-script too
(standing convention, see memory `feedback_features_via_experiment_first`), so they should be able
to call it directly rather than reaching into the pipeline package.

Rationale for fixing this now: it is the one thing parallel sessions on .1 and .2 would collide on
(both would otherwise invent a package `__init__.py`). See also the concurrency constraints — do NOT
run `uv` concurrently across worktrees (recorded failure: half-synced `.venv`, `ModuleNotFoundError`
for `six`/`py`, fix is `rm -rf .venv && uv sync`), and all `bd` writes from any nested worktree land
in the PRIMARY worktree's `.beads/interactions.jsonl`, so one session should own the beads commits.

description:
## What

A pipeline for evaluating AI-proposed candidate features end-to-end with minimal supervision:
an Opus/Fable session generates N candidate features + files one bead each; a **local** nightly
scheduled task runs one candidate per night; a separate local routine turns each run's artifacts
into a readable dossier.

Dual aim: (a) find new features, (b) **gain experience with an AI-sourced pipeline** — what an LLM
proposes, whether it can predict its own hits, how often it produces leaky or redundant candidates.
Aim (b) is primary; turnaround time is explicitly NOT being optimised.

## Why this shape

- **Local, not cloud.** GHA is out (2000 min/month budget). The existing worker routine is *remote*
  (docs/automation.md:80) with a fresh checkout and no data — structurally cannot run this.
  Viking OOMs on features.py. The Mac has all artifacts; the pipeline is gated on it being awake.
- **No new pipeline manager.** Beads is the queue. One bead per candidate. Scheduled tasks are the
  trigger. The runner is one Python script over the existing `experiments/lib/`.
- **No supervising Claude.** Overnight is Claude peak pricing. Claude is active only in short bursts
  at the start of a run and in the dossier routine.

## Architecture — three local pieces

| Piece | Claude | Does |
|---|---|---|
| **Launch** (nightly, ~10 min) | active | `bd dolt pull` -> claim next `experiment` bead -> validate candidate (static lint, differential PIT test, NaN-rate assert) -> `setsid nohup` the run -> exit |
| **Run** (hours, detached) | none | fits, realised arbiter, plots, rowpreds + fills parquet, `results.json`, status file, terse `bd comment` |
| **Dossier** (later, same night) | active | write-up + plots -> `experiments/<dir>/README.md`, INDEX.md row, close/annotate the bead |

The dossier routine's work queue is self-describing: any experiment dir with `results.json` and no
`README.md`. If the run is still going it exits quietly. It also inherits stale-claim recovery —
dir exists, `run.log` ends in a traceback, no `results.json`, started >12h ago -> post the traceback
to the bead and release the claim.

Detached launch must survive session exit: `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null &`, output to `run.log`.

## Batch freeze (decided)

Freeze once at batch setup, then all N nights run on day-0 data. Explicitly accepted: nights 2..N
do not see fresh data. This is what makes cross-night comparison valid.

Both seams already exist — **no changes to `fuel_signal/` required**:
- `load_features(path)` prefers a `.parquet` sibling when the CSV is absent -> snapshot
  `data/features.parquet` into the batch dir, call `load_features('<batch>/features.csv')`.
- `run_paired_realised_backtest(..., db_path=...)` (experiments/lib/realised.py:210) -> pin the
  516MB SQLite too, since stage B replays economics out of the live DB. Use APFS `cp -c`
  (copy-on-write): near-instant, near-zero disk.

Consequence: the DB refresh moves OUT of the nightly path and becomes a one-time batch-setup step,
hard-gated (if refresh fails, abort setup; never run on stale data). Record the snapshot date in
every dossier ("snapshot: data to 2026-08-13").

`SEEDS = (42,43,44,45,46)` is already shared in `experiments/lib/constants.py`. Frozen data + fixed
seeds + fixed baseline columns => **R0 is bit-identical every night**, so fit it once on night 1 and
cache the predictions in the batch dir (~12 min/night saved, and identity guaranteed not assumed).

## Candidate module format

One Python file per candidate, committed to `experiments/candidates/<batch>/`. (`experiments/**` is
exempt from the PR rule, so the generator session can commit these straight to main.)

```python
NAME = "tgp_accel_7d"
TARGET = {"axis": "regime", "expect_concentration_in": ["shock"], "folds": [4, 9]}
HYPOTHESIS = "..."              # mechanism in price-formation terms, not "the tree might like it"
PREDICTED_SIGNATURE = "..."     # what the numbers should look like if the mechanism is real
CONFIDENCE = 0.35               # generator's own prior — scored in the retrospective
COLUMNS = ["tgp_accel_7d"]
INPUTS = ["tgp_delta_7d", "price_date"]   # declared reads -> restricted-frame check + correlation
PRIOR_ART = "adjacent to station_minus_tgp_cents (rejected #215) — differs in ..."
def add_columns(df): ...        # pure fn of the features frame; no DB, no network
def add_axis(df): ...           # OPTIONAL — per-row group labels; see Slicing axes below
```

## Slicing axes (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

**What an axis is for.** A candidate doesn't only claim "this helps" — `TARGET` claims *where* it
helps. The dossier grades that prediction, which means the runner must split results into groups
along the named axis and compute a delta per group.

**`TARGET` must not be a closed enum.** Regimes (`shock`/`normal`/`late_descent`/`overdue`) and named
folds are *known* values, not the vocabulary limit. The existing taxonomy is made of axes past
experiments happened to slice on; a feature whose value lives on an uncut axis would otherwise have
no way to declare itself and would read as a null. Cheap because rowpreds are persisted — an
arbitrary slice is a groupby, not a refit.

**The gap that opens, and the fix.** Naming an axis does not produce one. For `regime` the runner
knows what to do (`zones.assign_regime()` over `cycle_pct_through`); for "absolute price level"
there is no column and no bin edges, so there is nothing to group by. Declaration without a
construction mechanism.

Fix: **the candidate supplies a function, not a name** — optional `add_axis(df) -> pd.Series` of
per-row group labels, same shape as `add_columns`, which is already unconstrained Python over the
frame. The candidate *writes* the axis rather than picking from a list, so this adds a construction
mechanism without adding a constraint. The runner groups by whatever Series comes back. No enum,
no registry, no new machinery. Omit `add_axis` and the runner uses the standard fold/regime cuts.

**There are real uncut axes** — this is not hypothetical: day-of-week (Sydney cycles have weekday
structure), wholesale direction (TGP rising vs falling — exactly where `tgp_delta_7d` lives),
competition density, cycle *amplitude* as distinct from length, brand class (independents vs
majors). Note the pattern: all are functions of columns already in the frozen frame. "Arbitrary
axis" in practice means "arbitrary expression over `features.csv` + `price_date`", which is
precisely what a function over `df` provides.

**`add_axis` goes through the same differential PIT test as `add_columns`.** Different reason,
though: an axis computed with future information is not a leak into the *model* (the model never
sees it — it groups results afterwards), it is a leak into the **conclusion**. An axis like "days
that turned out to be near the cycle trough" yields "helps a lot on trough days" — true, and
unusable, because you cannot know at 7am whether today is a trough. This is the one way an
unattended pipeline could produce a confidently untradeable recommendation, and the test is free.

**Granularity unifies; effective sample size does not.** `SHOCK_FOLDS = {1,4,9,13}` is a *fold*
property while `normal/late_descent/overdue` are *row* properties — the original `TARGET` example
mixed both in one dict. Under a per-row Series that conflation is harmless (a fold-level axis is
just a Series constant within fold). What does not unify is n: shock/non-shock is 4 folds vs 10,
while a row-level split is hundreds of thousands of non-independent rows, and a candidate declaring
a 12-level axis produces cells of ~30 rows whose delta is pure noise — printed in the same table,
same font, as everything else. So: **min-cell-n guard** — cells below threshold are flagged or
suppressed, never reported as findings.

**Continuous axes require explicit fixed edges, not quantiles.** Equal-count bins hide
non-monotonic structure; this project has been bitten by it before. A candidate binning a
continuous quantity (price level, volatility) must supply the edges.

## Per-run arms — two, not three (DECIDED 2026-08-17)

**R0 / candidate.** No per-night placebo arm.

The problem a placebo was meant to solve is real but narrow: the dossier is *written* by an
unattended routine with no feel for scale, so a delta of ~0.008c can be recorded as a finding when
an uninformative column would have produced the same number. That bites specifically once the
retrospective **ranks** candidates — taking the max of N deltas is a multiple-comparisons operation
the previous one-at-a-time workflow never performed.

**But a per-night placebo is the wrong instrument.** One draw per night is a single sample of the
null, so it compares a noisy number against a noisy ruler. And the noise floor is a property of the
*pipeline* (fold structure, seed count, LightGBM's response to one extra column), not of the
candidate — so it should be estimated once, well, rather than badly every night.

**Decided form — noise-floor calibration at batch setup:**
- One calibration run when the batch is frozen: 10–20 uninformative draws through the same fit +
  realised-backtest path, producing a **distribution**, not a point.
- Stored in the batch dir; every dossier prints the candidate's delta against that band.
- Zero per-night cost, and the runner stays at two arms.

> **CORRECTION 2026-08-21 (bd `fps-awz`). This section's DECISION stands; what was built to
> satisfy it does not.** Two departures from the text above, both material:
>
> 1. **"Uninformative draws" was implemented as an R0-vs-R0 SEED SWAP** (baseline@42 vs
>    baseline@47), not as an uninformative column. That measures the wrong operation. A
>    candidate is judged **paired** — same seed, same folds, one column added, so nearly all
>    the fit's idiosyncrasy is common-mode and cancels (batch0's two arms made identical
>    decisions on **741 of 752 fills**). The seed swap is **unpaired**: two independent fits,
>    nothing shared, both arms' full wander present. Different perturbations with no fixed
>    ratio between them, so the band cannot be rescaled into the right one. Direction is
>    knowable: unpaired ⇒ too WIDE ⇒ the gate is too strict. `noise_floor.py`'s own docstring
>    already hedges here ("a floor, not the true band").
> 2. **"10–20 draws" was implemented as 5.** With 5 draws the dossier's empirical rank can only
>    return {0,20,40,60,80,100} while the Bonferroni threshold at 5 candidates is 99.0 — so the
>    gate collapses to "beat all 5 draws", null probability 1/6 per candidate against a nominal
>    1%. batch0 could not expose this at N=1.
>
> **The fix returns to this section's own shape:** a bank of **placebo COLUMNS** computed once
> at batch setup — which is what "uninformative draws" meant. The rejection of a per-night
> placebo is untouched and correct; the objection was to ONE DRAW PER NIGHT, not to placebos.
> Construction is the hard part and fails the OTHER way if done lazily: white noise gets ignored
> by the trees, giving a null that is too narrow and a gate too permissive. See `fps-awz`.

The point retained from the placebo idea is that the range must be **written down as a number**, not
carried as intuition — the reader has the feel, the routine doing the writing does not.

(Permutation mechanics were explored and are not needed under this design. Noted for anyone who
revisits it: a within-date permutation is a no-op for a market-wide series like `tgp_delta_7d`,
where every station shares a value on a given date, so the permutation axis would have had to match
the axis the candidate claims to carry information on.)

## Outcome taxonomy (four codes, not two)

- `rejected` — run completed, doesn't help. Bead closes. Normal outcome.
- `disqualified` — differential PIT test failed. The candidate was invalid and the pipeline caught it.
- `aborted_candidate` — `add_columns` threw / NaN blowout. Repeatable; do not retry. Mark `blocked`.
- `aborted_environment` — OOM, disk, interrupted. Retry once.

Codes stay distinct **for the retrospective**, not for retry policy (neither aborted case is retried
automatically). A candidate that never ran is *missing data*, not a negative result — folding it into
`rejected` would bias the confidence-calibration analysis. And "2 of 10 candidates were leaky" is
itself one of the more interesting findings the batch can produce.

## Validation (in the Launch routine, before any fitting)

1. **`INPUTS` enforcement by restricted frame** (DECIDED 2026-08-17 — replaces the static lint).
   Call `add_columns(frozen_frame[declared_inputs].copy())`; any undeclared read raises `KeyError`.
   Exact, unevadable, free. This is a **provenance** check, not a leak check — it exists because
   `INPUTS` feeds the correlation/redundancy checks and the ledger's `inputs` field, and both are
   wrong if the module quietly reads a fourth column.

   The originally-specified textual lint (grep for `shift(-n)`, `closed='right'`) is **dropped**:
   it misses the likeliest LLM-authored leak, which is a whole-series aggregate
   (`df.groupby('station_code')['price'].transform('mean')` — no `shift`, every row sees the
   station's entire future), and it false-positives on legitimate code (`closed='right'` is correct
   for any quantity known at decision time, e.g. today's own price).
2. **Differential PIT test — the sole leak abort.** Compute the column on the full frame and on a
   frame truncated at date T; values at dates <= T must be identical. Catches the whole-series
   aggregate case on the first truncation. Must abort the night. **Applies to `add_axis` too** when
   present — see Slicing axes for why (leak into the conclusion, not the model).
3. **NaN-rate assert** + report the rate in the dossier. Not a new problem (warm-up NaN already exists
   and paired deltas are on identical rows) — it is newly *unsupervised*, since nobody reviews the code.
4. Columns-only smoke, **not a fit** — Claude should not be active for 20 minutes.

## Output / dossier

Facts, plots, key points and an overall recommendation — deliberately **not** a binary verdict.
This is a learning project; the dossier must be readable next morning and must support starting a
session to interrogate it further.

Requirements:
- Persist **rowpreds parquet** (`RowPredCollector.to_parquet`) and the **fills ledger**
  (`run_paired_realised_backtest(collect_fills=True)`). These are what make later re-slicing,
  regime re-cuts and the tau-sweep inertness diagnostic possible with zero refits.
- Always show the per-fold and per-regime breakdown (replaces the hypothesis-specific
  `GateSpec.target_fold`, which cannot generalise across candidates).
- `seed_variance_gate` stays a **hard, loud check**. A blown-up seed_std on one fold still prints as a
  clean five-seed average; it must shout in the dossier or noise reads as a finding.
- Report the candidate's delta against the batch's **noise-floor band** (see Per-run arms), as a
  number, every run.
- Grade the run against its own `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` — the teaching artifact.
- Realised CPL is the arbiter; WFCV log-loss is descriptive colour. Decided in advance because the two
  have demonstrably disagreed (cycle_mean_length; the raw TGP gap).
- Parquet artifacts are gitignored (`experiments/**/*.parquet`) and stay local-only. Acceptable while
  this is one machine; the dossier records the snapshot date so results stay attributable.

## Bead N+1 — the retrospective

Nothing currently produces the payoff artifact. After the batch: leaderboard across all candidates,
every candidate's delta against the batch noise-floor band (the ranking step is exactly where a
noise delta gets promoted to a finding), outcome-code tally, and **the generator's `CONFIDENCE` scored
against outcomes** — did the ones it rated 0.6 beat the ones it rated 0.2? For aim (b) that is
probably a more durable finding than any individual feature.

Also note: one-at-a-time additive screening never validates a *combination*. If 3 candidates each help
alone, "graduate all three" does not follow — that is its own extra run.

## Generator session (separate bead to spec)

Must be handed: the canonical columns; the **negative-results ledger**; docs/STATUS.md + the #262
headroom map (regime axis flat, volatility hump 12-16c, intra-series in diminishing returns); the
no-new-datasets constraint; the fold/regime taxonomy; and that the arbiter is realised CPL, a
decision-timing objective, not accuracy (cycle_mean_length is the cautionary example, verbatim).

Rules: every candidate states a mechanism; says why an existing feature doesn't carry it; engages with
prior art if adjacent to something rejected; declares `TARGET`, `PREDICTED_SIGNATURE`, `CONFIDENCE`;
and the set must span >=3 mechanism families with pairwise |rho| below a threshold, checked before any
bead is filed.

**The ledger's job is not deduplication.** "Don't propose existing features" already handles literal
duplicates — the model reads the column list. The three real failure modes are: re-proposing *rejected*
candidates (not in features.csv at all, so the column list gives no protection); reparameterisation
(`tgp_delta_14d` vs `tgp_delta_7d` — ~0.95 correlated, caught by the free correlation check, not by a
prompt); and redundancy against a *combination* of existing columns (regress candidate on the existing
set, look at R^2 — also free). So store rejections **with their mechanism-level reason**, since a
candidate may legitimately revisit a rejected series with a different mechanism. (The standing
example used to be "`tgp_delta_7d` graduated after the raw gap failed" — **that graduation was
retracted 2026-08-19 as inert**, so the illustration is now: the raw gap was rejected on the SHOCK
axis, the velocity was measured and came back below the arbiter's resolution, and the TGP series is
*still* open on a third claim nobody has tested — the gap versus depth-remaining on late descent,
bd `fps-x0f`. Which makes the point more sharply than the original did.)

## Negative-results ledger — format (DECIDED)

**Not a new document.** A ledger entry is the candidate spec plus that run's conclusion, stapled.
The dossier is the long human-readable version; the ledger entry is the compressed machine-readable
residue that feeds the *next* generator session. Same run, two audiences.

| ledger field | source | when |
|---|---|---|
| `candidate` | `NAME` | spec, before the run |
| `inputs` | `INPUTS` | spec, before the run |
| `claim` | `HYPOTHESIS` | spec, before the run |
| `falsified` | dossier conclusion | after |
| `not_tested` | dossier judgement | after |
| `outcome` | status code | after |
| `evidence` | experiment dir path | after |

**Key design point: the ledger is keyed on the falsified *claim*, not the feature name.**
`station_minus_tgp_cents` was rejected but the TGP *series* was not. A generator reading
"TGP: rejected" would draw exactly the wrong conclusion. **Updated 2026-08-20:** the second claim on
that series (`tgp_delta_7d`, velocity) is now recorded as `inconclusive` rather than `graduated` —
measured below the arbiter's resolution, so neither a win to build on nor dead ground to avoid. That
three-way vocabulary (rejected / inconclusive / graduated) is mirrored in
`features.NON_MODEL_COLUMNS`, and it exists precisely because collapsing it to two would tell the
generator the wrong thing in both directions. So `inputs` (what data) is held separately from `claim` (what was asserted).

Worked example:

```
candidate:   station_minus_tgp_cents
inputs:      AIP Sydney TGP, station price
claim:       "distance to the wholesale floor predicts remaining descent"
falsified:   helps calm (-0.012) but HURTS shock (+0.011) — today's TGP misleads
             when the floor is moving
not_tested:  velocity/acceleration of the floor   <- became tgp_delta_7d
outcome:     rejected
evidence:    experiments/2026-06-20_leading_indicators/
```

`not_tested` is the field that earns the ledger's keep. Without it the ledger only says "don't go
here", which makes the generator timid; with it, the ledger actively points at remaining room — in the
TGP case it would have handed the generator the winning candidate.

Two consequences:
- **`PREDICTED_SIGNATURE` grading writes `falsified` almost for free** — spec predicted "concentrates in
  shock", it helped in calm, that's the line.
- **`not_tested` is the only field requiring actual reasoning**; everything else is transcription. It is
  therefore the one thing the dossier routine's Claude step genuinely has to think about, and probably
  the highest-value sentence it produces per run.

Entries are generated per-run by the pipeline from `batch0` onward. Historical entries (the ~20 dirs in
`experiments/INDEX.md`) need a one-time hand backfill — INDEX.md's Result column already carries the
mechanism-level detail, it just isn't in these fields.

**Serialisation: a single `experiments/ledger.yaml`, newest-first.** YAML because a human needs to read
it; one file rather than per-entry files because per-entry would avoid write conflicts that don't exist
here (one machine, one writer) at the cost of skimmability. Newest-first matches INDEX.md ordering —
a trivial prepend for the dossier routine.

**Relationship to INDEX.md: both stay, different jobs.** INDEX.md is the reverse-chronological lab-book
narrative with the rich prose Result column; `ledger.yaml` is the structured claim record the generator
consumes. There is real overlap, so the rule is that the dossier routine writes **both in the same
pass** — neither is derived from the other, but they cannot drift independently either.

## Batch sizing (DECIDED)

Runs per night: **1**. Candidates per batch = N = the freeze span (N nights on day-0 data) and the
number of results the retrospective compares.

> **NUMBERING CORRECTED 2026-08-21.** This section numbered batches from 1 while the
> directories numbered from 0, so "Batch 2" below and `experiments/batches/batch1` are the
> same thing. Batches are now named by their **directory**: `batch0` (calibration, DONE),
> `batch1` (first AI-sourced set), `batch2`+ . Canonical statement lives in
> `docs/routines/generator.md`.

- **`batch0` = 1 candidate — DONE 2026-08-19.** A **known graduate** (`tgp_delta_7d`), because
  the point was exercising the whole pipeline end to end and a known graduate gives a right
  answer to check against. Two steps it did NOT exercise: the R0 prediction cache (nothing
  reuses it at N=1) and the retrospective's actual analysis (nothing to rank, no calibration to
  score) — fine, it proved those steps *run*, not that they say anything.

  **Outcome, and it is not what this section anticipated.** The pre-registered criterion was
  *sign plus concentration* — pooled delta negative AND gains in the expensive high-headroom
  folds, magnitude explicitly excluded. What the pipeline returned was `delta_cpl_held`
  **+0.0059 c/L**, reproducing an independently-written reference to every printed digit. The
  **pipeline was validated**; the *feature* was not. June's −0.039 c/L does not reproduce, and
  was never resolvable in the first place — smaller than one buy/wait decision flip (~0.05 c/L
  pooled). Two contract defects were found and fixed along the way: wrong column SET
  (`fps-sa1`, PR #309) and wrong column ORDER (`fps-zci`, PR #310).

  **So the premise below is void: `tgp_delta_7d` did NOT graduate.** The retraction is recorded
  in `experiments/ledger.yaml`, `experiments/INDEX.md` and `features.NON_MODEL_COLUMNS` (as
  `evaluated-inconclusive`). **#271 is closed as superseded**; successor `fps-x0f` asks whether
  *any* TGP expression earns a place rather than assuming one does.

  **The ordering constraint this section imposed — "batch 1 → finish the TGP re-lock → batch 2"
  — is therefore DISCHARGED, not pending.** It existed so the first AI-sourced candidates would
  not be judged against a baseline missing a proven feature. There is no such feature: the
  re-lock will never happen, and no TGP feature is in the lock. Do not treat it as a gate.
  `docs/routines/generator.md` carried the same text verbatim and was corrected (commit
  `35b183e`).

  **What DOES still hold from the above: pre-register the pass criterion.** That reasoning was
  sound and is the reason batch0's result is readable at all — the criterion was fixed before
  the number was seen, so "pipeline validated, feature inert" could be stated cleanly instead of
  argued after the fact.

- **`batch1` = 5**, the first genuinely AI-sourced set. Small enough that a runner bug costs 5
  nights rather than 10, and re-freezes onto fresher data sooner. **Blocked** (2026-08-21) on
  `fps-awz` (the noise floor above), `fps-15c` (cadence stamp), `fps-oqz` (the 7d→1d cadence
  re-lock) and `fps-aay` (the freeze itself). It will be frozen at **1-day cadence**.
- **`batch2`+ = 10-15**, once the machinery is trusted and retrospective statistics start to
  matter more than iteration speed.

## Decision boundary (hard)

The pipeline NEVER touches `fuel_signal/features.py`, `experiments/results.csv`, or `data/models/`.
`results.csv` especially — it is main-only/ask-first by convention and an unattended routine appending
to it is a plausible accident. Graduation is a separate, human-initiated PR.

## Queue isolation

Experiment beads get a **fourth label: `experiment`**. Without it the remote worker's
`bd ready --label chore` will eventually claim an experiment bead and try to implement it in a cloud
container with no data. The local runner queries `bd ready --label experiment --unassigned --sort oldest -n 1`.

Must be a **separate scheduled task** from the existing chore/polish worker: that worker exits
immediately if any `claude-authored` PR is open, so sharing the routine means one un-merged chore PR
silently stops every experiment for days.

## Open / to spec separately

- [ ] One-time hand backfill of the ~20 historical experiments into `experiments/ledger.yaml`
- [ ] Three prompt files: launch / dossier / generator. **Location DECIDED: `docs/routines/{launch,dossier,generator}.md`**,
      tracked in the repo. **But only TWO are scheduled tasks** (revised 2026-08-17, fps-3jj.7): launch
      and dossier are nightly; the **generator is invoked interactively by the owner at batch setup**,
      because its cadence is an event ("the experiment queue has drained") rather than an interval, and
      because its output commits N nights of compute and is worth reviewing first. Each scheduled task's
      stored prompt (local `SKILL.md`) is a three-line shim — who you are, working directory, which repo
      file to read and follow — and nothing else. `.claude/` is gitignored here so prompts cannot live
      there. Rationale is fps-6zj: both existing stale prompt copies went stale precisely because
      instructions were duplicated into the scheduler instead of referenced from the repo. Do not repeat
      that with the new routines.
- [x] **Prerequisite: fps-6zj** (both stale worker prompts fixed, `docs/routines/` established) —
      CLOSED 2026-08-14; `docs/routines/worker.md` exists, so this no longer blocks.
      fps-sk0 (remote worker's Dolt push blocked) also raised to P1 but is NOT a blocker here —
      local `bd dolt push` works.
- [ ] fps-6zj — the stale local worker prompt at ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/fuel-price-signal-worker/SKILL.md
      still references GitHub Issues (pre-Beads) and is orphaned (list_scheduled_tasks returns none)
- [ ] `docs/feature-pipeline.md` once this settles

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `experiment` label exists and the remote worker cannot claim those beads
- [ ] Batch freeze produces a runnable snapshot with zero `fuel_signal/` changes
- [ ] Differential PIT test implemented and demonstrably aborts on a known-leaky candidate
- [ ] Launch routine claims, validates, launches detached, exits — verified surviving session exit

## What
.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml only auto-merges PRs carrying all three labels: claude-authored + chore + auto-merge-ok. Dependabot PRs only ever get dependencies/python:uv-style labels, so they structurally can never qualify — they sit open forever even when green and old, regardless of urgency (including security patches).

## Why I noticed this
Investigating fps-e9z (16 open Dependabot alerts). PR #277 (soupsieve 2.8.3->2.8.4, one of the three fixes fps-e9z asks for) has been open since 2026-07-10, MERGEABLE, all checks green, auto-merge workflow's own "auto-merge" check reports SUCCESS — but it never actually merged, because it never matched the label gate.

## Decision
Extend the same age (900s) + all-checks-green gate to a second PR set: open PRs authored by app/dependabot carrying the dependencies label. Confirmed via `gh pr list --state open --author "app/dependabot" --label dependencies --json number` that this cleanly identifies Dependabot PRs without false positives. No distinction by semver bump size (major vs minor/patch) — matching the existing risk tolerance for the claude-authored chore gate, where CI (ruff+pytest, signal-regression) is the safety net rather than manual bump-size triage. Flagged as a possible future tightening, not built now (avoid scope creep).

## Files likely affected
- .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Auto-merge workflow also considers Dependabot-authored PRs with the dependencies label, subject to the same 900s age gate and all-checks-green gate
- [ ] Existing claude-authored chore path unchanged
- [ ] PR #277 (and future Dependabot PRs) merge automatically once eligible
title: Auto-merge workflow never merges Dependabot PRs

description:
Settled 2026-08-10 (fps-luw). Per-snapshot re-query over an overlapping trailing window is
the from-scratch DB rebuild's dominant cost — 79% of classify's read+compute, 99% of
lga_leadership's. Range paths load once and slice; single-snapshot paths stay as they are.

Which shape is forced by memory, not by taste: preload the full range when SQL has already
aggregated (30 MB), stream a sliding window when it has not (a naive full load is 540 MB
resident / 881 MB peak and OOMs Viking).

Argument lives in AGENTS.md § "Backfill (`--start-date`) paths: load once, slice in memory"
and experiments/2026-08-10_backfill_requery_profile/README.md. This record is a pointer,
not a second copy.

Implementation: fps-53j, fps-2us.
title: Backfill range paths load once and slice; shape depends on SQL aggregation level

description:
## Start here — working prototype already on main

A profiled reference implementation exists. **Read it before writing any code:**

    experiments/2026-08-10_backfill_requery_profile/

- `proto_backfill.py` — has a working `day_bucket_stream()` and a parity
  check against the current query. Lift this shape; don't re-derive it.
- `README.md` — full profile table, memory measurements, and why the two
  backfill fixes have different shapes.
- `profile_backfill.py` — re-run to reproduce the before-numbers:
  `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python $EXPDIR/profile_backfill.py fuel_signal.db`
  (where $EXPDIR is the dir above)
- `run.log` is gitignored repo-wide and will NOT be in your checkout; the README tables
  carry every number it held.

Also see AGENTS.md § "Backfill (`--start-date`) paths: load once, slice in memory".

---

## What

`classify_range` calls `daily_prices_in_window` once per daily snapshot with a 45-day
window — 3597 times over a full backfill, re-fetching ~31k rows each time when the whole
history is 2.23M rows.

Replace the per-snapshot query in the **range path only** with a single
`ORDER BY dp.price_date` scan feeding a `deque` of per-day buckets: append day `D-1`,
evict day `D-window`. `classify_snapshot` keeps its direct query — the daily path
(`daily-db-update.yml`, no `--start-date`) must stay as-is.

See AGENTS.md § "Backfill (`--start-date`) paths: load once, slice in memory".

## Why (profiled, not assumed — fps-luw)

Measured against the real 492 MB DB (2.23M E10 `daily_prices` rows, 3597 dates,
744 councilled stations):

| component | per snapshot | x3597 snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| `daily_prices_in_window` (45d) | 47 ms | **169 s** |
| python compute (`_classify_lga`) | 12 ms | ~30 s |
| writes (delete + upsert) | 5.2 ms | 19 s |
| `commit()` | 8.4 ms | 30 s |

End-to-end measured 284 s projected on Mac; 471 s on the GitHub runner (PR #279,
gh run 31300192738). Mac→GHA ratio 1.66x.

Prototyped: 45 consecutive windows byte-identical to the current query, identical class
counts; read+compute 199 s → ~21 s projected (9.5x). Expected step time on a GHA runner:
471 s → ~90 s.

## Two constraints that shape the implementation

1. **Do not naively load the full range.** A full-history `daily_prices_in_window` is
   **540 MB resident / 881 MB peak** (2.23M Python tuples) — it will OOM Viking. The
   45-day deque is ~7 MB. This is why classify needs a different shape from
   `lga_leadership` (see the companion issue), whose SQL has already aggregated.
2. **Yield day buckets, not a flattened row list.** Flattening the deque into
   `[(station, lga, date_str, price), ...]` per snapshot rebuilds 31k tuples each time and
   eats most of the win. Have the consumer iterate buckets straight into `by_lga`.

`ORDER BY dp.price_date` is free — `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows `daily_prices_fuel_date`
already delivers that order with no sort step, and the ordered full scan costs the same
2.5 s as the unordered one.

## Secondary lever (in scope)

Batch commits in range mode. 3597 commits at 8.4 ms = 30 s on Mac under WAL +
`synchronous=FULL`, and disproportionately worse on Viking's storage. Keep the
per-snapshot commit in single-snapshot mode.

## Files likely affected

- `fuel_signal/classify.py` (`classify_range`, `classify_snapshot`)
- `fuel_signal/db.py` (new streaming/bucketed helper alongside `daily_prices_in_window`)
- `tests/test_classify.py`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `classify_range` performs one ordered scan; resident set stays O(window), not O(history)
- [ ] `classify_snapshot` unchanged for the single-snapshot (daily) path
- [ ] Test asserting range-mode and per-snapshot-mode produce identical `station_class` +
      `classification_summary` rows
- [ ] Commits batched in range mode, per-snapshot in single mode
- [ ] Before/after wall-clock captured for a multi-snapshot backfill
title: classify backfill: single ordered scan + sliding day-bucket deque

description:
## Start here — working prototype already on main

A profiled reference implementation exists. **Read it before writing any code:**

    experiments/2026-08-10_backfill_requery_profile/

- `proto_backfill.py` — has a working `lga_sums_slicer()` and a parity
  check against the current query. Lift this shape; don't re-derive it.
- `README.md` — full profile table, memory measurements, and why the two
  backfill fixes have different shapes.
- `profile_backfill.py` — re-run to reproduce the before-numbers:
  `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python $EXPDIR/profile_backfill.py fuel_signal.db`
  (where $EXPDIR is the dir above)
- `run.log` is gitignored repo-wide and will NOT be in your checkout; the README tables
  carry every number it held.

Also see AGENTS.md § "Backfill (`--start-date`) paths: load once, slice in memory".

---

## What

`score_leadership_range` calls `_load_lga_sums` once per weekly snapshot with a 730-day
window. Successive windows overlap ~98%, so the same 3-way JOIN + GROUP BY is re-run 523
times over what aggregates to only ~106k rows for the entire decade.

Replace the per-snapshot query in the **range path only** with a single full-range
`_load_lga_sums()`, bucketed by `date_int`, sliced per snapshot via `np.searchsorted`.
`score_leadership_snapshot` keeps its direct query — the daily path
(`daily-db-update.yml`, no `--start-date`) must stay as-is.

See AGENTS.md § "Backfill (`--start-date`) paths: load once, slice in memory".

## Why (profiled, not assumed — fps-luw)

Measured against the real 492 MB DB (2.23M E10 `daily_prices` rows, 3597 dates, 32 LGAs):

| component | per snapshot | x523 snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| `_load_lga_sums` (730d window) | 982 ms | **513 s** |
| python compute (trough detect, matching) | 13 ms | 7 s |
| writes + commit | ~20 ms | ~10 s |

**SQL is 99% of this step.** scipy/trough detection is 1% — not the problem.
End-to-end measured 583 s projected on Mac; 1019 s on the GitHub runner (PR #279,
gh run 31300192738). Mac→GHA ratio 1.75x.

Full-range load costs 4.5 s and **30 MB** resident — no memory concern, because the SQL
has already aggregated to `(date, LGA)`.

Prototyped: 4 sampled windows byte-identical, read cost 513 s → 5.3 s projected (97x).
Expected step time on a GHA runner: 1019 s → ~40 s.

## Parity is provable, not just testable

`_load_lga_sums` has `HAVING COUNT(*) >= MIN_STATION_FLOOR` grouping on
`(dp.price_date, s.council)`. Every group lives entirely within a single `price_date`, and
the window filter only selects which dates are included — so windowing cannot change any
group's membership or count. A full-range load returns exactly the union of every
windowed load.

## Files likely affected

- `fuel_signal/lga_leadership.py` (`score_leadership_range`, `score_leadership_snapshot`,
  `_load_lga_sums` call sites)
- `tests/test_lga_leadership.py`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `score_leadership_range` performs exactly one `_load_lga_sums` call
- [ ] `score_leadership_snapshot` unchanged for the single-snapshot (daily) path
- [ ] Test asserting range-mode and per-snapshot-mode produce identical `lga_leadership` rows
- [ ] Before/after wall-clock captured for a multi-snapshot backfill
title: lga_leadership backfill: preload LGA sums once, slice per snapshot

close_reason:
Design complete. Root cause confirmed by profiling against the real 492MB DB: per-snapshot re-query over overlapping trailing windows is 59% of classify.py and 99% of lga_leadership.py; scipy/trough detection is 1%.

Decision: both range paths load once and slice, but with different shapes, because memory is the binding constraint on Viking:
- lga_leadership (SQL already aggregates to (date,LGA); full history = 106k rows / 30 MB) -> single full-range _load_lga_sums + date-bucketed searchsorted slicing. Parity provable: HAVING groups on (price_date, council), which no window can split.
- classify (raw per-station rows; full history = 2.23M rows / 540 MB resident, 881 MB peak -> would OOM Viking) -> one ORDER BY price_date scan feeding a 45-day deque of per-day buckets, ~7 MB resident. Yield buckets, not flattened rows.
Single-snapshot paths (the daily daily-db-update.yml path) unchanged in both.

Prototyped both: windows byte-identical to current queries. Projected on a GHA runner: classify 471s -> ~90s, lga_leadership 1019s -> ~40s; the two steps 25min -> ~2min, seed-db.yml 46min -> ~23min (history.py's network-bound 16min becomes the bottleneck).

Convention recorded in AGENTS.md § 'Backfill (--start-date) paths: load once, slice in memory'.
Implementation split into fps-53j (lga_leadership, do first — bigger win, simpler) and fps-2us (classify).
description:
## What
Diagnose and fix why the from-scratch DB rebuild (seed-db.yml) is so slow on Viking — classify.py and lga_leadership.py are the two heaviest steps and both scale badly on Viking's weak CPU (APU3) vs a GitHub Actions runner. Needs a design pass (algorithm/architecture decision), not a mechanical fix — leave to an interactive/Opus session.

## Why I noticed this
Measured actual per-step wall-clock from the PR #279 seed-db.yml run (gh run 31300192738, GitHub-hosted runner, ~46min total from-scratch rebuild):

| Step | Duration |
|---|---|
| history.py | ~16m19s |
| db.py | ~4m05s |
| fill.py | ~20s |
| classify.py (station Sticky/Competitive/Discount classification) | ~7m51s |
| lga_leadership.py (LGA leadership scoring) | ~16m59s |

lga_leadership.py + classify.py together are ~25min of the 46min total on fast hardware. Both are pure-Python/SQLite CPU-bound work (unlike history.py's network-bound downloads), so they're the disproportionate cost on Viking's APU3 — consistent with [[project_viking_deployment]]'s "~5h on Viking vs ~46min on a real runner" note, and with the last step in the pipeline being the one that visibly hangs.

Suspected root cause (needs verification/design, not assumed as the fix): both classify_range (fuel_signal/classify.py) and score_leadership_range (fuel_signal/lga_leadership.py) re-query SQLite in a loop — once per snapshot (daily for classify, weekly for leadership) — over a sliding window (45d / 730d respectively) that overlaps heavily with the previous iteration's window. That's a lot of redundant JOIN/GROUP BY work re-run across ~3,660 (classify) or ~523 (leadership) snapshots for what's ultimately a bounded number of unique days.

## Files likely affected
- fuel_signal/classify.py (classify_snapshot, classify_range, daily_prices_in_window call site)
- fuel_signal/lga_leadership.py (score_leadership_snapshot, score_leadership_range, _load_lga_sums call site)
- fuel_signal/db.py (daily_prices_in_window — potential new bulk-load helper)
- .github/workflows/seed-db.yml (timing will change if fixed; may inform whether Viking on-host rebuild becomes viable again)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root cause confirmed (profile, don't just assume the sliding-window re-query theory above)
- [ ] Design decision made and documented on approach (e.g. load full range once + slice in memory, vs. incremental/cached aggregation, vs. something else)
- [ ] Before/after wall-clock comparison captured (local backfill or a seed-db.yml re-run)
- [ ] Output parity verified — station_class / lga_leadership rows identical before and after for a full backfill
title: Optimize seed-db.yml's slowest steps (classify.py, lga_leadership.py) — Viking perf

description:
## What
`fill.py` has no date-range or incremental option — every invocation rebuilds the entire `daily_prices` table by forward-filling gaps across the full history. Add a way to reprocess only the recent tail (e.g. `--since-date`, or auto-detect the most recently filled date and reprocess from there, with enough lookback to correctly resolve forward-fill gaps that straddle the boundary).

## Why I noticed this
Designing a 3-workflow GitHub Actions plan (seed DB once, daily ingest, occasional model build) for running fuel-price-signal against Viking's data. `db.py` (loaded_files tracking), `classify.py` (default = today only), and `lga_leadership.py` (default = single snapshot) are all already incremental by default. `fill.py` is the odd one out — full rebuild every time. Currently cheap enough (it fit inside Viking's ~5h full-history budget), but it's the one step in the daily flow whose cost scales with total history length rather than with "how much is new since yesterday" — it'll get slower every year the history grows, unlike its neighbours in the same pipeline.

## Files likely affected
- fuel_signal/fill.py

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `fill.py` supports processing only recent history (e.g. `--since-date`, or auto-detecting the last-filled date) while still correctly resolving forward-fill gaps that straddle the boundary
- [ ] Full-rebuild behaviour stays available (flag, or remains the no-args default) for the seed/reset case
- [ ] README's build-from-scratch and daily-flow docs updated if the recommended daily invocation changes
title: Add incremental mode to fill.py (full daily_prices rebuild every run)

description:
## What

In the #262 headroom map (`experiments/2026-06-19_headroom_map/`), per-zone headroom (`model_cpl − oracle_cpl`) sometimes goes **negative** (e.g. monthly 2025-01 −3.6, 2023-10 −2.9; ≥16c band −0.5). A perfect-foresight oracle cannot lose, so these are **attribution artifacts**, not oracle failures. Improve the per-zone estimator so the numbers are trustworthy enough to drive feature decisions.

## Why the artifact exists

`oracle ≤ model` is guaranteed only at the level the oracle optimises: **whole window, per station**. Slicing by fill-date breaks it because:
1. The arms fill on **different dates and different counts** (≥16c band: 77 model vs 101 oracle fills) → pooling `spend/litres` within a zone compares different fills over different litres, not a paired quantity.
2. **Path coupling**: the oracle buys cheaply *just before* a high-price zone and coasts through it on forced minimal fills, so its in-zone fills are disproportionately expensive — the saving lands in the neighbouring zone. The per-zone decomposition of a path-coupled total is non-unique.

## Proposed approach

**Bias (the negatives):**
- Attribute cost to **consumption per station-interval**, not to purchase events. The car burns identical litres per zone regardless of strategy, so prorate each fill's cost across the intervals the fuel is consumed and compare arms per (station, interval) → identical per-zone denominators, paired difference. Removes the differing-fill-count term (the dominant artifact). (Caveat: still won't *guarantee* per-zone ≥ 0 since the oracle optimises the global total; the only fully-clean statement is window-level. Document that.)

**Variance (the ±spread):**
- **Station-bootstrap CIs** per zone, so a cell reports `7.09 ± CI` and ≥16c shows as 0-within-CI rather than a spurious −0.5. (Highest value-per-effort.)
- Optionally widen the station set (oracle is fit-free; only the model-harness pass costs) to shrink every bucket.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/<date>_headroom_attribution/` (new) reusing `model_fills.parquet` / `oracle_fills.parquet` — or extend `experiments/2026-06-19_headroom_map/headroom_periods.py`.
- Possibly a small `experiments/lib/` helper if the consumption-attribution proves reusable (coordinate with #264).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-zone headroom recomputed via consumption-interval attribution (paired denominators).
- [ ] Each reported zone carries a station-bootstrap CI; cells indistinguishable from 0 are flagged.
- [ ] Writeup states which granularities the `oracle ≤ model` bound holds at, and confirms whether the 12–16c ~7 c/L peak survives with a CI clear of 0.

## Notes

- Do NOT change `run_oracle_backtest` — it is exact-DP optimal; there is no slack there. This is purely an attribution/estimation issue.
- Not needed for the #262 conclusion (which already reports the noise floors); this is for if/when the volatility band is revisited.
title: Tighten per-zone headroom attribution: consumption-interval allocation + station-bootstrap CIs

description:
## What

Split out of `fps-cl7` (closed as a duplicate of `fps-jrl` for its other half) during the
2026-09-02 backlog review. This is the one part of that report that is NOT the
grading-clobber bug.

`experiments/candidates/batch0`'s `noise_floor.json` carries `null_method: None` — it
predates `fps-awz`'s placebo-column rework (closed 2026-08-21), which by its own scope
never touched batch0's existing floor. `dossier_tables._noise_band()` now refuses any floor
whose `null_method` is not `placebo_column`, so it reports:

> "noise_floor.json's null_method (None) is not 'placebo_column' — this floor predates the
> fps-awz placebo-column rework ... and does not grade this run."

Consequence: **`batch0/tgp_delta_7d` can no longer be graded against any noise floor at
all** under current tooling. Its committed facts.json / README / `ledger.yaml` entry record
`verdict: matched` with an explanation that explicitly cites the now-refused band ("z=+0.14
vs a band of mean -0.0135, std 0.142 c/L") as the reasoning that confirmed it inert. The
ledger currently lists that run as `graduated`.

## Why it matters now, not later

`fps-cde` proposes re-measuring `tgp_delta_7d` at the canonical 1d cadence as a batch2
candidate precisely because batch0's reading is on a retired cadence. If batch0's floor is
also methodologically retired, that is a second, independent reason the batch0 reading does
not count — worth stating explicitly so the batch2 decision rests on a complete argument.

## The decision to make

Either:
1. **Recompute** — `experiments.pipeline.noise_floor batch0 --force`, then re-grade
   `tgp_delta_7d` on equal footing with batch1+ and update its README/facts.json/ledger
   entry if the verdict moves (it is `graduated` today, so a re-grade is not cosmetic); or
2. **Grandfather** — record explicitly that batch0 is a pre-fps-awz calibration batch whose
   numbers are not comparable to batch1+, and stop treating the refusal as a defect.

Option 2 is cheap and may well be right: batch0 was a single-candidate PIPELINE validation
run, not a measurement anyone is building on. Price option 1 before choosing it.

## Files likely affected

- `experiments/candidates/batch0/noise_floor.json` (or wherever batch0's floor is rooted)
- `experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/{facts.json,README.md}`
- `experiments/ledger.yaml` — the `tgp_delta_7d` entry, currently `graduated`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Decision recorded: recompute, or grandfather with a written reason
- [ ] If recomputed and the verdict moves, README / facts.json / ledger.yaml updated together
- [ ] `fps-cde`'s argument updated to cite whichever answer this lands on
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-05: GRANDFATHERED (option 2), no code, batch0 untouched.

Statement lives in experiments/batches/batch0/RETROSPECTIVE.md § Grandfathered,
with pointers from experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/README.md and the
batch0 entry in experiments/ledger.yaml.

Option 1 (recompute) priced first, as this bead asked, and it is not available
from the shipped CLI at any price: `noise_floor batch0 --force` is refused by
check_freeze_cadence (fps-oqz) because batch0's freeze.json declares
50/3.571/7d/10% while the CLI resolves TankParams() = 1d and exposes no cadence
override (compute_noise_floor takes tank=; main never passes it). Already
asserted by tests/test_noise_floor.py::
test_batch0s_real_freeze_manifest_refuses_the_current_default_cadence against
the committed artifact, and already documented at docs/CONVENTIONS.md § cadence.
So option 1 costs new code first, then compute (batch1's 10-draw floor was
8,368s wall; DEFAULT_N_DRAWS is now 20).

Two corrections to this bead's own premises:
1. "The ledger currently lists that run as graduated" was WRONG at filing time.
   The batch0 entry has outcome: inconclusive, and did on 2026-09-02 (verified
   against experiments/ledger.yaml at commit 3cbf496). The June entry is also
   inconclusive and marked SUPERSEDED. So a re-grade IS cosmetic — the bead's
   only stated reason it would not be does not hold.
2. Sign forecloses the upside anyway: delta_cpl_held is +0.00585 c/L, the
   UNFAVOURABLE direction. No floor of any width graduates a positive delta; a
   narrower placebo band could only leave it inconclusive or push it to
   rejected.

Acceptance criteria:
[x] Decision recorded: grandfather, with the written reason above.
[ ] N/A — not recomputed, so no README/facts.json/ledger verdict move. facts.json
    deliberately untouched (owner: do not touch batch0 again); its stored
    noise_band block is a historical seed-swap record, and _noise_band()'s
    refusal at read time is the live, correct behaviour.
